If you on your own or with a friend can clear them as best you can I will award you with a very special gift. I have one pair of legs left to which I will color and give to the winner. If you fail to get through the mazes then you will be killed.
Boondar

Boondar is actually based on an old CBM64 and Spectrum smash-hit game called Bounder. The aim of the game is a simple one, yet a brilliant one; you are a ball, and must get to the end of a huge scrolling course. See? Excellent!

There are number of stepping stones along the way, some of which allow you to bounce on them as many times as you like, while others will dissolve away, leaving you to fall to your death. Other obstacles to be avoided include the many hedges that block your way, along with the odd nasty thing that plops in front of you and jumps up and down. To help you along the way, there are number of bonus tiles (shown with a “?”) which, once bounced on, will award varying effects.

Anyway, the joystick controls everything, and other than getting used to the bounce delay and the way the ball reacts to various tiles, it's all pretty damn simple! Have fun, courtesy of The One.
Booze-o-Meter

Quite the surprise when suddenly the drunk driving came up in what looked up until that point like a predictable events-based party game with events like Barrel Weightlifting and Beer Shooting. A substantial amount of effort went into it even though it was probably played only by drunk sceners at The Party 1994 and by not many people afterwards.
Bop 'n' Plop

A single-player, homebrew vertically scrolling shooter created by Fez Software using the Shoot-'Em-Up-Construction Kit (SEUCK). Called a Cute'em-up this game also had a sequel: Pee Bee: Revenge is Cute.
Boppin'

Boppin' is a puzzle-oriented video game created by Jennifer Diane Reitz in 1991, developed under the company name Accursed Toys and published by KarmaSoft for the Amiga computer with only 32 colors on screen. Around that time KarmaSoft held a level design contest. The game sold poorly with 284 copies, so Jennifer got it republished by Apogee Software (now known as 3D Realms) with up to 256 colors on screen. Due to mature content containing blood and Seppuku, the game was rated for players aged 25.

The game takes place in a multiverse where fictional universes exist mostly by the minds and dreams of people. One such universe called Arcapaedia is inhabited by video game characters, especially the two stick-figured, triangle-headed Yeet and Boik. However all the arcade games have been diminished due to the lack of bad guys and villains taken away by the puristic Hunnybunz Family.
Border Zone

It is the 1980's, and the Cold War between the Western Bloc (led by the USA) and the Eastern Bloc (led by the Soviet Union) is at its peak. The town of Ostnitz is located on the border between the fictional Eastern Bloc nation of Frobnia and the equally fictional neutral Litzenburg. The US ambassador is about to arrive in Ostnitz in order to deliver a speech on the occasion of the local Constitution Day. However, a plot to assassinate the ambassador, hence escalating the tension between the super-powers, is soon revealed.

Border Zone is a text adventure game in which the player controls three different protagonists throughout three chapters: an American businessman and two special agents - a Western and an Eastern one. Besides the traditional text-based exploration and puzzle-solving, the game has real-time elements: time passes even if the player does not interact with the game. Some stealth-oriented sequences rely on these elements, timing being crucial to advance.
Boris Ball

Boris Ball is a Breakout variant. The player controls a paddle at the bottom of the screen which can move left and right. A ball bounces between the paddle and blocks which are placed towards the top of the screen. The goal is to remove all destructible blocks by hitting them with the ball. If the ball falls out of the bottom of the screen, a life is lost. Destroying blocks may cause a power-up to fall down which has positive or negative effects when picked up, e.g. a longer paddle, shooting out balls straight from the paddle, reversed controls or a level-skip. There are overall 100 levels and it comes with a handy level editor.
Born Again Bad
An action puzzle demo written with AMOSPro 2.0 brought to you by Larry McGahey in 1996.
Borobodur: The Planet of Doom

Borobodur: The Planet of Doom is an Action game, developed by Softeyes and published by Thalamus, which was released in Europe in 1992.

As a platform and blast adventure, you must progress through all levels by collecting the various icons scattered at the most inconvenient of places. Who put the required object on a platform that demands a super-hyper jump from a dangerously high-up ledge?

It's not all run, jump and shoot, though. Sub-levels include a puzzle game against the computer where you shuffle square blocks about a board in an attempt to recreate the original pattern. There's also a turbo bike section, featuring an Outrun/Lotus perspective. Final words: Frustratingly slow and tedious with minimal action.
Borodino

The sequel to the 1989 game Waterloo takes us back to the village of Borodino on the 7th of September, 1812, during the bloodiest battle of Napoleon's invasion of Russia.

As in the previous game, the player is observing the battle area through a 3D perspective while issuing commands by typing in certain pre-defined text commands that are combined with the names of commanders, places, and the time of execution. Players receive reports from their officers indicating whether or not the orders have been carried out to the letter.
Boron

Probably best known as the precursor to the genuinely loved sequel Boron II, this game is difficult because you are dead with a single hit. Just as in real life you get one shot at it. It is a shooter, but offers some challenging navigation elements as well, plus a pretty intimidating boss. It is unfortunately the first and final boss rolled into one. It's a short game which can likely be played in less than 2 minutes by someone who knows the foes and challenges of it.
Boron II

This game starts out looking like a straight-forward horizontally scrolling shooter, but the entire first wave you might as well not shoot your weapon, it is all about avoiding shots fired and oncoming meteors, but from then on becomes a full on shooter. Like the first game in the series you only have one life to give for your hobby. If you get hit you have to start from scratch. Unlike the original, you proceed past the first boss and are greeted by a mix of shooting and avoid-it areas throughout the alien complex to a second boss. If you can take him out, the game is complete. Though you might want to let it play on after completion as the music is pretty funky.
Borrowed Time

Borrowed Time is set in mid-1930's. The player assumes the role of a private investigator named Sam Harlow, who has to solve the kidnapping of his ex-wife Rita Sweeney. At the beginning, he runs away from two thugs, who want to kill him for an unknown reason. They fail, and he begins to search the town for clues, asking its inhabitants for information. But if the player makes a wrong move, Sam dies - killers come from nowhere and murder him...

The player has to type in combinations of verbs and nouns to make an action. Locations are described in text form and presented by pictures, the latter often providing additional information not contained in the text description.
BosCar

BosCar is very unplayable because of the way the action is viewed. Especially when you have to drive side ways or towards the screen. Just imagine playing Lotus while the viewpoint is directed towards your front windowscreen so you can only see what happens behind you! I've seen the idea of BosCar also in some other games and demos but the “more freedom approach” just doesn't work that well most of the time.
Bosseln

Bosseln is a game of skill in which two players have to try to throw wooden balls as far as possible in a landscape. The throwing technique rather than luck determines the distance of the throw. The game requires 1 MB. Author: R. Werner in 1991 and is freeware.
Boston Bomb Club

In this humorous puzzle-action game you as one of the members of mad scientists club have to play the game with other members. Billiard table is now a puzzle maze, where opponents throw bombs, and you have to operate some mechanisms to pass the bombs in certain places. Level after level the mechanisms are added and the difficulty is raised.
Botich Story II
A Czech language high school dropout text adventure game by Amiga Bestware Company in 1993.
Botics

Botics is a Pong variant set in the future. It is disguised as futuristic sports event in which the player fights against five opponents. The basic idea is that each playfield has a large opening on two sides which are guarded by remote-controlled robots. Each of the opponents controls a robot with the goal to reflect a bouncing ball so it enters the opposite opening. If that happens, the screen switches to the next of five areas, e.g. if the players were in the second chamber, they either switch to area one or three depending on who scored. A player needs to score a certain amount of times to win a match.

Variations to the areas (which are the same for each opponent) consist of obstacles covering the middle of the room. There is also the possibility to charge up the robot which results in a more powerful and fast returning of the ball, but when overdone it causes the robot to explode.
Botss 3

It is two years after Botss 2. President Gilbert Bates is dead. Zackaria is presumed gone. The EDF becomes less vigilant. Earth Force space station Z35 is attacked. The five pilots who fought Zackaria before were not onboard the station when the attack came. The station is quickly overwhelmed. Mars Force DRAGON jumps into Earth Force space attacking immediately. The EDF tries valiantly but cannot hold. DRAGON uses the antimatter cannon and the defenses are obliterated, save a handful of fighters. With the station taken and the crew mind-probed, the strike to earth has begun. Only you can save us, our last line of defense.
Bottles

A freeware AMOS game by Tony Kingsmill, created in 1995. Choose from 3 level of difficulties and attempt to guess the word in this Hangman style game. For every guess you miss, a bottle falls off the wall. If they all fall, you lose the game.
Boulder Bash
Boulder Bash is a single player Boulder Dash clone created by Robert Wille in 1991 and was part of the BoulderDash Clones Compilation.
Boulder Crash

An action puzzle in the vein of BoulderDash, created by Wolfgang Schulz in 1989. You start the game with 4 Rockfords and must gather all the diamonds on the screen while avoiding a boulder to the head. Make your way through the underground by moving stones and destroying goths.
Boulder Dash (C64)

No One is a legend for Boulder Dash heads and this is considered one of the best Boulder Dash games for the Amiga. It underwent multiple versions over the years but contains levels converted from the C64 games from multiple Boulderdash games including Boulderdash, Boulderdash 2-4 and the Boulderdash Construction Kit. The setup screen might lead you to believe it supported the usual 2 players, in fact it only supports a single player.
Boulder Dash 2

This fan game created by Lazer or Laser (depending on which title screen you believe) of No One inc. It has a setup screen like Emerald Mine. The usual rules apply except that the falling diamonds don't crush the butterflies, although they can crush you.
Boulder Dash CK Collection
A collection of Boulder Dash games made by various individuals/groups using the Amiga version of the Boulder Dash Construction Kit.
Boulder Dash Construction Kit

Rockford the Ant returns in another Boulder Dash adventure contains 15 new levels, in addition to the easy-to-use game editor. Players can build, save, and play their own levels. The software includes a feature to sequence your levels on a separate game disk.

All of the elements and hazards from the previous Boulder Dash outings are back: The fireflies, butterflies, growing amoebas, enchanted walls, and of course, the boulders. New features include titanium (indestructible) walls, growing walls, and slime that allows boulders and diamonds to drop through it at a varying rate.
Boulder Däsh

BoulderDäsh is a clone of the original Boulder Dash on C64.
It has seen many development updates since 1987.

Features:
• 1:1 BoulderDäsh clone
• Full speed under MC68000 Amigas with AGA, ECS or OCS
• Full graphic board support! Up to 256 Colors (depends on graphic set)
• Full sound card support (AHI)!
• System friendly! Can be paused and resumed at any time.
• requires OS 2.04 or higher
• Commodore styleguide conform
• Locale 
• Great GUI
• Online Help
• many preferences windows
• Up to six players
• New game elements
• Unique record and play feature to show others how you solved the caves.
• Internal music player with playlist
• Optional full screen mode when running in RTG mode.
• 10000 Levels
• 36 graphic sets
• 6 character sets
• 5 sample sets
• Several hiscorelists for each game (game, level and level time records)
• Level and game editor
• Supports C64 and Atari Construction Kit Level and game files.
Boulder Engine

A revamp of BoulderDash for the Amiga created by the originator of BoulderDash, Peter Liepa along with Levas Vabolis, together known as Savel Software who released this as a fully Open Source initiative in 1995. Called variously, Boulder Dash!, Boulder Dash 2.x and the Boulder Engine, this version didn't spark quite the enthusiasm as hoped as Emerald Mines was already very well accepted in the Amiga community. However, enjoy the fully open source code and editor written in C!
Boulderdash 3D
Boulderdash 3D is a Boulderdash Clone in FPS mode, a 1996 demo game by Szymon Ulatowski. Originally intended for commercial use, it was never finished.
Boum
A freeware, workbench enabled minesweeper clone from Olivier Fabre in 1999.
Bounce

Bouncing balls run in the blood of the Amiga from the start. It should be no surprise that there are bouncy creatures aplenty in the Amiga gamespace. This PD\Freeware game by Ben Wyatt is one of them, written in AMOS. The game comes with the level editor.
Bounce 'n' Blast
A single player platform shooter created by Digital Realms Software and released as shareware in 1993.
Bounce (Bob Akerberg)

A one person, bounce the ball game. Use your joystick to keep the ball bouncing onto the boxes. Each box contains a point value and you get that if you can stop the ball on the box. If the ball stops bouncing click the fire button to shoot it upwards. There are bonuses to grab, nasty critters that will pop your ball and a unique control system.
Bounce Ball
An unreleased two player pong game by Ben Darling and Matt Gorle in 1997.
Bounce(LunchHour Software)

Use the left and right cursor keys to move the balls to the crystals and collect'em up! Avoid the holes! A game by Todd Lewis of LunchHour Software and playable on the workbench. This game was a coverdisk in 1990 and also published by Amiga Club Systems.
Bouncer (5th Dimension)

Bounce on the points, follow the rules of the board to clear everything out and get to the exit. Nice jumping and skill game with a ball. This must be transported over a dismembered board. But there are still many enemies who want to prevent that...
Bouncer (Diamond)
Bouncer is a Breakout-style reaction game released in 1987 by Diamond.
Bouncer Shaker
Stack the blocks, avoid the bees, smash the block grabbers, stop the chompers and attempt to fill the board with blocks.
Bouncing Balls

Bouncing Balls is a Puzzle game, developed and published by Markt & Technik, which was released in Europe in 1991. Two players thunder through three-dimensional landscapes with their balls. Who does the most laps in the given time? Bouncing Balls offers professional features such as split screen (split screen: each player sees the landscape from their own perspective) or level editor as well as many setting options (acceleration, friction, thrust of the balls, etc.) and extremely fast graphics. Bouncing balls, that's absolute ball fun for one or two players!
Bouncing Bill

Bouncing Bill is a non-scrolling platformer in which the player controls a ball which moves through four scenarios (house, jungle, forest and space). The ball can roll or jump which is necessary to leap over gaps, collect items (e.g. keys) and avoid enemies which move through the screens on fixed paths. The screens are interconnected with exits and can be explored in a non-linear fashion. Running out of time, jumping too far down or touching an enemy results results in the loss of a life.
Bouncy

Bouncy the spaceball is lost in space. You have to guide him through five different areas of space back to his home planet. Each area features five puzzling levels. Some are very simple, others are not. To complete a level you must have the key that opens the exit. It may sound easy but there are several obstacles in your path.
Bouncy Bonzo’s Space Journey
Bonzo is on a space journey to destroy evil enemies on three different planets.
Bounder

This is the latest addition from Roger North. This is a platform game where the aim is to bound upwards to reach an exit hole at the top of the screen. Not as simple as it sounds! Between you and the exit are platforms, gaps appear randomly as the platforms move across the screen.

You have to jump up through these gaps to reach the top exit. There are no meanies on level one, so you can get the feel of the game before progressing onto the higher levels where you have to avoid these beasts as well as trying to get to the top of the screen! An AMOS based freeware game by Roger North in 1992 and distributed by Spielekiste (Berlin PD) and later by The Assassins.
Bounty Hunter
Called the demo for what would be the greatest jump'n-shootie ever made, this game from Deadsoft was released in 1996.
Bowl!

10 pin bowling scores archive system created by Mark Ward of Wacky Carrot Software in 1990. Create league tables, add players and teams update the info and manage your bowling teams and team competitions and championships. Create next year's handicaps and all the things your alley will need to bowl a strike for all your patrons.
Bowlen
A solitaire card game by the prolific Harald Müller (Mueller), released by both Intersoft and Schatztruhe in 1995.
Bowls

Bowls is a game based on the sport with the same name. You start by rolling a small white ball (known as the jack). Once it has come to rest the players roll bigger and heavier bowls towards the jack. After each competitor has used up their allocated number of bowls,one player is awarded points for the number of his bowls are closer to the jack than his opponent's closest bowl.

The game screen is divided in three parts. Half of it is the lane viewed from a top down perspective, with two markers one for the position of the player and the other for the direction. The upper right part of the screen is where you change you position, direction and spin. The lower right part of the screen shows the player from the sideline. It can be played on different lanes (inside, outside and beach) and can be played against the computer or another player.
Box: The Adventure

Box is a shareware interactive adventure novel in which you guide the main character, making his decisions and interacting with the world about him. Interaction is achieved through an advanced text-only interface which can understand plain(ish) English sentences entered by the user.
Boxing Masters
Boxing Masters is a boxing sports and boxing management game by Paul Dowers, and published by ESP Software, which was released in Europe in 1994.
BoxWorld

BoxWorld, the sequel to MazezaM, is a puzzle game where the player have to rearrange boxes in each level in order to be able to teleport to the next level. The game is based on the classic Soko-Ban genre with a twist: new types of boxes and terrains. The latest version includes more than 525 puzzles.
BoxWorld 2

The followup to BoxWorld continues in the same Sokoban fashion, with 34 new levels. In addition to the normal boxes that must be pushed into place, there are holes that must be filled so that the player may pass, and ice boxes that glide until they reach a wall or another box.
Boxx

Boxx is a game for the Commodore Amiga, made by Lemming880, member of the EAB. The game is a platform game and is made in Backbone. An Amiga A1200 or higher is recommended, but it will work on a A500 at a slower speed. In the game you must collect all coins, kill the nasties and eliminate the boss!
Boxx 1 remake

Boxx is a small platform game that was originally made in 2014 for the Commodore Amiga. But it was made with Backbone so it had poor performance. Now, in 2022, the game is ported to the much better Scorpion Engine and runs a lot smoother.
Boxx 2

Boxx 2 is an Amiga title developed by Lemming880 of EAB that features more than it's fair share of fun. A run and jump platform game developed in Backbone where your goal is to collect all the coins and kill the baddies. Boxx 2 features worthy enough detail, bright colours and cool game play which would usually be found from indie developers on such sites as Gamejolt. A fun game indeed and one that works well enough even on the Amiga 500, but Amiga 1200 or higher is recommended.
Boxx 2 Remake
Boxx 2 Remake is a platform game with shooter elements for Commodore Amiga. The original game from 2015 is now remade with Scorpion Engine and has upgraded graphics.
Boxx 3

Enjoyable, albeit a bit on the easy side. Boxx 3 is a standard platformer: You walk from level to right, jump over platforms and on the occasional baddie, pull levers to open doors, and collect coins. The gameplay changes during the boss battles at the end of each level. You get a gun and enter an arena fight against a large sprite with a lot of hit points. These bosses have simple attack patterns and are not very challenging. If you defeat one, it drops a key that opens the level exit door. I like that the graphics that were drawn by the author and not ripped from other games. The music, which was not made for this game, is very good.
Boxx 3 Remake
Boxx 3 Remake is a platform game for Commodore Amiga. The original game from 2017 is now now remade with Scorpion Engine and has upgraded graphics.
Boxx 4
Once upon a time, in a distant land, there lived a little box-like creature named Cubo. Cubo was a happy-go-lucky creature who loved nothing more than exploring his world and find new areas.
Brad Zoom in Better Dead Than Alien

Brad Zoom takes on the Brain Eaters from the Purple Planet, in this homage to vintage action games, primarily Galaxians. There are 75 levels, accessed via passcodes.

You control a spaceship at the bottom of the screen facing upwards, firing at arrangements of aliens. You can move up and down as well as left and right as you shoot them. At set intervals an alien will emerge from the main pack and sweep down towards you.

Other levels feature Asteroids which split when shot, or a single ‘boss’ alien. Aliens with green eyeballs release power-ups, such as improved weapons, shields and bombs. You have a single life with which to survive the carnage. You get points for surviving as well as scoring, so slow but cautious play is more rewarding.
Brain

A freeware game created by Cluster (André Wichmann) in 1990 to give people a puzzle to solve while assembling\compiling the programming they are working on. Try to match the numbers on the sample box, when you increase the numbers in any square, the ones around it go up. This forces you to plan in an inverted way and think steps ahead.
Brain Artifice

Brain Artifice is a puzzle game in which the player needs to build combinations out of given blocks. While initially the combinations simply consist of the the same picture or colour, in later levels there are certain patterns to achieve. The blocks are initially divided over the playfield and after grabbing one of them, the player can move it freely over all the unoccupied space. If the block is near another block from the pattern - the detailed requirements change from level to level - it is stuck and can't be moved anymore.

When a whole pattern is done, the stones transform into bricks so the player knows it is time to work with the rest of the stones. All this has to be done within a time limit, and unwinnable situations are entirely possible. The game features 100 levels which introduce additional gameplay elements over time, e.g. static blocks, blocks which change their colour or hidden blocks.
Brain Blasters

The wizards are revolting (and it's not just their personal habits). Whichever one passes the test of IOZU will become the grand master and dominate the rest. To pass this test the wizard has to defeat the dark side of his spirit by completing a series of memory puzzles. A pattern is displayed at the start of each level, which then has to reproduced by you. Unlike most games you don't control the pieces. Instead you operate a little wizard who has to scurry around collecting the pieces of the pattern as they fall from the heavens and then place them on board. The presentation is very slick. There's a good intro with sampled sound and a snazzy picture. The menu screen has a couple of finely animated dragons and there's an option that lets you trade gold (points) for tips which is another nice touch. 

Brain Blasters is fun to begin with, but after the fifth level, or so, the novelty value begins to pale.
Brain Braiser

Player one will always move on the horizontal axis while player two will always move on the vertical axis. Pick the tile with the highest score or force your opponent to pick a lower score in the next turn! Thinking ahead is the key to win the game.
Brain Challenge

Brain Challenge: The Arena of Death is a strategy game with strong similarities to the board game Stratego. The background story is about an evil lord who has to driven out of his castle. Each player has 24 playing stones with different ranks which are divided over the own half of a chess board. In each round the player can move one stone with the goal to conquer the stationary palace (represented by a flag). However, the main catch is that the ranks of each enemy's stone is hidden until it gets attacked. During an attack, the higher rank always wins. If both have the same rank, both lose. Additionally every player has also stationary bombs which are always deadly when attacked.
Brain Damage

This single player puzzle game was created by Digital Perceptions and relesed in 1994 in two forms, a PD demo version or a commercial full version. In it you must recreate the pattern given by shifting columns and rows. It starts out relatively easily allowing you to understand how it works and then gets progressively harder with each new level.
Brain Fodder

Brain Fodder is a set of English language learning programs. * Funtest - consists in making a word from the letters in three rows.

- Scrabble - is a classic scrabble game.
- Speech Snatch - checks the correct pronunciation.
- Puzzle - consists in arranging a sentence from scattered puzzles.
Brain Killer

The demo for this game was released, but the full version was scheduled for release in 1998. According to German interviews with Michael Garlich of Titan, the game was cancelled because the "final version" submitted by the programmers was considered too buggy for commercial release [Sources: Amiga Future, Apr/May 99 issue; NoCover #53, June 98 issue.] and because of military, school and other commitments by the primary coders. Still this first person shooter in the shadow of Doom\Wolfenstein games was intriguing enough to have a lot of people willing to play the unfinished product.
Brain Man

BrainMan is a top-down puzzle game. The player takes control over a blob who has two tasks in each level: collecting enough stars and finally finding the exit. However, there are obstacles, including blocks (which can, similar to Soko-Ban, only pushed but not pulled), closed doors, a time limit or other blobs which should not be touched. Keys, which act like the blocks mentioned before, can be used to open the closed doors. If is possible to get a level into an unwinnable state, e.g. by pushing a key into a corner.
Brain Shave

Considered a hidden gem of Amiga games, this was released on ASI-GAMES-VOL 144 and was created by Andrew Campbell. It has two variations of game: Gravity and Sliders. Brain Shave is the sequel to Enigma a PD game available on the Funhouse disk and on the Assassin's collection, in this new game. It is a game like White Rabbit or Enigma where the object of the game is to match up all the colored tiles by dragging them around the screen using a joystick controlled cursor. Select, press and hold fire and drag the file if it is free to move.
Brainball

Brainball is a puzzle game where the objective is to guide three balls, each made of different materials—glass, wood, and metal—into corresponding holes. Each ball behaves differently due to its material properties, which affects how it bounces off surfaces and interacts with obstacles. Players must carefully plan their shots to overcome these challenges and complete each level.

Players control a cue stick using either a mouse or joystick. The cue can be aimed around each ball, and the strength of the shot is determined by holding down a button before releasing it. Levels feature timers and a limited number of shots, requiring precision and efficiency to succeed. A password system allows players to resume progress after completing levels.
Brainbow

Brainbow the rainbow puzzler by Aaron Fisher, released in 1992 and part of the Assassins game releases. Each level gives you 3 shapes to use. The goal is to make the whole screen the same color. You are given a certain number of shapes to use on the screen and must make all the changes in that amount of moves. Medium and Hard difficulty give you less shapes to use.
BrainScrambler
BrainScrambler is a picture reconstruction puzzle game. You can select a number of included pictures or load your own. You can also select the size of the puzzle grid from 6x4 up to 31x19.
Brainsphere

A strategic board game for up to 4 players, coded in Amos Pro by Volker Stepprath. Several different starting boards are available for use. The goal is to get the largest amount of dots changed to your team color. Jump and work around to leave balls. A strategic game for 1 up to 4 players, the aim is to leave balls after you turned so that other player couldn’t take a move anymore. But be careful cause there are pitfalls on board.
Brainstorm (Amigo!)
The Tüfftelspiel play\puzzle game, written entirely in assembler, was published in the Amiga Fun by CT Verlag in 1993. Something fun to rack your brains on.
Brainstorm (King Size)

Brainstorm is a straight conversion of the game Concentration (also known as Memory). There is a set of 54 cards flipped on their back so every card looks the same. On the flip-side, there are 26 pairs with different motives. The players (in turn) flip over two cards each while trying to find a pair. When a pair is found, it is removed from the table. The goal is to find more pairs than the opponent.

This version features six card decks and the option to play alone (with the goal to have the least turns as possible), against the AI (nine difficulty levels) or against another person.
Brainstorm(Thomas Behrend)

A version of the Shanghai solitaire tile game created by Thomas Behrend and published as a cover disk on Amiga Special (media GmbH) in 1991. The game was created in Amiga BASIC and it allowed one or two players, which you don't see in this game often. The game play involves 144 tiles, each depicting different images, which have to be removed by matching them into pairs. The tiles are arranged in a grid pattern, which is higher near the center. A tile can only be removed if it has no tile next to it on at least one side.
Brainwave

Brainwave is a memory/concentration variant for up to three players. The goal requires finding all the covered pairs on the board in the shortest time. Failed attempt hides the uncovered element. Discovered pairs remain on board. The game features three modes, four difficulty levels and eighteen sets of elements covered.
Brainy

An AMOS based, freeware quiz game created in 1991 by Michael Flad. Brainy v1.10 is an entertaining knowledge game in the style of "Trivial Pursuit" for up to 6 players. The aim of the game is to complete the 6 "knowledge corners" (e.g. sports & entertainment, art & literature, entertainment, etc.) and finally land on the top left starting field. In the finale, at least 3 of the 6 questions asked must be answered correctly. With question editor.
Bram Stoker's Dracula

One of several adaptations of the 1992 film version of the classic vampire tale, the Amiga version is a side-scrolling action game.

The player controls Jonathan Harker, who, on his quest to destroy the Transylvanian vampire, must make his way through nine levels, starting at a tavern near Dracula's castle and then the castle itself. Back in England, Dracula and his minions must be driven out of a convent, an abbey and the house of Jonathan's fiancée Mina, among others. A primary task in each level is to find and destroy several coffins of Transylvanian earth. Hindering Jonathan on his way are henchmen as well as critters under the vampire's control: bats, rats, snakes and more. The last coffin in each location is usually guarded by one of Dracula's stronger minions, which include his three brides, the madman Renfield, and Mina's friend Lucy, now turned undead.

To defeat the enemies, Jonathan uses punches and kicks.
Brands Hatch

Brands Hatch is a Racing game, developed and published by Robtek.
It was originally released in Europe as 'Rallye Master' in 1987, then re-released in the UK in 1988.

This is a top-down racing game similar to Super Sprint. The player gets confronted with ten non-scrolling course on which ten rounds have to be finished in a limited time. Collisions with the crash barriers or the opponent (either controlled by the AI or another player) do not damage the car and only result in the needs to back up a bit. The courses can be played one after another in a tournament or individually.
Brasure
A shareware shooter from Consix for two players in vs mode with top and bottom split screen. Released in S p i e l e k i s t e # 402 in 1993.
Brat

In Brat you must guide a baby, Nathan, through levels with features such as dynamite, bridges and holes. You do this indirectly, by specifying which direction he goes in, in a manner vaguely similar to Lemmings. You also tell him when to use objects in a simplistic manner similar to the Dizzy games.
Brataccas

Brataccas is a game that combines exploration, puzzle-solving and combat. You play a character named Kyne, a man who has a price on his head. You must search the mining asteroid, Brattacus, to gather proof of a government plot against you and to try to stay alive. Surveillance cameras are watching you, so take any chance to disable them.

Brataccas is a place where greed and corruption rule the day. The residents are treacherous, and while they can be bribed they are not above murder, so the player has to be careful.
Bratwurst

A multi-scrolling shooter created by Three Little Elks and released to PD\Freeware in 1995. Bratwurst is the same kind of game as Gravity Force and Roketz. The difference is that it uses vector graphics instead of ordinary bitmap graphics. This enables the map and players to be scaled easily which means that when the players are close to each other the camera will zoom in on the players to get a more detailed view. Another difference with Bratwurst is that four players can play simultaneously.
Bravo Romeo Delta

Bravo Romeo Delta is a single player game that allows you to control either the United States' or the USSR's nuclear arsenal during an escalating exchange. Its interface is very basic, with only four screens for reports and input. The game plays in real time and can be set faster. There are dozens of different weapon systems at the player's command, including: air dropped gravity bombs, sub-launched ballistic missiles, ICBM silos, and mobile launchers. Data for each weapon and vehicle is accessible. Locations are displayed as geographic coordinates. Success at destroying a chosen target relies on several factors such as weather or hardness penetration of an attacking missile.

The game begins as a Soviet submarine has launched a salvo of three missiles at the United States. The player takes control of one nation and must slowly "out-nullify" the computer player's ability to command, communicate, and attack with his payloads.
Breach

Breach is not exactly a new product, having surfaced on the Amiga through the American company Omnitrend in 1987. The game is based around tactical-level ground combat of the future, space marines serving as the backbone force in nine conflicts.

As in Laser Squad each unit has a finite set of movement points per turn depleted by firing weapons, moving across rougher terrain etc. This system of command allows units to perform multiple tasks within a 'turn'. Unfortunately the effects of such actions are purely short term only, no long term strategic thought can be allowed for, the inflexibility of it all preventing the player from performing more complex actions.

The conflicts provide some variety to the proceedings, increasing in difficulty very quickly from the first few 'seek and destroy' and rescue missions to near suicide combo-missions. The hardest mission of all involves a single Squad Marine entering the heart of an enemy fortress to rescue an Admiral.
Breach 2

Science Fiction has not really had its fair share of role playing/strategy games. Basically up until now there has been Breach and Laser Squad. This is a shame since it is a field of great scope for imagination. The deficieny has been slightly redressed now with the long awaited update from Omnitrend, Breach 2. The game is set, as were Breach and the Universe series, in the world of a post-Earth Empire, with rival factions of liberated colonists in constant battles for supremacy.

The central philosophy of combat in this system revolves around a squad leader. If the squad leader is killed during a mission then, even if all objectives have been achieve, the mission has failed. Therefore the natural reaction is to protect the leader, surrounding that unit with a mobile armour of more expendable marines. In order for squad leaders to improve in all abilities and become a general super-hero, they have to practise.
Breach: Scenario Disk: The Serayachi Campaign

Breach: Scenario Disk - The Serayachi Campaign contains additional levels and campaigh for Breach.

The first moon of Kiskismok is under Federated Worlds control, and they have allowed both Federated Worlds (FW) and United Democratic Planets (UDP) to establish research stations there, even turning a blind eye to the squatter colonies that have started turning up along the jungle and coastal areas of the moon.

When the Unification Talks failed, civil unrest among the squatter colonies rose sharply. Intelligence reports there are organized groups planning to form their own planetary government with military assistance from the UDP. Intelligence has concluded that the UDP will attempt to take control of the moon sometime in the next few days. Several squads of FW teams have been sent to the immediate area to respond if trouble breaks out.
Break Down

Exercise your Amiga's mouse in this fast-paced arcade-style game. Are you ready for 16 levels of arcade action? If you are, pop in your Resource Disk and double-click on tine Break Down icon. This Breakout-style game features unique background patterns and blocks with special powers. And it's our first game to include a full blown musical score.

There are three kinds of blocks In Break Down: standard, wall, and special. You progress through the levels by using your paddle to knock a ball into every standard brick on the screen. The standard blocks are translucent red, green, and yellow. Wall bricks are solid gray and can never be broken. Power blocks each give you a different special benefit.

Red power blocks give you a second paddle which floats above your main paddle. This paddle gives you an extra chance to strike the ball. It also provides you with a quick way to change the trajectory of the ball if you get into a rut with the single paddle.
Break Out Revolution

Break Out Revolution is another Arkanoid clone. This one is done very well. The game play is very tight and the graphics are very nice too. The game has 2 modes, mode 1 is regular breakout. Mode 2 is an advanced type of breakout with lots of stuff happening during play like the ability to move the player platform up and down as opposed to just left and right in normal mode. There's also a lot of stuff falling down for you to collect when you break the bricks. It's one of the best unlicensed Arkanoid clones out there.
Breaker

An Arkanoid style freeware game from Paul Stevens in 1989. 10 different special drop bricks may show up to help or hinder you from clearing the bricks. Special score bonuses and lots of twists and turns.
Breaker!!!
Breaker!!! is a public domain Breakout/Arkanoid clone for the Amiga. It was developed by Niels Provos and released in 1990.
Breakin' Briks
An Arkanoid style game created by Lodge and released to PD in 1995.
Breaking Out

Breaking Out is an action game similar to Breakout or Arkanoid by Carsten Hund, published in Amiga Extra Nr. 5: Spiele by Markt & Technik in 1988 along with MegaMind and Wikinger II. The aim is to clear stubborn stone walls with a ball. If difficulty levels are not enough for you, you can create new levels at any time with the editor.
Breakline Rugby 5

Breakline Rugby 5 is a native Amiga AGA sports prototype built around short, tactical matches. Carry the ball, link backward passes, send a teammate on a crossing run, and slide your defensive line toward the open side. Six touches turn possession over. A forward kick must be caught before it hits the ground.
Breakout

A freeware Arkanoid style game made by Jeroen Knoester of Power Programs made in 1998 written in AMOS. Sadly, it only really worked smoothly on an Amiga with at least a 68020 processor, but I hope you enjoy it. If any level is too hard just use the included level editor to make your life easier. Bugfixes released on Aminet makes it appear multiple separate games with this name were released, in fact the slightly later release is just a bugfix to the original. As usual remove the bricks while keeping the ball in play as long as possible. Missing the ball loses a life.
Breakout 2000
A very simple breakout game with some updates to make it more attractive and interesting. It was created by Paul J. Champion and released to PD in 1994.
BreakThru

Your Mission: To retrieve the PK430 secret fighter plane stolen from your country and fly it back. There is no time to weigh our options, you must drive deep into enemy territory to recover the PK430 using the military’s most advanced land vehicle, capable of leaping high into the air at the push of a button. This is a one-way trip pilot, you’re coming back home in that fighter jet, or not at all.

Gameplay: Breakthru is a horizontal shoot 'em up where the player controls an armed vehicle, with the first button shooting the main gun while the second button is used for jumping. During levels the player must face off against enemy soldiers, turrets and vehicles, as well as various obstacles along the way. The player can run over drums and crates, while other obstacles will cause the player to lose a life, so you must either avoid or jump over them.
Breathless

In Breathless, the human race has been enslaved by evil alien overlords. But some rebel groups haven't given up hope yet and fight against the oppressors. When one of them gets caught, they are being transformed into cyborgs and stuck in complicated mazes that function as arenas, where they have to fight for their honour and maybe their freedom.

Breathless is a first-person-shooter, where the player has to navigate various stages infested with enemies out to get them. The player has a status display at the bottom of the screen. It contains the current score, the remaining health and shield as well as energy and credits. Energy functions as a universal ammo stock, with each of the weapon depleting a certain amount. By picking up credits, the player can buy or upgrade weapons at computer terminals.

The player's goal is to reach the exit of each of the 20 levels.
Breathless A32

Breathless is a first-person-shooter, where the player has to navigate various stages infested with enemies out to get them. The player has a status display at the bottom of the screen. It contains the current score, the remaining health and shield as well as energy and credits. Energy functions as a universal ammo stock, with each of the weapon depleting a certain amount. By picking up credits, the player can buy or upgrade weapons at computer terminals.

(A32 version)
Patch for Amiga AGA/RTG bringing some new sprites, performance optimizations, improved enemy AI, CD32 Pad support.
Breed 96

In the year 2032 the earth was terraformed to restore it's crumbling atmosphere. However evil factions sabotaged the terraformation resulting in the deaths of 29 billion people.

The federation government sent a deep space colonisation ship to a remote galaxy in the Daarion cluster with a mission to colonise a planet in that sector. The Daarion cluster was chosen because it is home to three alien races which had become dependant on Federation technology and advice. Unforeseen by the federation, civil unrest in the alien communities became apparent resulting in the colonisation ship being fired upon. The crew inside the ship, under cryogenic suspension, were helpless against the attack and the severely damaged vessel crashed into a desolate planet nearby.
Brian Clough's Football Fortunes

Brian Clough's Football Fortunes is a football management computer board game suitable for two to five players. 

Each player takes on the role of a club manager. The object of the game is for each manager to successfully steer his team through the season using his skill to make his team stronger as the game proceeds. Each manager competes with human and computer controlled teams in a ten strong league and the F.A. Cup. From the second season onwards, each team will also enter a European competition (League Champions to the European Cup, F.A. Cup Winners to the Cup-Winners’ Cup, and the remaining clubs will go to the UEFA Cup). 

The winner of Brian Clough's Football Fortunes is the manager who survives to the end of the game and has the highest number of game points. Game points are points awarded by the computer program, based on each managers performance in League and Cup competitions and on the amount of cash the player has left at the end of the game.
Brian Lara's Cricket

On Monday 18th April, 1994 Brian Lara broke a cricketing record that had stood since 1958, long before Lara himself was born.

Lara's 375 for West Indies against England is the highest individual score ever recorded in a test match, beating Sir garfield Sobers' 365. In more than 12 hours at the crease he faced 536 balls and hit 45 boundaries.

Just weeks later, Lara was in record-breaking form once again, hitting 501 not out for Warwickshire against Durham, the highest score in first class cricket!

BRIAN LARA'S CRICKET allows you to get in on the action, controlling batting, bowling, and field placing, Spectacular graphics and authentic player statistics make this the most realistic cricket simulation ever!

How many records will you break this season?
Brian the Lion

In this game, you play Brian, the lion that closely resembles the Paddle Pop mascot. You must carry out the task of rescuing your friend Chris the Crystal, who has been kidnapped by Geeza the Dragon. His other warped jungle animal friends, Barry the Bear and Graeme the Gorilla, prevent you from getting to him and rescuing your friend.

Your job is to run through each level, destroying enemies that get in your way by either "clawing" them or jumping on their heads. Along the way, collect as many crystals as you can so that you can use them at the shop to buy extra lives, credits, heavenly hit points, jinormous jumps, really raj roars (which also kills enemies), and splendid speed. There are many secret areas in a level, some will take you on a different route other than the one you take when you reach the level exit. However, you must complete certain levels in order to progress further in the game, but you can return to a level that you have completed.
BrickFast

An Arkanoid shareware clone with many new features. Choose between 3 level sets, has multiball, fire, brickthrough, ball saving guard, many falling object. Has bump\tilt motion by pressing spacebar will modify the path of the ball.
Bride of the Robot

In Bride of the Robot, you play Brad Stallion, a galactic hero/playboy, who has been called on to rescue the new Miss Galaxy, Allura. It seems that she was kidnapped by the sex-crazed and unimaginatively named Robot, the first machine with a sex drive. As dramatic as that sounds, the program goes downhill from there.

The majority of the input for Bride is handled with the mouse, clicking on objects on the screen. However, the objects you can click on aren't distinguished in any way from the background clutter, so when you enter a room, you must slide the mouse around, pretty much randomly, until you happen across something with which the program will let you interact. The sentence parser, if it can be called that, has trouble with the simplest input and doesn't even recognize the same verb when it's used with different objects.

If Bride of the Robot has a saving grace, it's the graphics.
Brides of Dracula

Brides of Dracula is a two-player split-screen game similar to Spy vs. Spy in gameplay. Each player (human or CPU) controls either the vampire hunter Van Helsing or Count Dracula. Van Helsing is summoned to the Bistritz village to kill Dracula and his brides. His goal is to find thirteen tools to kill Dracula, bring them back to Helsing's home and store them in the cupboard. For Dracula, the objective is to create thirteen brides by finding women, biting and leading them back to the crypt, where thirteen coffins are lined up waiting for their recipients.

Both characters can be killed by certain hazardous environments and non-player characters (NPCs). Some of these dangers may effect only one of the characters (ghouls only attack Van Helsing, while priests and villagers only harm Dracula). Each player starts with three lives. Collected objects and women are displayed at the bottom of the character window, along with the health bar.
Bridge 5.0

Bridge 5.0 is the fifth in a series of 1-player card game simulators.

Gameplay follows standard bridge rules, and cards are graphically displayed on the screen as they are played. Bidding is based on the five-card Stayman and Blackman conventions. The program reviews the bidding, keeps track of the score, and informs the player of any illegal moves. The player can choose from a number of different hands to start, and can also choose to play as their computer partner or have them automated. The player can store interesting hands to disk, and change hands from one player to another.
Bridge 6.0

Bridge 6.0 is the longest continuously published bridge game series and second for the Amiga platform. The game lets you save the game in progress, can give you hints and can play the entire hand automatically for you. Bridge 6.0 is a contract or duplicate Bridge program. You and your computer partner play against two computer opponents.
Bridge Ball
Move the available pipes and platforms around in order to move the ball towards the end of the level.
Bridge Player 2000 with Tutor

At last. . . . . a bridge player that gives you a challenging game with a really tough opponent. We can promise you hours of enjoyment as you pit your wits against this powerful program.

And now a superb new feature for the beginner and improver . . . . a special tutorial section devised by an expert to guide you through the intricacies of bidding and play with twenty set hands and detailed explanation.

This is a bridge player for both the expert and the beginner, with versatile bidding routines that really set a high standard, matched by the emphatically powerful play of the cards. The computer will play as either defender or declarer. Generates random hands and allows proper bidding in the Acol system, including the Stayman and Blackwood conventions.

Bid against the computer, then prove your skill as it takes you on playing both your opponents hands.

Make use of the many superb features - including one or to that can give you the edge against the machine!

OPTIONS INCLUDE. . . .
Bridge Player Galactica

Bridge Player Galactica is a Bridge card game with betting elements, developed and published by Oxford Softworks, which was released in Europe in 1989. Game written in HiSoft BASIC. Original coding by Richard Wheen and Nicola Gardener; Amiga conversion by Ian Stirzaker and Chris Whittington.
Bridge Pro
An Amiga bridge playing program. You play with a computer partner against two computer opponents. It includes an online Bridge tutorial. A hint mode is available in all situations.
Bridge Strike

Bridge Strike sees you take control of an aircraft fighter as you fly into combat against insurmountable odds with the sole objective of eliminating as many enemies as you can. The aim of the game is to accumulate as much points you can by destroying various on screen objects. You will come across bridges which must be destroyed. Destroyed bridges act as a checkpoint from which the game begins, when your aircraft crashes. When your last aircraft crashes, the game ends.

The shooting mechanism is borrowed from River Raid in that you can steer the bullets after they have been shot…but beware that doing this also moves your plane in the same direction and if you’re not attentive when doing this, you’ll find your plane crashing into the side of the canyon environment.

In addition to navigating the landscape, you will have to deal with a number of enemy units, ranging from ordinary patrol boats to complex automatic rocket systems.
Brigade Commander

Brigade Commander is a 2D top down real-time hex-based tactical strategy game. The player is commander of a tank brigade (and several other types of vehicles, each vehicle are based on the real-life counterpart).

The player commands units in the fight against computer opponents by using several commands: move/stop movement, attack/cease fire, or combine units. Each type of vehicle has own statistics. The game is based on scenarios - each scenario has its own story. It also has a build-in editor and special data-disk with new scenarios.
Brik Fighter

An Arkanoid style game created by Jean-Baptiste Bolcato (Starsky) and released in 1997. In it hitting certain blocks will release capsules that when caught offer power ups when caught. Some will advance you to the next level, some contain disadvantageous items like speeding up the ball or decreasing the size of the bat you must catch\hit the ball with.
Brilliant English

Welcome to Brilliant English!
In this program there is the possibility of training in eight different areas of the English language. Exercises are available of varying degrees of difficulty and you can choose one that suits you well. I hope that this program facilitates your studies in English. 
 
ENTER YOUR CHOICE
Prepositions
The vocabulary
Find the shape
A or AN?
Plural
Shining
Review
Briscas Españolas

A one or two player card game using Tarot cards. Each pack of cards has 40 cards, 10 for each suit, the suits are Gold (coins), Cups, Clubs and Spades (swords) and are numbered 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,10,11 and 12 (there are no 8's or 9's). Only 1,3,10, 11 and 12 are worth points (Briscas). 1=11 points, 3=10 points, 10=2 points, 11=3 points and 12=4 points. There are 120 points total available, if each player gets 60 it will be a tie. After dealing one card is dealt face up and this card represents LIFE and the rest of the un-dealt cards are face down next to LIFE. At each turn, a card is played and the other player tries to KILL that card. The one that kills keeps the pair. Players keep 3 cards in their hand, drawing to keep that level. 
 
LIFE kills all cards except another LIFE of a higher value. 3 of LIFE kills a 12 of LIFE, but a 12 of LIFE kills any other suit. You can kill a card with a higher number of the same suit. Modem play was available.
Briscola (Fabio Lopiano)

Briscola is one of Italy's most popular games, together with Scopa and Tressette. A little-changed descendant of Brusquembille, the ancestor of Briscan and Bezique, Briscola is a Mediterranean trick-taking, Ace-Ten card game for one against the computer, played with a standard Italian 40-card deck.
British League Speedway

A motorcycle racing management game for Division One racing created by VGS Software and released in 1993. VGS Software released several versions, of this game with additional heats and another game for Division Two riders.
British Manager

A graphical management game based on the text games of old, with the majority of the game being created statistically rather than through gameplay, showing the outcome of goal\penalty kicks as you work your way through you season. You play as the owner\manager with rights to transfer, change the squad, view the finances, make changes to the stadium and work player trades to improve your outcome and income!
Brod
A Galaxian style space shooter written in AMOS by Zeljko Kolarevicis and released on Amiga Format cover disk 136B.
Broker
A one to four player wall-street strategy game created by Andreas Page and released as shareware in 1987. A very good German stock market game for up to 4 stock market speculators.
Bruce Lee

BRUCE LEE - Amiga port of Kagesan's Sega Master System version (2015)
by Tim Kovack (2026)
Bruce Lee: The C64 Game
Your Jeet Kune Do is unstoppable but can you guide the little dragon to victory in this homebrew platformer written in ASM 68k and released like water over the rocks in the year 2000.
BruceLee: The War Criminal

The story takes us to the Tian Shan mountain ranges, in the extreme northwest of China.

Legend has it that inside a lost valley, protected behind difficult-to-access gorges, a pagoda is hidden behind hectares of endless bamboo forests, sculpted by an order of ancient Buddhist warrior-monks. Fearful after the events that occurred during the Chinese Cultural Revolution, with the conquest of Tibet by the Maoists, the warrior monks have decided to resist. To do this, they have accepted the help of Lord X, a former criminal from Vietnam, wanted by the Hague Tribunal for the use of chemical weapons. He soon resumes his fateful experiments. Soon myriads of zombies begin to appear around the place, while the locals quickly flee to the hills. War of war,

Only you can stop it. As an expert martial arts fighter versed in Jit Kun Do, you have to face endless hordes of enemies that will crowd on both sides of the screen, barely being able to contain them.
Brus Lii

This side scrolling beat 'em up puts you in control of Brus on a rescue mission to save your kidnapped girlfriend from a criminal organization, hell bent on stopping you from entering the martial arts tournament.
Brutal Football

Similar to Speedball 2, Brutal Sports Football is an ultra-violent sports game. Matches last 7 minutes, and the aim is to get the ball into the goal, kept by a net-minder. The oval ball can be thrown or kicked, this resulting in frequent up-and-under type kicks.

Violence is the pivotal element of gameplay: rather than rare occurrence, punching, stomping, use of weapons, and even decapitations are what the game action is rife with, and key to victory. Bonus and non-bonus items appear on the pitch, such as bombs to throw at opponents, rabbits to speed up the current player, or tortoises which slow him down.

Teams are a total of eleven and consist of seven humans and aliens, some of whom have unique skills. There's a lot of blood and flailing limbs, giving things a gruesomely humorous edge. Victory is achieved not only by scoring more goals than the opponent team but also decapitating all the players of it but one.
Brutal Homicide

Brutal Homicide is a game for two players, each player is awarded one
 half of the screen.

The year is 2045, and the prisons in the world are getting crowded with hardened criminals. Until now the guards and the prisoners often had a game in secret where two of the prisoners meet with weapons and slay each other. The winner was released, or he was helped to escape. The guards bet money, drank beer and laughed at the tournament.

Recently the government got hang of what they were doing at nights, and after a bit of discussion, they decided to legalize the killing. Although they changed it a bit... The fighters now begin in a maze, with weapons from the 2000-century, and limited ammo. And as a final touch, and probably to make some money, they will broadcast it on television (yes, they still have telly's in the future, even thought they don't look like nowadays). And its here you get in...
Brutal Homicide 2: The Future Forces

Development started 17 February 1997. The aim was to create a 1 or 2 player game in the style of Chaos Engine. During the development, the game became more and more like the old Brutal Homicide (a 2-player versus game).

Sadly, the game never got really stable and development stopped. This beta version was the only release made.
Brutal Tenia

Another little arcade worm game with "hi scores" at stake that will guarantee you some wild games :-). The principle? You are a kind of worm, at the top of the screen, and undergo a vertical scrolling, namely that the screen moves from bottom to top, and that on the playing area, there are plenty of obstacles. On your side, you can only move to the left and to the right, the goal being to accumulate the greatest number of points possible (a bit like for Fnurr 2000 ) while avoiding as many obstacles as possible.
Brutal: Paws of Fury

The Dalai Llama has organised a martial arts contest for animals of all species to prove their skills, and you are competing in it. There are a wide variety of furry creatures to take on, and finally the Dalai Llama himself.

Brutal: Paws of Fury is a one-on-one fighting game across a variety of levels, with mostly outdoor terrain. You can choose of the many characters. Throughout the game, your character travels across Dalai Llama's island, fighting a series of duels before getting to the final showdown.

During a duel, you can punch and kick your opponent, try to use special attacks on him/her, or use a "taunt" that restores a bit of your health. Each battle lasts a number of rounds (how many - that is determined in the options menu); once one combatant has won that number of times during the battle, he wins. If the computer-controlled player won, it's game over (but you can still use a continue to start the fight anew); if you won, you move on to the next opponent.
Brydż

Brydż is a computer adaptation of a classic card game for up to four players. The game is highly customizable introducing all the rules from the real gameplay. Training mode allows practicing bidding and party skills. The game can be played with or without scoring.
Bubba 'n' Stix

Bubba is a happy-go-lucky animal delivery guy for the local Zoo here on Earth. One day, while going about his daily routine, Bubba is abducted by an alien that plans on delivering him along with several other aliens into his zoo. On the way back to his home planet, the alien spacecraft loses control and crashes and it gives the opportunity for Bubba, the other aliens and Stix (a sentient twig like alien) to escape. Bubba and Stix become friends and start on their journey home, They're now on an alien planet where things are a little bit different than they are on Earth. Take control of Bubba as he wields Stix as various puzzle solving tool (including a weapon), as they try to find a way back home. You'll have to solve mind-boggling puzzles and fight all kinds of wacky aliens. If you're planning to return to Earth, you'll have to have fast reflexes and be able to think fast and sometimes sideways.
Bubble +

You control a ghost with the mouse and have to help him get a bubble from one side of the level to the other without bursting it. The ghost can be rotated with the mouse buttons and you blow the bubble by pressing space. You have to avoid sharp objects such as needles and obstacles such as candles. Fans blow the bubble off course.
Bubble and Squeak

Bubble and Squeak starts off similarly to many other platform games. Controlling a bald child, you move through a scrolling array of ledges, avoiding contact with nasties who release coins when shot. There are hidden areas to find as well.

Halfway through the first of the 30 levels, you meet Squeak and the full nature of the game starts. Squeak is a blue alien, who must also be guided through the levels. As he can't jump as high as you, he must sometimes be instructed to wait while you flick a switch or otherwise solve the puzzle of how to guide him through. If you stand on top of Squeak you can be launched into an extra-high jump.
Bubble Bobble

Bubble Bobble is the story of two humans, Bub and Bob who wander into the mysterious cave of monsters and magically turn into dinosaurs. The only way to transform back is to reach the end of the cave...

Bubble Bobble is a platform game, with each level being a single screen. The enemies must be cleared from a level to go to the next one. With one player controlling Bub and the other controlling Bob, the player can jump and collect items for points (such as fruit). The real power Bub and Bob have however is the ability to blow bubbles. These bubbles can be as platforms to leap on, or to trap enemies. Enemies trapped in a bubble must be popped by jumping into them, wherein they'll turn to fruit. Additionally, power-ups sometimes float by in bubbles. They include lightning, which flies out horizontally at enemies, and water, which drags the player and enemies straight down flowing over platforms.
Bubble Dizzy

Bubble Dizzy eschews the usual arcade adventure format of Dizzy games, instead being a simple action game.

You must guide Dizzy through the underwater worlds, collecting pearls as you go. Dizzy starts at the bottom of the sea, and you have to get him to the top. You do this by jumping across bubbles, which only have a limited time before bursting. Enemies to avoid include sharks, octopuses and swordfish. Dizzy has limited oxygen, but more can be collected from O2 canisters. 

After completing a level, you get a bonus for the amount of pearls you collected and the amount of oxygen you have left.
Bubble Ghost

This French charmer first appeared on the Amiga, and it's a game in which you play the part of a ghost trying to guide his soul (represented by a bubble) through the rooms of a castle. But how do you move a bubble without bursting it? Simple - you blow.

Anyone who thinks that computer games are lacking in imagination or originality at the moment would be forced to change their mind after playing Bubble Ghost. The concept of a ghost blowing his soul around a castle full of spiked objects is just so-o-o-o weird! Having said that, I have to stress that it's great fun to play, each screen requiring even more dexterous mouse handling than the last – things get very tricky on the later levels. A special mention must go to the game's use of sound, which comprises a catchy title tune, and some humorously appropriate sound effects, such as the ghost's hacking cough when he's made to blow for too long.
Bubble Gun

Bubble Gun is an Action game, developed and published by Weathermine, which was released in Europe in 1994.

The story behind Bubblegun is a simple one. You are a small crocodile with a gun that can fire bubbles (hence the inspired name) who is trapped in a castle and has to find their way to freedom. Quite why they are trapped in a castle, or why they are carrying a large gun, or indeed why they are trying to escape isn’t made clear at any point, but then who really takes any notice of game plots these days?

What you are left wit is a very basic platform game, where you begin somewhere in the middle of a four-way scrolling maze. Dotted around the maze are a variety of objects, such as points bonuses, energy bonuses and time bonuses, but the most important things to look out for are sections of keys. You can carry three items at once, and there are three sections to each coloured key, so it isn’t too much trouble to build up a complete key.
Bubble Heroes

Similar to Bust-A-Move/Puzzle Bobble, Bubble Heroes is an action-puzzle game in which the player shoots randomly colored bubbles at the other bubbles above. Once 3 or more bubbles of the same color are in contact, they pop and are removed from the screen.

There are 3 game modes: Story, Championship (both single-player) and Death Match (two players). The player must also pick a character before the start of the action proper, each with their own special power: a brave knight, a cat girl or a prince turned into a frog.

The Story mode tells you about the planet Radya and the four nymphs that need to be freed from the evil Gonzul. There are four worlds, each divided into two areas of five levels each. Most levels require the player to remove all the bubbles on screen without any of them reaching below a certain point, but some other level play a bit differently and require the player to free a nymph from the bubbles surrounding her. The last level of each world is played against a boss.
Bubble Killer

Bubble Killer is a simple but increasingly challenging arcade shooting game where the objective is to achieve the highest score possible.You are positioned at the center of the screen, surrounded by an ever-growing threat. Bubbles appear around you and move towards your position. Your only defense is to shoot them before they reach you.
Bubble Pop Memory

Bubble Pop Memory is a freeware Memory-style game. 32 cards are placed face down in a random order on the screen, and the goal is to locate the 16 pairs of identical cards in the least possible amount of trials. The player can click on two cards at once to reveal their value. If they are identical, they remain visible. If they are different, they are flipped down again. The player has 4 minutes to complete the game.

The best scores are recorded in a high score table.
Bubble Stones

Bubblestones is a game by Guy Maysonnave, several versions were released with the most common being BubbleStones v1.4 and BubbleStones v2.0. They are the same game with only minor modifications. The goal of BubbleStones is to clear all the Bubbles from 25 different levels before they touch your base. When you connect 3 stones of the same color, they disappear and in doing so they remove any stones that were connected below them. At the beginning of each level you start with 1999 points and the countdown starts. A destroyed stone brings back 10 points, a stone which falls 50 points, a bonus clock gives 200 points. All these are added to the meter and at the end of the level what is there will be added to your score or withdrawn if the number is in the negatives. 
 
You can continue past the 25th level at a faster pace.
Bubble Trouble
A simple bubble popping game from Tony Philipsson released as a coverdisk on the 1992 Jumpdisk magazine. Shoot the various balloons that fly across the screen, making sure they don't hit you!
Bubble Trubble
A puzzle game created by Generation X coder Paul Nordovics and released in 1994.
Bubbles
A Puzzle-Bobble / Bust-A-Move style bubble shooter.Game was written in AmiBlitz3 entirely with the help of AI
BubbleStones 2

Bubblestones 2 is a Puzzle Bobble/Bust a move clone on the Amiga from Guy Massonanve

This is my first ever play of the game.

- AGA, 256 colors
- possibility to change the look of the game. (Read the doc)
- keyboard support
- new game mode : HOT
- many improvement for best gameplay

Bucherwurm

A freeware, German-language game from Jörg Woyke and Meik Woyke, with version 2.5c releasing in 1992. A challenging quiz on literature! After up to three clues, you have to guess a title or author. Listing available from the author as Charityware, send anything and they would send you the game code. Released in S p i e l e k i s t e # 136.
Buck Rogers: Countdown to Doomsday

The RAM (Russo-American Mercantile) organisation is based on Mars. They want to control the Solar System - a natural enough ambition, I suppose. They rule Earth with an iron hand, thus NEO (New Earth Organization) has been formed to counter the tyranny. After Buck Rogers was found and revived from his frozen snooze he joined NEO and helped to remove RAM troops from Earth. However, fear of RAM is still high as they could strike any at time. You join the NEO, one of many new recruits. Buck's task is to form a team, get the hell out into space and put the stellar wind up the dreaded RAM.

Buck Rogers uses an uprated AD&D system although there are many similarities. The swords have been replaced by laser guns, the towns and villages by planets and space stations. You still control a group of six, the menu interface is structured in the same way, even the 'meanwhile' screens appear to have the same artistic 'feel' to them. However, there are many improvements.
Bucktooth Bob's Jungle Adventure
An oddball single-level platform game where your goal is to kill the animals and find the crown or trophy.
Budokan: The Martial Spirit

Budokan is a martial arts game covering Karate (unarmed combat), Kendo (using a wooden sword), Nunchaku (using piercing chain weapons) and Bo (using a staff). The player has a realistic range of moves and must use them wisely, as Ki (life-force) is drained for every move made, whether successful or not, and both this and your stamina level must be kept high.

You can practice your skills alone, or spar against the instructors or your friends. Finally, when you feel you are ready, you can travel to the martial arts world championship tournament at Budokan.
Buffalo Bill's Rodeo Games

Buffalo Bill presents a collection of six Wild West themed mini-games, which hang together around humour-lead presentation and backdrops.You can play as many or as few of these as you like, and can always have another go at them if you fail.

First task is to throw knives at a spinning board upon which a surely-terrified and fortunately-skinny lady is locked - make sure to adjust for the rotation that will occur in the time your shot takes to hit. You get points for missing as many times as possible before hitting. Event 2 is based on shooting ability and is in two stages. First you must shoot the targets of criminals (but not innocents) as they emerge from the ground, next you must shoot the bottles they throw at you from over the horizon.

Event 3 is Calf Roping, in which you must position yourself so as to be able to throw your rope around the poor cow's neck.
Bug Bash

The time is early morning; the place a usually tidy black garden, well cared for by the humans. But to your dismay you notice that your domain has become very untidy overnight. As you look up you see swarms of insects and bugs flying about mindlessly; with no apparent intentions of helping you clear up the mess. It would pear that the 'Evil-Slug' has been up to his old tricks again, and brain-washed the insects and bugs with a wicked spell. It soon dawns of you that it is going to take several days rather than hours to clean up and restore order in the garden. Quickly arming yourself with an insecticide spray gun you begin your quest.

Your task is to clear up all the trash in the garden by placing it in the trash can. When a piece of trash is picked up, it may be dropped by flying directly above the trash-can. You will see and hear the falling piece of trash. You can only pick up one piece of rubbish at a time, and you cannot drop fruits or other pick-ups into the trash can.
Bug Blaster
Released on the red floppy coverdisk from Amiga Computing, this single player shooter by Morgan Henry has an upgrade path to improve parts of your "ship" and choose shot type.
Bug Bomber

A computer’s mazelike circuitry is infected with bugs, and you have been sent in to destroy them. You are armed with bombs, mines, blockades, and various types of hatchlings, which when released will track the bugs and hopefully stop them.

The basic gameplay is inspired by Dynablaster, but it differs because there is more than one way to kill the foes off. Depending on which way you push the joystick as you press fire, you will either release a quick-exploding bomb, a proximity mine, or a hatchling. Collecting ‘EN’ symbols will restore your energy, and ‘IQ’ symbols increase the ability of your hatchlings to track and hit your foes. Be careful when placing blocks; it is possible to shut yourself in.

The single-player game gives you three lives, plus another when you complete each of the 50 levels. The multi-player game can be played in 2 different ways – co-operative (work together to clear the computer of bugs) or competitive (Dynablaster-style free-for-all destruction).
Bug Squish

In Bug Squish the player has to protect their own arm from blood-sucking insects. Using a fly-swatter (controlled by the mouse or a touch screen) they need to be squished before they suck you dry. There are 32 waves, with various bug types, and occasional "extra blood" and score multiplier bonuses. It is based on the Macintosh shareware game Blood Suckers.
Bug!

An AMOS based shareware platform game with puzzle elements by Asa Margetts. You've been turned into a frog but must save your pet, Joe Bug. Make your way through the witch's castle to reunite with your trusty companion and maybe you'll also find a way to get back to being a human being!
Buggles
This tricky platformer has 100 levels of fun and challenge for you as you control a grasshopper and jump your way around the underground cavern, avoiding all manner of baddies and ghosts.
Buggy Boy C64
BUGGY BOY - the Commodore 64 version, on the Amiga
Buggy Commando
A great remake of the 8 Bit classic game. Move the buggy along shooting at the enemies. Simple but great fun. Tested on Amiga 500 with 1 meg expansion and kickstart 1.3.
Build-It: Das Bauhaus

In Build-It: Das Bauhaus, the player takes the role of Joey, the construction worker. He won in the lottery, is rich and wants to fulfill his wish for his own house. However, he does not use his money to hire help, but does everything himself.

This is a tile matching puzzle game. In every one-screen level, there is a number of squares which are divided into two differently-colored triangles. Joey needs to pick those squares up and create a new square of the same color in order to make the four blocks disappear. He can also turn a block on the spot. The goal of each level is to create a certain number of those same-colored squares within the (optional) time limit.

Of course there are a number of difficulties: walls may restrict Joey's movements, new blocks appear in fixed intervals and tools roam around the levels and kill Joey by touch.
Builderland
