A crash course on rules of evidence and judicial procedure is presented in the manual for legal neophytes. The graphics are crude and there is no sound, but your quid pro quo for pulling up with these minor irritations is an entertaining, educational jaunt into our jurisprudence system. Verdict: An original, well implemented concept. Court adjourned.
Cover Girl Strip Poker

Yet another strip poker game. What is there to say about it?

Well, here you can play with up to three players against one of eight digitized women. Each time you make a girl lose all her money, she takes off some of her clothes (4 of the 8 girls feature "movies" of the strip, which consist of half a dozen frames).

At the beginning of the game, you may select your language at the beginning and can also choose to turn the girl's comments on or off. Finally, the game features a zoom function with which you can get even bigger pixels.
Cow Wars

An AMOS artillery game where the projectiles are cows. A two-player only game with a silly sense of humour. Note the cows will say hello to each other in mid-air. Avoid the mountains and any floating, evil penguins.
Cozumel: Ci-U-Than Trilogy-I

The scene chosen for this adventure, the first one of the "Ci-U-Than" trilogy, is the Yucatan, a mysterious land in which legends say there are a lot of dangers, hidden treasures, unsolved mysteries, temples filled with traps... in short, the ingredients to which the good adventurer is used to deal with.

The adventure is developed in the island of Cozumel, where you must guide an archaeologist who had an incident. He was sailing towards it perfectly equipped, when an unfortunate shipwreck left him without anything. Do not think he only lost the map or the machete, no, he lost everything, including the trousers and the underclothes, reason why it's quite possible that an entrance in San Marcos, coastal town near the place of the shipwreck, would carry serious problems with the justice. The main mission of the adventure is to discover all the hidden secrets of the island and then be able to escape from it.
Cpt. Custard

A multi-scrolling space shooter where the enemies are all around you and the mission is to kill 'em all. You can overhead your guns if you fire too much. Enemies have homing missiles as well as lots of other ordinance to use against you and they attack in a coordinated fashion to take you off guard and overwhelm you with close range missiles. .
CPU Challenge
A puzzle game released as freeware from Dr Strange in 1992. Trace connections and items on the motherboard to repair and improve it in the quickest time.
Crack

Swiss developed Arkanoid style game, with a prehistoric theme. Play is for one or two players simultaneously (including a battle-mode), and options are available for mouse and joystick controls. A comprehensive level editor is also included.

The players’ bat here is made out to look like a bone, and the ball is a spherical stone. Level backdrops are randomised pixel-painted scenes featuring different types of Dinosaurs. 

The bricks to knock out sometimes contain pickups to collect, such as a laser gun, an automatic CPU controlled bat navigation mode, extra life, slow-ball etc. A pickup is immediately activated upon collection, but subsequent ones collected are not if one is active, and clicking the right mouse button will cancel out the current effect for the last pickup collected.
Crack Does Pay

One-of-a-kind German business simulation around the illegal cracking, copying and selling of software. Shipped as number 12-01 of the Nordlicht software series. It holds some historical value to show what the Amiga market was like in 1993.
Crack Down

At the beginning of the 21st century, a mad scientist by the name of Mr. K has created an army of artificial soldiers. He conquered the industrial city of Atlantis, and is now preparing to take over the world. The United Nations decided to retaliate by sending two of their top class Special Forces officers, Ben and Andy, infiltrate the city and destroy the enemy base using a newly developed time bomb--Sigma.

Crack Down is a time-limited action game. The two heroes, Ben and Andy, have to get through the levels as quickly as possible placing bombs on X marks scattered around the levels. Although the levels are heavily defended, the player has an array of weaponry including a cannon, machine gun, and superbombs. 

The game may be played as either a one or two-player game.
Crack Out

An Arkanoid style bat and ball game, created in AMOS by C. Hodges that was originally released to public domain in 1992, the 1.4 update was released on October 30, 1997. The game features what some would call sideways play as the bat is on the right side of the screen and the brick configuration is on the left, rather than the traditional top and bottom arrangement.
Crack the Code

A freeware version of Mastermind with a Hi-Score table and full instructions from Graham Woodcock in 1991. You start by having to guess two colors then three and so on until you have to guess six. At five numbers it starts to get more difficult. Codes given show if right color, wrong color, right or wrong position.
Crack the Wall
A very simple Breakout style game with a few extras from Peter Bakota, released to PD in 1993.
Cracked
The idea is to rearrange the pieces on the right hand part of the board onto the left hand side so that all the adjacent edges match.
Cracker

This MasterMind clone was published on the coverdisk of the August 1991 issue (#25) of Amiga Format, first released on July 11th, 1991. The computer will generate a four colour code, from a maximum of five different colours. Can you crack the code in less than TEN guesses and beat the computer.
Craft Defense

First Tower Defense Game on Classic Amigas. Including Editor for new Maps.
Its Alpha with only 1 Level and 10 Waves and Boss Enemy at the end of Wave 10.
CrapMan
A freeware game created by David Hobbs (Hobbsie) in 1991, this is a pac-man clone, created in AMOS and distributed by APDC.
Craps Academy

Craps Academy is an Amiga dice gambling game released in 1988 by MicroIllusions.

Description from the packaging: With Craps Academy's accurate professional simulation, you effortlessly learn the casino game of craps. Whether novice or experienced you will find Craps Academy a vauable tool for developing or sharpening your game skills. You can learn how to make favorable bets, and avoid those designed for suckers. You can learn the bets that must be handled by the dealer, the bets that don't show on the table, and how your bet size can increase your winnings.
Crash & Burn

Crash & Burn is an action racing game, clone of Bump 'N' Jump, played from a top down point of view. As you race through the treacherous and ever changing roadways, the numerous enemy cars will be trying to bump you off the road. You need to make sure you bump the cars out of the way before you get bumped and crash into the sides yourself!
Crash Garrett

Crash Garrett is an adventure in the mold of the classic 1930s film serials: you take on the role of dashing Crash Garrett, a flying ace who makes a living by flying rich Hollywood types around on private flights across the west coast of the United States. As the game opens, Garrett is taking journalist Cynthia Sleeze to an exclusive interview with a high-powered psychoanalyst to the stars, as part of a red-hot story. He soon becomes entangled in the story himself, and must use his wits, cunning and fists to save the day.

While the game takes typed commands, the action is shown as a sort of animated comic book. There is a background image that sets the scene (it may be a mini-map, that shows Garrett's current location marked with a red X) and on top of this are comic book panel-like portraits of the characters currently in the scene, that move around the screen and speak in speech bubbles.
Crash Landing

Crash Landing is a Platform game which was released in Europe in 1992. No intro, no ending, the only sound being an ear tearing tapping noise. Graphics are barely okay but that is no reason to play this game, avoid.
Crave
Head to head dueling game, find a buddy or a rival and pummel them info submission.
Crazy Ball 2
A puzzle shooter mix. You have 20 balls to reach the required score on each level or it's game over. Easier said then done. Hit the score requirement and head off to the next level.
Crazy Cars

Starting Titus' racing series of third-person perspective racing games, Crazy Cars encompasses the American Cross Country Prestige Cars Race. This takes in several parts of the USA, in several powerful cars. Initially you have a Porsche 911 Turbo in your hands, but this can later be upgraded to a Lamborghini and then a Ferrari. There are other cars on the road, which you must avoid contact with. Bumps and divots in the road throws the car off course, as does contact with any of the roadside barriers. Each race must be completed within the time limit.
Crazy Challenge
Move your joystick only to the right in order to run at the fastest speed as you race against an opponent or against your own best recorded time.
Crazy Clock
A freeware puzzle game created by Holger Brunst and distributed with AmiNet in 1993. This is like a Rubik's Cube of clocks. The hands of several clocks must be brought into the same position.
Crazy Colors

A freeware puzzle game created by Norbert Ossenkopp in 1991. In this one person game the aim is to place 32 colored double-stones on the game board so that no stone remains. The Amiga has randomly distributed the stones on the board but what is their position. Place a stone on the game board, click on the game piece with the mouse arrow. A frame appears that shows the stone position, rotation is done with the right mouse button. Left click places the stone, click on a placed stone to delete it. there are three levels of difficulty in this thinking game and a timer to push your thinking faster.
Crazy Columns

Another Amiga news story for you all, thanks to a heads up from our good friend and Twitch streamer Amiga Bill. As if you loved the 1984 game of Tetris or the 1989 game of Columns, you'll pleased to know that a brand new Amiga puzzler inspired by those games has been released for the Commodore Amiga 500 and above. This game named as 'Crazy Columns' is a puzzle game developed by Jochen Hoffer and team, and comes with all the features you would expect of a cool looking Column inspired game for your Amiga.
Crazy Cones

Crazy Cones is a very straightforward little game where you have to collect cones, while avoiding nasties or killing them using mines. There are also obstacles which have to be destroyed using missiles.
Crazy Eights

A nicely made game of Crazy 8's, similar to UNO with lots of user customization available. You can change sounds, music, cards, palette at any time during the game. You can change scoring options, player names, and locale, with the ability to have multiple player preferences. User selectable music, sounds and many languages supported.
Crazy Froggy

A freeware action game written with ASM 68k by Spider Arnaud Guyon aka Spider in 1991. A freerunner style game where you must run\jump on the colored sections and avoid the black sections. Your score increases as you continue to be able to progress forward. the longer you go, the faster the track moves under you. SPEED KILLS, so run and jump smartly.
Crazy Pipes

A game of strategy and reflexes by Joe Rumsey. A Pipe Dream clone where you need to avoid spilling any water for as long as possible. Use the mouse to place sections of pipe on the board so that the water has somewhere to flow. The water flows from the S (source) and can be sped up by hitting the F key. In this version cross pieces can be used with great safety, if there is pipe on the other side water will not flow through the unused ends.
Crazy Priest

CRAZY PRIEST, initially previewed as a playable demo at the RetroKomp/Load Error 2015 demo party, was released as a full PD/freeware game two years later at the RetroKomp/Load Error 2017 demo party in Poland. The game was ranked a very respectable 3rd in the RetroKomp GameDev Compo.
 Consist of 2 modes - single player and multiplayer. Seeking...collect and destroy!
Crazy Seasons

Crazy Seasons is an arcade game about two cute penguin scientists who are working on a time machine on their space station when their computer crashes (poking fun at the Amiga's "Guru Meditation" crash screen), which threatens to create a temporal anomaly and mixing up the Earth's seasons. It is up to the two penguins to rearrange the blocks powering the time machine in order to avert the catastrophe.

The gameplay is very reminiscent of Taito's Bubble Bobble and Parasol Stars: the penguins are respectively blue and green and move around single-screen levels defeating a variety of cute enemies which leave food and valuables behind when killed. The twist here is that the goal of each screen is not to clear every enemy, but rather to arrange four blocks bearing four distinct geometrical shapes in a specific pattern shown on the bottom of the screen, which changes for every level.
Crazy Speedway

A polish racing game where you can choose up to nine different rounds per race and up to 4 racers can play. In classic mode you don't get a point for the round if you crash. Game can be played in Polish or English, and the graphics are very basic, but still great for parties. Saves best time overall.
Crazy Sue

Crazy Sue is a 2D platform game, which was first released in 1990 in issue 1 of the Amiga Fun magazine by MC Publications.

Crazy Sue is a cute little schoolgirl, whose quest is to rid the land of Ereanor of the Evil Wizard of Doom and the Mistress of Death. This was foretold by an old gipsy – meddling itinerants, getting kids into trouble.

Sue is a first-rate platform game. A joystick is needed because the mobile nasties are animated and can blat her with the wink of an eyeball. In looks, Crazy Sue is really impressive. As she walks, the ribbon tying her hair bobs up and down, and when she is still she stakes a few licks of her lollypop. Everything is bright and fast and the collision detection is spot on.

If you think all PD is a waste of time and completely amateurish, look at this. It will change your tune. Frustratingly addictive, it is very touch, springing surprises on you at every leap, and requires thought as well as skill to succeed.
Crazy Sue Goes On

Crazy Sue Goes On is a Platform game, developed by Hironymus Jumpshoe and published by Amiga Fun, which was released in Europe in 1992 as a cover disk of the Amiga Fun magazine by CompuTec Verla in Germany.

The people of Ereanor were relieved when the brave girl Sue destroyed the horrible sorcerer "Wizard of Doom". The liberation of Ereanor was followed by a three day's celebration. But a dark shadow fell over the Kingdom of Ereanor. The sinister "Mistress of Death", the sorcerers wife, is out to get even. Ereanor became a hell on Earth. People became destructive creatures, animals became killer beasts and even plants turned evil.

Sue was not harmed by any of the spells, and from now on lived in her own world, which was worse then her scariest nightmare. To take whatever was left of Sue's pride, the mistress of death kidnapped her teddy-bear...

That really did it! Like she did once before with the "Wizard of Doom", she now decided to fight and beat the "Mistress of Death".
Crazy Tetris

An unfinished AMOS freeware Tetris puzzle game from Krzysztof Pichlak for one player. The screen info is in Polish, but easy to play for any language speaker. Don't let the unfinished part scare you away, this is a quality Tetris game.
CrazyBalls

Move one ball around the board to access the controls to move the blue ball around the same board to the X, then move yourself there to proceed to the next level. Don' leave the playing surface or cause the blue ball to leave the playing surface. Watch the timer! This game was released in Amiga Magazine 42 (Nov - Dec 1996) and came with a level editor to make your own games.
Crazyshot

This is a rather simple shooting range game simulating what one might find in an amusement park. From the menu you can choose between six different shooting range events such as shooting at moving ducks or shooting at balloons. When you run out of time or bullets you are presented with a prize that corresponds to how well you did on the event, for example a key ring if your aim was really bad.
Create Adventure Games

Originally released by Marco Pinto in 1992 as shareware, this AMOS title went to freeware as of version 5 in 1999. Have you ever wanted to create adventure games? Well now you can on your Amiga. This package gives you the ability to create adventure games similar to those that we all loved to play on our 8-bit computers with ease.

Features:
* Include up to 11 pieces of music
* Up to 65536 screens with graphics
* Create up to 65536 Rooms / Messages
* Create up to 256 System Messages
* Create up to 256 Objects
* Save your finished Adventure as an Executable
so that it will run without CAG
Creature

Distress calls received from deep space report hostile alien life forms, and you are the only space security captain within range. Responding to the distress call, you hurry to save a spaceship, a space station which has had its reactor put on self-destruct to prevent the station from falling into the enemies hands, and the lunar base that have become infested with Creatures.

The spaceship, although seemingly abandoned by the Creature, has inside, guard dogs and beastoids that fire weapons. They were left behind by their master. You must survive their attack to find life-sustaining supplies and the key to disarm the reactor. Upon receiving these, you must safely return to your ship to start your journey to the terror-filled space station. The space station has much greater danger. You must gather more essential supplies, but more importantly, you must disarm the reactor before it self-destructs.
Creatures

The inhabitants of the pretty but insignificant planet Blot decided to leave to find a trendier planet, and escape being called the Blotians, a most unhip name. Until they such a planet, they call themselves the Fuzzy Wuzzies.

Their colony ship collides with an asteroid, and crash lands in the Pacific Ocean, near an unchartered island, which they colonise, calling it "The Hippest Place in The Known Universe". Unfortunately the island is also home to rather nasty demons, who can't stand the commotion caused by the happy Fuzzies, or their silly name for the island.

The demons kidnap the Fuzzy Wuzzies by hosting a massive party, then capturing them in a net, and dragging them off to the torture chambers. The only Fuzzy not caught is Clyde Radcliff, who was already being sick in the bushes. He wakes up in the morning with a really bad headache, and fiery halitosis, and sets out to destroy the demons, and rescue his friends.

The game consists of 3 levels, each made up of 3 of stages.
Creeping Me Out

A Scorpion Engine created Action/Adventure/Platformer that doesn't just feature complex levels, but a story, enemies, big bosses and dangerous traps. Francis is waiting for his friends in the bar when disaster strikes! Some sort of magical catastrophe has befallen the town of Gorcester! No time to think! You’ll have to find your friends before setting off on an arduous journey to confront whoever, or whatever is responsible!
Creepy

Creepy is a maze game, developed and published by Thalamus, which was released in Europe in 1990.

Decent Snake clone with nice graphics and sound, but game play is frustrating where your time in the game is your score.
Creepy Crawlers Goliath: Reloaded
The game is inspired by the legendary arcade game Space Invaders and the not so known Space Monster made for the Videopac G7000 by Philips.
Creepy Crawley

Creepy Crawley is a novel game from Frank Dudley. You control a spider who has to eat the flies it catches in its web. Watch out in later levels, the flies fight back! Both of these programs are useful for beginners to look at, as usual, the code is on the disk for you to look at. This is the sort of program which can be played around with to see how it works. Packaged in APD473 with Amos Invader.
Creepy Crawlies

This is a solid unofficial Amiga port of Centipede. It's quite the endurance test. What you see in the screenshots is pretty much the whole game. Since the gameplay doesn't change much and there doesn't appear to be a final level, Creepy Crawlies may become exhausting after a while. The player controls a small Ship. It is moved around the bottom area of the screen, and your aim is to fire darts at a segmented centipede advancing from the top of the screen through a field of mushrooms. 

Each segment of the Centipede becomes a mushroom when shot, shooting one of the middle segments splits the centipede into two pieces at that point. Each piece then continues independently on its way down the screen. If the centipede head is destroyed, the segment behind it becomes the next head. 

The centipede starts at the top of the screen, traveling either left or right. When it touches a mushroom or reaches the edge of the screen, it descends one level and reverses direction.
Crib

An adaptation of the traditional card game, for one player against a computer rival, where each side attempts to beat the opponent to the goal of 121 points.

To start with, the deck is cut and the lowest card determines who deals first. Each side receives six cards, discards two to the crib, then both take turns playing their hand to the board - attempting to score by bringing the total value to 15 or 31, and by completing certain card combinations that score additional points. "Go" is called if no cards can be played without going over a total of 31, and the attempt is transferred to the opponent; the last player to place a card gets an additional point.

When all cards have been played, both hands are scored according to their contents and special combinations, and the score for the crib goes to its owner (each side gets the crib on alternating turns). A new round begins, and so on until one of the players hits a total of 121 or above - winning the game.
Crib Master

An implementation of "Cribbage" for the Amiga, running in no less than six windows on the Workbench screen. It plays against the computer with full muggins and bar rules. There are three difficulty levels and the game is entirely mouse-driven. Pressing the "help" key gives you hints on what hand to keep.
Cribbage

The David Addison games originally appeared on Fred Fish 28 (and 15 for his other original game set). This one, like the others was created in ABasiC and released to the public domain in 1985. This one is an implementation of Cribbage for the Amiga.
Cribbage King / Gin King

Play the games of Cribbage and Gin against a variety of computer opponents. Features include natural language advice, computer vs. computer, Cribbage and Gin variants, duplicate mode, and scenario set-up mode.
Cricket
Cricket is an Amiga cricket sports game released in 1990 by Soundware International.
Cricket Captain

Cricket Captains have a much greater role than their equivalents in most sports. Most major tactical decisions during the match ultimately come under their control, as they do in this simulation, in which you can play or merely watch the match action. Teams are real but the player names are fictitious.

Your options are quite similar to those of a soccer manager. You must hire a coach, scout and physio to enable you to train your players and keep them fit, and to acquire new ones through the soccer-style transfer market.

You must select your team of 11 players before the match, with talented all-rounders more common than in real-life. The game takes in the four main tournaments of the time - a single-division league of four-day unlimited-overs matches, the Sunday League of one-day games, and two cup competitions.

The match view features a plan view of the fielding setup, and a forced-perspective view of the batsman as a shot is lined up.
Cricket Crazy
Cricket Crazy is 2D sports Cricket game by Paul Dowers also released as International Cricket in 1992. Touting itself as the ultimate in cricket simulations, combining management and arcade action.
Cricket Masters

Cricket sport managerial game written in HiSoft BASIC. Game design & coding by Paul Dowers. The game concentrates on the strategy and offers up plenty of relevant statistics. The game has been designed and developed by a true fan of the sport. It replicates everything that a real manager has to deal with.
Crillion

Crillion is similar to Breakout except there is no paddle and the player controls the ball directly. The ball always bounces up and down and the player only controls its horizontal movement. When the ball hits a block of the same color it will dissolve. The ball can change color when hitting a color changer blocks, marked with an asterisk. The object of the game is to clear all blocks while avoiding the skull blocks.

When the player hits a skull block, a life is lost and the level restarts, resetting any progress made so far in that level. There also are unbreakable walls and slider blocks. The slider blocks can only be moved around when the ball has the same color. The Amiga version was to Amiga and later to PC using the version released by the original author, Oliver Kirwa, to the Markt & Technique publication Happy Computer in July of 1988 as a type in game.
Crimbo

It's time for even more Christmas goodness, as if you have a Commodore Amiga at hand or an emulator installed, you might like to play this fun for all the family game of Crimbo by Spud. An unofficial ZX Spectrum to Amiga conversion of the game "Crimbo" by Little Shop of Pixles. Here is what Spud says about this brand new game of Crimbo for the Amiga 500 1.5MB and above : "I did a simple and very unofficial ZX Spectrum to Amiga conversion of the game "Crimbo" by Little Shop of Pixles. Somewhat rushed and unoptimized in an attempt to get it out before Christmas because who wants to play a Christmas themed game after that? There are one or two things missing, maybe they'll be added for next yea, but I know it is simple both graphically and in terms of game play so I hope you enjoy! Instructions: go collect the gifts the nasty elves have stolen from Santa, etc etc. Controls are left right and fire for jump on the joystick".
Crime City

Crime City is a classical point-and-click adventure. You play Mr. White, a poor chap who writes detective stories but wants nothing more than to be a real private investigator. It's a pretty classical story: one day, he can't really write a thing, but then, a mysterious blonde stands before his door, telling him his Father, Henry White, was arrested for murder. It's up to you to prove the police wrong.

A difference to the classical adventure exists: you need money to travel, get information or training. To get money, you can trade at the stock market. What's also different is that the time of the day really matters and that the protagonist becomes sleepy after staying up too long.
Crime Does Not Pay

Crime Does Not Pay is an Action Adventure game, developed by Eldritch The Cat and published by Titus Software, which was released in Europe in 1991.

By rights, this review should have been written from within the safe confines of a mental institution, for never as your reviewer been closer to eating his own head in a state of maddened frustration than after two hours in the vile company of this pseudo-gangster yam , Crime Does Not Pay.

So how does it work? Well, you are the head of a criminal organization – the game is 'endorsed by the Mafia' it says on the box – and it's your job to kill your enemies (i.e. Just about everyone else in the game), make pots of money and finally become mayor of a major American city. This plot, desperately weedy as it is, takes you through a series of inane arcade sequences and unworkable 'pick objects up and use them' scenes. Avoid.
Crime Inc

The programmer of this game launched a legal action against Rockstar North for alleged copyright violation due to the similarity of Grand Theft Auto to Crime Inc. and the fact that he had given them a demo of the game for consideration. A top down gangster themed game that was never finished.
Crime Patrol
Crime Patrol is a live-action laserdisc video game released by American Laser Games in 1993.
Crime Patrol 2: Drug Wars
Drug Wars is another in the long line of traditional American Laser Games arcade-conversion shooters.
Crime Time

Crime Time is a more or less classical 3rd person point-and-click adventure, with the major difference that you don't click on the graphics, but on controls below the graphics. Actions are done by clicking on words, as is movement.

The story is a classical mystery setting: two friends go hitchhiking, and since it's raining so bad, they rest in a small hotel. One of the two starts to drink till he's totally out of control. He stumbles into the wrong room, gets knocked out and wakes up next to a corpse. Now, you have to prove you didn't do anything.
Crime Wave

Crime Wave is a side-scrolling shooter with certain similarities to Narc in tone and gameplay. Controlling a police officer, the player shoots his or her way through slums, inner cities, and other locations, trying to destroy a powerful criminal organization and save the President's gorgeous, young, and single daughter. The game features digitized graphics.
Crimetown Depths

Rolling demo of the game, not playable, but worth a watch. Chancellor Jagoo from Murdrum Planet wants to pay you millions but don't ask too many questions and you must teleport immediately, this could be trouble. Crimetown Depths is set on a planet ruled by a despot, where one of the futuristic megacities is now inexorably controlled by crime, so much so that it is nicknamed "Crimetown". The player plays as one of the mercenaries hired to clean up the city. Crimetown has vertical development, a heterogeneous alien population and high-tech structures, but in a dangerous state of decay. The mercenary would have to reach the deepest levels of the city to ferret out the sources of corruption.
Critical Hit

Critical Hit is a highly detailed fantasy combat game, which re-creates tabletop war gaming on the Amiga. It features a complex and accurate combat system, in which the skills, equipment, health and injuries of individual soldiers are traced. Many real and fantastic creatures are included, each with their own skills, psychology profiles and leadership characteristics. 
 
Complete campaigns may be waged, which consist of series of individual battles. The result of the battles determines the flow of the campaign. Battles are depicted on stunning three dimensional landscapes, and a wide variety of fantasy combat figures and scenery is utilized.

The Unregistered Shareware version runs on 1MB machines, and includes a single campaign, “Goblin”. This version does not include any music, and uses only some of the available features of Critical Hit. 
 
Full version 1.2 is now available for free (requires 1.5MB RAM). I cannot guarantee support for free copies of Critical Hit.
Croak 2

This it an Amiga conversion of the classic Frogger that saw its birth in 1981. Croak 2 attempts to simulate, as accurately as possible, one of the most fascinating stages in the lifecycle of the Australian Cane Toad. As everyone knows (I didn't), the eggs of the Cane Toad are laid within the carcasses of dead sheep. The tadpoles quickly mature in this nutrient-rich environment, and soon there's a multitude of young toads, ready to begin their famous migration to the nearest creek or river bed. This journey frequently takes them across busy roads and rivers, whose erratic currents and high toxicity defy the bulky toad's best attempts at swimming.

If you can't remember, or if you have never played the game before (where have you been?), the basic idea of the game is to get your frog from one side of the road (at the bottom of the screen), over the river and into your home (at the top of the screen).
Croak!

A variation of the classic arcade game Frogger, designed to make use of the Amiga's hardware.

The basic gameplay involves guiding a frog into one of 7 home-bases at the top of the screen, which have hard barriers either side of them (avoid these). This involves first guiding him across a road, avoiding the vehicles, then over a river using moving logs.

In this version the road has a variety of machinery to dodge, ranging from standard cars to lorries - hitting one kills your frog and leaves a red splodge in that part of the screen - a nice touch. The rivers also have families of turtles appearing intermittently - these can be used to cross a level, but they don't stay up for long. There's also a 2-player mode in which both players compete to get into the same slots - player 2 using a yellow frog.

You have a 60 second time limit for each frog on the first level, and 5 lives at the start.
Croaker

Like Frogger with a twist - the number of lanes increases with each level. Supports two players. Password free by permission of author. This is Croaker by Brian Grier from 1993. You start with your Frog at the bottom of the screen, and your task is to get it into one of the spaces at the top of the screen. While this may sound easy, You have to cross a road, which as levels progress, will get busier, and busier with traffic, making this more and more difficult. When you get to the central part, which you may think is safe, a Snake can sometimes appear and it randomly moves across the screen, which you must avoid, otherwise it will cost you a Frog. Once the central pathway has been passed, it is onto the logs, where you will navigate them without falling into the cold harsh water, which will cost you a life. Then finally on the last log, it is your last jump to freedom, which you must time well, otherwise you will hit your head on the wall, which will cost you a life.
Croins

Destroy all the Croin Asteroids and eliminate the enemy ships you will meet within them. Every four stages or so you'll have to face and destroy an enemy mother-ship. In the subsequent stage you will need to pick up as many diamonds as possible before time runs out.
Cropky

Cropky is an Amiga version of Dots - an abstract strategy game played by two people on a sheet of squared paper. The rules are a bit different from original Dots game - your aim is not to capture enemy dots but to link two dots together with a line drawn in any direction you want as long as you don't cross already existing lines or you have where to draw another line (the dot is visible not farther than one square distance - vertically, horizontally or diagonally). Cropky is a conversion of a game under the same title from Atari XL/XE. The original idea comes from Krzysztof "Kaz" Ziembik who was persuaded to give permission to create Amiga version by Mariusz "Ramos" Rozwadowski. With the abilities and knowledge of Adam Stach (programmer), Piotr "Piesiu" Radecki (graphics) and Piotr "Pece" Cieślik (music) they created a neat and not so easy game.
Cross Check

CrossCheck is a hockey game which is played from a top-down perspective. Players can take control over one of ten national teams and participate either in a friendly match or a league (two divisions with five teams each). Each athlete has three stats which influence his performance on the ice; players have the option to change the lineup or make substitutions during a match. The focus of the game is on fast-paced matches which can be customized with a few options, e.g. if fouls and offsets are avenged or the length of a match. Players have control over the athlete which has the nearest position to the puck.
Cross Circuit

CrossCircuit by David Wright is an action logic game that calls for fast thinking and fast reflexes. Equipped with a mobile electromagnet, your job is to grab various shaped connectors and drop them in place, forming a complete circuit across the screen. CrossCircuit is played with a joystick in port 2 or the keyboard. There are 8 levels of play. Plus the connectors on the left side of the screen to those on the right. If you complete all 8 levels, it goes to level 6 except with more plugs to connect and more difficult to reach.
Cross Circuit(Jeff Sprague)

A shareware game from Jeff Sprague, created in 1993. This shooter is a bit like an AMOS version of Tempest. Electrical surges are pulsing through the power grid of the central defense computer network. You must detect and neutralize them before the reach the outer line. Unstopped surges will drain your energy until the network fails.
Cross Country

One day in prison a clown was waiting for the best moment... HIs name was Clowny and his goal was to escape, kidnap the princess and begin his rein of terror over the land. He even cut the tail off the fox, making in you a mortal enemy. Guide the fox in halting Clowny's escapade and save the princess. But you'll need to get past his minions first.
Cross Fire

Not to be confused with the *other* 1990 shooter called Cross Fire, this one was for just one person, was created by Roger North and features a setup very much like the Llamasoft game Gridrunner. Your objective is to shoot the baddies on screen, while picking up goodies all the while avoiding the shots from the guns outside the grid that put pressure on you from all sides.
Cross Maze

CrossMaze is a puzzle game by James Kevin Butts for one or two players. Determine by the number of letters and arrangement, how the 2 lists of words representing words going down and across intersect. It will be possible to put all the target words into the puzzle. You can save and load previous games, print them out in case you work better with pencil and paper, you can choose a list of 10, 20 or 30 words that need to be arranged and determine if there is a timer per word in place in the game.
Cross Out the Intruder
In this game you must discover the "intruder" object from four pictures
Cross Over

The aim of Cross Over is to collect all of the circles by moving your square over them and then moving the combined items to the nearest X. You must do all this within a given time limit. ON some level there are numbered tiles that can be used to help you reach normally impossible places, but be careful when you move these tiles as they can destroy each other. A 1 can hit a 2, 2 can hit a 3, 3 can hit a 4 a four can hit a 1.
Cross Words

The rules to this word puzzle game are simple. Three letter words are worth 5 points. Four letter words are worth 10 points. Use joy stick to move the letter around and position top left of letter in center of share you want to paste into. Words go across, down and through the 3D tiers. It is possible to score more than one word on a turn.
Crossfire

Precursor to Crossfire II, this shooter was created by Thomas Schulze, Dirk Böhme and Stefan Schulze was originally released but later changed to mailware as the author believed nobody was interested in it, the full version was eventually released to aminet.
Crossfire II

In "Crossfire II" you play the role of Karsten, a fighter pilot of the rebels. A wide range of missions awaits you, ranging from escort, defense to large battles in an armada of ships. These missions tell an extensive story with several surprising turns that take you to the strangest places of the known universe.
Crossover

It is a race against time to get all the stars! When you start the slider moving it will go until stopped. Move around your blockers so that you can slide them around and pick all the stars up in time without getting off track.
Crossword Construction Set
A program to help you create your own crosswords, give the word list and allow the program to craft the challenge with you!
Crossword Puzzle

Crossword Puzzle (CWP) was written by Mike Epting and distributed on Aminet as Freeware in 1992. This crossword game was written entirely in C. The game can be played from the workbench. For tough solutions you can get a single letter hint or check your solution at any time. If you wish to save a puzzle in mid game that is available. You can enter your own puzzles using a text editor. The first line is the height and width of the puzzle in squares e.g. 13, 13. The next lines are the puzzle solutions. Use upper or lower characters but be careful abut the spaces. To make this thing square you will probably need spaces at the end of some lines. The game was distributed via AmiNet and Genie.
Crossword Puzzle Creator

Crossword Puzzle Creator, created by Jurgen Weinelt and presented in German language, it had several versions, with the last version, v5.1 (Cross) released in 1993, the original version came out years prior. Version 3.3 was released on PD U1421. It allowed the creation of basic crossword puzzles without fancy graphics.
Crossword Wizard
A crossword puzzle game created by Greg Abernethy and Martin Fitzgibbons of Rush Software in Australia and published by the same starting in 1993.
Crown

Crown is a jump and run game. The goal is to travel trough six different countries to finally become king. The game is non-linear, so the player can choose which country he wants to go to. The levels are pretty different: in England, you need to control a knight on his horse. You need to jump over all hurdles and collect all 80 shields to complete the level. In Scandinavia, you control a Viking on his boat. Here you need to collect treasure chests and avoid the whales crossing your way. In Russia, you play a Russian bear who needs to imitate the dance of a girl next to him. If he succeeds, the bystanders will give him money. In Japan, you control a small dragon which needs to jump from island to island. On his way, he needs to collect 80% of the stuff floating around or he will starve to death. In India, the small Indian boy needs to walk over the bridge, avoiding the flying bananas (?) and catch 8 mice.
Crownfall

A medieval jewel-matching adventure for the Amiga 1200 / AGA, by Johannes Naumanen.

Journey through royal halls, frozen castles, overgrown chambers, swamps, lava and ivory. Match jewels, open new routes and choose when to unleash an arrow, a bomb, a homing special or a disco ball. Combine specials to turn a difficult position into a cascade of colour and sound.
Cruise for a Corpse

1927. When Inspector Raoul Dusentier is invited to a cruise upon a mighty sailing ship by the wealthy businessman Niklos Karaboudjan, he looks forward to nothing but a relaxing week on the sea. Instead, his host manages to get himself killed on the second day. Murdered, to be exact. Too convenient that a policeman is aboard -- Dusentier sets out to search for suspects. He doesn't need to search long. Why is it that none of the family members seem awfully sad about the demise of the old man? Is the mysterious Father Fabiani really as pious as he says? In the tradition of Agatha Christie, each and every person on board has a motive for the murder.

Cruise for a Corpse is a graphic adventure game with a point-and-click interface.You advance in the plot not so much by solving common object-based puzzles, but by talking to the right persons about the right subjects at the right time, thus collecting clues. You will also find pieces of evidence scattered throughout the ship.
Crunch Crumble & Chomp

A 1995 transmutation of the strategy\tactics game created by Epyx for 8 bit machines. This shareware version by Ronald Picardi in 1995 was created in AMOS and likewise lets you assume the role of a movie-style monster, becoming a kaijin titanic horror. Technically CC&C is a strategy game; you have to keep an eye on several statistics, including your health, appetite, and even such minute details as the tilt of your head (helps in aiming breath weapons). Destroy the city before the human military destroys you!
Cruncher Factory

Cruncher Factory is a Pac-Man variant. The player commands a cruncher (which looks exactly like Pac-Man) and steers him through non-scrolling labyrinths shown from the side. On every place not occupied with a wall are pills which have to be eaten by rolling over the field they are on. There are also ghosts which cause the player to lose a life when touched - at least until the cruncher eats a special ball which causes him to eat the ghosts. A level is won when all balls are eaten.

The game features 100 levels, a level editor (can be also used to change the existing levels) and a two-player mode.
Crunchman

This feels like an updated version of the 1987 Pac-Man clone from 1987, this one was released in 1992 by Dave Baldwin and appears on the original Assassins disk. It has your normal dot gobbler, avoiding a similar quartet of ghosts. In this one the ghosts do not hesitate to follow through the tunnel and speed is somewhat variable. The sound effects are the only letdown in this, as they are strange and unrelated sound samples.
Crunchman(Martin Esters)
A single player, Shareware, Pac-Man clone, collect'em up created by Martin Esters with multiple levels of difficulty and a high score screen.
Crush

A German-Language two-player action game from Roland Weber & Kim Troldner. At the center of crush is the duel between two players. both use a joystick to steer their figure across a playing field. On this there are stones that can be pushed by a playing figure standing next to it in the direction of view. The aim of the game is to crush your opponent with a stone.
Crypto-King

Crypto-King is a Shareware puzzle game created by Robert Bromley in 1991. A game for those who like to solve Cryptograms, (those coded sentences that have to be decoded to be read). This version of Crypto-King which will search 100 Cryptogram databases and will contain at least two 100 Cryptogram databases. The 'Scrambler' program which will enable you to create your own databases.
Crysis

Can the Amiga run Crysis? Let's find out. The idea for this game came to me towards the end of development of Trans-Pennine Express Simulator. I figured all I needed to do was record some game footage, and pause and display a picture whenever there was something for the player to do or shoot.
Crystal Caverns (Pollysoft)
Move the blue dude around the cavern, avoid the worms, zappers, ghosts, dragons and bouncers and find the way to get to the next level.
Crystal Dragon

Crystal Dragon follows the same genre and setting as Dungeon Master. It revolves around two adventurers, both controlled by you, in search for a powerful artifact. It is now in the possession of an evil wizard who has lead his minions across the world to find it and slaughtered anyone in his way. Now you must seek out and destroy this wizard in order to prevent him using the true powers of the crystal.
Crystal Hammer

One of the Amiga's many Arkanoid clones, Crystal Hammer is perhaps best remembered by its intro tune, which has been remixed and covered by many.

The game is all about reflecting a ball against a wall of bricks. Behind the wall of bricks live some worm-like creatures that will come out to disturb you when you've opened a hole in the wall. Prolonged contact with the creatures will kill your bat. Destroying bricks will often cause a coloured brick to come spinning down slowly. These spinning bricks are power-ups, altering your ball or bat according to their colour. You can have a sticky bat (green), a wide bat (blue), a slower ball (yellow), multiple balls (cyan), and the decidedly Arkanoid-inspired shooting bat (red). Whatever you do, don't pick up the grey brick, or you will be destroyed.
Crystal Hammer '93 Edition

A Sequel to CRYSTAL HAMMER. It contains 50 levels compared to 30 levels in the original game. Like the original version, this updated and improved version, is all about reflecting a ball against a wall of bricks. Behind the wall of bricks live some worm-like creatures that will come out to disturb you when you've opened a hole in the wall. Prolonged contact with the creatures will kill your bat. Destroying bricks will often cause a coloured brick to come spinning down slowly. These spinning bricks are power-ups, altering your ball or bat according to their colour. You can have a sticky bat (green), a wide bat (blue), a slower ball (yellow), multiple balls (cyan), and the decidedly Arkanoid-inspired shooting bat (red). Whatever you do, don't pick up the grey brick, or you will be destroyed.
Crystal Kingdom Dizzy

The magical crystal treasure has been stolen and scattered all over the islands, so it is up to Dizzy to find them and restore order. Once again, Dizzy's main enemy is the pirates, and some deadly island creatures, but all Dizzy's friends are around to help out when the going gets tough.
Crystal Kingdoms
An unreleased Amiga game known as ' Crystal Kingdom ', which was created in Blitz Basic and appeared in the Amiga Format Blitz Basic Competition.
Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace is an Platform game, developed and published by Amiga Fun, which was released in Europe in 1993 on Amiga Fun Magazine as a Coverdisk. 

Quite an interesting concept, this game involves you using the sparks from your magic wand to break blocks that may be in your way. You can control where to point the wand too. Other than that, very basic. The presentation is good, in terms of graphics and music, but the actual gameplay is a bit slow-paced and difficult to get the hang of. In all fairness though, it's pretty good for a freebie.
Crystal Quest

Buckle in and gear up for the classic galactic ride of your life. Far beyond known galaxies, the stars are scattered with precious crystals. As a renegade outer space prospector, your job is to scoop 'em up and bring 'em home. Just one problem: The brilliant glow of these gems attracts some of the universe's foulest pests. We call them nasties - and they're just that. So go ahead...zap the intergalactic vermin and cash in on the crystals. It's nasty-blastin' fun.
Crystal Skull

Lost for a 1000 years, the Crystal Skull is said to bestow upon the owner magical powers and internal life. After 20 years of searching, you, Dr. Indiana Smith have finally tracked it’s whereabouts down to one of four Aztec pyramids in the Amazon Basin. To retrieve it should be easy, except the Aztecs who built the pyramids don't want it stolen by a grave robbers and have built a few surprises into the pyramids to keep unwanted guests out. They shouldn't be a problem, should they?
Crystals of Arborea

The game is set upon the island kingdom of Arborea, the remnant of a world all but destroyed. According to the in-game mythology, Mogroth, the deity of chaos, became furious following his banishment from the pantheon of gods. In his rage, he instilled chaos in the minds of the populace and encouraged them to rebel. Orcs and Black Elves were amongst those who converted and chose to follow Mogroth. Unwilling to allow their creations to be subjugated, the remaining deities flooded the world and drowned all but those few who now dwell on Arborea. The four elemental crystals, of earth, fire, water and air respectively, are all that now guard against the ultimate subjugation of the kingdom by the forces of chaos.

Cuba 1898

You are a soldier recruited in the peninsula that has no money to pay the license and therefore must fight in the overseas provinces. For a few years now, the bandits are ravaging the rural areas of the island of Cuba. Some of these bandits are funded by the government of the United States that has put its expansive gaze on the island. US troops have landed on the island and are committing pillage where they pass. Your mission is to fight these troops and kill them... The game features plenty of enemies to defeat, a soundtrack by Ricardo Vieira, 4scenarios such as a port, Havana, Palm Grove, and the beach, and inspirations to Konami's late 80's game of Green Beret.
Cube-X
Cube-X is a solid puzzle game. Move all identical cubes to adjacent squares and they disappear. There are more than 100 levels, so this game will keep you busy for a good long time.
CubeMaster

CubeMaster is an arcade action game in the style of Asteroids. In the game, a CubeMaster is a combination of an athlete and an astronaut whose task it is to defeat wave after wave of CubeDrones. Like in Asteroids, the player moves his craft (the manned mobility unit) around a zero gravity environment where the player can use a thrust to move forward and a counter force to slow down as well as rotating left and right. The drones come in two sizes. Shooting the large ones will cause them to break into smaller ones. If the smaller drones are not destroyed quickly enough they will revert to the larger size again. The player's cannon builds up heat as it is used and when overheated it needs some time to cool down.

Drones of different colors have different abilities and if the player is not quick enough in shooting them down they will change. Among these are the yellow that when touched will make the player's controls all mixed up.
Cubic

In Cubic you have to destroy the rows of blocks that slide down towards you by wiping out similar blocks. You have extras at your disposal, such as the bomb to destroy several blocks at once, or the universal block, which wipes out all the others. Sound effects, or on request give the fun the finishing touch. 
 
Released individually and as part of the Intelligent Fun game pack along with Tygard.
Cubical Worlds
A freeware AMOS game created by JIP Soft (Joona Palaste) in 1996. In it you must activate the charges and destroy the skulls before they discharge.
Cubistix
Cubistix is a 3D Tetris game for 1 - 2 players. There are lots of different options for inputs and many stats about the game are shown.
Cubit
Cubit is an Amiga puzzle brain game released in 1991 by Panther Games.
Cubix
Cubix is a Puzzle game, developed by Xtreme D-Sign and published by Media GmbH, which was released in Europe in 1991.
Cubulus

How do you make an interesting computer game out of the venerable Rubik's Cube concept? According to cult programmer Tobias Richter, you view it from the top with all sides displayed, and allow the player to choose the number of sides, from 4 to 25.

A large number of different starting arrangements are offered, grouped by difficulty. Rather than having a level-based progression, you can choose any of these from the start. A number of different tunes are provided, written by Team 17 cohort Bjørn Lynne.
CUBUS

Can you handle Tetris in all the dimensions? You've got to build complete planes out of the pieces falling in the playing space. If a certain number of planes are filled, you get to go to the next round. If the play space fills to the top, the game ends. Initially designed by Fred Bayer with graphics by Oliver Siebert for full commercial release, previously interested suitors fell away when a similar game was released, so this game was released as Shareware in 1992.
Cuento de Navidad
A scrolling screen platformer for multiple languages intended to allow you to play the story of The Christmas Carol.
Cul de Sac

Published by Markt & Technik in the Amiga Spielesammlung Band 2 compilation. A 2D single screen puzzler where you push shapes into holes. In order to finally create order again, you balance boxes in a basement that is much too narrow. Very easily?
Curse of Enchantia

Little Brad didn't believe in witches until he met one. The evil hag torments the fantasy land of Enchantia, and has just summoned Brad from the Earth as an ingredient to her potion of eternal youth. Brad doesn't like this plan. And who would be better suited to rid Enchantia of the sorceress than a tender teen?

Curse of Enchantia is a graphic adventure game with an icon-based interface. The game contains almost no text: there are no object descriptions, and the purpose of most items is apparent. In the rare occasions of interaction with other characters, symbols in balloons substitute words. If there is text on the screen, it usually consists of either signs or comic phrases.

Starting in a prison cell, Brad will have to free himself and find his way on the ocean floor, through a medieval city, a junkyard and an ice castle. The player commands Brad via an icon bar that pops up if the right mouse button is pressed. The hero can perform a variety of actions, e.g.
Cursed Kingdoms Book Zero: A Tale from the Past
Most versions found are a very limited demo version where there are no cities, dungeons, functional battles, missions or purpose. All it has is wilderness, character sheets and inventory routines.
Custodian

In Custodian the player takes the role of the caretaker of an nuclear-powered alien cemetery. It was infested by parasites which drain the energy and the player's job is to fend them off.

There are three tombs, each of them are extensive environments which scroll in multiple directions. The player uses a jet pack for movement and searches for the pods which the parasites are using to extract the energy. They have to be brought to a special room to destroy them there. The goal is to get rid of all pods in a level, but the parasites have something against this. And so they actively try to kill the protagonist, but fortunately he has ten weapon systems at his disposal to shoot back. Well, at least if he bought them from special silos with earned points. The total energy reserves of the tomb act as time limit.
Cutesy the Bear

Guide Cutesy the bear through 10 levels in the garden eliminate the baddies that threaten it in this colorful platformer by J. Monday from 1991. Bump the baddies from below and kick them off the platform remove them from the garden patch. Collect the snacks before clearing the last baddie gives a bonus snack screen! Each level is timed, so don't waste a precious second.
Cutthroats

You live on small seaport Island called Hardscrabble -- hardly the hip place to be. Working as a professional scuba diver, you have the chance to salvage a sunken treasure from one of four shipwrecks, earn the respect of all the old farts and become wealthy beyond all imagination.
CWM Moria

The Dungeons of Moria, usually referred to as simply Moria, is a computer game inspired by J. R. R. Tolkien's novel The Lord of the Rings. The objective of the game is to dive deep into the Mines of Moria and kill the Balrog. Moria, along with Hack (1984) and Larn (1986), is considered to be the first roguelike game, and the first to include a town level. This game is a CWM Version created from this wellspring. CWM coding was done by Thomas Davies and Juha Niemimaki, who are somewhat hidden in the title screen but all in the name of full attribution to the work that had gone before. CWM Moria is an Amiga port of Umoria by Thomas H. Davies based on Umoria, the current version on aminet is from 1994, and is based on Umoria 5.5.2, the newest version, but Amiga CWM versions started much earlier. 
 
CWM Moria is open sourced with source code easily available.
Cyadonia

Significantly harder than its predecessor, C.Y.A.D. II features 49 new levels. Your goal is unchanged from the first game: Collect all diamonds and then get to the exit. C.Y.A.D. II introduces new gameplay elements like switches, blocks you can push, laser cannons that must be destroyed, and color-coded locks for which you need to retrieve keys.
Cyber Assault

Cyber Assault is a shooter, developed and published by Trojan, which was released in Europe in 1991. It was intended for use with a light gun but unlike some other Trojan titles, this one can either be played with a PHAZER light gun or with an ordinary Amiga mouse. In the 23rd century mankind has been forced to search the galaxy for mineral resources to survive. The U.E.F. Explorer, a massive automated reclamation vessel, has developed an error in the guidance computer and has selected Earth as the next target planet. Only you, Dexter Hartman, space adventurer, can board the Explorer and prevent it from coming home. Fight your way through the many ship levels, armed with your trusty Phazer, blasting rogue droids and aliens. Locate the ship's central computer and destroy it! This is the ultimate in high speed blasting action for your home computer.
Cyber Blast 2

"Cyber ​​Blast 2" is another piece of Amiga code that cannot be found in the depths of the Internet. The game was created many years ago and was released.. A sad curiosity is the fact that only one person registered the game, although it must be admitted that the production is quite interesting and impeccably made. Benedykt Dziubałtowski obtained permission from the author of the game to publish it, thanks to which in the 21st century we can feel the taste of the early nineties with our Amiga.
 
In the labyrinths of corridors player can shoot the horrible monsters in a very Doom\Hired Guns like way.
Cyber Blast-X
CYBER BLAST – Classic Amiga Action Reignited!
Cyber Cardz

Released as freeware as a, "work in progress" as Cyber Cardz 0.2 by Marco Guidone in 1998 this solitaire game was intended to display the excellent card artwork as much as provide the user with a fun and immersive pass time game.
Cyber Empires

Predecessor to the highly succesful (and more complex) Fantasy Empires. A tactical and strategic turn-based game of robotic combat, land conquest, and city siege. This game was released by Silicon Knights in March 1992. It was voted the best multi-player game in 1992 by Computer Game Review.

Five empires descend upon the neutral and strategic planet of Orion in an attempt to claim it as their own. The days of conventional warfare are over and the age of the cybernetic warrior is at hand. The game is a mix of strategy and battle action. First it has a strategic part where you build factories, cyborgs, gain control over new countries, plan your next moves, schedule attacks and build defences. Once you and the computer have completed your turns, its time for action - attack, defence or occupation. To win the game you need to defeat the enemies with your armies of cyborgs. Size of the cyborgs varies from the smallest type called Mercury to TITAN which is the largest one available.
Cyber Force

Cyber Force: Zniewolony Umysł is a sci-fi action adventure game, similar to Flashback. In 2017 a scientist foresees the destruction of the world due to a nuclear war. Therefore he decides to move his consciousness into a crystal. The game starts a few hundred years after this event. The player must reach the Syntec laboratory located in SpringCity and copy the awareness of the doctor to one of the cyborgs. The game is divided into five stages, travelling each of them requires solving a number of puzzles, finding and using the appropriate items, killing enemy units and finding a way out to the next level. The character may run, crawl, jump, climb, hang off ledges, use a gun and talk with encountered people.
Cyber Kick

Cyber Kick is a science fiction platform game. The action takes place in the space base of renegades on Mars. John Malkovitch goal is to collect all the radioactive containers and put them in the recycling stations. The player will encounter countless number of traps, such as electric barriers, sharp blades or vices and hostile opponents, such as alien creatures, drones, mechs, tanks and others. The only weapon of the player is a powerful cyber kick. In base teleporters can be activated only after finding the right access card.
Cyber Man

You are Cyber Man, a familiar pellet-eating entity. You travel through a 3D maze in first person view, avoiding your rivals who seek to send you back to the beginning of the maze. Collect the pellets and avoid the monsters. You can hear them coming and see them in the HUD. Once you've gotten the pellets, you can flee the maze. Or does that just lead to a new maze?
Cyber Race
An overhead racing game preview by Menato Denny from 1995. The demo appears to just support a single user.
Cyber-Cop

Four levels, no bosses, gameplay consists of monotonous trekking as many as seven screens back and forth through a barrage of respawning enemies that follow you to other screens, lasers, mines, spikes, swinging maces and mine carts to get the ever increasing amount of pods. I have no idea how anyone can survive this without an invincibility cheat, which is probably what they did to make up for the fact the game is so short. There isn't even a final boss, or any in game ending. Graphics are nothing special, but when enemies start to appear on the screen the action immediately slows down. All i
Cyberball

After American Football players started cheating by using bionic parts, the game was forced to change its rules. By 2022, the game was played not by humans, but two teams of seven robots. To spice things up, the usual pig skin ball was replaced with a 350 pound bomb.

Cyberball brings this fast and furious action to life. Gameplay is essentially the same as the real sport, although the 'downs' are replaced by the bomb's heat gradually increasing towards 'critical'. After this it will explode and possession will be swapped. This is prevented when you cross the 50-yard line, lose possession or score a touchdown, in which cases it resets to 'cool'. Field goals and punts are not featured - the only kick is the initial kick-off you receive.

Control passes from the quarterback (thrower) to the intended catcher as soon as a pass is released. The two-player game is co-operative - on offense one player passes and the other receives.
Cyberblast

Cyberblast puts the player in Fastrax Laboratories where the Trans-universal Portal Experiment in the solar system has gone completely haywire. The player must make it through all 64 levels until he finds the missing control chip. The control chip needs to be found in order to close the portal as it's being open allows for deadly aliens to enter our universe.

The game is similar to Gaunlet, and levels must be completed within a time limit which changes based on level complexity. In order to complete levels, the player has to locate and collect the five crystals and then find and use the exit. Walls, enemies, and other obstacles will impede the player throughout the game and players much maintain a supply of energy units or their game will come to an end. Players can select between two characters at the start of each level. The two characters have different qualities and limitations which make them more or less adept to each different level.
Cybercon III

The Cybercon III computer was built with the intent of looking after the world, but something went wrong—the computer killed people instead, and now the world lies in chaos. The player takes on the role of one of the few survivors, with the goal of destroying the Cybercon III computer.

The gameplay of Cybercon III revolves around exploration and puzzle-solving as the player works their way through complex where the computer is stored, with the player tasked with destroying or disabling the computer and its defenses and bypassing the computer's notice, made easier by way of a secret entrance into the complex.
Cyberdroid

A colorful multi-scrolling shooter written in Blitz Basic. Coding by Antonio Ruiz Fernandez. Graphics by Jose Maria Ruiz; rendered gfx by David Diaz Gonzalez. Music by David Diaz Gonzalez and sound FX by Juan Antonio Anillo. It is the year 25730 in the Extraterrestrial Era. The Supreme Sapience Computer suggested the correct rules in evolution for the human being to progress without senseless recessions. 

The first of these rules could only be: 1: to abandon the biological status. So was the way the first Homo Cyberneticus was born. In a few months thousands of them came to life, these ones being capable to squire in a period of hours conscience, ideas and feelings of, and for a whole life. And they were programmed to protect the living and through them experience generations of wisdom and teaching. But as does happen, resentments and schisms came between the two, and only you can do the work to save the species.
Cyberdrone

Cyberdrone is an RPG game with a sci-fi background; in this game you play the role of a cadaver. Well, to be more precise, of a clinically dead subject whose body has been sold to a corporation specialized in building cyborgs. The good news is that your brain has not been damaged and still retains all your memory; the bad news is that nobody cares for this and what is left of you is thrown into the productive process as raw material. Fortunately, a failure of the machinery avoids you the latest phase of the process, and this is the point where the game begins. Your task is simple: find the exit and flee.
Cybergames

You will face different opponents ranging in skills from mediocre to very tough to beat. There are 35 opponents and six locations in the complete game. Since this is a fighting game, the object obviously is to smash the other guy. You can either beat him with your weapon until he has lost all of his energy, or you can make it short by separating his head from the body (A Swedish shave).

Decent graphics, much better than in many commercial releases, but unfortunately animation is weak and control over the fighters is horrible. You can get used to it, but after some time it becomes tiresome. Nevertheless, if the game was a bit polished, it could have been quite good.
Cybergammon

Cybergammon is a Board/Strategy game, developed by Cyberstyle and published by Amiga Fun, which was released in Europe in 1990.

Released in 1992 on Amiga Fun Gold Edition issue 2.
Cyberman

CyberMan is a Dutch puzzle style game like the old Boulder Dash: you need to reach the exit, located in the upper corner right of the screen, clearing the way safely there by pushing the correct blocks.
Cybernauts

Cybernauts is a very simple 2D rail shooter/shooting gallery game. The player just controls a crosshair, and destroys various enemy robots and other objects on small arenas (first arena is in Moscow, USSR, second is New York, and third is San Francisco - the game has 3 levels). He must destroy enough enemies to go to next level.
Cybernetix: The First Battle

A shoot 'em up with decided Defender influences, Cybernetix has you strafing back and forth across a quickly scrolling screen which wraps at both ends. As in Defender, a radar at the top warns you of obstacles and enemies which you would otherwise crash into at high speed.

The obstacles are made up of asteroids, which split up when shot. If you destroy the smaller fragments, they will release small crystals which grant you bonus points. But crystals also draw in greedy enemies. Similar to Defender and Dropzone, there is a large assortment of enemies with specific behaviours, weapons and attack patterns, such as quick, relentless hunters homing in on you, slow bombers and spinners with spread fire. Destroyed enemies release power-ups from time to time, such as shields, faster fire rates and multi-directional fire. At certain intervals are special stages with enemy bosses and fortresses.
Cybernoid II: The Revenge

The follow-up to Cybernoid: The Fighting Machine is again a flip-screen shoot 'em up. In control of the deadly Cybernoid craft, your job is to rescue the cargo which has been stolen by a wave of pirate ships.

Using the range of weapon systems correctly is again a key factor. These include sideways aiming guns, bouncing bombs, 'seeker' smart bombs, bombs which move around th edge of the screen before finding a target, and time-sensitive bombs which explode a few seconds after you drop them. Shot pirate ships release cargo, and you must collect at least 1500 points of this, but on many screens it is more prudent to make an escape ASAP, as some screens have more hazards than others, and not all aliens on each screen act in the same way.
Cybernoid: The Fighting Machine

There are three asteroids, hidden among thousands, where various minerals and precious gems were stored. It was believed the riches would be safe there, until the Zoggians discovered them! Now you have to fly an experimental spacefighter, the Cybernoid, into battle to recover the asteroids. The Cybernoid is equipped with standard laser blasters, missiles, and the ability to pick up other weapons along the way. 

Cybernoid is an arcade style action game for one player. You can choose from three different skill levels; easy, hard and lethal. On some versions two different sound modes are also available, a basic music and sound effects mode, and a super sound effects mode with no music. Each room you explore is equipped with a time bomb. The bomb will explode taking you with it should you take too long to get past all the obstacles on the screen. You start the game with nine ships, and more can be earned by collecting enough points during the game.
CyberPunk Alien City

A game created by Johnny Acevedo and friends for Amiten Games. This is a space invaders clone with multiple weapons in a cyberpunk atmosphere. The Cyberpunk City of Night Bloom are invaded by the Aliens , Marc the Mercenary have work to do...
CyberPunks

Join the ranks of the elite and take control of a crack team... The 501st Cyber Assault Squad. The foreign legion of the future; armed to the teeth with high-tech weapons and wearing power assisted armour, only these rock hard commandos are tough enough to take on the universe - and beyond...

Lead Raa, Gee, and Bee into battle against terrifying alien life forms, on missions that are more than just another bug-hunt. Time is running out... The drop-ship is ready to roll; and you are about to board an express elevator to hell... Going down!

You are given five missions to complete, each mission has four decks. You can use teleport pads to warp to another area of the deck. If you don't complete your mission under the given time limit, you'll fail your mission and the game ends, and stopping you from completing your mission are a horde of aliens. Some areas are guarded by a steel door, and the only way that you can open it, is by obtaining a red, green, blue, yellow, or black ID card.
Cyberpunks 2: Next Generation

30 years on... Lead the next generation of CyberPunks on even more dangerous missions into space and beyond.

Engage in battle against relentless swarms of alien creatures with your team of cyber marines and return order to a chaotic planetary system.
Cybersphere

Cybersphere is an arcade game that is fundamentally similar to Breakout and Arkanoid. The player controls a "paddle" that can move horizontally which is used to direct a bouncing ball to destroy "bricks" arranged in different patterns. Some bricks may take several hits to destroy, and often drop gems that add to the player's score if collected, or various power-ups, including a temporary floor that will prevent the ball from falling outside the playing field, an extra ball, a wider paddle or cannons that the player may use to destroy more bricks.

The game does not feature any kind of plot. The levels are broken down into several "sectors". In addition to regular levels, there are bonus stages that may be accessed by picking a certain bonus item during play.
Cybersphere Plus

Cybersphere Plus is an updated version of Cybersphere featuring completely new, more challenging levels. The core playing mechanics are the same as in the original Cybersphere.

Cybersphere Plus was distributed via the Apogee shareware model. The game is broken into five "sectors", each several levels long. The freely distributed shareware version contains the first sector with three regular levels and two bonus stages. Later, game has been deemed freeware by coder Clay Hellman.
Cybertech Corporation

Earth: 2025 AD
Man's accomplishments in the last 25 years have been remarkable.The unification of the world's largest powers saw the end to the wars of the 20th century. Scientists, now working for the benefit of mankind, have managed to halt the ageing process. Now space travel is no longer a dream, but reality. The combination of positronic pathways and neural networks gave birth to a new breed do computer... 
 
The cyborg was developed by Cybertech Corporation in 2019. But, as with most of man's creations, the cyborg did not bring with it the benefits that man had striven so hard to achieve. 
 
Aboard the starship Sigma-5 the first stage of the cyborg rebellion has started. Most of the human crew have been slaughtered - only a handful of personnel are still alive. It is only a matter of time, a very short matter of time. 
 
The future lies in your hands. Have you got what it takes?
cyberTRON
cyberTRON is a tron light cycles type game for 2 to 4 players on Commodore Amiga.
Cyberwolf
Techdemo of our upcoming game, still buggy and unoptimized...
Cyberzerk

Cyberzerk is a top-down shooter in which the player has to cleanse a big space ship from all inhabitants. This is accomplished by using either the standard gun or a limited supply of grenades. The ship consists of various levels which in itself are divided into non-scrolling rooms which are navigated by using one of the exits of the current screen. The death of every enemy - which mostly move on a set path without actively hunting the player - within a time limit is the requirement for finishing a level.

Getting hit by an enemy causes the life energy to go down and running out results in an instant game over. To counter this, energy refreshments are sometimes left behind by killed enemies. Other extras are grenades and a map which shows the layout of the current level but can be used only once. The co-operative two-player mode features friendly fire.
Cybexion

CYBEXION is THE new addictive game. Various labyrinths have to be cleared by skillfully moving stones. However, your task is repeatedly hindered by many extras. A. Tactics game with a twist not just for puzzle fans and against the clock. Over 100 levels with password system, high scores.
Cyborg Crisis

A difficult challenge, aliens are popping up al over the maze. you can see where by the white transport dots. Keep your level of ammunition up by grabbing the red gun symbols, which pop up when you are getting low on ammo. So make every shot count!
Cycles

A snake\lightcycle game from John G. Gilmore in February of 1987, written entirely in C and released as freeware. The game had three levels of difficulty. Use the arrow cursor keys or the keypad combo of 8, 5 to go up and down 4 and 6 to go left and right. In the game you avoid other cycles and lines and try to trap the other cycles with your lines and those of other players. In case of emergency, you can run into the box outlined in pink. this will give you another chance at completing the same level. The amount of time you take to trap the other cycle and the difficulty of the level will determine the points awarded.
Cygnus 8

Cygnus 8 is an updated version of the C64 game Star Trader (released in 1984 by Bug-Byte Software). It's essentially a space trading game where the goal is to become rich and famous by buying and selling a variety of commodities, but it's different from most games in the genre in that your main character has a life outside his spaceship as well. He needs food and sleep, and he can do various things while visiting any of the planets in the game.
Cylogic
Cylogic is a puzzle game, developed by Cybestyle and published by Amigo!, which was released in Europe in 1990. It was released on issue 4 of Amigo!.
Cytron

Viewed from above, Cytron is inspired by Paradroid and Alien Breed. The robot Cytron has been sent into a research facility in which robots have gone berserk, and it must safeguard the area and rescue the trapped scientists.

The character control is skittish, meaning that the droid is hard to stop instantly, which makes progression through the levels harder.
