I have two problems with Embryo, though. One, as has also been noted in many contemporary magazine reviews, is that it takes forever to bring even a single enemy down. The enemy helicopter, gun turrets etc simply take way too many hits before being destroyed. Two, the gameplay is too simple even for a 3D shooter. All you can do is fly around and kill enemies, in very simple missions.
Emerald Caves

Emerald Caves, A New Emerald Mine Clone with 64 Brand New Levels for your Amiga! Emerald Mine is a 1987 puzzle video game developed and published for Amiga and Atari ST by Kingsoft. The series follows mines filled with various gems, such as emeralds. It is a Boulder Dash clone in which the player completes levels by collecting a specific amount of gems before reaching the exit. Emerald Mine was Kingsoft’s best-selling title with reviews generally favourable, and spawned several sequels.

Emerald Caves is an Emerald Mine clone, a nod to the past and features 64 brand new levels to test your skills. Challenging but fun! Emerald Caves is available for OCS and AGA Amiga.
Emerald Demo Mine 6
A Boulderdash game compiled by No One Inc and sold as shareware from Ruppelware and published by the Emerald Mine Club Holland in 1995.
Emerald Mine

Emerald Mine is a maze game, developed and published by Kingsoft, which was released in Europe in 1987.

Emerald Mine holds your interest even after the novelty has worn off. It is not unusual in that it is a series of puzzles you must solve in sequence but this game, however, contains over 100 levels! The levels are often difficult to master: you must learn the rules of each, maneuver around obstacles, and avoid the merciless creatures.

In each level, your objective is to gather all the emeralds in the allotted time. Besides emeralds, you will find: diamonds, which carry three times the point value of emeralds; rocks, which you can topple onto creatures; explosives; keys to linked rooms; wheels that attract enemy bugs and more. Emerald Mine is fast paced, but il doesn’t requite the reflexes of Superman. One or two people can play: two-player mode lets you and a friend play simultaneously as a team. The game saves 30 high scores for each level on the copy protected disk.
Emerald Mine 3 Professional

Emerald Mine 3 Professional is a Boulder Dash variant and features no gameplay changes in comparison to its predecessor. The player's goal is to collect diamonds which are surrounded by dirt within a time limit. When walking over an dirt spot, it is cleared and an stone above it will fall down - with unhealthy results if the player or a monster is hit by it. Other items are dynamite to clear out boulders and keys for certain doors.

The need to plan ahead and find out the required steps to reach the diamonds give the game a puzzle-solving character. Each player has to create a profile which is assigned a handicap (zero to eight), depending on the already solved levels. Each level has a difficulty level assigned to it and the player can freely choose levels which are equal or below the handicap. There are also additional levels for two players.
Emerald Mine 4 Professional
A Boulder Dash style game created with the Amiga Emerald Mine Editor and released commercially in November of 1991.
Emerald Mine Club Mine 1
A BoulderDash style game created with the Emerald Mine Editor released a part of the Emerald Mine Club Holland disk sets.
Emerald Mine II

Emerald Mine II is an Boulder Dash variant and features no gameplay changes in comparison to its predecessor besides the new level editor. The player's goal is to collect diamonds which are surrounded by dirt. When walking over an dirt spot, it is cleared and an stone above it will fall down - with unhealthy results if the player or a monster is hit by it. Other items are dynamite to clear out boulders and keys for certain doors.

The need to plan ahead and find out the required steps to reach the diamonds give the game a puzzle-solving character. Besides the about hundred levels in single-player, there are additional levels for two players.
Emerald Mine IV

Emerald Mine II came with a level editor which enabled everyone to create their own standalone Emerald Mine games. But at the time of the release of Emerald Mine (I) there was already a level editor by Headcrash available. The Emerald Mine Clubs also created other editors, which were sometimes (or maybe always) improvements of existing level editors by Kingsoft. There were also editors available in which people could draw their own graphics and use these in their games. This is the reason why some of the downloadable games below contain different graphics from the original Emerald Mine. 
 
There are several games with the name alternately Emerald Mine IV or Emerald Mine 4 because of this. This version is by No One. The first 40 caves are remixed by The Blockheads, the last 40 caves are the original version.
Emerald Mine Tools

Emerald Mine - Tools with versions continuing until at least V6.03 (Emerald Mine Editor), created by the duo of No One Inc and eventually Ruppelware starting in 1991 and released as Shareware. Created with ASM 68k and released with enough info and instructions to get you up and playing quickly and creating your own levels or modifying others to make them easier or harder to your heart's content.
Emerald Mine Tutorial 1

An Emerald Mine set of caves created by No One with the intent of teaching you how to better play Emerald mines and also to give those creating caves a starting point for creating their own caves and challenges, it was created with the Emerald Mine Editor and later published by Emerald Mines Club of Australia in 1989.
Emerald Mine Tutorial 2

It's been a few years and we've added a lot to Emerald Mines so here is a new tutorial from No One Inc and Emerald Mines Club of Australia to get you back in the swing. Published to Emerald Mines Club of Australia in 1991. Part of a set of 3 EMCA tutorials. There would eventually be a collection by Kingsoft that would include this title. But remember to always use the Ruppleware Editor for better Intro's than the Kingsoft version. Intended as a primer for new and returning players from No One Inc.
Emerald Mines CD

The Emerald Mines CD contains the Boulder Dash-clone Emerald Mine and a collection of 177 level sets for it, each of them containing 80 levels. The player can also choose to customize their playing experience by selecting different graphics or sound effects sets before starting the game. Most of the levels were created by Emerald Mine fan club members.
Emeraude Empire

A French language game created by Francois Lavialle of GFX Movies, make your way around the maze of danger and make your way towards the disk and then take the disk to the floppy drive to move to the next level.
Emetic Skimmer

1987 saw the release of Emetic Skimmer on the Commodore Amiga line of Computers. A shooter game created by Hack and Slay and published by Kingsoft.

In Emetic Skimmer, set in 5354, the first AI has gone rogue and needs to be stopped. It is the player's duty to use the advanced Emetic Skimmer space ship to put an end to the AI.

But before this can be accomplished, it is necessary to secure all space stations in the AI's command. This is done by deactivating the station's protective shield and then destroying the defenses on the inside. The player is mostly engaged with finding the way around the levels, which scroll in four directions, and dodging respectively shooting enemies.

Every level consists of multiple stations which rise in difficulty and complexity over time. When playing with two players, one controls the space ship and the other the weapon systems.
Emlyn Hughes Arcade Quiz

Emlyn Hughes' Arcade Quiz is a game based on quiz machines found in bars and public houses. The idea is to move through ten mazes of blocks and reach the Win bar on the right of the screen. Be careful though, as the maze scrolls to the left and if your not quick enough you will reach the Lose bar on the left of the screen.

When you reach the Win bar you enter a bonus game where on a time limit you have to answer as a number of questions based on how many coins you collected. Afterwards you have a choice to either cash in your money or move onto the next level which will cost you money to enter. Along with the main playing area, you can also see how much money you have and any bonuses collected.
Emlyn Hughes International Soccer

Emlyn Hughes International Soccer offers realistic arcade action and football management combined into one game. The wide range of facilities and control options have between designed in such a way that you can sit down and play without hours spent studying the manual, and getting to grips with the controls. One or two can play, whether against each other, or against the computer. You can even watch two computer teams playing each other! Player skill levels and fitness levels vary, so picking the right team is just as important as the way you control your players during the game.

Fixture lists, results, and league tables may be displayed at any time during the season, and if you have a Commodore or compatible printer you can even print them out as a permanent record.
Emmanuelle

This adventure is licensed from an autobiography of the rather sordid life of Maryat Rollet-Andriane. It centres around a man's efforts to attract her - suffice to say, he doesn't do so by offering her a can of Pepsi, and the game is not aimed at the young or prudish. Most of the game involves using multiple-choice dialogue to produce the correct outcome. You will visit bars, beaches, and many glamorous cities. There are also several sub-games, as you visit a casino, fend off love rivals, and face down smugglers.
Emotional Conflict

It was like Christmas eve on the night of July 14th 1987 and the asylum was all amok with sounds of desperate psychotics, chewing their way through the leather straps on the straight jackets. Suddenly there was a large shrill, as the torn-up carcass of one of the doctors came hurtling through the swivel doors, almost landing on top of you. As you looked into the eyes of the corpse, a bedpan hit you in the back of the head, causing you to fall headlong into the remains of the somewhat mutilated doctor. 
 
You awoke some several hours later in the penitentiary state hospital, surrounded by armed troops. The nurse came over and gave you a shot of morphine. Later that night, the law came to talk to you. "Do you have any idea what happened?" asked one of hte officers. "Nope, I think I was hit on the back of the head with a steel potty." And then things started to get really weird....
EmotiWorld
Avoid the moving mad faces, stay off the death heads and the spikes, pick up all the hearts and complete the level as quickly as possible or :( for sure.
Emperor of the Mines

You are now the Emperor of the Mines and are charged to command a vast fleet of spacecraft to explore and exploit the mineral deposits in your quadrant. Many hazards must be faced, including: battles against the elements, mechanical failure, financial problems and the neighbouring warrior-race in this 'real-time' space wargame where money is king.

The game consists of 2 parts/episodes, either of which may be played by following the instructions at the CLI prompt after booting the game.
Empire Soccer 94

Rather than copying Sensible Soccer or Kick Off, this football game features a number of comical and unrealistic touches. Although the view is top-down, the pitch is small and square, and the players appear huge on it. A range of moves including overhead kicks, trapping the ball and quick 1-2 passes can be mastered.

Before each match your team can choose special moves to assign to each player - power shots with ludicrous curve, super dribbling (making the ball stick to your foot), and a Barge power to push players out of the way. A full world cup tournament is offered, which up to 8 human players can partake in, as well as single exhibition matches. The action replays feature a VCR-style control.
Empire Soccer AGA

The AGA version of the 1994 quirky classic. Although Empire Soccer 94 was released on the A500 there was a special unreleased AGA version which featured better graphics, team editors an indoor pitch and other improvements. Rather than copying Sensible Soccer or Kick Off, this football game features a number of comical and unrealistic touches. Although the view is top-down, the pitch is small and square, and the players appear huge on it. A range of moves including overhead kicks, trapping the ball, and quick 1-2 passes can be mastered.

Before each match, your team can choose special moves to assign to each player - power shots with a crazy-big curve, super dribbling (making the ball stick to your foot), and a Barge power to push players out of the way. A full world cup tournament is offered, which up to 8 human players can partake in, as well as single exhibition matches. The action replays feature a VCR-style control.
Empire: Wargame of the Century

Empire: Wargame of the Century is a Turn-Based Strategy game, developed by Northwest Software and published by Interstel Corporation, which was released in Europe in 1988.

Empire’s a strategic game of conquest that can accommodate up to three players (computer or human). The player starts the game with one city and has to conquer all the other cities (between 50 and 80) on the planet. Each city (once captured) can be assigned to produce a particular unit e.g. army, battleship, transport ship etc to help in the war effort.

Each unit has a movement limit per turn: the player can either use the mouse or numeric keypad to move them one step in any of eight directions until their allowance is used up, or can use the mouse pointer and click on a destination several paces away, whereupon the unit will then move toward that objective every turn until it either gets there or its path becomes blocked.
Emporos: The Trade
A shareware strategy game by Roland Richter set in Europe. The aim of this beautiful game is to acquire a country - but the way there is not revealed! Successful trading simulation.
Enchanted Land

Enchanted Land is set in the peaceful land of Damiran. But as it is in video games, an evil wizard stops by and takes over. In this case, he broke the heart of wisdom and the only way to bring the story to a good end is to collect the pieces from the five levels of this game. The protagonist is the magician Kurgan who jumps through the multi-directional scrolling platform levels.

A big boss stands at the end of each level, but defeating him is not enough to get access to the next: the hidden parts of the heart need to be found first. Besides platforming, there are are lot of enemies to fight. To do so, the magician has twelve weapons at his disposal which need a certain amount of energy to use. Just like the other two bars (jumping and life energy) it can be refilled by collecting crystals.
Enchanter

You are a dim ignorant Apprentice Enchanter, but your task is enormous. You must save the world from the warlock Krill who is ruling the land with his evil powers. You are not the first in this quest but hopefully you will be the first to succeed, as the more experienced members of the Circle of Enchanters are powerless. You know the basics of magic and will have the chance to learn many spells. Keep your wits and use everything you can to your benefit!

Enchanter is a text adventure set in the Zork universe, following the original Zork trilogy. As in the previous games, the player interacts with the environment by typing in text commands, usually combinations of verbs and objects. A new feature in the game is the player character's ability to cast spells. These spells must be memorized before the protagonist is able to cast them, and are learned during the course of the game.
Encyclopedia of War: Ancient Battles

Designed to recreate pitched battles in the world of antiquity, 'Ancient Battles' lets you command the armies of 'Julius Caesar', 'Alexander the great', 'Hannibal', and 'Attila the Hun', in the great battles of the ancient world.

An 'easy to use' system allows players to design their own armies in a matter of minutes so that every game can be different. Forces can be selected from those available to any of 24 different nations.

The game comes with a number of preset scenarios and includes a comprehensive 'Historical Notes', covering Battle Notes, Warfare in the Ancient World and Army Notes.

GAME FEATURES: 1 or 2 player game, computer control of subordinate generals, hidden movement, automatic deployment, variable sized battles and map designer.
Endurance

A shareware game made by Ozzy O'Mara and published in 1995, this game was made in the 3D Construction Kit. A point and click 3D adventure game. A space station threatens to explode if you cannot deactivate the reactor in time, then you can turn your attention to the missiles on the planet surface. 3D puzzle adventure with polygon graphics in the familiar style.
Enemy 2: Missing in Action

The adventure in the vastness of cold space continues. After a failed research mission the crew got stuck in alien spaceships. In the fight for survival they meet old friends and new enemies. It is an emotional roller coaster between despair and hope. The big question is: Will any human ever return to earth?

Originally released in 2013 as a mail order commercial game. Rereleased in 2022 as freeware.
Enemy: Tempest of Violence

Enemy: Tempest of Violence is an action game shown from the side. A seemingly abandoned space ship was the goal of a research team. Unfortunately aliens were still there and assaulted the humans. Now the player's mission is to purge all 34 floors. There is a fix set of objectives which have to be completed within a time limit, e.g. rescuing survivors, destroying alien eggs, finding weapons or killing aliens. Some of the objectives are not at the same place in each playthrough.

The defying feature of this game is variety in gameplay and objectives. It introduces more gameplay elements as it goes on and the player has to solve sections which rely on quick action, solving puzzles or both. Besides the expected movement options, the player character also has some more exotic moves like double jumps and walking backwards while shooting; equipment includes a variety of weapons, e.g.
Energie-Manager

In a typical business simulation, your job is to open a restaurant chain. But watch it: to succeed in Energie-Manager, you will have to pay close attention to ecological aspects. Try to win eco prizes, reduce costs with power saving washing machines and water saving toilets.

The game was published by German federal authorities in the early nineties to teach children about eco-conscious business behaviour and has been distributed for free since then.
Energy

Scheduled for release circa 1995, the Amiga version of ENERGY was never released due to the ailing Amiga market following Commodore's bankruptcy in 1994. A horizontally scrolling futuristic, alien Shoot 'Em Up.
Energy Mover

Energy Mover is all about building an energy supply system. The player must find a proper way to change one type of energy to another (for example water energy to electrical energy), using specified number of available machinery and wires/pipes. The task must be done by a certain time limit. Some of the boards, which actually are world continents, contain an obstructions in the the shape of randomly occurring black holes or walls, destroying parts of the installation.
Enforcer

ENFORCER demo is available on Vulcan's CD. Known as both Atmosfear and Enforcer, this is a very early version of a fake Doom clone written in AMOS. The selection of three weapons are standard; a pistol, shotgun and machine/plasma gun. Some sound and graphics, including the hand and pistol image, seem to have made a jump from Doom directly! A few monsters appear and attack from all directions.

It’s similar to Death Mask in that no real time 3D or texture mapping is involved. The first person view is created using the old Dungeon Master technique but some nifty animation makes the transition between blocks smooth. When walking forward the view bobs up and down and progresses convincingly. Similarly, turning around on the spot looks right, because the background is being scrolled horizontally to simulate the changing panorama. The bogus Doom style has its drawbacks in this case and produces a maze which is like the lines in graph paper.
Engine Adventure Code
A shareware program from Matthew Briggs of Engine Nine Design, created in 1998. A compilation of tools intended to allow you to create your own adventure and other games.
Engines

"Engines" is a game in the Gravity Force-genre. Other games in that
 genre is e.g. Turbo Rakketti, Gravity Force II, Roketz and Bratwürst.
 You have a space-ship. Gravity pulls the ship downwards. By rotating
 the ship and using the engine you can navigate through the 2-dimensional
 landscape. Add cannons and another player, and presto, you've got a
 shoot'em up-game.
England Championship Special

Featuring the English national squad in a top-down soccer game, England Championship Special represents British publisher Grand Slam's attempt to cash in on both England's respectable semi-final entry at the 1990 World Cup and the popularity of Anco's acclaimed Kick Off series.

With its 1991 release, English Championship Special is somewhat awkwardly set in between the 1990 World Cup (England made the semi finals, its best result since 1966, then lost to Germany and to Italy in the third-place match) and the European Championship of 1992, to which the "Championship Special" part of the title refers. The squad composition is based on the 1991 status quo, which means you'll go into the Euro tournament with World Cup veterans such as Waddle, Beardsley and Wright, but without 1992 players like Alan Shearer or Alan Smith, infamous substitute to Gary Lineker in the Sweden match.
English Tester

Even if the title screen shows 'English Tester 2' it was sold in a box just labelled 'English Tester'. The 2 in the title means version 2. ENGLISH TESTER is a program supporting the learning of words, phrases and idioms. Very attractive graphic form, ability to add your own lessons, interesting visual and sound effects. These are just some of the possibilities of the ENGLISH TESTER program! The game was created by No Name Team (Rafal Kolano, Marek Koszel) in 1995 and was created in AMOS.
Enigma(Black Dragon Design)
A 1993 freeware puzzle game by Andrew Campbell of Black Dragon Design, created with AMOS and alternately known as X-Tiles 2. "Simple, well-realised, and addictive!" - Amiga Computing (August 1993)
Enigma(James Pretorius)

Addictive board game with tactical and strategic Elements for 1 or 2 players according to simple rules. To win you just have to have more stones than your opponent ends up owning. First released on CD by Jump-Disk.
Enigmatik
An AMOS based shareware, single player puzzle game by Guido Raffinatore under the company name Anubis in 1994.
Enigme a Oxford

Enigme a Oxford is an Adventure game, developed by Inference and published by Coktel Vision, which was released in Europe in 1989. Jonathan left the library of the university where he studied in Biology. He had managed to associate his studies and his passion for history in a thesis dealing with Captain Cook's diaries. He was no reaching the most fascinating point and was working on the micro-fiches reproducing the original documents. He regretted, however, that he would not be allowed to see any original drawings. Or could he?
Enlightenment: Druid II

One hundred years after Hasrinaxx the Druid defeated the evil Acamantor, his nemesis is back, and although now older and having lost his Druid status after experimenting in black arts, he feels worthy of banishing this terrible foe.

The gameplay uses a forced perspective top-down view, and strongly resembles Gauntlet in the way Hasrinaxx moves, shoots, avoids enemies and collects health items. 

Matters are more complex in terms of the spell system however. 32 spells can be collected and used, including a fireshield to allow you to pass fiery areas, water and fire walls to attack immediate enemies, a deathlight to clear the area of enemies, and a teleport. You can also summon one of 4 Elemental beings, who can be controlled simultaneously to attack creatures for you. Only 8 spells can be carried at a time, but you can drop and later re-collect them.
Ensignia Maze
Find your way out of the 3D first-person maze in this freeware game created by Vaxine in 1990.
Enterprise

Enjoy the experience of orbiting a planet and then flying on the surface. Mankind has spread its roots to many solar systems both far and wide, and has colonized planets far beyond today's beliefs. This is not for the sake of exploration, but to mine for precious minerals and metals. The memory of man's first home has been lost to the sands of time and only myth remains. It is said that the planet that started life as they know it is Sola III, a politically important planet. However, the ozone layer has been fading well beyond your ability to regenerate it. The only chance for the planet is to find 6 rare nuclei to stabilize the ozone layer. You must take to the controls of the Enterprise and scan the galaxy for the needed items. You start in the cockpit of your ship with the controls at your fingertips.
Entity (CMS Software)

You control the Stix and are being invaded by the entity. You are enclosed inside an electrofield which must not be touched by the controller. If you do, your energy will be drained and the bonus will be set to zero. The entity is in multiple parts and can be harmless or harmful. These various forms will attempt to get to the side walls and cause a drain of energy. If it makes contact with the wall, it will mutate into more harmful form. To stop them reaching the walls, you simply sweep Stix over them. A bonus life is given every twenty thousand points.
Entity (DAS Software)

A point and click adventure created by DAS Software and released in 2001. It was originally begun in 1998 and had a few releases including bugfixes along the way. Entity follows on from Bud Lightening's adventures in The Experiment, and pits our hero against a new, more terrifying threat to Freedom and Justice than ever before encountered.
Entity (Loricel)

Entity is a side-scrolling platform game in which you control a female (in her bare essentials) trying to save a planet from an evil creature (the entity) that has broken lose from it's petrified state and is about to wreak havoc. An elder informs her that she is the chosen one, whom we get to see in the intro.
Entropy
A 1-2 player cooperative shooter developed by Paul Shepherd and published by Berliner Spielekiste in 1993.
Eor

An XOR clone. 15 levels of play which will melt your brain or whatever you are using in its stead. Only tested for Amiga 1200 and above. Magus and Questor are trapped in the 15 mazes of EOR. These include Dolly's Revenge, Patience Pending and The Decoder, and can be played in any order. Before going through the exit, they must collect every balloon from within the levels. All of this must be done in a limit of 2000 moves.

The characters have differing abilities, and can be swapped between at any time. Hazards to avoid include bombs, falling boulders and barriers. Four pieces of the map can be found and collected.

The physical rules of this top-down maze are somewhat bizarre, but consistent: dotted force-fields can be traversed (and neutralized) by horizontal passage, waved ones by vertical passage; fish will fall as surely and as lethally as the boulders in Boulderdash, while chickens will travel in the direction they are pointed until something gets in their way.
Epic

The sun is about to go supernova and humanity must find a new home. All the population is packed into a huge fleet of ships and they set off for a suitable planet. Unfortunately the route goes straight through the territory of a hostile alien race, the Rexxons. 

The game is a space shooter but you also get surface missions on different planets. The main emphasis on the game is the graphics which were excellent when the game was released but this meant that the game was very short with just 7 levels. There are loads of cutscenes all with music from Holst's planet suite.
Epsilon 9: The Revenge of the Stingons

Yeno Hou returns in Epsilon 9: The Revenge of the Stingons, a sci-fi point & click graphic adventure and the sequel to Starbase 13. The game opens with Yeno Hou reporting to Galactic Forces headquarters immediately after the events of the previous game. He is told they already need him to deal with another urgent situation: a vital mining operation on a distant planet (Epsilon 9) has stopped responding to communications. Yeno Hou immediately takes off in a ship, and the game begins as he arrives at the mining facility's deserted front desk.

The interface divides the screen vertically into two parts: the top half shows the current scene from a third-person perspective, and underneath is a panel that displays the inventory items you are carrying, six action buttons ("Examine", "Operate", "Use ... with ...", "Take", "Talk" and "Shoot"), as well as an additional button, "Switch", that allows you to select between multiple playable characters -- but only during certain parts of the game.
Equality

Originally released in 1991, improved and updated in 1992, vastly modified and finished for wide release in 2003. 
You must find the balance between the two sides. Each object has its own mass:
– The green ball weighs 1 Kg.
– The yellow ring weighs 2 Kg, it crushes the green ball.
– The blue triangle weighs 3 Kg and crushes yellow and green objects.
– The brown diamond weighs 4 Kg and crushes blue, yellow and green objects.
– The red pentagon weighs 5 Kg and it crushes all other objects when it falls.
– The gray square has no mass

The value of the next weight is displayed on the side of the central bar. The balance of the plateaus is visualized by a progress bar.
Equilibrium Spectre

Match colours to clear it, the way you already know how. But every tile has mass. Clear a match on the left and the left gets lighter, so the beam tilts -- and every tile still standing slides diagonally into the new low ground. The move you just made rearranged the board you were about to solve.
Erben der Erde: Die große Suche

In this game you are Rif, a young fox, who is falsely accused of stealing the magical orb of storms. This orb is capable of predicting when storms will arrive. Obviously this is important to farmers, but it is just as important to the boar tribe, for their supply of mud.

You'll have to find the Orb and the real thief, to clear your name, save your girlfriend and prevent war with the boar tribe. While your doing this you'll encounter a much larger mystery: What is the origin of the tribes? Legend has it that the humans gave the animals the power of thought and speech, and then vanished. Who were they and what happened to them?
Erben des Throns

Fantasy-themed strategic/managerial wargame. The premise is that in a vast continent made up of warring fiefdoms a king arose and unified the whole land. Eventually the once warring barons agreed that they couldn't live peacefully with each other and the king was assassinated while the sole heir was conveniently out fighting in the Crusades. You play one of this barons who must expand his starting territory and conquer the entire kingdom. Gameplay is phase-based and you have to do all sort of things from commanding armies and devicing combat strategies to managing your budding villages and fiefdoms by collecting taxes, recruiting, and balancing your checkbook.

The game includes a series of gameplay options to modify and create your own game modes.
Erdkunde 1

Erdkunde 1 (Geography I) is an educational program of the M&T software series "Learning by playing!" The topics are wide-ranged. It covers the entire Federal Republic of Germany including the new federal states. The learning part provides information about the historical development of cities, the geographic location of rivers, industrial development, sights and much more. It was created by Harry Herweg, Holger Manz of CD-Soft using The Director and published by Markt & Technik in 1991. 

The quiz contains 300 different questions about the items described in the tutorial. In addition, some questions about general knowledge about Germany are built in. The questions are asked in such a way that a learning effect is also achieved when guessing. Using the boxes A, B, C, and D, the possible correct answer is selected with the left mouse button. If the answer is incorrect, the correct answer is displayed and the option is left to compare the question with the correct answer.
Erdkunde II

Erdkunde II is the sequel to the original game, and the next level of Geography training and edutainment, covering, not Germany, this time, but the USA. Erdkunde II (Geography 2) is an educational program of the M&T software series "Learning by playing!" The topics are wide-ranged. The quiz contains 300 different questions about the items described in the tutorial. In addition, some questions about general knowledge about the U.S. are built in. The questions are asked in such a way that a learning effect is also achieved when guessing. Using the boxes A, B, C, and D, the possible correct answer is selected with the left mouse button. If the answer is incorrect, the correct answer is displayed and the option is left to compare the question with the correct answer. 
 
Let's combine the inspiring with the useful and create the series while learning through play! It shouldn't only work to reassure worried parents, but also to impart knowledge to all Amiga friends.
Erdkunde III

The third game in the German-language trilogy, this one also made using The Director by Harry Herweg and Holger Manz of CD-Soft, but this one is a rehash of a game originally put out in 1988 by Commodore, but by the same authors. Still a multiple selection quiz, edutainment game. This entry is back to being focused on Germany and surrounding areas.
Erections

And God appeared to King Lickerish in a vision saying, "Build up a tower to my glory that its tip touches heaven." And Lickerish replied but surely there is no-one who could build such an erection. And God did rebut him saying, "Now that's where you're wrong mate."
Eric the Warrior

A Gauntlet inspired game created with the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit where you shoot swords at familiar wizards and ghosts as well as piles of bones. You must avoid the pits and not get touched by the baddies. There are power ups for your weapons, potions and gold to pick up to increase your score.
Eric Watch Your Step

A freeware puzzle game created by Colin Naylar and released in 1992. Part of Assassins PD 149. Help Eric to get home. Landmines litter the way through 6 levels of difficulty. A nice touch is hitching a lift on the train in a couple of levels. In the final stage you must help Eric reach his front door.
Erik

Erik is a platform game that scrolls vertically but not horizontally. The titular hero is a friendly viking whose peaceful living is disrupted when the evil god Loki is reincarnated. Not happy with Erik's refusal to join the pursuits of more violent vikings, Loki casts a spell on the lands turning the world into a terrible place. Erik's now has to overcome all the dangers so that he once again can live in peace.

The game consists of four worlds, each divided into seven levels. The last level of each world contains a guardian that has to be defeated for Erik to be able to move on to the next world. On his journey, Erik will come across many monsters and traps to overcome but cash in the form of jewels can also be found. Collected jewels can be used in shops to acquire extra weapons, shields and lives. In each world there are also two secret rooms where Erik can get extra lives and weapons that are not available in the shops.
Erinia

Get ready to relive the experience of old-school text adventure games on your favorite retro computer, with all the charm of the ‘80s and ‘90s, as you unravel the secrets hidden on the island of Project Erinia.
Escapade
A Breakout\Arkanoid clone by L. Donoghue that was released to PD in 1992.
Escape (Crossfield)

Escape is a graphical adventure. Your character, Basil, has been falsely accused and convicted of robbery. Your task is to help him escape from prison. Move your character around a prison. Talk to other prisoners and pick up items to help you escape.
Escape (Kryptic)

Escape is a PD/Freeware puzzle game where you have to operate floor-switches in order to open the doors and progress to the next level. Simple graphics and decent music. Gameplay is not that great since you have to be perfect navigating the corners or you might get stuck in a pixels while floor is collapsing below you.
Escape from Colditz

Loosely based around the Gibson Games board-game, you are in control of a team of 4 POWs – a Brit, a Frenchman, an American and a Pole) and must guide them all to what many attempted and few achieved – escape from the notorious Nazi POW camp. You control each of the 4 men separately, each of them starting within their own quarters on different floors of the camp, and can always switch between them. 

The gameplay has a similar feel to isometric-view Spectrum games, notably The Great Escape and Head Over Heels. Collecting and using objects is a significant part of your task – lock-picks for the low-security doors, keys for the more secure ones, German uniforms to allow you to move around freely, and shovels to dig for freedom. You must avoid entering forbidden areas – do this and you will be placed in solitary confinement and have your equipment confiscated – if you attempt to run from the guards in such areas they will shoot at you.
Escape from Hammy Town

Escape from Hammy Town is a point & click graphic adventure. As the game begins, the main character has just emerged unharmed from the wreckage of a car, after veering off the road and crashing into a tree on the outskirts of an unfamiliar town. Our hero has almost no money, the car isn't going anywhere, and so the only option is to head into town and find some alternative way to get back on the road...

The game interface splits the screen vertically: the current scene is shown from a third-person perspective, while underneath is an action panel that displays the inventory items you are carrying, along with nine action buttons ("Give", "Pick up", "Use", "Open", "Close", "Talk to", "Look at", "Push" and "Pull") for manipulating objects and interacting with characters.
Escape From Jovi

A fast action machine-code game (Escape From Jovi) featuring hi-res scrolling, large play field, disk based high score list, stereo sound, multiple levels, a cheat mode, realistic inertia and gravitational effects, an animated sprite, and more. Use a joystick in port 2 to control the ship. This is version III, an update to the version on disk 148. Includes source in assembly code. Shareware. Fish Disk #0259 amd Fish Disk #148, and Tag Disk #3.
Escape from Limbo

An overhead maze action game created by Greippi for the Finity Games group in 2022 and released at the Posadas Party 2022 Autumn, ranked 1 in the Game Competition. In the game you are stuck in Limbo. The only way out is to clear most of the freaks on the way. Collect and use blasts to explode walls. 12 levels of AI generated wisdom await!
Escape from Mos Eisley
Star Wars: Escape From Mos Eisley is a homebrew 2015 simple text adventure game created using AMOS.
Escape from Mount Doom

A shareware role playing game from John Scott. Mt. Doom, long dormant is about to erupt! IN a futile attempt to prevent this, the cave dwelling Trogs have kidnapped Princess Elena and intend to sacrifice her to the mountain gods. Your mission is clear - inexperienced as you are, you must enter the caves, set her free and Escape From MOUNT DOOM!! 
 
There were two versions of this game, a PD demo version with limited scope and the full shareware version.
Escape from Tharkan

A breakout-clone that tries to beef things up by adding stages in which the player must navigate a glider through a maze. Nothing spectacular but this low-budget title was programmed solidly enough to guarantee a modest level of entertainment.
Escape from the Panic Society

Hillery and her Liberal friends have taken total control of the world. You are one of some 10 million people left, scheduled for transferring to the country of your origin. But, someone has tampered with your environmental control causing you to awaken from a mind controlled state. Your objective, to learn all you can about Panic Society, escape from your prison, find master control, shut it down, and rebuild society. Panic Society uses the mouse and keyboard. A Multilevel graphic puzzle adventure by Ronald F. Picardi in 1995.
Escape from the Planet of the Robot Monsters

Based on the arcade game, in Escape from the Planet of the Robot Monsters you are sent in on a rescue mission to Planet X. This planet has been taken over by robots and you must find and evacuate the remaining humans.

It's a shooter similar to Gauntlet, only with an isometric viewpoint. You run around the levels shooting robots, rescuing humans and picking up items.
Escape Haunted Castle

A stranger offers you a deal, if you win you will receive $1.000.000 in cash, lose you die! Your task is to find map pieces, when you have enough they also form a password for exit door. You have 1 Hour .. Do you accept the bet ?
Escape II

Good quality puzzle game only has 16 where the prequel to this one had 50, the point of the game is simply to get from point A to point B to escape. The good thing with this version is that you can create the your own game with the included compiler and level editor.Escape II is an Amiga labyrinth/maze arcade game released in 1992 by The Assassins and could be had directly from the creator as well. The second disk contain all levels from Escape and lots of music modules for use with the compiler. The compiler program could be obtained by sending 5£ to the author as this was a shareware release.
Escape III

The third in a series of maze puzzle games games from Mark Page, Daniel Leyden and the Mad Phantom, collectively known as first Kryptic then as Cybernetix. While the first two entries of the game were freeware, this one was released as Shareware in 1992. 
 
Like the first two, the aim of the game here is simply to get from point A to point B. The problem is that you have to take the kind of circuitous route that involves visiting every other point from C to Z and well into Greek alphabet territory as well. Escape 2 is a futuristic puzzler featuring matter transporters, vanishing tiles, switches which operate sliding doors (usually on the other side of the screen) and tight time limits.
Escoba Simulator

A Spanish language, homebrew AMOS casino game. Escoba is a Spanish variant of the Italian fishing card game Scopa, which means "broom", a name that refers to the situation in the game where all of the cards from the board are "swept" in one turn. The game is usually played with a deck of traditional Spanish playing cards, called naipes.
Eskadra

Eskadra is an action side-scrolling flight shooter. The game begins with the conflict of three neighbors. The storm destroyed the border fence. The lack of agreement means the air war. The game offers for boards with fast flying action for up to three players, human or computer. The goal is simple - shoot down all enemies. The airplane ammo is unlimited. Some power ups may appear randomly on board.
Eskimo Games

Eskimo Games takes the winter sports multi-event format and emphasises the winter rather than the sports. Operation Snowball is similar to the arcade game Cabal insofar as it resembles Operation Wolf but adds a roll manoeuvre. You must fire snowballs at people who are trying to make a catapult, and destroy the shots they aim at you.

Eggsterminator places you at the top of a cliff, which has 5 ledges containing a bird’s nest. Birds will periodically land on these and lay eggs, which you must collect. Contact with the birds themselves causes you to fall and lose time. Ice N’Igloos involves using your axe to collect ice, and taking it to your incomplete igloo to complete it. Avoid the seals, as contact with these costs you time.

Miami Ice is a clone of Tapper, except that instead of beer you are serving ice cream to people. From one side of the screen you must ensure that each line has enough ice creams sent down it to match the number of people coming.
Esnake
Classic snake game with highscore list created by Erik Johannessen in 1994. Runs from the workbench with square aspect ratio. Was released on AmigaByte 51/1994 as a coverdisk.
ESP

An AMOS based shareware game by Paul Taylor, that is basically an Ashido puzzle clone. It is a puzzle solving game, where the player must place stones with symbols in an appropriate manner on the board. Laying stones correspond to the appropriate rules. The full registered shareware version comes with un-compiled AMOS BASIC source code, a high score table, one limit screen limit extended to four minutes, background soundtrack and many more levels. The section on the right of the screen tells you what is coming up next
España: The Games '92
Espionage: The Computer Game

Espionage is based on the board game of the same name. Up to four players (either human or computer-controlled) compete to become Master Spy by returning all the micro film canisters back to their base. A player has 12 agents in their team including secret agents, surveillance agents and courier agents. Each type of agent moves around the board in a different way, not unlike in chess. Besides getting the micro film, another objective is to terminate any enemy agents. This is done as in draughts, by jumping over the agent into a free space. Killing enemy agents nets points, which, combined with points for recovered film canisters and surviving agents are tallied for the final score.

The board is viewed from above. It does not fit the screen all at once, so scrolling is necessary. The game offers a hint function (indicating what the computer thinks is the best move to take) as well as the option to show the last move made.
ESWAT

Crime is getting out of control in Liberty City, and to combat the problem, the LCPD establishes a new unit, called ESWAT (Enhanced Special Weapons and Tactics). Police officers who are promoted to this unit wear a cyber-suit that contains state-of-the-art military equipment including two Turbo-Booster Thrusters, extra ammunition, and increased protection. In order to become an ESWAT member, all a dedicated police officer has to do is arrest enough criminal masterminds to progress through the ranks, which include Captain, Assistant Chief, and Chief.

ESWAT: Cyber Police is a horizontal-scrolling beat 'em up where you have to make your way from left to right and defeat a mastermind. There are 15 stages to complete, and have you patrolling through Liberty streets, car yards, stadiums, restaurants, the CBD, construction sites, and boat docks. While you're out on patrol, you can pick up ammunition, and the amount you get varies.
ESWAT: Cyber Police (Sunteam)

An Amiga port of the popular arcade game by Sunteam in the style of GameGear ESWAT. Just as in the original ...crime is getting out of control in Liberty City, and to combat the problem, the LCPD establishes a new unit, called ESWAT (Enhanced Special Weapons and Tactics). Police officers who are promoted to this unit wear a cyber-suit that contains state-of-the-art military equipment including two Turbo-Booster Thrusters, extra ammunition, and increased protection. In order to become an ESWAT member, all a dedicated police officer has to do is arrest enough criminal masterminds to progress through the ranks, which include Captain, Assistant Chief, and Chief.
ET's Rugby League
E.T.'s Rugby League is an Amiga rugby sports game released in 1992 by Ozisoft.
eTeacher Angielski

ETEACHER from Bilang Software & Nahlik Soft, as the name suggests, is intended to act as an English teacher. The program has a very user-friendly installer, correct interface, efficient Help system, ability to choose from several different (very good) music. It features dictionary connections, sentence completion, transformation of sentences with beginnings, transformation of sentences with words, formulating questions and translating sentences. 

There are three options for working with Eteacher: learning (we can make mistakes with impunity), test (our achievements will be assessed by the program) and editing (we can create our own intelligent device mounted by default in the Devs directory). The remaining types of tasks accept up to six correct answers. In the manual, we read that the program has very strict requirements regarding answers.
Eternal Rome

History strategy shareware game that is fast, complex and easy to play. Mouse controlled with a zoomable map of the Roman empire. Had two additional data disks of scenarios to explore, also shareware.
Ethos: The Game Of Greek Mythology
A shareware featuring the gods and legends of Greek mythology created in Blitz Basic by William Jordan in 1993.
Etrain
For model train enthusiasts, Etrain is heaven. It's a model train—or rather, a digital train construction set. Published by DevWare in January 1990 in North America.
Euchre!

A homebrew, freeware Euchre card game created in C by Rick Keller and the last version (1.2) was released in 1998. Euchre is a trick-taking card game where players try to win at least three tricks. The goal is to be the first team to reach 10 points.
Euphorion

The ship is broken and so are you! Shoot the enemy in this vertically scrolling space shooter by Carsten Magerkurt, released in 1992. A public domain scrolling "shoot'em up" action-game, which contains eight different levels, bonus-stages and a high score table. It as released on Fish Disk #0804.
Eureka Maths 4ème/3ème

With the EUREKA collection, you will discover the marvelous worlds of knowledge! EUREKA software is a new generation of software based on the most advanced research in computer science and educational sciences. From a captivating scenario, they develop a pedagogy active and lively based on reflection and personal work. An interactive and user-friendly range:
- incorporating high-performance tools (calculator, word processor, logbook, electronic calendar, etc.) - aids adapted to each question asked, documentation sheets (Album of Worlds) very easy to use: everyone has their own windows of work and his tools as he sees fit. 

. A personalized follow-up:
permanently displayable success rate, personalized graphic reports - the software adapts to the level of the user, allows him to progress more quickly in the event of success or offers him
reinforcement tests in case of difficulties.
• Each software includes thousands of questions, very varied exercises, games.
Eureka Maths 6ème/5ème

With the EUREKA collection, discover the wonderful worlds of knowledge! EUREKA software is a new generation of software based on the most advanced research in computer science and educational sciences. From a captivating scenario, they develop a pedagogy
active and lively based on reflection and personal work.

An interactive and user-friendly range:
- incorporating high-performance tools (calculator, word processing, logbook, electronic calendar, etc.) - aids adapted to each question asked, documentation sheets (Album of Worlds) - very easy to use: everyone has their work windows and its tools as it sees fit.
- A personalized follow-up:
permanently displayable success rate, personalized graphic assessments the software adapts to the level of the user, allows him to progress more quickly in the event of success or offers him
reinforcement tests in case of difficulties.
- Each software includes thousands of questions, very varied exercises, games.
Euro League Manager

Euro league Manager includes 4 divisions of eighteen teams, 2 domestic cup competitions & European competitions. Promotion & relegation are based upon four up & four down. Game starts in one of 3 difficulty modes. You must manage your team to the top of the heap and win big!
Euro Round-Up: Czech Republic

A football manager game which was due out for the Commodore Amiga 1200 in 2000/2001. The game was being created by the Barczyński brothers, and was written in AMOS. Euro Round-Up: Czech Republic was the first of several management games planned by Frey United Software, which would simulate European football – all games would utilize the same interface and style. This particular development would focus on Czech Republic and its teams.

The creators were heavily inspired by the original Championship Manager, with each release concentrating on a single country, and trying to simulate the internal structures of their football leagues.

Apart from Czech leagues in this particular title, there would be a snapshot of other domestic leagues from around Europe – where you could take part in international competitions, have options to improve the stadium, send scouts abroad and buy players directly from those clubs.
Euro Soccer

The game represents the most powerful European teams of 1992 season. England, Germany, Scotland, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, France, and Sweden propose the best teams of their premier divisions such as Bayern München, Manchester United, Celtic, Ajax, AC Milan, Real Madrid, FC Barcelona, Monaco, IFK Göteborg, etc. for player's choice.

Gameplay flows in side view, where soccer players are controlled either by human or CPU. There are two modes of playing. The first one is "Friendly match" for 2 players (playable only if a joystick is installed along with keyboard). The second one is "Euro Cup tournament" for 1 player. Different options such as match length (2/4/6/8 minutes), weather conditions (wet/dry), formation of the teams (4-4-2/4-3-3/4-2-4), and national anthems (on/off) may be adjusted.

Simulation of the players` team actions lies in the following. When the ball is near the player of your team, this player is selected as active and becomes controllable.
Eurofighter
Eurofighter is a horizontal scrolling shoot 'em up for the Commodore Amiga. It was developed by S2N and released in 2017.
Europa 2.1

A Polish language multi-game Geography edutainment program for one player created by Janusz Łukasik and Barbara Łukasik as part of the Produkcja developers and published by Atares in 1994. The 2.0 version had come out earlier in the year and Europa 3.0 would be out in 1994. At the time it contained educational materials on all European countries with eye-catching graphics, maps and games to help you learn and remember!
Europaspiel
What do you know about Europe? Begin your journey on the way to Europe, a journey of learning awaits you. Europaspiel is a German language educational game for one player created in 1991.
European Champions (Idea)

Depending on which version you have, either the Italian Serie A sides or the leading European international teams are featured.

The game is played using a top down view. You can choose if each match should be three, six or nine minutes. When starting the game you can choose from playing a single match or a full season. When choosing single match you have to choose the two teams you want to play and whether they should be controlled by player or computer. When done with that you have some tactical options such as mentality and marking an what players that should play.
European Champions (Ocean)

This football game aims for a higher level of realism than most of its contemporaries. The game can be viewed top-down (similar to the Kick Off games) or side-on (similar to Manchester United Europe). Three different passing modes are offered, with the aim of providing precise one-touch passing or the ability for long-range direct through-balls. The match options include 10 skill levels, variable wind, five different pitch conditions, and variable match lengths. You can play league and cup tournaments featuring up to 32 of the game’s teams, which are taken from the top clubs in top European countries.
European Championship 1992

Conversion of Tecmo's arcade soccer game World Cup 1990, though the computer version has been licensed to the European Championship of 1992. It's a standard isometric view arcade style soccer game - easy, simple, as mediocre as a soccer game can get. You can choose from 25 European teams represented in that tournament, although there's hardly a difference between playing, for example, Greece and Italy. If you like the arcade game, you might find this one a bit nostalgic-- although not necessary fun at all. There are simply far too many better action-oriented soccer games to occupy your time with.
European Football Champ

European Football Champ was released to coincide with the 1992 European Championships. The game scrolls horizontally at a slight angle, and recreates the coin-op's close-up zoom effect after a player scores. Only a small area of the pitch is on screen at a time, but there is a scanner to show the whole pitch.

Although the game has a referee, he often loses attention, and these moments give you a chance to foul, punch or side-swipe opposition players. One and two player options are included.
European Player Manager

European Player Manager, a new and improved version of 5th Dimension Licenceware's British Manager. While it could scarcely be described as being at the cutting edge of computer football game development, being more on a par with the original 8-bit Football Manager than the likes of Championship Manager , it's nevertheless quite good tun. You pick one of forty European teams, choose your kit and then it's on into die football season.

You pick your first team from the squad of eighteen players who are at your disposal and send them into battle in three competitions - the league, a European knockout cup and the UEFA cup. The two cup competitions have curiously reverted to one-legged affairs, and the European Superleague actually consists of four divisions of ten teams hut, as you’ll realize very quickly, realism isn't what European Player Manager is all about.
European Soccer Challenge

European Soccer Challenge is a Sports game, developed by Smash 16 and published by Software Sorcery, which was released in 1990.

European Soccer Challenge allows you to play as one of fourteen European football teams (including the mighty Wrexham) against another player or the computer. Options include the number of players, your skill level and the team you want to play as.

The match is viewed from above showing a small part of the pitch. The joystick controls the nearest player to the ball and the fire button allows you to shoot or pass. The keyboard is used to select your options on the menu screens.

The game is actually pretty bad and should be avoided.
European Superleague

European Superleague is a managerial soccer simulation which is about an fictional European league featuring eight of the most successful teams (PSV Eindhoven, Glasgow Rangers, Liverpool, Arsenal, Real Madrid, Olympique de Marseilles, AC Milan and Bayern Munich). The player takes control over one of those clubs and is responsible for its athletic and financial success. The player has all the usual options available, including tactics, lineup, transfer market or training. A speciality is the weekly board meeting in which the chairman gives his opinion on the team's current stand. Each team has 20 athletes with abilities which influence their performance during the match (no graphical representation). The game is completely menu-based and the sub-menus are reached through the main menu which has a different graphical or text presentation depending on the used platform.
EuroTrotter

Created by (King) Knut Olav Loite using AMOS and the Amiga E program. It was released as shareware and as part of the CU Amiga Magazine Super CD-ROM 8. Learn as you travel around Europe. Gather info on the places and the people you can see.
Evasive Aksion

A puzzle-platform shareware game by C. Dire, released in 1994. Collect the gems and avoid the robots. We find our hero, Yao, trapped in a dream in which he finds himself traveling through a crazy world, which includes futuristic settings inhabited by droids, to ancient settings occupied by mummies (who are surprisingly swift and flexible in their movements). 

At first, Yao is pleasantly surprised to find that there are enormous diamonds just waiting to be collected. Unfortunately, Yao's dream is not as straight-forward as it first appears... The inhabitants of this world are actually there to protect the diamonds and give out harsh punishments (namely death) to those caught trying to steal them. Rather than risking his welfare, Yao could forget about the diamonds (and his greed) - but in the strange way that dreams are, he realizes that collecting the diamonds is his only means of escape from this crazy world...
Evil
A turn-based fantasy strategy game from Kimmo Kasila released on the Amiga in 1998.
Evil Dawn
Evil Dawn is a very simple sideways beat 'em up game. Evil Dawn does not offer anything new and if you're after a beat 'em up leave this one lying on the shelf.
Evil Garden

Evil Garden is a Centipede variant. As with the original, the principle is that a centipede roams around the playing field and the player, stationed at the bottom row, tries to shoot it. Every time a part of the centipede is hit, it disappears. If two different parts are left, i.e. a part which is not the front or back is hit, they continue to move on their own. There are multiple obstacles, e.g. mushrooms which bounce back shots or lice which drop stones on the player, which try to hinder progress. On the other hand helpful power ups can be collected which have useful effects, e.g. an extra life, a better weapon or a shield. There are 32 levels, the goal is achieving a high score and the background story is about a mercenary who takes part in a competition for money and fame.
Evil Insects

An indirect fire rethinking of the Space Invaders formula. In this your pistol-packing protagonist squares of against a small, but ever increasing amount of formation-flying bugs. Shooting the roof over the bugs causes chips to fall down that will kill the bugs, you can also hit them directly, but it is a tough shot as your bullet is much smaller than the roof chips that fall. The evil insectoids will also be dropping who knows what deadly shots at you, avoid those and stop the Evil Insects!
Evil Tower
A German language adventure game from Culture and released to PC in 1991.
Evil's Doom

A classic dungeon crawler made by Croatian developers Olympia Entertainment Group that was never officially released. According to some sites it was due to bugs however Evil's Doom became a victim of software piracy, after the beta version was sent to magazines, the first cracks appeared and the developers cancelled the game and left the Amiga.
Evolution Cryser

Evolution Cryser is a side-scrollong shooter with very simple game play where player controls a space ship, flies straightforward and shoot nasties. The enemies are in many shapes, colours and types. After all five ships are destroyed, game is over.
Excalibur

Excalibur is a Shoot 'Em Up game, developed by Next Generation and published by Kingsoft, which was released in Europe in 1988.

The game hasn't real story and has quite a simple game play - the player controls a red space ship, flies straightforward, avoid obstacles and shoot enemies in various locations (mostly mountains with space background). The enemies are in many types, shapes and colours - spaceships, 'molecules', geometric figures, etc. If a spaceship flies too slowly, then it has a tendency to fall down. The player has 2 lives.
Excavation

An AMOS based shareware strategy game by Joona Palaste of JIP Soft in October 29th of 1995. An arcade strategy game set in the underworld. In this game, the player is in charge of an Excavation Company and it's four excavators. The excavators work in a deep mine on the planet of Mineralia, digging up the jewels so that the company can sell them. Search for the gems and excavate deeper and deeper for success!
Excellent Card Games

Five card games are brought to life in this title – Baroness (AKA Five Piles), Frustration, Yukon, Stonewall and Black Maria. The basic game mechanics offer straightforward visuals, a range of card sets, saveable statistics, and click-to-drop or drag-and-drop control options.

Black Maria is a three-player game, which is similar to Hearts but with the opposite objective – i.e. you must hold the hearts and queens. The others are all solitaire, with Baroness and Frustration being largely luck based and involving matching cards up so they add to 13 in Baroness (aces low; kings go automatically) or 10 in Frustration (face cards pair with cards from the same rank).

Stonewall and Yukon both involve getting the cards to the foundations, which are built up in suit, and moving cards on the main play area (the ‘tableau’) by playing, for example, a red nine on a black 8.
Excellent Card Games II
The sequel to Excellent Card Games and it would be followed by Excellent Card Games III. Collection of 5 solitaire games: Quads; Rapide; Sir Tommy; Betrothal; and Cribbage.
Excellent Card Games III
The third game in the trilogy of Excellent Card Games titles.This one contains Poker, Czarina, Colours, Scottish and Napoleon solitaire games.
Exile

When a terraforming team on an unexplored planet sends some disturbing messages back to Earth and then stops responding altogether, a space-adventurer is sent to find out what happened.

The gameplay is a side-on 8-dimensionally scrolling action-adventure set on a planet. The player must find a way to the lower depths of the planet to rescue the terraforming team and defeat the evil Triax!
Exit-13
A shareware game by Ian Quigley and Simon Leigh, released as Shareware in 1993. This single screen shape matching puzzle game has over 80 levles of play.
Exitor
An unfinished shooter created by Christian Weber and Roman Werner using ASM 68k in 1987 as an alpha tester\demo version.
Exodus 3010: The First Chapter

They all ignored the endless warnings. Now Earth is dying and it is your task to find a new and flourishing planet.

Exodus provides us with an excellent blend of role playing strategy and 3D space combat. It's also fairly easy to get into and you will soon be building impulse systems and the like with the best of them. Although the combat system may be fairly simple, don't be misled as it serves its purpose well, and in combination with the other many fine aspects, they add up to one first class game.
Exodus: The Last War

The Zelds and the Moroi are at war, and only one can survive. Whichever side you take on, you have 20 different missions to win.

Basic gameplay involves building facilities to produce the units required to conquer your opposition. These include tanks, planes and various infantry units with different strengths and weaknesses - most are available to both sides. The more advanced units can only be produced by building factories and research facilities. All of this cost money, which is obtained through mining.

There is variety and the game's missions, as some involve attempting to survive in a tough position, others involve escorting a convoy, and there are levels conducted entirely at sea.
Exodus: Ultima III

After the defeat of the evil wizard Mondain and his mistress Minax in the previous two Ultimas, peace has returned to the land of Sorsaria. Times passes and eventually geological disruptions and a resurgence of the monster populace occur, and it is soon learned that Mondain and Minax had conceived a child named Exodus before their death. Now that child has become an adult with the power to avenge the death of his parents. Obviously, it falls upon the hero from Earth to find and stop him.

The third title in the Ultima series was the first to feature a party of adventurers instead of a single player character. The party is created at the beginning of the game by assigning various class combinations and determining the characters' attributes. The game has larger and more detailed towns, populated by NPCs the protagonist can converse with to obtain clues. Like in earlier Ultima games, exploration is divided between top-down overworld locations and first-person 3D dungeons.
Exolon

This action game combines shoot 'em up and platform elements, as you control a flying man who can gain an exoskeletal suit for extra protection (hence the name). Your task is to progress from left to right in each level, either along the ground or by using the arrangement of platforms. Most of the baddies can be avoided rather than shot, and this is often easier, especially as you can duck or jump to avoid them. As well as a standard gun (activated by tapping fire) you also have a limited number of missiles to take out installations (activated by holding down fire, which makes autofire facilities useless). The scrolling is flick-screen, perhaps as the game was designed for the C64, and the Amiga version was identical to the ST's.
Exorcism
A freeware text adventure with optional graphics not compatible with the AGA chipset by David Lacey and Adam Balcomb. Written with the CAG adventure generator.
Expansion

Freeware game originally entitled Expanshell before release, from Ramtronics software. This is a resource strategy and exploration game where you gather resources such as wood, explore and identify different land types that can be used and find villiages that can be built up into cities. Built in access to protracker for music while playing. Kickstart 3.7 required. Messages can come in that may impact your growth! Version 1.0 released on January 1, 1998.
Expello

An AMOS based shareware board game created and published by Andrew Kreibich in June of 1993. It is a clone of Othello where you can set the board size from between 5x5 to 12x12 and if you turn on the explosion facility then things blow up, which is always really good.
Experts Only Mercenary Simulator

Experts Only is a 1987 freeware crosshairs shooter game by Daniel Cardenas. It was released as PD on Fish Disk 78 and feels the answer to the question of what arcade Battlezone would have been like as a crosshairs military shooter. A neat (and tough!) PD game that was originally developed for eventual commercial release but for various reasons the author decided to release as PD instead.
Explora III: Sous le signe du serpent

Explora 3 is a french point-and-click adventure game, the final sequel of the original Explora (released as Chrono Quest in English-speaking markets). The time traveling antics of the other games continue on this title, albeit in a more tangential way. You play as a writer with a severe lack of ideas that has a 3 month deadline to deliver a manuscript to his publisher. While watching TV you see your name linked to a report about a mysterious murder. It is your job to unravel this conspiracy.

The interface of the game has a more minimalist approach this time, the icons were reduced to only three revolving on the bottom-right of the screen: a magnifying glass to examine the scenario, a hand to pick and drop things, and a hammer as the "use" verb. Above these icons there is a clock: the developers added a dimension of time to the proceedings, and certain actions can only be performed at an exact time point. This installment also ditches the synthesized speech of the second game.
Explorer

Explorer is a timed puzzle board game. The player takes the role of a gold digger, named John Smith. His goal is to collect all the gold pieces on the board before the time runs out. To do so the player must appropriately push the crates blocking the road, use teleporters and generators of matter forming bridges over the abyss. Some of the fields are mined or marked as non-stopping area (requires two blocking crates next to it to remove the effect). The remaining time after the completion of the board is rewarded with additional points. The game features 60 levels all together. After each completed board the player receives a password.
Explosive Chaos

A one or two player bombing game, featuring great graphics, cool levels and some thumping music (with additional download). Mr. Manix, the psychotic scientist has been experimenting on innocent people, turning them into monsters to be controlled by his computers. Naturally you (Billy) and your twin brother (Joel) are the only ones who have the nerve and the bombs to save the day! 
 
Almost every level contains a number of computer consoles that most be destroyed to get to the next area. If you destroy all the computers the remaining monsters will break down into wiggly blobs (your mother is a wiggly blob).
Extase

The screen display in Extase depicts a symmetrical network of wires, some buttons, some fuses, some switches, and a picture of a female android in the middle. The overall aim is to restore sensory functions to the android, one in each level. All of this is done against an opponent, either human or computer, who controls the opposite half of the board.

This is done by guiding electrical pulses through each of the wires, however this can only be done once the wires have been woken up. You are in control of a cursor, which can click on the activation buttons to release a ball, which you direct using the cursor to reactivate wires on its path. Switches must be set to make all parts of this available – this can only be done when no ball is active.

Electrical sparks move around to make life harder, by destroying balls and fuses. Fortunately these can be 'zapped' using the cursor.
Extasy

Extasy is our virtual drug. If you follow Lucky Ball in this adventure, you will find yourself immersed in fascinating and colorful worlds. Perhaps you'll feel your mind expand and conquer unknown horizons. It is fun to play but almost impossible to stop!
Extensor

If you had a fresh planet to colonise, probably the last name you'd think of (barring a few other unacceptable options) would be Spazm. Pity the Spazmoids didn't think like that…

Having saddled themselves with such a depressing name, the Spazmoids need something to cheer them up - so (wait for it)… they flock to the lazercycle arena. Obviously really. In glorious 3D, you try to get your computer-controlled opponents to crash into the energy trails emitted by their vehicles or the arena walls.

If you win, you're a hero, if not, you're dead. Isn't sport great?
Exterminate
A vertically scrolling space shooter developed by Klaus Helmkem using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit, and released into the public domain in 1990.
Exterminator

Of all the mundane tasks which've been turned into action-packed games, bug-repelling must be up there with being a Paper Boy or a Trashman. These aren't average bugs; Chicago is under siege from mutated insects, rats and even toy tanks.

You'll have to work through seven houses, each of which has the typical rooms. You control a seemingly-dismembered hand, which must deal with the hordes as they come towards it, into the screen. They can be shot, thumped, or squashed depending on their type. To clear a room you must kill a certain number of creatures in each of the vertically-divided 'lanes' of the room - this causes squares on the ground to change colour.
Extrema
A vertically scrolling shoot 'em up game for one or two players including cooperative play.
Extreme Pong
A 1-player Pong clone with some fancy background graphics. Developed by Am Development and released in 1996.
Extreme Violence

Extreme Violence is a Shareware Duel Action game, developed and published by Simon Green, which was released in Europe in 1992. Game is now a Freeware.

This is one of of those games that sneak up on you. Terrible graphics and no music, still tremendous fun in this epic two-player combat game written in AMOS.
Extreme Violence 2

It's an unofficial sequel to the Amiga Public Domain game Extreme Violence created by Simon Green in 1991.
AmiGameJam 2024
Extrial

In Extrial your mission is to collect the soldiers that are running around on the platforms by reaching them and crouching down so they can hop into your robotic machine whilst avoiding / shooting the baddies.
There are 3 levels to get through, each with it's own boss which obviously you must defeat to be able to progress to the next level. Incredibly hard game but pretty cool too.
Exxon
Exxon is a Puzzle game, developed by Braindeath and published by Maxon, which was released in Europe in 1991.
Eye

Eye is closely based on the board game with the same name. The game is played with two to four players on a board with differently coloured squares. Each player has playing stones of one colour and the goal to get a certain amount of the own stones on the corresponding fields. The spin on this concept is that the board is placed on two rotatable spirals which change the square distribution on the field when used. During each turn, a player has a different amount of moves available (changes depending on the current match situation); each move consisting of moving a square or turning a spiral. This computer version also allows some rule modifications in comparison to the original game and all opponents can be replaced by the AI.
Eye of Horus

As a mystical shaman, go through a pyramid in ancient Egypt to get the magical eye of horus. In a cool twist, by pressing the up arrow you turn into a birdy and can search through the levels. Just press the down arrow and voila! Human again. Many traps try to trick you.
Eye of the Beholder

Something evil is lurking below the city of Waterdeep. The Lords of Waterdeep summon a group of heroes to investigate, but someone or something has been watching the proceedings. After the heroes enter the sewers, the ceiling collapses behind them. The only way out is the way down, into a dungeon filled with monsters, traps and puzzles.

Eye of the Beholder is a dungeon crawler RPG with a first-person perspective based on the 2nd Edition AD&D rules. The starting party consists of four characters and up to two NPCs can join later. Combat and magic happen in real time, similarly to Dungeon Master. There is a variety of monsters to fight and spells to cast. The game features a point-and-click interface for fighting, spellcasting and handling objects.
Eye of the Beholder II: The Legend of Darkmoon

The Archmage Khelben summons the Heroes of Waterdeep, slayers of the Beholder Xanathar, for another mission. Strange things are happening in the forests near Waterdeep, centered around the Temple Darkmoon. People have been disappearing and shallow graves containing human remains have been found. Khelben teleports the party to the forests near Darkmoon so they may find out what kind of evil is working in the towers of the temple.

Eye of the Beholder II: The Legend of Darkmoon is, like its predecessor, a first-person dungeon-crawling role-playing game based on the second edition of AD&D rules. It uses the same point-and-click gameplay mechanics and controls as the first game, with only minor changes. The game is set entirely in pseudo-3D maze-like areas; no automapping is available. Combat flows in real time, and characters can move as a single unit to lure enemies or avoid blows.
Eye of the Dragon

Eye of the Dragon is a nice little Mahjong game. The game offers a no-frills, no-nonsense Mahjong experience.
