A Mastermind clone aka Fluster Mine created by Russell Stapleton using BlitzBASIC and had several freeware releases, with 2.0 arriving in 1997.
Fly Harder

Your homeland's precious limited energy is being taken advantage of by the evil Thargoid Empire, and you and your spaceship must do something about it. There are 8 bases to enter, with the aim of using energy pods to cause the reactors to overload and thus malfunction.
Flyers

Another great party game from Czech provenience. Huge dogfight fun for four. A game based on The Dogfight Simulator game. It was created by Michal Franc, the graphics were provided by Michal Vrzáček and Jan Šulček. There is a humorous but short intro to the game. Up to four players can play. You can also use three different scenes, such as day, night and aurora borealis.
Flyin' High

Without any substantial background story or colourful characters to back it up, Flyin' High is all about racing.

One of the few fully 3D racing games on the Amiga, you must race your car on 20 tracks divided into four worlds; city, forest, jungle and arctic. Spread out on the tracks are not only obstacles, but also money which must be picked up so that you may mend or upgrade your car between the races. If the computer drivers are not interesting enough for you, you and three of your friends may race simultaneously in split-screen mode. Apart from tyre and engine upgrades, you also have a limited weapons arsenal to slow down the competition.
Flying Eagles

The game combines elements of Galaxian and Phoenix. It was programmed by Dirk Conrad in 100% 68k assembler. The music was composed by his buddy Carsten Schacht. We had three tracks for the music and one track for sound effects. The whole game fit on a 880 KB floppy disk. Blast the aliens, use your shields if they get too close. Avoid the falling asteroids and shrapnel that comes from some types of enemies.
Flying Shark

Flying Shark is a top-down shooter similar to Raiden. You start off with four lives and three bombs. With that (you can get more lives at certain point intervals, and more bombs can be found), you, the "Sky Shark" of your squadron, blast through five levels of enemy-infested battlefields with as many as six gun upgrades (Aside from the bombs and the gun upgrade, there are no other weapons to be found at all). Includes three difficulty levels and two-player support.
Flying Shark Remake

Flying Shark Remake is not a completely new game for the Amiga, what we have here is a polished 2022 version of the vertically scrolling shoot'em up, which is based on the original, released in 1988. You fly a biplane and shoot everything out of the sky that turns out to be hostile. And these are super tanks, gun emplacements and other things.
Fnurr 2000

Game created by Richard DawnBringer Fhager is simple yet incredibly playable. You control a single pixel being chased by 25 other pixels. If two or more pixels collide they explode. If any of the enemy pixels get caught in an explosion they also explode. If you hit any enemy or explosions you die! You score n^3 points for the pixels that collide at the SAME time!You also get 1 point/sec for staying alive. The longer a single enemy pixel is alive, the faster it gets. Luckily you get a little bit of a head start. New pixels will respawn after a bit.
Follix

Follix is a puzzle game heavily inspired by Atomix, a game from 1990 where the player had to build chemical molecules by connecting correctly the atoms they were made of. Using similar mechanics, in each of its 30 levels, Follix challenges the player to build a piece of a message by sliding in the correct places the tiles that contain the relevant text characters.
Follow That Tune

In Follow That Tune, a person jumps between five colored platforms. You have to memorize the sequence and repeat the pattern by clicking on the platforms in the right order, similar to any Simon Says... Game. Use Mouse to aim cursor at the appropriate mushroom, Left click for decision. Released as part of the Easy and Fun: Four in One compilation in 1988. Follow That Tune was created by Brian Moats of Polyglot Software.
Football

A freeware, AMOS based Footie\football game focused on statistics and management from Stephen Binder and likely released in 1992. Billed as a, "Footie program featuring no gameplay, no action, no excitement and hardly any graphics or sound." The game indicates it is all about Leagues, cups and stuff.
Football Boss
Football Boss is a sports and sports management game, developed and published by Cult, which was released in Europe in 1989.
Football Business
A German language freeware soccer\football management simulation created by Dirk Schaper in 1996 with updates continuing until 1998, the final known version was v1.9.
Football Champ

Remember I Play 3D Soccer? Well, in their almost obsessive quest to make the ultimate 3D soccer game, Simulmondo have gone a step further. Now, instead of just viewing the pitch from one angle, you rotate the whole world around your player.

The effect is impressive as vectors and sprites are scaled and stretched to create a convincing pitch environment. Unfortunately, the game is practically unplayable: it's almost impossible to keep track of what's going on and you can't instantly swap control from one player to another. This leads to an overwhelming feeling of disorientation. There's a comprehensive tactical and team management aspect to the game, but when it plays as badly as this, who cares?
Football Club Manager
Football Club Manager is a sports and sports management game, developed and published by D & H Games, which was released in Europe in 1992.
Football Crazy
A footie sports and sports management game by Simon Rush for ESP and created for your amusement in 1991.
Football Director II

Football Director II is the successor of Football Director, slightly extending the gameplay of the predecessor. Still, you are managing a football team in England, but you can start now with a top division team. For more challenge, you can also start with a small team in league 4 and fight your way to the international competitions.

Managing a club starts with the staff, you can hire and sack coaches, physios and scouts. You can trade players, if there are any good offers on the market. Building stands helps to increase funds, as well as negotiating contracts to save some money. You get some statistics of your performance, can build up a youth team, set extra training if the team is not performing too well.

The games themselves are not playable, you just see information about goals and cards and can get some more information after the game to make your conclusions what to change.
Football Glory

Football Glory is a Sports game, developed by Croteam and published by Black Legend, which was released in Europe in 1994.

From Croatia came this overhead view football game resembling Sensible Soccer. The standard selection of competitions are on offer, with a full range of club and national competitions.

Far more moves are possible in this one though, including overhead kicks, backheelers, riding tackles and even some impressive overhead kicks, all of which need practice to be perfected. Passing works in a similar way to Sensible, but requiring a longer tap, and giving more versatility in where the pass is placed. Extra details such as an on-screen referee and a zoom feature on replays are included. Kits can be edited in more detail than most games of the time as well.
Football League Editor

An editor for Football League games to allow you to update stats or fix issues, make your dream teams and play them together to find out who really would be best. Play Pelé, Diego Maradona, and Lionel Messi against Cristiano Ronaldo, Johan Cruyff, and Franz Beckenbauer for a dream team game. The options are endless.
Football Manager

Football Manager is the first game in the Football Manager series.

The player chooses a team and then must try to earn promotion from the fourth to the first division. The player also competes in the FA Cup. While the team and player names are real, they are not accurately represented so whichever team is selected, the player always starts in the fourth division and their team is randomly populated with players.

As the match is played, the screen is updated if a goal is scored. For versions with animated graphics highlights like the Amiga, attempts on goal are shown in isometric 3D at either end of the pitch with a scoreboard showing the current score. The player can not affect the game while it is in progress.
Football Manager 2

Football Manager from Addictive was the first game of its kind, and this sequel followed several years later, absorbing ideas from the many similar games released in between. Teams can now choose formations, and assign man-to-man marking. Players have individual skills and fitness ratings, in a more realistic way, with half-time substitutions and tactical changes supported. The whole 92-club league is incorporated, as is the League Cup alongside the FA Cup. It is now possible to watch and assess the individual performance of the players, with match graphics differentiating the attack / midfield / defense areas more clearly. Training allows passing length and height to be specified.
Football Manager: World Cup Edition 1990

Football Manager: World Cup Edition 1990 is the third game in the popular Football Manager series. This time your mission is not to coach an club team, but one of the national teams that started in the real World Cup 1990 qualifications. Master the qualification games to reach the final tournament and try to get the World Cup. You can fill up your team with 22 players, and can give each of them individual tactical game instructions. Before each game you give an interview that has influence of the morals of your players. In every half-time you can give new instructions to your team and make tactical corrections.
Football Masters

Football Masters is a football management simulation from ESP Software. The game allows the player to control a team from the four English divisions. Very easy to pick up and play with no fancy graphics, just a simple clock counting up and goal, cards and injuries highlighted. There were two versions of this game, one supporting 512K systems and one supporting 1MB Systems.
Football Simulation
Football Simulation is a football\soccer game, developed and published by SPORTsoft, which was released in Europe in 1990.
Football Statistician Professional

A Sport - Football (Soccer) themed predictor program intended to predict game and league results using current statistics, which at the time were for the 93/94 Premier League. Football Statistician Professional is a Sports game, developed by Craig Smith and published by Amivision, which was released in Europe in 1993.
Football Tactician

A Sport - Football (Soccer) management game by the Talking Birds development team: Camy Maertens, Tony Godfree, The Untouchables, Damon Barwin and Roger Stones in 1992. A popular sequel would be released the following year, followed by four more updates in the coming years. It featured flash updates on injuries and sicks lists, trade and other information including sponsorships and other updates that will impact teams in the league and your career!
Football Tactician 2

Football Tactician 2 is a Sports management game, developed and published by Talking Birds, which was released in Europe in 1993, where up to 22 people could compete. FOOTBALL TACTICIAN 2 NEW enhanced version sets even higher standards and breaks more records. 

Firmly established as the definitive interactive football strategy game. FOOTBALL TACTICIAN 2 is now available in three superb versions, the primary one being FT2 ENGLAND the original and the first ever management game where tactics and real-time match intervention are the main requirements for a successful campaign. One soon realizes that FT2 is no ordinary soccer manager THIS is the REAL THING. You're in charge. Events on the field are the direct result of your inputs. 
 
Even when trailing badly, a match can still be retrieved and won if you make shrewd tactical interventions. There are risks involved, uncertainty and even luck. But in the end.
Footballer of the Year 2

Fed up with football (soccer) management games, with all the match strategies, financial turmoil and prima donna players? This game offers a unique twist, leaving you ‘managing’ the career of a single player, involving matches and transfers.

You start with 10 ‘goal cards’ - up to 3 can be played in each match, each of them giving you a shooting chance, at which point arcade action skill comes in. The action sequences involve studying a move plan on the chalkboard, then getting into the right position to execute the final shot. Fail to score enough goals and you may lose your place in the team; do especially well and you may gain a transfer up the league. The better you perform, the higher your wages are, the more chance you have of a big-money transfer and international call-up, and the less chance you have of being dropped from the team.
FootMan

What you get from TopDown is a hog standard Pacman clone with very few frills. You use joystick or cursor keys and troll off round a whole bunch of mazes - you get 50 on the disc - while being pursued by some arthritic ghosties. Yup, there are dots, power pills which give you the ability to put the ghosties out of their misery, and wraparound corridors that'll take you from one end of the screen to the other.

Gameplay, when you get down to it, is not particularly fast or startlingly responsive. So far, so standard, but the redeeming feature of Footman is the comprehensive Maze Editor. This lets you design your own mazes in which to weeble, providing all sorts of opportunities to shock maiden aunts and generally be terribly rude.
For President
For President is a German-language, political strategy game set in the US, developed and published by CompuTec Verlag, which was released in Europe in 1994.
For the Love of Money

A semi overhead view perspective, space fantasy arcade adventure. You are a Space Mercenary available for hire. The main employees are political organizations, but you have worked for paramilitary on past missions. The aim of the game is to assassinate the leader of a rebel faction on an alien planet and solve the puzzles you find.
Forbidden forest

Forbidden Forest on Amiga: Paul Norman's 8-bit Horror Masterpiece, Purist and Remastered

Some games are remembered for their gameplay. Forbidden Forest (Cosmi, 1983) is remembered for how it made you feel.

On a humble Commodore 64, Paul Norman built something nobody had seen before: a forest that breathes, a sky that moves from day to dusk to a starry night, parallax backgrounds, giant spiders, bees, frogs, dragons, a snake, skeletons rising from the ground, and finally the Demogorgon, unseen in the darkness until the lightning reveals it. It was cinematic, violent and genuinely frightening, years before anyone spoke of "survival horror".

This project brings that masterpiece to the Amiga in three editions: two purist ones, faithful to the last pixel, and a remake that reimagines its world with new graphics while keeping its soul intact.
Ford Capri Challenge
Ford Capri Challenge is a top-down racing game for the Commodore Amiga for 1 or 2 players. It was developed by Total Recall Crew and released into the public domain in 1998.
Forest Dumb

Forest Dumb is a side-scrolling platform game. The aim for the player is to reach the designated number of coins and the exit gate before the time runs out. All the levels are quite extensive, full of hostile animals, deadly spikes or vanishing stone platforms. Besides the coins the player can collect numerous fruits (points) scattered around the board or use trampoline mushrooms to perform high jumps. The hostile creatures can be killed by a jump on their head. The player can use the quick run which increases the height of the jump. After each level a stage code is provided.
Forest Dumb Forever

Forest Dumb Forever is a platform game, developed by Eagle Software Ltd and published by L.K. Avalon, which was released in Europe in 1998.

Forest Dumb Forever is a side-scrolling platform game and the sequel of Forest Dumb. The action has been moved from the forest to a castle. The aim for the player is to reach the designated number of coins and the exit gate before time runs out. All the levels are quite extensive, full of hostile animals, deadly spikes or vanishing stone platforms. Besides the coins the player can collect numerous fruits (points) scattered around the board or use trampoline pods to perform high jumps. The hostile creatures can be killed by a jump on their head. The player can use the quick run which increases the height of the jump. After each two levels a stage code is provided.
Forgotten Empires I

An adventure role playing game with some similarities to Elite and Privateer. Written by Tommi Nieminen in Blitz Basic 2 and released as freeware in 1998. In the game you could pick from a number of Star Trek races, Human, Klingon, Romulan, Vulcan, Minbari, Narn and Cenauri, pick your sex and you get a rolled set of stats you can re-roll. From here you can trade, move around the galaxy and make and spend credits on outfitting your ship and goods to trade.
Forgotten Mine

Forgotten Mine is an improved Boulderdash clone, equipped with new gadgets, switches, rock or critter generators, remote-controlled balloons, stretchy walls, push trap on enemies, special land that only monsters can dig.
Forgotten Worlds

Forgotten Worlds features two characters known as The Nameless Ones, who both look like Arnold Schwarzenegger, one even has a mohawk. It's their job to rid the planet of the attacking aliens.

Guiding your character around the screen as they fly with jet-packs, guns on full auto, you control a satellite which you rotate around your character for the direction in which your gun is firing. At the end of each level is a boss which needs to be killed to progress.

Enemies that have been killed drop money. At the end of every level is a shop where you can buy weapons, armour, items and first-aid packs.
Formido

In Formido written by Herbert Klackl, Mika Halttunen, Costel Mincea you have to defeat a plaque of insects. Formido is one of those games, where you are loaded with some guns and you go shooting different things. 'Things' in this case are big, ugly, - not green though - alien insects. The idea is to kill as many of those bastards as possible. Eventually they will overcome you, but struggle as long as you can. There are some power-ups to aid you in your honorable quest. Keep in mind, that those critters are rather tough and generally do nasty things when in close range of any player-characters.
Formula 1 3D

Formula 1 3D is a Racing game, developed and published by Simulmondo, which was released in Europe in 1991.

Simulmondo was running warm-up laps with Formula 1: They promise fast 3D action with variable detail, giving players the choice of true speed or high realism but at the end this was a wasted opportunity from Simulmondo to make a good racing simulation game. They mixed some arcade elements (timer, few laps, easy handling, no damage) with a bit of simulation. Unfortunately, the mix didn't get well and the result was a dull game (considering also that there was just only one circuit). On the other hand, the downs become up when played hotseat with a friend. Play it with some friends and game is really enjoyable.
Formula 1 Grand Prix

A simple arcade game, where you have to test your skills with F1 cars. The sound effect consist of the now standard engine drone and the 'kaboom' as two cars collide and, on the whole, they are sufficient. Some of the graphics are well presented, the scrolling background is used well and changes with every track. The track itself, however, is patterned with dark and light shades of gray and can be very off-putting. Overall, Formula 1 Grand Prix is something and nothing. It is by no means an outstanding game but it may be worth a viewing.
Formula 1 Manager
An F1 management game for up to three players created by Crystal Interactive in 1996.
Formula 1 Masters

You can try your hand at managing a Formula 1 team of your choice in this simulation. First of all you must choose your team and sign deals with drivers and engine and tyre suppliers, all from within your budget – pit crews must be hired and engine performance maximised within the remaining budget.

Between races you must select tyre compounds and wing settings for the circuit, and can peruse championship standings and records. The races are depicted form a side-view of the cars completing the laps, with any position changes, retirements or changes in track conditions reported. You can call your drivers in for new tyres, although refuelling isn’t a feature.
Formula Ace
On overhead racing game in the style of Super Sprint by Nikki Corruptions and released and sold via mail order starting in 1990.
Formula One Challenge

Formula One Challenge falls, sadly, with a disappointing splat into the boring category. There is nothing actually wrong with it, as such, but it just doesn't have any pizzazz, any zing in it. You are, in a very virtual sense, the manager of a Formula One racing team. Armed with only a few hundred thousand quid, you must buy some engines, hire some drivers and equip your team to take on the might of McLaren, Williams, Benetton and all the rest. There's a moderately neat graphic interface where you make your managerial choices (tires and stuff) and then the race storms off. You watch a leaderboard with occasional comments as to what's going on. On the face of it, it's a corking idea. Formula One Challenge just doesn't have whatever it is that makes these things fab. Errors and sloppiness aside, it does have a certain charm. There's plenty of detail in there for F1 enthusiasts, but precious little to enthrall them for long. Sorry.
Fort Apache

Fort Apache is turn-based strategy game with action on the Wild West, graphically similar to The Charge of the Light Brigade or Cohort: Fighting for Rome. The player is a new captain at Fort Apache - American's fortress. He commands groups of soldiers (up to 44 units under command), and his forces fight against Indians, Mexicans, or thieves. He gives commands that the soldiers perform after clicking the turn button. Possible actions, like movement, shooting, rearrangement or dismount, are available from the sidebar.
Fortress

You take control of BlubberLip. A brave warrior king who's divine quest is to seek out and destroy enemies. The enemies had first consisted of anyone and anything that moved. This proved counter productive after a while, mainly because the troops were attacking not only peasants and live-stock, but each other. Lately, new enemies started to take land that belonged to the others. The details were not important, they were creatures of violence. As such, the urge to fight summoned a war king to the throne. The time of cow herding was over. The time of war had arrived! At last! Take thy role and be victorious.
Fortress (Bsp Design)

Released as a preview on Amiga Future 129, this game is a clone of the old game Fort Apocalypse for Atari and C64, in which you traverse an underground prison area, destroying enemies and liberating its prisoners.
Fortress (Paul Ciulla)
Fortress is a 1-2 player scrolling co-op shooter developed by Paul Ciulla using Sensible Software's Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit, and released as freeware in 1992.
Fortress of Fear

A 3D, isometric Diablo style RPG, based on unreleased Digital Reality SoftworX PC version. It was scheduled for release on Amiga/PC in late 1998, but was abandoned by the developers in 1999 due to the excessive complexity/size of the game. Italian developers Insonnia Team, headed by the game's gfx coder Marco Farace, reportedly took over the project from Digital Reality SoftworX, but nothing further was heard about the game and it remains unreleased. Internet previews of FORTRESS OF FEAR appeared on: Amiga Nutta (June 97) and Amiga Flame.
Fortress Underground

A hostile power station has been discovered in a huge underground cavern. Your mission is to destroy it. Your battle chopper is equiped with a cannon and a limited supply of fuel. As you navigate the maze-like cavern avoid the bad guys shooting at you and head for the nearest way-point where you can rest for a minute, save your game and refuel your helicopter.
Fortuna (B.B)
A shareware, Polish language Wheel of Fortune game for up to three players by Gabriel Kalinowski in 1993.
Fortuna (Twin Spark Soft)

Fortuna (or Kolo Fortuny) was an AMOS based Polish language commercial release from Twin Spark Soft in 1993. This is a Wheel of Fortune style game in Polish where you would try to solve the puzzle while dealing with the randomness of the what the wheel gave in terms of points per correct guess, while avoiding the bankrupts.
Fortuna 2000

Fortuna 2000 is a one to four player game loosely based on the TV show Wheel of Fortune, created by TAIR Chorzów and released by Atares in 1993. The players take turns guessing letters to form a word or a saying. The game can be played with up to four human players. During their turn the players can spin the wheel, guess a consonant, buy a vowel or guess the password.
Fortuna Core

Fortuna Core is the second mini-game release from BlitterForge, developed for a standard Commodore Amiga 1200 running Kickstart 3.0. The game requires no accelerator or additional memory. It has also been successfully tested in WinUAE using Kickstart 3.1. Fortuna Core is not intended to be a large or ambitious production, but rather a passion project that combines retro computing, experimentation, modern AI-assisted development, and the joy of creating something new for a legendary platform.
Fortuna v1.0

Koło Fortuny is a simple video game loosely based on the TV game show of the same name, Wheel of Fortune in the US. The players take turns guessing letters to form a word or a saying. It can be played with up to two human players. The game takes 5 rounds all together. Each vowel costs 200 points. There are no graphics (like wheel spin) in the game, all is presented in text mode.
Foundation: Gold

This was the final version of a real-time strategy game influenced by Command & Conquer and The Settlers. This package features the 40 levels from the Director's Cut edition, and the 40 levels from the Undiscovered Land add-on disk, as well as varied difficulty levels.

The game features 20 different buildings, many of which require resources produced or modified from another building. As well as knights, your population includes Maidens (breeding is covered more realistically than most God-sims, in which the guys seem to reproduce by magic), Wizards (who can use the bodies of the dead to create buildings) and peasants, who can be trained to become guards, who can graduate into being full soldiers. Combat can be initiated by sending soldiers into enemy terrain, and attack methods such as arson can be taught to the peasants. There are 4 distinctly different types of landscape - Summer, Winter, Lava and Gloomy.
Foundation: The Undiscovered Land

"Foundation: The Undiscovered Land" refers to an expansion pack for the real-time strategy game "Foundation," adding new gameplay elements and missions that involve exploring and developing uncharted territories within the game world, essentially introducing a new area to build and manage beyond the initial map boundaries. 
Key points about "Foundation: The Undiscovered Land":

 Expansion pack:
 It is not a standalone game, but an add-on that requires the base "Foundation" game to play.
 New map areas:
 The expansion introduces fresh environments to explore and build upon, offering new challenges and strategic possibilities.
 Additional gameplay elements:
 May include new resource types, building types, units, and mission objectives related to the new land.
 Exploration focus:
 Players are often tasked with discovering new parts of the map, uncovering hidden secrets, and adapting to the unique conditions of the "undiscovered land".
Foundations Waste

Foundations Waste is a vertically scrolling shoot-'em-up, in which you have to collect extra weapons, like a side shot, shields, a drone which can be controlled by the inverse control of the player ship and some kind of seeking missiles. Sometimes the power ups are fakes, inverting your control or slowing your ship down. You lose all extra weapons either on dying or on entering a new level.

The enemy forces are tanks, ships, flying vessels and later even space ships. Each level is featuring an end-of-level guard, which can be destroyed for extra points, but can even passed if your fire-power is too low at that moment.
Four iIn a Row (Pery Pearson)

This game is a classic among simple games that require concentration and cunning to win. In this Amiga version, you can face off against the computer or another player in a battle to the finish.

It is a widely known game, and the objective is to line up four of your pieces—horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.

Naturally, while trying to complete your own lines, you must also block your opponent to prevent them from forming their own.

To drop your piece into a specific column, simply click one of the knobs located at the base of the game board. The menus allow you to start a new game, choose between playing against the computer or another person (One Player/Two Players), decide whether to go first or let the computer take the opening move, and exit the program (you can also exit by closing the game window using the close gadget).

Published in the Italian AmigaMagazine OnDisk #08.
Four in a Row(Ola Lundkvist)

This is the result of me studying algorithms. A very nice version of Four in a row, or Four wins. 0-2 players (yes you can watch the computer play against itself). Plays fairly good and fast, I would say. (That is - beats the crap out of all other four in a row games I have seen.) Written in C on various computers 1993-94. Included a version that uses 2.04, a less featured version for 1.x and a windows (yuk) version (which you may use or delete, whatever pleases you). A game created by Ola Lundkvist and released in the WizoGames - first public compilation release.
Fourmaze

A one to four-player Pac-Man variation. Another stand-out feature is that it runs in high-res (or med-res) 640x256 mode in 16 colours. There are several bonus items, but the ghosts are not nearly as aggressive as in the original.
Foxy's Run
A fox, a forest, a floppy. Foxy's Run is a side-scrolling platformer for the Amiga
Fracas

Fracas is a Shareware Mech Fighter from Casco/John Smith on the Amiga. It says in the readme this took 3 years to make.

Basically you have to search down the enemy/ies and destroy them on each generated level. The game also offers a 2 player mode but suggest you use something to split the screen to stop your opponent cheating.

You do have a selection of different mechs too. This is a nice game I have only just discovered 28 years later.
Fracman

Only few words for this masterpiece of the games revisited by Axel Software! It was inspired by 'RealPacman' of 'De Videorakkers&Peace', developed during spring/sumer of 2021 and ultimated on 2022. The early PC version was born in 1996, but it never was released; the old 2.0 Amiga version have too many bugs to see the light. Finally we got it, and... ... It Works!
 
As usual eat all the pills and avoid the ghosts. Pick up the bows to get a good or bad gift.
Fraction Action

The action takes place in the basement of the Mad Professor's Mansion, where his motley crew is holding you captive. These creatures hold the keys to the electrified gates blocking your way to freedom.

Only after answering Fraction problems correctly will the gatekeepers unlock the gates and permit you to pass. But you'd better move fast!!
Incorrect answers are given full screen explanations and an occasional drop down the basement's chutes by the mansion's ghastly ghost.

For one or two players, multi-screen arcade action --- ADDITION, SUBTRACTION, MULTIPLICATION, DIVISION or a VARIETY of problems on three difficulty levels.
Never before have Fractions been so fun.
Fraction Goblins

An educational text adventure with still pictures from Caroline and Ian Coombe and released in 1991. Yọu̟ have been invited to go, and play with your friends, the Fraction Goblins and have spent a messy hour or two with them in their Art Room. The problem is that the young goblins were learning Borrowing, at school today and they were set some homework. So, while you were taken to the kitchen for a snack, the goblins did their homework, using the contents of your pencil case. You return, to the Art Room to find that your pencil case has been ransacked. All you have to do now is find the
contents again. 3 pens, 4 pencils, 4 crayons, a rubber, a sharpener, a ruler and the key to your bicycle padlock. Oh, by the way, if you meet any of the older goblins as you wander round the caves, they may make you answer a fractions problem before they will let you pass. If you get stuck, you can cheat a little bit. Type in the word HELP for some magical assistance. Press a key.
Fractions

An educational mathematics game written in HiSoft BASIC by Lascelles Productions in 1992, which focuses on fractions. Simplify, add, multiply and divide them! Review the results and get info about the problems in simple English. Get help on the specific problem and how to approach it most successfully with step-by-step instructions.
Frank Brush

A simple demo of a bloody fighting game being developed for the Amiga by Mauro Antonio Radice aka MARadice with soundtrack by Alex Ciarelli. The game is being created in both English and Italian. In it you play Frank Brush and you and your two knives take on the world.
Frankenstein

Baron Frankenstein has instructed his hunchback servant Egor to collect tools and bodies for him to use in his quest to create artificial life. As Egor, the player must search through Frankenstein's castle, the dungeons, the surrounding forest, the local village and other areas in this side-scrolling platformer. Despite the grim themes, the game is a humorous cartoonish one.

Each task begins in Frankenstein's lab with the Baron telling Egor what item he requires. Egor must find it, put it in his sack and return to the lab to receive the next task. Along the way there are enemies such as ghosts, skeletons, rats, bats, animated body parts, local townsfolk and others. Instead of a health bar, Egor has a Frightometer with a range from calm to panic. Touching enemies moves it ever more towards the maximum. Once that is reached, Egor will drop what he is carrying, flee to the lab and in so doing lose a life.
Franko: The Crazy Revenge

Franko: The Crazy Revenge is a Beat ‘Em Up game, developed by World Software and published by Mirage, which was released in Europe in 1994.

Alex and Franko were a pair of great friends, born in times where Poland was morphing from communist country into something else. Lost in the world, they couldn’t find them self in the new reality. Living in the Polish city of Szczecin, the two were growing up in a rather unfriendly neighborhood. Mastering martial arts, they found their life tough but very interesting. Until one day a band of thugs attacked them. After a long fight, when Franko was able to see and feel again, he saw a body of his friend, and in his ears he still heard the laughter of the band’s leader, Klocek. Now it’s time for revenge.

Franko is a classical Double Dragon-style action game. With excessive amount of blood and violence, it is suitable for mature audiences only. The player walks right through the streets of a Polish city.
Frantic Freddie

From the people who brought you that excellent version of Donkey Kong a couple of months back comes Frantic Freddie, yet another platform game. If anything (and some may find this hard to believe) it's even simpler than Kong. Hero Freddie has to be maneuvered around the network of platforms and ladders whilst picking up the goodies and avoiding the roving nasties. Not so bad, eh? Ah, but the twist here is that Freddie can't walk through the ladders, so if he's not careful it's very easy for him to get trapped in a dead-end. However, that aside, that's pretty much all there is to say.

It's simple, enjoyable and very fast paced. However, it can get a bit frustrating simply due to the ease with which you can get caught by the ghoulies. (Ahem!) All-in-all, Frantic Freddie's unlikely to keep you glued to your monitor all night long, but it's the sort of game you're likely to load up from time to time just for a quick go.
Frantix

Two players try to snatch each other's gems away in this AMOS game by Chris Banks in 1990. Released with Mutant Zombie Psycho Pigs on Spielekiste # 077. This is a two player game, a duel to grab your opponent's Gem and survive. Different squares have different effects. Each player controls a Squiggly. Players take turns to jump 1 square in either direction But hurry as if you run out of time your Squiggly will explode. You Aim is to capture your opponents GEM. Some blocks that you jump on have special effects. Choose to read the (I)nformtion at the beginning of the game for full instructions.
Franzosisch II Plus

The second in the game series that helps those who speak German to learn to speak French. Grammar: in 12 or 11 interactive chapters, all important grammar areas are explained in detail and with many examples. Practice included with around 1000 integrated grammar tasks. 7 vocabulary trainers with the entire basic vocabulary (approx. 2300 words and 1200 idioms), editor for your own libraries, learning in context, and much more. Verb trainer & verb tables (French II only): irregular verbs can be displayed as verb tables in the course and learned completely flexibly in the trainer. Precise correction function for all keyboard entries. Online dictionary and technical terminology are available at any time. 
Independent of textbooks - therefore suitable for adults as well as students. Update service for registered customers.
Fratzen Geballer

A sequel to Trapped 2, based on a revised and corrected version of the Trapped 2 engine. This new marvel will be called Fratzen Geballer and will implement new and spectacular effects such as mipmapping. lensflares, dithering and very atmospheric lighting effects. Everything will be set in a space station. The game would remain unreleased, with this demo dropped in 1997.
Freak Mine 1

All caves designed and tested by Freakie for this Boulderdash\Emerald Mines clone, published by Emerald Mines Club of Australia. This version featured lots of beginners levels and was published in 1991. There would be four sequels.
Freak Mine 2 Easy

All caves designed and tested by Freakie for this Boulderdash\Emerald Mines clone, published by Emerald Mines Club of Australia. There were two versions of this initial sequel, one easier the other much harder, it featured lots of beginners levels and was published in 1991. There would be a total of five games in the series.
Freak Out

Freak Out is a fast-paced strategy game where each level takes the player to a different location, to contain the attack of the fuzzy intruders. The playing field consists of interconnected cells, arranged in concentric squares. The Freaks (which come in four different colors) pop out of a hatch at the center, and can be moved about by rotating and smacking them, which sends them jumping to the next cell (if it isn't occupied). To score points and eliminate Freaks, three of the same color must be placed in adjacent cells, making them vanish in a puff of smoke.

Speed is essential, since the quickly-reproducing aliens line up behind the hatch: if you let the queue get too long, it's game over. Random items and obstacles pop up occasionally, like bonus gems, freezing ice, stone walls, or colored circles (which can only be occupied by a Freak of the same hue).
Freak-Out
Clear all blocks across 100 levels solo or in two-player co-op mode, and don’t freak out by the various enemies!
Fred Diamond

A Boulderdash\Emerald Mine clone published as shareware by Eric Hambuch in 1990 for one player. The game also game with a level editor, a trainer and could save high scores. Avoid or crush the monsters, watch out of cave-ins and grab all the diamonds you can.
Fred the Frog

Fred the Frog from Robert W. Benjamin requires you to eat insects to enable you to progress through the stages. The problem is during your journey you have to avoid bees, birds, seagulls, knives, bottles etc as one hit and it's game over and back to the 1st level you go.

The game requires patience as the 1 hit and it's game over is a bit tough.
Fred's Journey

The game stars Fred, a legendary C64 persona. Fondly remembers his past journeys. Deciding to relive his adventures he heads out again! You can buy this game with some goodies on APC & TCP. Includes 20 levels from Fred's Back 1 & 2 in Amiga style and 7 chiptunes, high scores and a hidden trainer!

This is essentially a clone/update of the 1993 C64 game, Fred's Back.
Free Cell(Perry Rosenboom)

A shareware, AMOS version of Free Cell solitaire created by Perry Rosenboom in 1994. Similar to SeaHaven Towers. FreeCell is the sixth in the package of card games made by Australian developer Perry Rosenboom. The first five were Classic Solitaire from 1992, Tut's Tomb from 1993, Aces Up in mid 1993, Golf late 1993 and Cruel from January 1994. The basic gameplay involves trying to move all 52 cards to the foundations at the top of the screen. In the main play area, they can be stacked down by alternate colour (red 7 on black 8, for example). The unusual thing is the Free Cells at the top of the screen, which can be used as temporary storage locations for the cards. Only one card at a time can be moved, either to another Tableau pile or a cell, but you can use the cells to move multiple cards in what appears to be one move. For example, you can put a black 6 in a cell, move a red 7 onto the black 8, then put the black 6 onto the red 7's new position.
Free Trading Company

A German-language, shareware trading and management from Chris Hodges and Peter Hodges. Version 1.27 came out in 1997. The game allows you to create factories of all types based on available mines\forests\fields\plantations. You will need to get the money for them as well. For instance, you can build cigarette factories. For each cigarette factory you need four tobacco plantations. You can produce an average of between 0-250 cartons of cigarettes with one factory. 

Similarly with oil you can drill for $1. If you find 1, you can demand an average of between 0-200 barells with an oil tower. Or fields, you know how to spray pesticides against insects that may be on your property. You cannot spray poison in advance because the pesticide only has an effect for a short time. Every field that is infested with a swarm of insects must be sprayed once with poison. There can also be several swarms of insects in one field. 

You can go to wars with your fellow players.
Freedom

Freedom: Rebels in the Darkness is a game that combines elements of strategy, stealth and fighting games. The main character is a rebellious black slave working on a sugar plantation that tries to incite a revolt among the slave population to gain freedom and to give comeuppance to each of their old masters.

At the start of the game there is four characters to choose, each with different statistics and abilities like "constitution" and "lock-picking". The main game screen is a map of the plantation, where you guide a small icon of the character while trying to avoid the guard dogs. If the dogs find you, they either bark and alert the owners or attack you. When they do, the screen switches to a first-person screen where you have to avoid being bitten and killed by the animal.

On the top of the screen there are four buttons, each with a unique function:
Path-finding lets you click on the map with a cursor and see a description of each hut and house.
Freestyle

Freestyle - Tales of Itch is something that has been in my mind since I first created most of these characters in 1995. I lacked the ability to be able to put together a game back then and my focus was creating comic book stories that revolved around Stupid Cat and the gang anyway. Then I discovered Scorpion Engine...
Freeway

A freeware, AMOS-built update to the Atari freeware game from Adam Hap where you must help your little guy get across the busy 5-lane freeway to safety on the other side. Try to score as many points as you can by crossing safely.
French Grammar I

Learn French (for English speakers) with French Grammar 1, created with AmigaBasic by Intellectual Software and published by Queue in 1988. 10 modules to help you review French Grammar, including 2 modules on gender of nouns, gender and number, plural of nouns, nouns and articles, definite articles, prepositions, avoir and etre, idioms with avoir and il est and c'est. When you finish this you can move on to French Grammar 2 and 3, published the same year.
Frenetic

Frenetic is a traditional vertically scrolling shoot'em'up. The action moves through eight levels, set both in space and on the ground (with such environments as a jungle planet and a water world). While most levels have a technological theme, some feature organic enemies and backgrounds, reminiscent of games like R-Type or Xenon 2. Going with tradition, each level has a huge end boss.

The player's ship can collect a variety of power-ups: lasers and missiles, shooting to the front, the back or the sides. Speed-ups and shields are also available. Power-ups are revealed by destroying certain enemies or special bonus capsules, and several are given to the player for free at the start of a level. The weapons can be upgraded by collecting the same power-up several times.

The game features a two-player mode, with two ships moving against the aliens at the same time.
Friday Night Pool
Not just a pool game, but for just a few quid you can turn on the strip pool version.
Friends

A Dynablaster\Bomberman clone for up to 3 players created by Allan Jensen and released with known bugs because it was required that you release a game commercially or to PD prior to being part of their developer program.
Fright Night

Fright Night is based on the 1985 Columbia Pictures movie of the same name. You play vampire Jerry Dandridge in this arcade-style action game. You prowl the rooms of the mansion searching for victims. You have to dodge the Crucifixes thrown at you and sink your teeth into anything that looks tasty. Once you've drained the blood of all your victims, you can proceed to the next level. Keep an eye out for the unhealthy as they will drain your lifeforce; too much bad blood and you're a dead vampire. You can run back to your coffin if you're low on health to regenerate, as well, you must be back in your coffin before the sun comes up, or you're a toasty vampire.
Frisbee Fox
A self published frisbee game from Gianluca Troiano aka The Fox. FRISBEE FOX was based on Data East's 1994 Neo Geo arcade game WINDJAMMERS.
Frogger
A beautiful single player recreation of Frogger for the Amiga platform created with and by Fungus.
Frogger 500
This is a 1:1 arcade port of the game FROGGER by KONAMI from 1981 for the Amiga 500. The game is written in 68k assembler, based on the original Z80 code.
Frontal Assault

A remake of Artillery Duel. Hall of light calls it a 2D Artillery Puzzler, the puzzle is how much power and what angle to shoot your weapon to hit the other players\artillery guns on the screen. And up to 7 can play!
Frontier: Elite II

Frontier: Elite 2 is, of course, the sequel to Elite and it continues in much the same way. You have a ship and limited funds, and nowhere to go but out into space. Trade, fight, hunt criminals, work for the various governments, anything goes in Frontier. There are few, if any, limits on what you can do or where you can go. And Frontier's universe (with approx. 100,000,000,000 planets and moons) is so big you'll never see the end of it.
Frontline

Frontline is a squad-level tactical strategy game set in many fronts of the World War 2. The included scenarios are Monte Cassino 1944, Guadalcanal 1942, Stalingrad 1943, Pegasus Bridge 1944 and two tutorial missions.

The player commands 10-man infantry squads, to which assigns leaders (their leadership skill having a direct influence on squad's morale) and support weapons (like heavy machine guns – affecting not only firepower, but also movement rate), artillery pieces with crews are also available. Walls and shell holes may provide cover on the varied battlefields. The game features an icon-driven menu-based interface.
Frost Byte

In Frost Byte you control Hickey the Kreezer, an elastic curve which moves sideways, jumps and shoots. You must navigate your way through planet Cosmica, and rescue your brethren, within the limited 'Twang' energy you have.

Cosmica is full of hideous monsters, many of which can be shot. Your character builds momentum as it moves, so some hazards are easier to clear from a running start. You can only jump vertically, although you have control as the character falls. Ammunition is limited, and must be collected throughout your quest.

Three sweets which enhance your character can be collected - the red one increases your speed, blue increases the height of your leap, and green means you can safely fall further. There are additional objects to pick up and use as well.
Frozen Bubble

The classic bubble-shooting puzzle game comes to the Amiga 1200!
Frozen Bubble – Amiga 1200 AGA Edition brings the much-loved bubble-shooting game to the Commodore Amiga 1200, featuring AGA graphics and a port developed using AMOS Professional and Motorola 68000 assembly language.
Fruit Crush

A mouse based memory\puzzle game by Mark Cameron. Originally released in 1991 and appeared on many public domain game compilations including AMOS PD146 along with Fruit Machine, Norlich Spiele Pack 2 and AMOS Megahits 3. Not an easy game.
Fruit Machine

Fruit Machine is as can be expected a simulation of slot machine. The game is for one player who controls the machine with the keyboard. There are four reels and the player has to get three of four fruits in a row to win. After a win it's possible to gamble the earnings by choosing if a number is higher or lower than the that is about to appear. The fruits on the reels have number on them and if their sum is ten or greater the player reaches Club Casino. This give access to features and the higher the numbers the better feature is available. To get a better feature it's possible to gamble. If the player gets a question mark he is given a bonus chance which can be additional Club Casino numbers, a free respin or a skill chance.
Fruit Machine (Steve Potts)

A nice, modern 5 reel fruit\slot machine from Steve Potts that will run on even stock Amiga 500's. Has all the extras, nudge, hold and gamble your heart out. Many sites have this title listed as being by Mark Cameron, but it was released as part of a 2 game compilation with Fruit Crush that WAS by Mark Cameron.
Fruit Panic

This is actually a remake of a classic MSX game with the same name. It is a nice twist on the Pac-Man formula. Get all the fruit before the ghosts get you and instead of running through a maze, you'll have to reach fruit on different platforms. You reach higher platforms using a springboard (is that an English word?!) and when a ghosts is tailing you, you can kill it with a limited number of bombs.
Fruit Salad

Welcome to the world of Fruit Salad, a platform game from Grand Master Design. The idea of the game is to collect all of the gems from each level and get to the exit but since evil Triax has turn all of your friends into mutant fruit and vegetables, try to avoid them or die in the process by touching them. The game has 20 levels and the enhanced version has over 60. Every five levels you will be given a level code, you can use these as the main menu screen, and this will start you at the last level code received. If you collect the letters "GAME UP", then you will be able to play the Surf Game! This will enable you to collect extra lives. You can also collect bonuses on screen. They are "F"reeze, "B"onus, "T"urbo and "S"hield.
Fruit-Mania

An AMOS based shareware release from JP Hamilton of a four-reel video slot machine, released in June of 1994. It features multiple betting lines, nudge, repeat and all the pub-slot features you expect.
FruitMachine
A fruit\slot machine game with 3 reels, multiple betting lines, hold and double! A playable demo\preview from Project A on December 08, 1994.
Fruitmania

Fruitmania is a slot machine simulator for one person. Guus Hildesheim, who also did the graphics for this game, was sysop of the 'BBS de Saen', a Dutch modem-based bulletin board system (BBS).

This game is based on a real fruitmachine. It uses the same bars and the same points. It doesn't check whether or not you are winning and it doesn't cheat.
Frust

An AMOS based freeware shooter in the style of Thrust created by Mark Potter and Ian Jeffray in 1993. An editor was included with the game. As a Resistance fighter, the player must fly into enemy lines in order to steal Energy Pods to power more advanced starships, using your tractor beam to take them. A network of mounted guns are aiming to shoot the player down, disable these by blasting them.
Frustration

A text-based adventure game by Jim MacBrayne. You've been given a shopping list by your aunt. After a gust of wind snatches it from your hand, you give chase... and then unfortunately fall into a manhole with a missing cover. A short while later, you find yourself at the bottom of the shaft, with a sword and lantern nearby.
Frutis

Frutis is an action game with puzzle-solving elements, a mix of Robbo and Boulder Dash games. The player must collect all the fruits and access keys, avoiding enemies and traps, moving cases blocking the road or switching different mechanisms. Contact with hostile creature or bullet blaster ends with the immediate death.

The game features a level editor.
Ftype
A freeware shooter created with AmiBlitz in 2020 by Fabrizio Radica aka fabbroz. It is an upcoming top scrolling shoot em up, in which you must destroy waves of enemies and end of level bosses.
Fugger

Die Fugger is an economy simulation combining elements of games like Kaiser and Hanse. Up to six players can compete on one machine.

You're an impoverished nobody in Germany in the year 1500. However, the death of an uncle leads you to inherit 20 barrels of beer and 500 Talers of money. Start your career heading forwards to getting an renowned and rich member of the society. There are six goods to trade, across 11 different cities. But there's a lot more to do then only trading with goods: attack your opponents or bribe them or build alliances with other players.
Full Contact

A fighting game that you can play in several different ways. You can fight against your friend or a foe on the same computer, using two joysticks, or joystick + keyboard combination. You can play tournament, or as a solo, fighting through the serious of computer AI controlled fighters (even a dog), with one tougher then the other. The reward is as usual, being top on the top 10 list.
Full House
Full House is a beautifully done video poker game for one from BBS De Seen in 1990.
Full Metal Planete

Full Metal Planète is a tie-in of a board game of the same name. Up to four players land on a planet with their motherships, trying to gather as much ore as possible within 24 game rounds.

This almost sounds like a happy, idyllic round of pick-the-flowers, if it weren't for the truckload of tanks and destroyers that each players happens to have in the cargo area of his mothership. So the players usually spend an equal amount of time picking up ore and bashing their contenders' heads in.

The computer game is an accurate conversion of the board game; virtually every feature is present. Strategy is needed to succeed in the game. The only semi-random thing are the tides (high tide, low tide, and something in-between) which can strand boats and engulf tanks, but even they can be partially predicted.
Fullspeed

Fullspeed is a simple racing game against the time. It takes place on a highway with six lanes which is shown in a top-down perspective. The player can control the speed and needs to dodge slower vehicles by moving left and right. Released in a two-pack along with Microbattle.
Fun at the Sea

Fun at the Sea is all about aiming to opponent's battleship by correct arrangement of deck cannon. The player may move the cannon left or right and change the angle to determine shot distance. Sinking the ship requires several customs hits. The game is designed for two players competing on a single horizontally divided screen.
Fun School 2: For 6-8 year olds

Fun School 2: For 6-8 Year Olds is an educational game part of the Fun School series with this version aimed at the ages of six, seven and eight. Parents can choose a difficulty level for each game and also enter their own words to use. There are eight activities for a child to play and these consist of:

Number Train: A coloured train moves along the rails and the child has to stop it at the matching coloured station to drop off and pick up passengers. Once the train has stopped at the correct station, a maths problem appears and when the correct answer is typed the train moves on and changes colour.

Maths Maze: The child has to move a frog around a maze full of creatures and when the frog touches a creature a maths problem appears and the correct answer is needed to move on.

Shopping: The child has a shopping list and the child must move the frog to the correct shop from a choice of four to select the highlighted item on the list.
Fun School 2: For the Over-8s

Fun School 2: For the Over-8s is an educational game part of the Fun School series with this version aimed at the over eights. Parents can choose a difficulty level for each game and also enter their own words to use. There are eight activities for a child to play and these consist of:

Build a Bridge: A square sits underneath a bridge and it must be filled with various shapes and placed in the correct position to hold the bridge up.

Passage of Guardians: The child controls a robot and moves him down various passages and attempt to get past the various guardians. When a guardian is touched, it reveals a word with the letters mixed up and the child has to type the correct word to move past..

Unicorn: A robot has to save an unicorn from a burning forest by moving three objects in front of it around a winding path. The robot can only carry one object at a time and certain objects cannot be left alone with each other while the robot is away..
Fun School 2: For Under 6s

Fun School 2: For the Under-6s is an educational game part of the Fun School series with this version aimed at the under sixes. Parents can choose a difficulty level for each game and also enter their own words to use. There are eight activities for a child to play and these consist of:

Shape Snap: Two shapes appear and the child must say whether the shapes are the same or not.

Teddy Count: A certain amount of Teddies move about the screen and the child must say how many are on the screen.

Find the Mole: There are five mole hills and the child selects one. If the child is wrong then the computer will say if the actual number is bigger or smaller.

Write a Letter: Here the child can move the teddy about the screen and type any letter and can also type words.

Colour Train: A coloured train moves along the rails and the child has to stop it at the matching coloured station to drop off and pick up passengers. The train changes colour once it starts moving again.
Fun School 3: For 5 to 7 year olds

These six small educational games star Freddy the Frog. Each uses simple controls to ensure that children can play without difficulty from the software.

Using forward, back, left and right keys Freddy must get to various important buildings as depicted on the screen. In Adding he is presented with a network of lily pads, some of which contain numbers or mathematical symbols. Land on these in the correct order to produce a correct sum. In the Toyshop, first identify toys from their names, then choose a toy at a specified price, and then combine goods to meet a specified price limit.

Electricity allows you to learn about circuits - by working out whether an existing layout will work, and modifying it so that it will. The next game involves telling the time, so as to get the prince his key. Funtext teaches information searching using a Ceefax-type environment.
Fun School 3: For Over 7s

Fun School 3: for the over 7s is an educational package which is part of the Fun School series. This package is aimed at the over sevens and consists of six programs with four games starring Robbie the Robot and two utilities. Each game has various skill levels and can be adjusted to suit the child's needs. The games are:

Wordsearch: On screen is a list of words and the child has to find them hidden in a grid of letters.

Planet Maths: Each maths sign (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) can be played on its own or all together as a maths problem scrolls from right to left towards a force field. Get the answer right and the problem fires a missile that destroys the force field.

Treasure: There are various pictures and on each one are directions (north, south, east and west) to the treasure, and distance in either cm or mm.

Sentences: A paragraph with spelling and grammar mistakes is seen on screen. The child must adjust the mistakes to move on to the next paragraph.
Fun School 3: For Under 5s

A friendly teddy bear is on hand to help teach the skills children should have on starting school. They are controlled using the space and return keys, so young children should be able to play with little support. Most games have multiple difficulty levels, which reveal themselves after the easiest has been solved.

If Teddy's friend is to climb the tree successfully, you must recognise which of the items in front of you can be paired up. Initially there are 6, rising to 18 as you get them right. The Gallery game involves matching pictures with the correct label, with more and more options as the game difficulty increases. In the actions game you must choose an action word and watch Teddy act it out.

To help teddy get up the steps to his beloved honey, you must correctly count the numbers of everyday objects such as teddies, trees and clouds on a screen. The Letters game takes place at the fair - matching the letters displayed will earn your Teddy an ice cream.
Fun School 4: For 5 to 7 year olds

Freddy the Frog presents six games designed to help school-starting children build on their numeracy and literacy skills. The rules for each game are explained in the form of short stories. Controls primarily use the cursor keys and enter.

Freddie is building a house, but can only add a log to his work if you solve a maths question. In the library, a list of book titles must be sorted into alphabetical order.

Successfully ordering letter and number sequences on the basketball court results in shots going in. Knowing which word is the opposite of the displayed one will help Freddy's diving.

In the shop, you have to identify which coins pay for which items, and then total up a shopping load and work out which coins pay for it. There is also a simple typing test included.
Fun School 4: For 7 to 11 year olds

Fun School 4: for 7 to 11 year olds is an educational game part of the Fun School series with this version aimed at seven, eight, nine, ten, and eleven-year-olds. There are six games and activities that allow the child to help Sammy the Spy (Agent Q) find and retrieve the stolen riches of King Raram by completing six missions with varying skill levels. The six activities consist of:

Desert Dates: Sammy and his boss have found various pyramids containing gems and secret parchments hidden behind various blocks with a date written on them. The computer will ask a question and the child must select the correct block to smash.

Travels: Sammy has to travel the world in various vehicles to find a secret destination. The computer will give a Continent, Ocean, Country, City, Sea, or River, and the child must move the vehicle around the screen to get to the selected destination.
Fun School 4: For the Under 5s

Fun School 4: for the under 5s is an educational game part of the Fun School series with this version aimed at the under-fives. There are six games and activities that allow the child to spend the day with Teddy and each activity has varying skill levels. The six activities are:

Teddy's House: Teddy's house is being painted but the painters don't know which colours to use so the child decides which colour to use for various parts of the house. After the painting is completed the child then has to tell the computer what colour certain objects are before being told a colour and what object to paint.

Fun Train: Teddy is at the funfair in the park and the child has to decide if a picture matches the picture on the train as well as words matching pictures.

Teddy Paint: This activity allows the child to use a simple art package to draw pictures with.

Teddy's Book's: It is time for bed and Teddy is having a sleepover with his friends.
Fun School Specials: Merlin's Maths

Now the fun really begins! The range of Fun School Specials has been developed to help children with specific areas of learning. Following the success of Fun School 4, parents and teachers have been asking for software which would focus on subjects like spelling, maths and creativity skills in much greater depth. The aim of the Fun School Specials is to complement children's school work. All comply fully with the National Curriculum syllabus. MERLIN'S MATHS encourages pupils to learn the basics of counting, decimals, fractions, volumes and much more while retaining the fun element common to all Fun School programs. Brilliant graphics and eye-catching sequences reward children as they progress from level to level.
There are six activities and each game has three levels. Help screens can be called up at any time. 
What this program contains
CRYSTAL CONFERENCE: The knights of the round table help with counting, subtracting and fractions.
Fun School Specials: Paint And Create

fun School Paint & Create. Now the fun really begins!
Dear Parent.
Learning can be fun-at least it can if you get the right balance of educational content and pure entertainment. Our ten years' experience of producing educational software, including the phenomenally successful Fun School range, have given us the edge. We have listened to your demand for more specific subjects such as maths, spelling and creativity, and address this with this new, specialized range of Fun School packages.
Each program has been finely tuned by teachers and educationalists to ensure it meets the requirements of the National Curriculum, but will still provide children with hours of mind-boggling fun as they discover new and fresh ways to learn. So, you can be sure that your child is achieving the right standard for his or her age, and making the most of the time spent at the keyboard.
Fun School Specials: Spelling Fair

Fun School Specials Spelling FAIR
Now the fun really begins!
The range of Fun School Specials has been developed to help children with specific areas of learning Following the success of Fun School 4 parents and teachers have been asking for software which would focus on subjects like spelling maths and creativity skills in much greater depth. The aim of the Fun School Specials is to complement children's school work. All comply fully with the National Curriculum syllabus. SPELLING FAIR helps children master basic techniques of spelling and grammar All the programs are set in a colorful, noisy fairground, incorporating the essential "fun" element that has enabled the Fun School series to achieve sales of more than 430,000 packages in the UK alone. It encourages children to discover the delights of plural similes suffixes, prefixes and homophones.
Funtris (Pasi Laaksonen)
FunTris is a multiplayer-tetris. 2-4 players can play at the same time.
Funtris (Xact)

Funtris from Xact (as there is another Funtris from Pais Laaksonen is a single player Tetris clone but with extras. The usual Tetris Gameplay is present, But occasionally you get either a Wizard which usually helps out or gives you Bonuses, and an Evil guy popping up during Gameplay whos job is to create big problems for your Game! 
 
The Evil Guy can turn the screen Black and White, Deep Red and even change Key controls, and put large peices in the play area, in order to try and stop you from completing the level

The Wizard pops on, and gives you Bonuses, sometimes removes a line or two from the game, and other effects as well

These additions can help or hinder your Gameplay, which gives the Game a neat touch, and as the Wizard/Evil are completely Random, each Game you play is completely different, Giving the Game quite a decent appeal

While it can make the Game impossible or easy to complete, The Wizard and Evil Guy do add to the Gameplay in terms of variation throughout the Game,...
Funturatum

Funturatum is a turn based managerial game played on the planet Whorn. The main goal is to acquire four pieces of a magical object called Funtolmin and combine them with the fifth part being in the hands of the Funturatum mayor, who's willing to sell it for a large amount of gold. The artifact is searched by four rival families, each possessing one element. The game takes place on the 174x174 grid randomly generated map. Each player has a ship with a crew. The turn is restricted to twenty moves, but it may be extended up to thirty one by the purchase of a better ship. The player may move across the sea and send an expedition to the mainland. Finding the plantation allows the production of twelve types of crops, building agricultural facilities, granary, setting military defense and trade with the merchant.
Furball

Furball is a shareware platform game written in AMOS, developed and published by Dimensions Software for the Amiga.

The game is called Furball and is free. You may remember (if you’ve been using an Amiga for any length of time) the small game Dithell in Space? Same author. The game itself plays smoothly and has lots of colourful graphics. Sprite collision works well, and the game is a nice little time waster. You need to eliminate baddies by jumping on them and find the exit to complete the stage. 
Some baddies need to be jumped on more than once or from greater heights.

If you like platformers, give it a try!
Furmyre
A vertically scrolling space shooter created by Andrew Fereday of FEZ Productions using the SEUCK in 1993.
Furtum Sacrum

Furtum Sacrum is the new videogame from the IronGate team that places us in the late Middle Ages. Specifically, in the Northwest of Spain, where there are a number of pilgrimage routes and roads with a lots of monasteries flourishing everywhere. These monasteries offer services to pilgrims in exchange for alms, they also have their own sources of funding, their crops and local products.
Furtum Sacrum: Dark Time

DARK TIMEThe Count has commissioned the Knight Esquio to clean a section of the Camino de Santiago from all kinds of creatures, witches, dogs, even the Holy Company... Don't forget to save the pilgrims you meet along the way. This seems to be the end of magic times. The Count has the Caballero Esquio clean a stretch of the Camino de Santiago of all kinds of creatures, witches, dogs, even the Holy Company. Do not forget to save the pilgrims you find on the road. This seems to be the end of magic times.
Fury of the Furries

In Fury of the Furries, you control a cute, round creature called Tiny, who must defeat "the wicked one" who has captured the King, and turned all the Tinies into mindless monsters. Fortunately your Tiny has special powers. It can transform himself into a swimmer, rock eater, fireball spitter, or rope swinger during its quest.

The game takes place on a huge island separated into eight regions: Desert, Lagoon, Forest, Pyramids, Mountains, Factory, Village, and finally the Castle.

For the US release, the title was changed to 'Pac-In-Time'. It's exactly the same game. Only the characters were changed : the not-so-known European Tinies (from the Skweek, Super Skweek, Tiny Skweeks/Brainies/Tinies games) were replaced by the widely known Pac-Man.
Fuse Cutter

A 1994 freeware puzzle game created by Rune Espeseth aka Lakris using ASM 68k. Move around the playfield, pick up fusecutters and bombs. Avoid the gravestones. You cannot go on the paths you make. If you walk outside the bounds of the screen you will appear on the opposing side. If you take all the bombs and fusecutters on each level you move to the next. First get a fusecutter, then a bomb and off to the next fusecutter. There is a time limit so be quick!
Fusion

Fusion is an action game in which your job is to find nine pieces of a fusion bomb scattered over 13 levels. There are two craft at your disposal: a fighter and a detachable ground vehicle. To find the bomb pieces, many enemies and their spawning points must be destroyed. Barriers block the access to other levels and keys must be found to open them. Certain areas can only be reached by the ground craft which is not as powerful as the fighter, however - some careful planning is required.
Fussball Manager

A German-language football\soccer management game written by Neudelsoft (Andreas Neumann) in Kick-PASCAL with text output throughout, early versions came out in 1989, version 2, the one most widely distributed, in 1992. The game came packaged with an editor so you can make sure your players and teams are always up to date.
Futsal
Futsal is a fast one-screen 3-versus-3 indoor football game for the Commodore Amiga. Play against the computer or challenge a friend in local two-player mode.
Future Basketball

One of the first Speedball clones takes the basic court layout of basketball as its inspiration. There are 5 players on each team, on a small court with 2 and 3 point shooting areas. The difference is that physical contact of a fairly violent nature is allowed, and the court is littered with mines and bombs to wound the players. Shooting involves holding down fire to get the height right, so avoid being tackled as you prepare your shot. Other basketball rules such as double-dribbling and the 25-second hand-over are unsurprisingly waived. A 3-division league is included to progress through.
Future Bike Simulator

Future Bike Simulator is a futuristic action game set in 1999. The government forbid motorcycles and so the billionaire Finnius M Houlder built a hovercraft replacement. And while he was at it, he also added some guns. So now his goal is to drive and kill people who move slower than him (which is everyone). Killed enemies leave behind money which can be reinvested into vehicle upgrades between levels. A life is lost when the energy bar is completely drained, so it is advised to dodge obstacles and vehicles. Movement is restricted to left and right; the speed can't be regulated.
Future Classics Collection

The Future Classics Collection is a collection of five distinctly-themed games that stress action and strategy equally. The programmers of the games had previously worked for Cinemaware and MicroProse.

The gameplay options are also quite varied: Each game can be played one player alone, two players alternately, two players simultaneously, or one player against one of three computer personalities -- including split-screen play for head-to-head competition.
Future Combat

Well the myth or mystery if you choose is over for some of us. For many many years Future Combat pt.II was available to playbut this was not the case for pt.1, did it ever exist or was pt.II just named that way we thought as there has been no pictures or any video footage of it anywhere,...well now that's changed and this mystery is finally closed and another missing gap in Amiga history has been filled. Thanks to one of the programmers confirming the first game did exist, there were a couple of ADFs available but neither worked but thanks to Ross "The Boss" he was able to fix the issues and now finally the first game can be played and here it is in full.

The game is very difficult, ship isn't spry and weapon upgrades will keep you wishing for more. No bosses but at least it has an end screen, the music is fine especially the high score table but really improves on the sequel.
Future Combat: Part2

A scrolling vertial shooter created by Ard Joosse (Bitboy), with excellent music by Christian Blaha (The Fox) and additional assistance from Marc van den Ouden. The hostile forces have returned and are trying to take over your planet. They have come in large numbers. The Earth's defense system is overwhelmed, we have plans for a new type of fighter that can stop them, our only hope is if you can somehow get the plans to the factory in time. So you must strap into your shuttle fighter and take them on like it is 1942 in space!
Future Miner

Homebrew demo platformer created by Pacific Software in 1996. Avoid the various enemies, the robots and penguins that will take you down. Pick up all the stars and make your way to the exit transporter to move to the next level.
Future Shock

The Master of Darkness has taken the possession of the Diamond Goodness splitting it into a thousand pieces and hiding them in his underground caves. Fear and terror are spreading since Diamond of Goodness doesn’t emit it’s positive energy anymore. As the best commander of the Federation, you are charged with the task of collecting the pieces of the diamond.

“Future Shock” is composed of three different levels which have to be flown through. Each level consist of several screens (horizontal and vertical). Collect in each setting up to nine diamonds eliminating as many adversaries as possible. As soon as you get all the diamonds, you automatically move onto the next level.
Future Space

The plot of Future Space can be summed up easily: Evil aliens attack Earth and the player, in the role of an experienced fighter, has to kill them. Unfortunately his space ship crash landed and his whole crew died - now the mission has to be concluded on foot. The game features about 30 stages in which the player basically needs to walk from left to right while shooting all opposition with one of the two hand guns - touching the enemies is not advised as it eventually leads to death. However, the exit at the end only opens when all scattered diamonds were collected. To make matters worse, there is also a time limit for each level.
Future Sport

Future Sport is certainly a copy of the film, The Running Man, but in own way is it similar to the game of the same name by Grand Slam. Although the game is not bad and has a few addictive qualities, it lacks much variety and becomes repetitive very quickly. I must say that Future Sport is not one of Actual Screenshots' better products.
Future Tank

Future Tank is a one or two player shoot 'em up which lets you control a tank from a bird's eye view. You are able to drive through big scrolling maps in all four directions. You have to fight your way through enemy lines in order to find the level's exit similar to popular Gauntlet style mazes.
