You will have to complete the level within the time limit, and avoid contact with these foes. However, bombs and improved weapons can be collected, as can extra lives, time bonuses and an improved jump.
Prehistorik AGA
A first-level demo of my ongoing AGA enhancement of Prehistorik, originally released by Titus in 1991
Preludium

Preludium is an educational game with arcade elements. The game takes place in the land called Chochland. Krzysztof's goal is reaching the stone with orthographic puzzle. The correct answer to the three tasks opens the door to the next room. The correct spelling indicated at the bottom of the screen needs to be selected from two different choices by using the left or right cursor keys and pressing the fire button. Incorrect answers and contact with obstacles takes one energy level. Topping energy withdraws the players of the two chambers. Arcade part of the game requires a jump over obstacles and avoidance of hostile creatures.
Premier Collection

Featured games in this compilation:

 • Zynaps -This horizontally-scrolling shoot 'em up features 16 levels and 450 screens of Nemesis-inspired action. You pilot a spacecraft through the levels, shooting as many of the encroaching meanies and mounted turrets as possible. Power-up tokens are offered for shooting some, which can be used to obtain better weapons including ground-attack lasers, speed ups and multiple bullets. Extra lives are on offer as well, which you'll certainly need, especially as you have to go back a long way when losing a life.

 • Nebulus-You play a small green guy who needs to blow up eight towers because their presence is somehow poisoning the water of planets which could potentially be ideal colonies. Unfortunately, you need to get to the top of these towers to blow them up. 

 • Exolon-This flick-screen action game combines shoot 'em up and platform elements, as you control a flying man who can gain an exoskeletal suit for extra protection (hence the name).
Premier Division
Simple English division football manager game with unusual twist - apart from the normal version there was also board game version.
Premier League
A statistics driven one or two player Premier League game where randomness is driven by a card choosing system that keeps things exciting. An F1 Licenseware game created by Dave King in 1993.
Premier Manager

The first game in Gremlin's series of football management games. You start off managing a team in the Conference (the fifth tier of English football) and aim to progress up the leagues, either by improving your existing team or earning jobs at better clubs elsewhere.

The features at your disposal include selecting training regimes, planning tactics for each match based on your opposition's strengths and weaknesses, scouting for new players including youth prospects, and arranging sponsorship and stadium improvements (so as to attract more fans).

The transfer system is a crucial part of the game, as you aim to sign players (who are broadly rated in each of the main skill areas) up against other teams who want them, and sell off players you don't need. You have an overdraft available, but make sure not to exceed it.

The game supports up to 4 players, whose matches all take place at the same time. You can make tactical changes and substitutions mid-match.
Premier Manager 2: The New Season

This football management game features all five national English leagues. The player begins the game managing one of the teams in the Conference, with the ultimate goal of trying to reach the Premier league and win European competitions, either by improving your current club or doing well enough to earn job offers elsewhere.

Each match involves selecting the team, and choose a formation and a set of match tactics - intensity of tackling, height and length of passes, and shooting range could all be varied. In total there are almost 500 permutations of these options, as well as 18 basic formations.

The game's transfer system involves making a financial offer to both club and payer and hoping that no other club offered more. Players whose contracts have expired can be signed for no club fee - so make sure all your players are under contract.
Premier Manager 3

Premier Manager 3 (also known as PM3) is a football management simulator video game for the Amiga and MS-DOS platforms. It was released in 1994 by Gremlin Interactive. The objective of the game is to manage a football club successfully within the top 5 divisions in the English league system, starting from the 1994-95 football season.
Premier Manager 3 De-Luxe

This is a compilation of Premier Manager 3 and its Multi-Edit Construction set. PM3 has been updated to 1995-1996 season data, with promoted and relegated teams moved divisions and player transfers activated - this means that previous saved games aren't compatible.
Premier Manager: Multi-Edit System

This editing system for Premier Manager 3 allows you to edit almost every aspect of the default database. You can change the names and abilities of each player, and transfer them to other teams. You can choose which divisions each club starts in, and can manage any of these, rather than having to start from the Conference league. You can even insert European teams to create a Superleague-type setup. The length of time particular injuries keep a player out for can be changed, as can the points system of the league. Once you've saved the changes and started the edited game, you can load it back into the Multi-Edit System and make further changes.
Premier Picks

Premier Picks is an unusual card game based around football (soccer). The game takes the form of a 'season' of variable length involving the 20 real-life Premier League teams of the time (name can be edited, but displayed kits can't). Players pick one of the 18 visible cards, to dictate the result of the match.

There are several different types of cards in the game - your overall aim is to get more goal cards than the opposition. The other cards include free kicks (which give you another pick), substitutions (which replace that card with another), and penalties (in which you have to run the pointer across the screen, clicking on as many cards as possible - you have a few seconds to find a goal card). The game is split into 2 halves, and each of those has a card which immediately ends the half.

Before each half there's a 'card reveal' feature, which, depending on when you click to stop the pointer, reveals between 1 and 6 cards.
Premier Sixes

Gives you the opportunity to guide one of ten top Premiership sides to the Premier Sixes Cup. One club will ask you to take over the running of their club's squad and you have to guide them to the top. Players such as Owen, Yorke, Shearer, etc, will be at your disposal however it's up to you to pick the right team. Spread over an eighteen week period you must try and shuffle your squad around to ensure that they stay fresh for the run in. 

Versions of this game continued until 1999 with updated players and rosters. The exciting Championship Manager-style match sequences complement the managerial side nicely, together with enough tactical options to make the user feel he is really doing something
Premier Soccer

Compete for eight different championship cups including 1993 English or European trophies, Premier Champions, European Cup, FA Cup, League Cup, UEFA Cup or even the Cup Winners Cup in this soccer management simulation written by Malcolm Howard of The Midnight Oil. Define your players, manage and your team and coach. Play at many different difficulty levels for the most fun fantasy football available.
Premiere

The sets are themed around six different genres of film, and the backdrops, weapons and enemies fit these sections. There is a slapstick comedy played out in black and white (complete with greyscale background) a cartoon with lots of Road Runnering and goofy facial expressions, a Wild West romp, Sci-Fi complete with aliens, and so on. After each platform level you will have to pass through a film scene - piloting a runaway mine-cart, navigating a scrolling shoot 'em up level, or similar.
Present Drop 1

Can you help Santa deliver all his presents in time? Avoid the rooftops and shoot those presents into the chimneys and pick up treats for your reindeer along the way, which will give you extra time. Avoid the tempting sherry if you want to go fast, it will slow the game down....though slowing down at Christmas time isn't always a bad thing.
Present Drop 2

The sequel to the 2021 Christmas present for the new year! Published in the Amiga Addict issue 17 as the cover disk. Use the Gift-o-matic 5000 to make sure the right presents go to the right homes. No more shooting every present into the chimneys!
Press Fire PONG

Press Fire PONG for Commodore AMIGA 500 isn’t just another Pong clone, it’s a reimagined arcade experience with unique gameplay mechanics and dynamic visual effects. Unlike traditional Pong, in this version, you must move the paddle up or down in a different way: Hold FIRE → paddle moves up, Release FIRE → paddle moves down
Primal Rage

A meteor struck the Earth and caused great chaos. Seven gods from ancient times awoke, and are now attempting to take control of the post-apocalyptic world.

Primal Rage is a one-on-one fighting game featuring dinosaurs and giant apes as the fighters. The graphics are done with digitized stop-motion animation. Gameplay is similar to Mortal Kombat in that it is viewed from a side perspective, and features deadly finishing moves at the end of the match.
Prime Mover

Prime Mover is a motorcycle racing action game, viewed from behind the bike. There are twelve riders and five bikes (with different top speeds, acceleration and handling) to choose from. The full championship includes 12 races against a field of seven riders (computer opponents are loosely named after real riders of the day – Rain Wayney and Lucie Kavanora for example). 

Circuits are set around the world, with various weather effects, with a rendition of each national anthem played on the pre-race screen. Handling is loose and arcadey. It is not possible to fall off – contact with hazards or other bikes simply results in you losing time.
Prime Time

Don't you hate it when your favorite TV show gets cancelled? Prime Time from First Row Software lets you be the moron who cancels all of the intelligent but low-rated TV shows in favor of popular pseudo-dramatic tripe and identical sitcoms. Take on the duties of a TV network executive in this highly unusual simulation game. Pick the shows you want to air, from 160 regular programs and 15 network specials. Plan a schedule, recruit advertisers, bump shows around optimal time slots, but whatever you do, keep the ratings high if you want to keep your job.
Princ Jasoň

A Czech language text adventure based on Jára Cimrman's fairy tale Long, Wide and Short-sighted. As Prince Jason, you must overcome the evil giant Kolodej and save Goldilocks from her lost beauty. Created as freeware by Martin Orlický in 2009.
Prince

In this early medieval real-time strategy war-game, two feuding princes on a small island have it out for each other. The king is dead and his successor must be determined through elimination, 'The Code of Steel'.

At the start of the game you decide upon the size of your army and the island on which the conflict takes place and the objective is to kill the other prince before his army gets yours. Once the setup is over and done with, the armies are put down on the island and the conflict begins. The units can be commandeered at three different levels of granularity, from the prince's banner down to the company, showing each individual soldier. Commands are issued by selecting the company or commander and issuing one of a set number of options to the unit. Once the armies meet they will battle it out until one of the princes is killed, terrain and conditions will affect the outcome of any conflict.

Two player games can be played via a null modem cable on two different computers.
Prince of Persia

The Grand Vizier Jaffar has thrown you into a dark dungeon and plans to marry the girl of your dreams in an hour. You're not going to let that happen are you? Try to escape from the dungeon, take out Jaffar's guards, find your way through the Sultan's palace and defeat Jaffar himself. Now go, you've got 60 minutes!

Prince of Persia is a 2D platformer with run and jump gameplay. Your hero must avoid deadly traps, solve some simple puzzles and engage in sword fights with the guards. The player has an infinite amount of lives, but has to restart at the beginning of a level each time he dies, and must complete the game within an hour. An especially noteworthy aspect of the game is the very fluent animation of your character.
Prince of Persia 2

After having defeated the evil Grand Vizier Jaffar, the brave Prince claimed just one reward: the hand of the beautiful daughter of the Persian Sultan. However, as the Prince approached the palace, his appearance suddenly turned into that of a beggar. Someone who looked just like the Prince ordered to throw him out. It turns out that Jaffar is alive and back for vengeance. Banished from the palace, the unfortunately Prince must travel to faraway lands and find a way to defeat the villain.

Prince of Persia 2 is, like its predecessor, a cinematic platformer. Much of the gameplay is reminiscent of the first game, focusing on precise jumping puzzles, swordfighting, and overcoming many hazards in order to stay alive. Swordfighting is more prominent and features situations where several enemies attack the Prince at once. Reinforcements may arrive after the Prince has eliminated all visible enemies. Like its predecessor, the game must be completed within a time limit.
Prison

An Unforgettable Adventure.
The year is 3033 AD. Criminals are no longer sent to jail, they are sent to the abandoned planet, Altrax. You have been wrongfully convicted of a crime and sent there. A long life is not that likely among the galaxy's worst undesirables. Your only hope is to escape!

On your way to Altrax you learn that a pleasure craft ignored warning beacons and strayed into the electro-security net of Altrax. The craft was wrecked but the tiny escape pod was never found. Your only hope is to find it and escape, unfortunately, criminal gangs are also fighting to the pod.
Prisonnier
A two player AMOS based freeware game created by Off Game in 2015. Game code is available freely on GitHub, but it is a classic game reworked from 8-bit roots.
Prisonnier III
An updated version of the original 2015 game Prisonnier by Off Game in 2020. Based on an old 8 bit game this update added much better graphics and speed.
Prize Fight

the year is 2049 and boxing, wrestling and karate have all mutated into a single sport. See if you can win and grab the cash in the Prize Fight! Programmed in ASM 68k by Powerhouse, this shareware martial arts game was released in 1992. As shareware there was a freely distributed demo, and you could send in to own and play the full game.
Pro Boxing Simulator

On ST and Amiga features a full range of jabs, uppercuts and weaves. All fights take place to realistic WBA rules, as you aim to rise the rankings and fight for the title. The crowd frequently shout encouragement and insults, which are displayed using speech bubbles.

The 8-bit game is a little different, featuring illegal moves such as kicks and groin punches. There is a referee, so you'll have to wait for him to look away before using those moves. Fights last 15 rounds, and a knockout ends that round, not the entire fight.
Pro Gammon
Pro Gammon is a computerized version of the popular board game, Backgammon. It was developed by Kevin Glynn and released into the public domain in 2003.
Pro Poker
A spartan video poker game created by MicroSys and released in 1992.
Pro Powerboat Simulator

If this 'simulator' is to be believed, powerboat racing is a chaotic race across a number of largely one-directional tracks with fjords and inlets forcing you down one of two lanes, and sections where a bridge needs to be cleared by hitting a ramp at the right speed beforehand (as you jump over these, you can land so as to skim off other boats). Your boat is fitted with bombs, which can be placed so as to force the other boats to run over them, gaining you points. Extra bombs and fuel litter the course, often close to the banks, which you must avoid contact with, for fear of crashing your boat. When this happens you are forced into the next one, which is, as if by magic, available at a convenient point just beforehand. A helicopter flies overhead, dropping bombs which you must avoid, and often obscuring your view. The other boats often crowd together attempting to force you into the wall.
Pro Tennis Simulator

This tennis game offers bare-bones action for one or two players. There are 3 computer skill levels on offer, and matches can be 1, 3 or 5 sets. The gameplay is viewed from above and behind the net, with a slight 3D effect. The type of shot played is determined by how high the ball is as you hit it. The full service rules are implemented, and the fire button must be pressed once to throw the ball up, and a second time to hit it with the racket.
Pro Tennis Tour 2

Great Courts 2 is a tennis game and the sequel to Great Courts. You start the game by creating a player and distributing character points, for instance on speed, forehand, backhand etc. The initial skills are raised after winning a few matches. There are different tournaments to choose from, such as all APT tournaments and the Davis Cup. Prize money is provided by doing well in a tournament. The game supports both single and double matches. In the training mode you can play against a ball machine or against a friend. There are different settings to program the ball machine, for instance to practice a certain type of shot. It is also possible to have matches with one player competing against two.
Prodigal Son Adventure

A freeware game from John Filsak and released in 1991 based on a story told by Jesus. You, Taz, are the Prodigal Son. The plot centers around the younger son who, impatient and greedy, asks his father for his inheritance. The father agrees, but the son wastes his money, eventually becoming homeless and destitute. In the end, to the son's great surprise, he is welcomed back into the family by his father and brother. However, based on your choices, your ending may be different.
Professional Bingo

Set up and run your own successful Bingo game in real life. The shareware software allows you to create flyers, betting lines, jackposts, prizes and to present it to a full house and rake in the dough. Released by Dave Brown in 1993.
Professional Football Masters

The sequel to Football Masters, this football management simulation game had many interations, all commercially sold by ESP Software and coded by Simon Rush. The last known and most popular release was version 5.08 in 1994. Data disks for different years including the 96/97 season.
Profezia

Profezia is set sometime during the Middle Ages, in a mountain area between the two Italian regions of Abruzzo and Lazio. The player takes control of a mercenary who has been hired to retrieve a golden crown from the castle of Capistrello, where Duke Attilio intends to use it on an ancient Pagan rite.

Profezia is an adventure game with a multiple-choice interface: as opposed to classic adventures where the player is free to roam around the game world (or part of it), the storyline in Profezia develops automatically. Whenever an action is to be taken, the player is presented with a set of choices, which will affect the rest of the adventure.

It is worth noting that there is no unique path to complete the game: the player may follow alternate branches, provided that the actions which follow are coherent with their previous choices.
ProFlight

ProFlight simulates a Panavia Tornado F Mk3. Through the accompanying 134 page manual, the budding pilot is guided through: an overview of the Tornado and its history, the cockpit functions, flight theory, advanced flying techniques, combat and maneuvers. Added up this gives a indepth insight as to what it takes and feels like to operate and fly the Tornado.

ProFlight aims to incorporate every detail of flight. Accurate taileron, rudder and elevator effects are present at all angles of pitch and roll. You can reach airspeeds of over Mach 2, yet speeds are precise to 0.0006knots, your position within the 200 nautical miles of terrain is accurate to 0.00001ft, and your angle of flight to 0.01 degrees.

You have radar-guided and heat-seeking missiles at your disposal. Gravity and wheel braking have their effects on motion. Waypoint navigation helps you find your way through this vast world, and a full heads-up display brings the crucial information to you.
Project 1

This is "Project 1" for the Commodore Amiga. It was released back in 1988 as a coverdisk for the "Amiga Fun" magazine. The game was developed by Coma programming team.

It is a "River Raid" clone for the Amiga and it is a good one. The graphics are nice, well colored and with enough detail. 
 
The downside of the game is that it is very very hard. It demands pixel perfect control of your ship and it doesn't forgive any mistake. Although the controls are very responsive it is the inertia feature that makes the ship control a difficult job.
Project Battlefield

Project Battlefield is a timed FPP shooter with a main character modelled after Robocop. As a cybernetic police officer the player will face five stages of fight against terrorists and robots, occupying government buildings. Some places may be reached by using teleports, others require the player to find a proper access card or a hidden passage switch. The player may use some objects as shields, such as barrels and containers. The screen size can be adjusted depending on the Amiga power.
Project Buzz Bar

Project Buzz Bar combines gameplay elements from Asteroids and Defender. On each level there are several men to rescue by flying over them. They float loose in space amongst different types of enemy ships, many of which fire at you. Your ship is constantly moving due to a strong gravitational pull from the planet's surface, making it harder to direct the ship at first. The game is written in Blitz BASIC 2, and not only is the source code provided, it scrolls through it on the title screen. The game was released as a coverdisk on The One magazine.
Project Horizon

Project Horizon is an 8-way scrolling top down shooter sci-fi game for Commodore AMIGA. 
The player is a NASA astronaut on the Moon (1977 - alternate timeline) who is find himself in a war situation.
Project Intercalaris

Project Intercalaris is a successor to Project Battlefield. This time, the action takes place on an alien planet. As a scout, the player must deal with the rebellion of alien races, introducing mostly fighting with hostile mechanized units. The game is divided into four stages with the possibility of selecting standard and advanced level area. Using the map requires finding an electronic map. The player may find many useful items scattered around the base. The game features one novelty - an action menu allowing the player to take, view, abandon and use items. A curiosity is the ability to remotely control a robot.

The screen size can be adjusted depending on the Amiga power, additionally it's possible to turn off the floor and ceiling textures.
Project Neptune

Taking on the role of special agent Robert "Rip" Steel, it is up to you to destroy the evil Yellow Shadow's network of undersea mining bases. At the same time, you must protect your own bases from attack. You are in command of a small but powerful submarine, and must work quickly and strategically, if you are to succeed.
Project Quest: Chapter I

Quest is a game from Electric Black Sheep, it is an an 8-way scrolling top down fantasy shooter with a very nice audio-visuals released in 2021. A map-editor will be available with Project Horizon giving you the opportunity to create new maps for the game, which uses standard ABK (gfx or sound bank) used in AMOS and the ability to add new graphics, to create a whole new shooter game if you wish.
Project-T

Released on Power-Disc issue 3.

Although it looks very similar to it, this is NOT another "ordinary" Tetris clone. There are some additional shapes including a W-like shaped tetromino that don't make life as easy for you as with "normal" Tetris.
Project-X

Taking place many years in the future in colonized space, military scientists have disposed of countless, defective military droids on an un-colonized terrestrial planet called Ryxx. The droids eventually become sentient and, by way of revenge, start an attack against mankind, using a station to continually create more war machines. It is the player's mission to undergo Project X and eliminate the droid forces.
Project-X (Revised Edition)

Project-X (Revised Edition) is a slightly enhanced version of Project-X, and was released by Team 17 at a budget price in 1993. Release of this enhanced version was mostly prompted by customer feedback that the difficulty level of the original (particularly level 2) was too high. Enhancements include:

- Inclusion of a rookie mode allowing players making easier to progress to later levels

- Starting the game with a better ship

- Shortened levels

- Removal of some extremely difficult passages of play from game levels

- Reducing the amount of disk swapping by fitting the game on 3 disks instead of the original edition's 4 disks
Projectyle

Projectyle is a single or multiplayer (1 to 3 players) hockey-type sports game of the future. It features smooth-scrolling, frantic action, colorful graphics and digital music.

A total of five goal rooms, arranged in the shape of a cross, are connected with tunnels. The camera smoothly follows the puck/ball (the "projectyle") and scrolls to the adjacent rooms when entering one of the connecting tunnels. Each player, whether computer-controlled or not, has a room in which his own goal is located (their "defense" zone.) A fourth room -- the Frantic Zone -- contains a goalmouth for each player, while the central room, where action begins, allows access to the four other rooms.

The object of the game is for each player to protect their own goal while trying to bring the puck/ball into the other players' rooms to score a goal.
Projekt Prometheus

Projekt Prometheus is a German text adventure with graphics. It is set in 2012 directly after the explosion of a nuclear plant. The only way to get rid of the radioactivity is to fetch a resource only available in space. Unfortunately the whole crew of the space ship was killed by a plague and only one man, a journalist, remains. He has to figure out the space ship controls and solve puzzles, e.g. dealing with a contaminated command console.

The player communicates with the game by typing in commands with the keyboard and reading the game's text descriptions. However, the player can associate often used orders to the function keys. The icon bar, controlled with the mouse, offers additional functions or notifications, e.g. a compass which is used to leave a room, switching between text and graphics (not available for all rooms) or a mini map of the space ship.
Proker
A professional style pub poker game with statistics created by Christian Warren and released in 1992.
Property Market
An AMOS based property management simulation created by Martin Warne and released as freeware in 1990.
Prophecy I: The Viking Child

Welcome to Odin's world. A land full of good and evil, within which you must become Brian, The Viking Child, whose heroics have been foretold by the prophets and recorded in the oracle of the gods. But there's trouble in the land that you live in... Your family and friends are being held on the astral plane, imprisoned by the forces of darkness in an effort to foil the prophecy and install chaos throughout the land...

As Brian, your adventure in Prophecy 1 - The Viking Child will take you through many beautiful, but dangerous places, where you'll encounter great adversaries. Amongst these will be the eight apprentices of evil, slaves to the Dark Lord Loki, who will force you to fight or question your purpose under threat of punishment or penalty. Friendly shopkeepers will sell you items of worth, that will aid you on your quest. There are sixteen levels, each with its own backgrounds, enemies, and items. There are even puzzle elements similar to Bitmap Brothers' classic Gods.
ProSoccer 2190

ProSoccer 2190 is set in the future in which soccer tournaments are mix between real-life outdoor and indoor soccer. The most important difference to outdoor soccer is that there is no out because the ball bounces back from the indoor walls. The three other changes are the different match division (four quarters à 15 minutes), a time-out system and that the athletes wear American Football helmets.

The player takes control of one of 16 fictional teams and, depending on the team's origin, participates in either the American or European league. The winners of each league fight for the championship. During the matches, the player either controls the athlete with the ball when in offense or switches between athletes when in defense. When starting a shot, the game switches to "kick mode" in which the player needs to position the cursor in a box. Depending on the position, this changes the power, swerve and elevation of the shot.
Prospector in the Mazes of Xor

Xor involves guiding two characters through 15 complex mazes to collect all the balloons within a move limit. Hazards such as boulders, volatile ducks and teleports make this harder.

In this update, 15 new levels have been added. The characters are now called Herb and Pip. A full level designer is also included.
Protector

Protector is a split-screen horizontal side-view shooter where one or two players try to carry supplies to their base before bombing the other players base to win the game. You are a trainee at the US Army Helicopter Training School based in Fort Rucker, and to graduate as a helicopter pilot you must complete this final mission. Scattered around the area are supplies, and flying left or right, you must take them one at a time back to your base while the other player does the same. your helicopter is armed with a 30mm gatling cannon, with limited ammo, to shoot the other player and you must keep an eye on your fuel levels as well. Landing on your base places any supplies carried and you can re-arm and re-fuel as well. If you are shot while carrying supplies then the supplies are dropped and you lose part of a damage gauge. If you run out of fuel, take too much damage or crash then you go back to your base.
Protector (Paradox)

Protector takes the idea from Defender: the player is controlling a ship over a horizontally scrolling landscape, able to fly to the left and right with different speed. Some residents of the planet are standing on the floor, with alien ships trying to kidnap them. The player has to prevent that by destroying all the enemy ships first. This can be done with the laser cannon or smart-bombs. If all enemies in a level are destroyed the level is finished. A radar helps to keep track of the enemies in the level.
Prototype

A cross-hairs military shooter with a Special Forces theme. Prototype is a crosshair shooter in the style of Operation Wolf. The graphics and gameplay are surprisingly decent. Sampled speech is a nice touch. I also like the weather effects and the gore. The shooting sounds could be improved, as could the intermission screens. 
 
The first mission is to destroy your enemy's communications tower and progress to the city.
ProTris
A shareware Tetris clone for your desktop with Beavis and Butthead samples created by Mirage in 1993. Play Tetris to the giggles and grunts of the zany duo.
Prudent Dactyl
An AMOS based, Czech language, freeware game by Hologram from 1999. A complete remake of the rather strange prehistoric text game ported from the 8-bit Atari.
Pseudo-Cop

Eventually released as a homebrew game, this Robocop inspired shooter came to most people's attention via a playable demo in 1989. The feel of a beat-em up but with scads of bullets flying everywhere. The Robocop project was taken off line after several fundamental errors were discovered during the "Live Situation" tests. OCP Spokesperson said that the project was neither reliable nor effective in certain situations. It has been noted that the biological side was no longer correctly interfacting with the loyalty\command circuits and Robocop had become a liability. Three years later in a joint OCP\military operation, the new edition 209 Mk2 cop was put on the streets and has been put into service. A fully armored, fighting machine to protect the innocent, and serve the public trust of upholding the law. You are ED 209 Mk2 you are.... Pseudo-Cop!
Pssst

Unofficial conversion and upgrade based on the ZX Spectrum game. Growing the best Thyrgodian Megga Chrisanthodil possible is the sole purpose of Robbie the Robot. When insects invade his garden, he has to stop them ruining his work. He has a canister of insect repellent, a smoke-bomb and a startling streamer, each placed on walls at the side of his garden. Each will stun any particular vermin, but you will need to find out exactly what kills what.

As the plant grows, aided by the timely addition of compost bags, leaves will start to shoot outwards. The more leaves there are, the quicker it will grow (a simple incorporation of the concept of photosynthesis being boosted by having more sunlight absorbed), so don't let the bugs near it - those whose programmed movement path takes them towards an existing leaf should be your priority. Once the plant is high enough, it flowers and you move onto another level, where increasingly tough foes are on the prowl.
Psyborg

You are a psyborg named Duncan Norton, who must travel through the vortex from a space vessel trapped in a galaxy very far from Earth. An alien race is threatening to take over 38 planets and you've got to stop them. 

Starting from Anacreon, you will mentally pass through the Krypton, Kalgan, Zorgon, Terminus, Trantor, and finally Sol systems. Each stellar system has a certain number of planets, which you will traverse from one to another. 

The game is a first-person virtual reality race, where you run as fast as possible on the tiles that are formed in a pentagonal prism. At the starting point you accelerate, and then change the facets of the prism in order to avoid falling through the gaps. When the tile's path spirals, you may decelerate your velocity. Time runs out, and you must refill your time meter by standing on tiles marked with a "T". Standing on certain tiles that are marked with shapes of different blinking colors will give you a different amount of points.
Psycheual
Each level is a maze to be navigated through while fighting off hordes of aliens. Navigate the space station as a lone marine shooting alien creatures and collecting keys, health packs and ammo.
Psycho

Psycho is a graphic adventure game with a key-based verb interface.

A set of jewels has been stolen. At the time of the theft, a curator was with the jewels, so he got stolen, too. And who's the suspect? Norman Bates, of course. The next night, a daring detective drives out to the sinister Bates Motel. His plan: a) find the jewels, b) free the curator and c) take a nice hot shower, should time suffice.

Psycho is entirely controlled with the keyboard: direction keys for moving your character around, shortcut keys for performing actions. You need to stand close to an interesting object in order to examine it. Adversaries will appear at random throughout the house, putting you to sleep by touch and thus draining your precious time -- you've only got four hours to solve the case. You may shoot the enemies as soon as you find a weapon. As there is no other option for character interaction, this is how you'll deal with the Bates family as well.
Psycho Path
Published in the October 1997 issue of AmigaMagazine OnDisk #93. One of the final issues.
Psycho Santa
Exclusively published on disk A of THE ONE issue 52 in January 1993. The game itself is shareware; an enhanced version was sold commercially.
Psycho Squares Deluxe
A puzzle game where you slowly reveal the picture hidden below. The game does have it's fair share of nude and scantily clad females.
Psycho Toad

In this freeware shooter by Cult in 1990 your mission is to destroy all Bazookabears in the slime. On level one it is a vertically scrolling shooter where you fly to the Slimezone and must avoid Red-Acid-Cloud and can avoid or shoot enemy missiles. On level 2 it is a crosshairs shooter you blast the Bazookabears just aim for thier Bazo for best results.
Psycho Ward!

An Amiga freeware point and click and text adventure game made by Robert Sedler in 1994. The text adventure Psycho Ward is a surreal dark comedy set in a mental institution. The main character is a nameless patient, driven to escape the institution, who seizes their chance by falling down a laundry chute into the basement while the nurses aren't looking.

Psycho Ward was created using the Dream Weaver authoring system (not to be confused with Adobe Dreamweaver). The interface is similar to adventure games produced by Legend Entertainment in the early 1990s such as Spell casting 101 and Eric the Unready, where about a quarter of the screen is used to show the actual game text, then there is a small static picture of the current scene (shown from first-person perspective), and the rest of the screen is filled with helpful GUI gadgets that the player can use instead of manually typing in commands.
PsychoBlast

In PsychoBlast, a crosshairs shooter from Team Manga and released to PD in 1997, you have to protect a circle in the middle from the onslaught of a large variety of wiggling sprites. Shoot them all before they touch that precious shape!
Psychoblast (Ordyh Software)

This is Psychoblast from 1993 by Ordyh Software (This Game was given away with the special version of SEUCK distributed with CU Amiga Magazine) and was otherwise sold as Shareware. 

It is a one screen game, where you remain in the middle of this over-powering blue screen, you remain inside a box and just have to shoot out towards enemies such as Dice and Triangles and other flashing enemies what appear. You have a counter top-left what counts down from 999, and your score is as usual centre bottom of the screen. There are also decent sound effects as well, not a bad Game to play, But quite challenging due to the limited play area you have.
PT-45
A commercially released horizontally scrolling nautical shooter created by Oscarsoft using the SEUCK engine and released by Pactronics in 1989.
PTC

PTC is similar to the C64 game Centepede. PTC is an Action game, developed and published by Rainbow Arts, which was released in Europe in 1987, it was included on the compilation: Magic Seven. P. T. C. stands for "PEN TI CEDE", which is an anagram of "CENTIPEDE", a 1980 Atari arcade classic where the game idea was taken from. As another side-note, "Centipede" was the first ever video game designed by a woman: Dona Bailey.
Furthermore, in level 4, there is also a reverence shown for pioneer video game designer JEFF MINTER, by deliberately using his "trademark" camel for the enemies' sprites.
Pub Darts

Official game readme file by Bryan Black:
 Picture this: Saturday night, pub`s closed, nowhere to play darts and drink lots of brown booze. But not booze for t` baby. Solution: Play Pub Darts!! and hence forth bequeath supreme knowledge through Jimmy Nail`s Adidas bag. From this bag shall reach an arm that shall reach up the central aisle and from this hand shall reach two fingers, one with the face of Jimmy Saville and the other hence begat Jimmy Hill, this finger shall reach forth and touch someone on the forehead and he shall be the new messiah who will forthwith give birth....
Pub Trivia

A Polish freeware pub trivia quiz intended to have the questions come from the computer and have viewers answer on paper or by calling it out and then get the answers and scoring from the computer, so the number of users\teams is infinite the way the game is played. The game has difficulty settings, the ability to set sound responses and prompts, record and score keeping and to set up team names and information.
Pub Trivia Simulator

Pub Trivia Simulator is a game that attempts to simulate an Arcade Quiz Machine found in public houses. The idea is to move up a pyramid answering questions on various subjects to reach the top so you can attempt another pyramid but for money. Before you start the game you can select how many players (1-4), which question block to load (1-3) and which avatar for your player.

The game costs 10p and you select a square on the bottom row of the pyramid with various categories. When you have selected your question you then move to a new screen and press the start button. The question appears with the choice of three answers and you must answer before a timer reaches zero and if you get it correct you receive points and move back to the pyramid screen. You pick a new question on a new row and one that is touching the square you last answered. If you get it wrong and you are on the bottom row of the first pyramid you can try again but get it wrong at any other time and it is game over.
Pucman Worlds

Game design by Petri Häkkinen and Olli Hänninen-Pelz. Coding in AMOS by Petri Häkkinen. Graphics by Olli Hänninen-Pelz. Music/sound FX by Petri Häkkinen. Game includes a map editor allowing players to create their own levels. Pucman Worlds is a collect-and-avoid maze game inspired by Pac-Man, written in AMOS and released Christmas 1994.
Puffy's Saga

Puffy and his fortuitously-named girlfriend Puffyn are trapped in an alien world full of threats, traps and surprises. Taking control of one or the other (Puffy is more powerful but Puffyn can move faster) you must find your way through.

Puffy's Saga is an overhead view maze game that represents a cutesy variant of Gauntlet. Each of the 20 levels has a quota of dots to eat before the level is completed. These levels are inhabited by foes who surround you and reduce your energy on contact. Meat restores 100 energy points each time - this total can go beyond its starting level of 500. You are armed with a gun, which not only kills foes but also turns many of them into edible energy-giving snacks.
Puggles
A supercharged Q-Bert or Pogo Joe published in the Amiga Power 9 (January 1992) coverdisk 9b, created in 1991 by William Bell.
Puggsy

Puggsy is a platform game with a combination of action and puzzle-solving elements. You control the the creature Puggsy, who has crash landed on an alien planet and had his spaceship stolen. Your goal is find the spaceship so you can get off the planet and return home. To do this, you will need to make your way from the start to the exit of numerous levels which take place in a variety of environments. Throughout each level are a variety of objects which you can pick up; on many of the levels you will need to figure out how to use the objects available to you in order to reach the exit. Some objects can be used (like a gun or keys), and objects may be thrown, moved around and stacked. Of course, each level will also have a variety of bad guys wandering about which will cost Puggsy one of his lives if he's caught. On your quest there will also be six evil guardians which will need to be defeated before you get your spaceship back!
Pulsar

Pulsar is a side scrolling shoot 'em up similar to R-Type. As a fighter pilot the player moves constantly in the right side fighting with numerous waves of hostile creatures and objects. Contact with any object or enemy means a loss of life. The ammo is unlimited. At the end of each level mega boss appears, guarding the passage to the next planet.
Pulsator

An unreleased horizontally scrolling space shooter created by Fullspeed Creative Development in 1997. On planet Aktris the Tektrons have one of their biggest station of producing Warships, it must be destroyed. 96% of the planet surface is water so keep your ship dry fighting these ocean-based aliens.
Pump Up The Volume
A puzzle game similar to games like Pipemania for the Commodore Amiga
Punkt Punkt Punkt

This is a conversion of a former german TV-Show. The rainbow-ball was the logo of the channel Sat.1 in the nineteens.Blessed with Thomas Heinrich's consistently creepy character art. This was the very last release by from PCSL.
Punter

Want to play the ponies? You start the game with £10,000 and through various options: betting, selling or buying horses and making and taking loans you can make a ton! Lots of horses, jockeys, courses to check, distances and conditions to take into account. High strategy for short riders.
Puppy Love

Puppy Love is an early example of a virtual pet simulator. The player becomes the owner of a puppy that has just been rescued from life in a junkyard. The puppy dreams of winning ribbons and trophies at a dog show and it's the player's task to train it up to do so.

When starting out the puppy will run around the player's front yard and doing tricks on its own. After it has done a specific action the player can press the spacebar and name it. When the name thereafter is typed in the puppy will attempt to do it again. The player can then reward the puppy for doing it right by giving it a bone and it will then eventually learn it. When a few tricks have been learned it is possible to create choreographed routines. This is done through a built in programming language using simple English sentences where the player types in plain text which tricks each routine should contain and how they should be performed.
Purple Saturn Day

Every 4 galactic-years, alien athletes from every inhabited planet in the galaxy gather to compete in the Purple Saturn Day games. Four interplanetary events await the player: Pilot a ship through time and space, race around the rings of Saturn, solve a fast-moving electronic puzzle and navigate a futuristic obstacle course.

Although not an official entry in the series, this game is in the same vein as Epyx's popular Games "series" titles.
Pursuit to Earth

Pursuit to Earth is a shoot-'em-up game in the tradition of single-screen shooters in which the player controls a space craft defending himself against waves of approaching enemy formations. Like in the arcade game Gyruss, the player moves along a circle around the centre of the screen, and moving left and right on the circular path. The playfield is three-dimensional, with the player's ship firing to the distance. Enemies are approaching from behind the player or from the depth of the screen, but contact with alien ships does not do any harm. The aliens are also firing bullets, which are instantly deadly to the player, bringing the ship back to the Hyperspace portal.

During the fight red pills are flying from the depth of the playfield, which should be collected to be traded for extra weapons. Those contain speed buffs, missiles, shields and satellites.
Push
A Soko Ban style 2D puzzler commercially released by the infamous Courbois Software publishing house.
Push 'n' Shove
Push 'n' Shove is an Amiga puzzle brain game released in 1995. A Sokoban clone with elements borrowed from other games.
Push It II
Push It II is a Puzzle game, developed and published by Media GmbH, which was released in Europe in 1994. Also released as part of the Fun Games compilation of 11 games.
Push n' Pull

Fun little game similar to the Pengo games. You must push blocks to kill the enemies and such small levels produce nerves! It's an original concept.

At least 3 versions of this game exists. The only difference between the versions seems to be in which order the levels appears.
Push-Over

You're playing a small ant that is willing to help a friend in rather inconvenient situation. Apparently, your friend, doggie, likes to eat cookies that has his picture on their box, and he got himself so carried away that he lost the balance, and a bag of cookies fell deep down into an ant-hill. Now, you're goin' in, in a mission of solving puzzles, and retrieving the cookies for your friend.

Now, this ant-hill is a bit different from the ones you saw, and especially from the one you live in. It's path is filled up with boulders, and all the gates, and you must travel the quest to find the cookies. After each different place inside, you'll fins a small bag of cookie, and bring it back to your friend doggie.
Pushem

Pushem is a game that requires a lot of creativity and creativity from the players requires forward thinking. The player must, if he wants to solve levels, PUSH red balls onto target squares. At the same time he can just push ONE ball. A level is considered solved when every target field is occupied by a ball. Another nice sliding game from the 'Sokoban'- Genre for many hours of fun.The game came with a built in level editor.
PushPush

There are two versions of this shareware puzzle game by A-Heart Software creators Luigi Recanatese, Stefano Tamascelli and Riccardo Santato. One a 10 level demo\preview version and a full version with many more levels.
Pussy Quest 1: A Weekend in the Bush1

A sexually explicit text adventure with more than mildly misogynistic themes and some outright racism thrown in with a poorly spelled story, all created by the aptly named Sick Minds Software and unleashed on the world in 1992.
Putter

Your goal on every level is to knock the potato into the hole marked by a flag. Only potato is vulnerable for the enemies and terrain obstacles.Frog steering by the player can walk through spikes, electricity and enemies with no harm. Remember, you can always restart the level by pressing the Return key on your keyboard. If you want some extra points, try to hit stars with the potato and eat flies with your frog. You can move your character left, right, up (jump, swimming and climbing the ladder) or down if you are under water. You can high kick potato using direction and Fire button or low kick using direction plus down (down-right or down-left) and Fire button. Of Course you can always push the potato, which can be the best option sometimes.
Putty

In Putty, the player controls a blue blob with eyes. Putty has many moves that he could use to attack enemies or to navigate around the level. These abilities include being able to stretch out upwards, downwards, left and right to access far-off ledges. He also has the ability to inflate. This allows him to provide a cushioned landing for any falling bots. Over-inflation also acts as a "smart bomb", with Putty bursting, killing all of the enemies on the screen, whilst reducing his health in the process.

Putty is able to form part of himself into a fist, allowing him to punch left or right to dispatch enemies.

Putty is also able to melt into the floor, making him invulnerable and also allowing him to absorb enemies, recovering a small amount of health in the process. With certain enemies in the game, such as the clockwork orange, once Putty has absorbed one he is then able to morph into the enemy's shape to use its abilities.
Putty Squad

The C.I.A. has formed a crack covert team to parachute into hostile areas and rescue the Putty M.I.A.s. The team consists of Super Putty and his one time enemy Dweezil the Ginger Cat. They must also terminate the rogue Commander Napalm the Cat who having gone crazy has set himself up as a god to the native population of spotted frogs in the area. This is their mission and they must not fail or the Putty M.I.A.s are doomed.
PuzCat

Game deliberately made in the style of an 8-bit game, for some imaginary 8-bit machine. Except the music, which was a placeholder for some suitably bleepy chip tune. The aim of this game while playing as a Cat is to eat all the mice in a level before moving onto the next through each exit door. Be careful though as throughout each level there are dogs that if touched will kill you and you will lose a life. However PuzCat isn't weak and can push blocks to squash the dogs or enable you to jump over them when properly placed.
Puzlex
Shoot various baddies coming towards you. You must shoot the enemy that is the same colour as you. A shareware puzzle shooter, created with AMOS and released by AIM Design in 1997.
Puzzle
A 20 tile scramble of a scene that you must slide to fix, like a 15 puzzle with a few more squares. Released November 25, 2017 by Pozo at the Capacitor 2017 Game Competition.
Puzzle 3.0

An AMOS based freeware puzzle game from MAGE software in 1994. This single player 15 puzzle game was dedicated to Anna Bartosiak and challenged you to solve each randomized puzzle in as few moves as possible.
Puzzle Bobble

This is the first game from the neogeo hardware/taito system B ported to the Amiga 1200 !
A native 680X0 assembly port, designed to take advantage of the AGA chipset and the Amiga 1200’s stock processor.
Puzzle Me
Slide the 19 piece mixed up puzzle to create the full image. A Shareware game created by Delf Schlüter and released in 1993.
Puzzle Slide

Puzzle slide 
Created by Ze Emulatron from Lee Hurley productions in 2011 use a joystick in port 2 to move the pieces in the puzzle. The tile pieces used in this game were made in deluxe paint iii and can be replaced. They are named t1 image, t2_image etc. There is an example t1 on the disk that is the correct size. The files have to be converted with ifftrans that is from compute's second book of amiga, it has been included as ifftrans.Bas. The palette used in this game is in the file palette_colours. Each line has 3 values, red, green, blue.
Puzzle Wizard

Fill the 15 pieces and create the picture in this freeware game by Ali T. Ozer of Kronos Digatal in 1987. Put the picture back together from the pieces. To grab a piece, move the mouse over it and click the left button. To rotate a piece (90 degrees CW) first grab it, then click the right button. To see what the full picture looks like, choose the SHOW option from the menu. To see how close you are to the solution, choose the CHECK option.
Many thanks go to: D. John Hodgson (for the small IFF reader), Tom Rokicki (for the bitmap rotations), and Helene (Lee) Taran (for the popup menus & her many suggestions). R.A.F. Spreading Service (Rome) for Mak Soft.
Puzznic

The challenge in each level of Puzznic is to manoeuvre a selection of blocks into place so as to clear them all, by making them make contact with blocks of the same design. You control a cross-hair, which can move a block left or right, which can cause it to fall if there is no block under the space it would occupy.

There are many complications in terms of solving the levels. Moving platforms meaning that you need to move a block at a particular time, or in particular order, to prevent them being blockaded. In some situations there are an odd number of a certain type of block - solving these requires positioning two of the blocks one space apart, such that a move will result in a piece making contact with two others, and immediately removing all three. You will also encounter blocks positioned on platforms suspended in space and gaps in level arrangements meaning that a certain number of blocks must be in place to make a certain move possible (by forming a stack, for example).
Puzzword
Solve the puzzle by matching the picture in the bottom left of the screen. You must slide letters to match. A 1992 shareware AMOS game from N. J. Harris.
Pyramax

In Pyramax, the player takes the role of an explorer on the search of the Thaalian crystal, a priceless artifact from a long extinguished race. This crystal is at the top of a six-level pyramid which naturally has to be conquered first. Each level consists of a number of rooms which have to be solved in a linear order by activating a touchstone. So the player walks through the rooms in a top-down perspective while dodging the enemies - contact causes the life meter to go down and an empty bar results in losing a live. Picking up power ups rewards bonus points, health refreshments, extra lives or smart bombs.
Pyramide

Strategy game in the style of "Kaiser". The aim of the game is to build a pyramid. To do this you can buy/sell boats, camels and slaves etc. It is always displayed how far the pyramid is already finished. Created in AmigaBasic by Martin Jochimczyk in 1990.
Pyro-mid
A game written entirely in Blitz BASIC. Take part in this maze game. Shoot bad guys and collect various items. Game supports Amiga 4-button joystick.
Pythagoras

A German language strategy game created by Marc Fischlin in 1990 (with version 2.0 coming out a year later). Pythagoras is a trading game where 1-4 players try to qualify as king of their city. It takes place around 550 BC. At the time of the colonization of the Mediterranean region. The player has many options for action: he can trade, distribute lands, fighting wars, levy taxes, plunder towns, buy or sell ships, buy land, etc. Almost the entire game can be controlled with the mouse.
Q-Bic

Q-bic is loosely based upon the arcade classic. Fuzzball (AKA Q*Bert) and has been written by Ronald Weeserik. Ronald's no stranger to writing classic games on the Amiga and a few of his smashes are Silkworm, SWIV and Rodland.

The idea is to guide a blobby little sprite around a three dimensional pyramid by hopping from square to square and lighting up all the cubes in the structure. It all sounds very simple, but Ronald has included some devious nasties to compete with your sprite. Bubbles roll down the pyramid from top to bottom, whilst other similarly-shaped creatures may roll down and move from side to side.

Amazingly, Weeserik has chosen to release Q-bic onto the bulletin board circuit, and is not hoping to make any money out of the venture. Game is released as a Coverdisk on CU Amiga disk 41.
Qatbol

In Qatbol the player is in control over a one-screen level which represents a real-life wooden board. Just like a real board, the player can change its angle in all directions. The reason to do so is a little ball which is also on the board and its movement corresponds to the board movements. The player has to solve objectives which change from level to level, e.g. collecting things on the board or moving the ball into a hole. Of course there are also obstacles like teleports, holes or mazes.
Qattro

When it comes to games of skill with a touch of tinkering, the simplest game ideas are usually the most ingenious - they say. man. But it is also said that every rule has its exceptions. Unfortunately, Silverbyte's dull "Kugelei" is such an exceptional case... 

The playing surface of Quattro consists of nothing but individual squares with different properties: some only allow the character (a small ball) to move horizontally, others only vertically; in later levels there are still dangerous killer fields. There are also malicious aliens, but also cute little barrels that give the lord of the ball extra life and extra time. Well, and what is the inclined player supposed to do with all that splendor? Nothing more than being in defiance of all the different special and special properties of the various fields.
QBall

QBall is a 1 - 2 player arcade 3-D billiards game for multiple systems.

The player plays billiards within a cube, where each corner represents the 8 separate pockets. The player aligns there shots with the white ball, and each player takes turns trying to place their shot. There is a 60 second shot clock, and the player can rotate the cube to examine the play area.
Qball II
Move the three balls so they are in a row, all the while using blocks and balls to keep the monsters at bay. 20 levels of fun created by B Kraeuter and released in 1989.
Qboid

Shoot your way through 5 increasingly difficult screens. Make blocks disappear by firing blocks at them. When they become cubes or cuboids they vanish. When you complete a stop block, the blocks will stop scrolling for 5 seconds. Tetris, mixed with a shooter and literally turned on it's head.
Qix

In this game, you guide a marker which must draw rectangles and other weird objects in order to claim your territory, and you can either draw these rectangles fast or slow. Drawing the rectangles using the "slow" method awards you the most points. Once a rectangle has been made, it will be colored in to show that you have claimed your territory. While drawing the rectangles, you need to watch out for Qix (pronounced "kicks"), a series of colored lines that crawl the screen. In addition to Qix, you also need to avoid the Sparks who travel around the border, as well as any lines that you have made, as well as The Fuse, who travels along the line that you are drawing. Once you have claimed enough territory, you proceed to the next level.
Quackers

Gather up the fruit for score and the keys to move to the next level, avoid the roaming baddies. When you get the proper keys the way out will open. Quackers is a freeware game created by Michael Pratt in 1990.
Quadralien

Quadralien is a real-time puzzle game in the tradition of Sokoban.

The future: Mankind's space stations throughout the solar system are powered by a huge space reactor, called Astra. Astra is about to break down. The enemy race of Quadraliens has captured the reactor; now, contamination is rising and total failure is imminent. The last chance are six remotely controlled droids, which are to clean Astra and destroy the Quadrailen mother in Astras core.

You're controlling two robots in each of the 19 levels, cleaning up the contamination on your way. Gameplay is a variation of Sokoban: You've got to push spheres in the right direction to clear the way. However, the spheres are magnetically charged, meaning that they repell or attract each other. You've got to consider chain reactions. 

Before entering a level, you may chose which robots to take with you.
Quadranoid

A charityware release, where the author desires you support a specific charity in order to own the game. The game is a breakout\Arkanoid clone whose author is Alexander Gebers and it was released in 1992.
Quadrel

Quadrel is a puzzle game in which you must fill each piece of the selected layout with different colored paints, without painting two adjacent pieces the same color.

At the beginning of a game, you can select the desired image or layout, as well as whether you wish to play with unlimited time or not. You can also select the "Imposed" game mode, in which the game points which piece you must fill next. Each layout has a set amount of paint available for use, in four different colors: red, green, blue and yellow. The amount of brush stokes left for each color is indicated on your palette. Some layouts have a large amount of a particular color and a very small amount of another, while other layouts have a more even amount of each color. The goal is to plan well from the start, so as to avoid running out of a particular color that will be needed to finish the layout.

The game can be played in solitaire mode, against the computer, or against another human player on the same screen.
Quadriga

QUADRIGA is based on the timeless game idea of ​​getting four stones in a matrix into a straight line faster than your opponent. You might be able to beat your opponent, but can you beat the computer? 
 
Game is included on Amiga Spiele 1.
Quadrix

Quadrix is your perfect everyday "Finger Workout Game". Move QUADS around the board using the free cell. Try to get same color QUADS into winning shapes:

* 4 QUADS forming a square
* 6 QUADS in line (horizontal, vertical or diagonal)
* 4 QUADS on board corners

Try to achieve this quickly! If the time indicator reaches the end, some of your QUADS will get locked (you can't move them anymore). But don't worry! You can always form a winning shape with those QUADS and they will get unlocked. You are sometimes awarded BONUS QUADS:

* Time Freeze (freeze time for 30 seconds)
* Unlocker (unlocks QUADS colored like the current shape)
* X5 Bonus (the score for the current shape is multiplied by 5)

FEATURES
* Colorful graphics
* Fun sound effects
* Optional voice effects
* Background music
* Saves game state

This game is recommended for fans of puzzle games such as Trism or Bejewled.

Try to build your own strategy! Good luck!
Quake

An enemy with the codename ''Quake'', which is believed to come from another dimension, is using teleporter gates to invade Earth. The player takes the role of a nameless soldier who arrives at his base only to find out Quake has overrun it and killed everyone. Somewhere in the base there must be a teleporter to Quake's realm. The mission is clear: take the fight to the enemy, overcoming countless hordes of monsters, and exact revenge.

id Software's followup to Doom and Doom II, Quake is a first-person shooter. Its main technological innovation is the use of a true 3D engine - the levels themselves as well as the enemies are polygonal. This not only allows for more natural level designs and character animations, but also for more realistic lighting and the inclusion of simulated physics that have an effect on gameplay: grenades can bounce off walls and around corners, for example.
Quake II

A sequel in name only, this follow up to id’s 1996 Quake, is a first-person shooter revolving around the Earth-Strogg war. The Strogg alien race threatens the Earth, but Earth has launched a counter-offensive, Operation Alien Overlord. Overlord takes the battle to the Strogg homeworld with the ultimate objective of securing their capital city and killing their ruler.

As a FPS, Quake II contains a variety of weapons including the fall back Blaster, the Railgun, and the secret BFG10K. Health, armor, and ammunition pick-ups can be found during levels, as can the classic Quake’s Quad Damage power-up. Game play involves mowing down alien opponents as the player progresses through levels, completing in-game objectives. Quake II also comes with multiplayer support for Deathmatches.
Quantox

Quantox actually turned out to be rather good. The game is a dead simple shoot 'em up game with Jeff Minter overtones, but it's fast, smooth, slick and pretty, and it kept me entranced for ages. Lots of little bonus games stop it from getting repetitive, and even the power-ups have a touch of imagination about them. In fact, I'd go so far as to say that this is one of the most original blasters I've seen in a long time (in 1988). This has to represent, then, something of a major bargain.
Quantum
A single player puzzle game by Ben and Emma James that was released as shareware in 1993
Quaptos

Quaptos is a timed puzzle board game. The goal of the game is to arrange an identical pattern in the second window within five minutes. Solving the task allows uncovering one part of prize picture. The screen is divided into three parts. Part one shows the information (points, remaining time, level code). Bottom window shows a pattern, which must be repeated in the upper window. Every square brick has a digit on it - initially "one". Each placed next to it brick increases the number by one point. After reaching the number "four" the brick number returns to "one". The bricks may be deleted at any time - in the reverse order of their placement on the board (last brick disappears first).

After each completed board the player receives a level code. The game allows to choose one of three available backgrounds.
Quartz

Quartz is a shoot 'em up with a variety of sections. The first section (and every odd-numbered one) is viewed from above and scrolls in every direction. As well as standard attack waves, there are large red/blue/yellow balls which split on impact a lá Asteroids, and once the smallest ones are destroyed they release tokens. Once you have collected 9 of each, you can choose a power-up form a range including various weapons, restart points (which effectively gives infinite continues when used with an emulator's 'snapshot' feature) and repairs to the ship. Destroying the whole of standard waves gives combined tokens which add one to each of the three colours.

The even-numbered waves scroll in a single direction, but include waves coming at you from other directions, even from within the screen in 3D. You can have up to 3 power-ups stored on your ship at a time, and choose one to activate by pressing F1-F3 - they all have limited firepower.
Quasar

Quasar is a horizontally scrolling shoot 'em up where the player's task is to retrieve the stolen Eye of Quasar. To do so he has access to three star class five space ships that are equipped with ion shields that can absorb some damage before being destroyed. The default weapon of the craft is a pulse cannon but by collecting star mines it can be upgraded into, multi, laser and missile weapons. At the same time it's necessary to avoid tractor mines which can be deactivated by fire. The game consists of five different sectors that the player has to fly through. Many different obstacles will have to be navigated past, including meteor showers, sun corridors, underground caverns, acid seas and ice barriers. There will also be enemies in form of guardians which can only be destroyed by shooting at their power globes.
Quasar Wars

Quasar Wars is a special kind of shoot 'em up because even if you will control a spaceship, here you will have complete freedom of movements (Thunder Force 1-like) unlike other games in which the scroll constantly "pushes" you to the right or to the top of the screen. To finish the game you will have to complete 16 missions spread over three worlds. But then again, not all of them will be the typical "kill them all" kind of missions you see in most shooters, since sometimes these will just be about recollecting certain number of capsules, or planting a bomb somewhere in the map. Of course, there will also be missions in which you have to kill everything that moves. Between missions, you can also select the items to equip on your spaceship or the weapons to use.
Quasarius

Quasarius is a Galaga clone with a pleasantly fast framerate. Just like in Galaga, gameplay can be broken down into three phases: In the first one, you fight a number of enemies ships. In Quasarius, their formation changes slightly each level and there is only a single type of enemy ship. In the second phase, you fight a boss, a larger enemy ship. There is just a single boss type in Quasarius. Lastly, you fly through a danger zone, evading asteroids and other space debris while trying to pick up bonus points.
QuasaurusX

A simple space invaders clone, each kill drops a green tokens that increase the score multiplier. Bonus enemies can also be killed for additional point bonuses. Boss levels to allow progress to the next wave.
Quasi

In each screen, move the Quasimodo over the battlement of the castle to the upper right and ring the bell. Enemies will try to stab you and shoot projectiles at you that you must avoid. A PD game created by Paul Young and released in 1993.
Quatro
Is a board game that can be played against the computer or another player. We won't reveal more here, except that it's great fun! Published as an Amigo! cover disk in August of 1995.
Quatro Processing Soccer
A nicely done public domain soccer\football game created by G-Sfot and released in 1991.
Quatromino
Available on POWER-DISC 6, this puzzle game was written in BASIC.
Quattro Fighters

This Codemasters Quattro compilation series contains the following four games:

SAS Combat Simulator
Kamikaze
Mig-29 Soviet Fighter
Guardian Angel (Freddy Hardest in South Manhattan)
Quest for Galaxia

Quest for Galaxia is a video game for the Commodore Amiga platforms. The game was released in 1993. The player controls a spaceship that can only move sideways. The player is attacked by the opponent's spaceships that try to shoot him down. The opponents come in clusters. For each plane shot down, the player receives points. Published in Amiga Power 26 (Jun 1993)
Quest for Glory II: Trial by Fire

The sequel to the first Quest for Glory game takes place in the town Shapeir and the desert surrounding it, in a Middle East-like environment. It seems that the powerful elemental spirits have been troubling the Shapeir folk recently. Something, or someone, is behind those troubles. It is your task to find out what is going on, to get acquainted with the many inhabitants of Shapeir and to prove once more you are worthy of your heroic title!

Just like its predecessor, 'Trial by Fire' is an adventure game with text-based interface, puzzles to solve, and characters to talk to, mixed with a role-playing character development system and battles. You can play as either a fighter, a thief, or a wizard, and also become a paladin in this game. The combat is action-based. You gain better parameters by fighting enemies, training, and performing other actions.
Quest for the Grail
A single player adventure game by Ad Camp made in 1992. A mixed format game of text with multiple choices, pictures an overhead map of your surroundings and your score.
Questionary
A French language, shareware quiz game created by Alphatron in 1989. There was a limited demo version and the full version that included additional question sets.
Questron II: A Fantasy Adventure Game

As the second title in the Questron series, this game follows the same basic formula as the original. You start out as a lowly peasant with only a few gold coins in your pocket and a bad attitude to defend yourself. By stumbling around the countryside and fighting hordes of creatures, you gain wealth, experience, and title.
Quetzalcoatl
An unfinished platform game from Denice Software in 1989. Set in a fictional time when both humans and dinosaurs roamed the earth and attacked each other.
Quick Money

A two-player only versus\duel game created by Ben Campbell and released in 1992 as an Amiga Format #35 (coverdisk 35b), June 1992. Game contains brief instructions on disk and supports PAL/NTSC screenmodes, mouse/joystick control plus a quit back to WB option. It is late within the 21st century. The public imagination is captured by network sponsored duels. Participants fight in arenas, remotely controlling their machines, matching their wits against each other and against preprogrammed droids. Fights are broadcast globally, there is much at stake.
Quicksilva

A shareware game by Entactogenic Design, released in 1996. It was another normal day for Daisy, another day of eating grass when suddenly Daisy felt strange and looked at the mushrooms accusingly with rolling eyes. They got her jumping through the air. Sadly all this jumping led not only to Mad Cow Disease but to the first milkshake. Your local burger place is a ghost town and the government had to act quickly so they commissioned a robot, the Quicksilver to trace the roots of the craziness and eradicate it.
Quik: The Thunder Rabbit

This platform game has much in common with console games of the era. There are 4 worlds including ice, desert and fields, and have multiple routes through. The bad guys are cutesy. You get past them by spinning at them, although jumping over them is often sufficient. Power-ups on offer include speed ups, energy, food and water (Quik’s thirst and hunger are measured separately). The bonus levels involve jumping through time, by finding the right doors.
Quiksilver Pinball
Quiksilver Pinball is an Amiga pinball arcade game released in 1990 by Actionworks
Quingo

A licenseware quiz game developed by Mat Fascione and published by Europress Software and Deja Vu Software in 1990 and re-released later in 1994. There were 4 versions of this game eventually released. Welcome to Quingo, a pub quiz machine simulator with 3000 questions in seven categories. These categories are geography, films, science and arture, people and more!
Quintette

Quintette is a computer adaptation of the board game Pente. It also features Gomoku which is the game that Pente is a variant of. Both game modes are played on a board where two players place Go stones. The aim is to get five in a row or to capture five pair of the opponent's stones. The game can be played against an AI or against another human. It's also possible to watch a game with two AI players. Game options include using tournament rules or not and it's also possible to choose if black or white player should start or if there should be a flip for it. With tournament rules turned on the first player's second move is restricted and has to be at least three intersections away from the center of the board. The game features eight different difficulty levels. An option to modify the board is also included.
Quiwi

Quiwi is a quiz game for multiple players taking turns. Players must answer questions from one of six different main topics like geography, art and literature or history and politics. After clicking the mouse once, an archer fires an arrow at a target that rotates colours corresponding to each of the main topics. The colour that is in the middle of the target once the arrow hits will be the topic for the next question. If the colour happens to be black, the player can directly select the topic of their choice.

Once a question has been asked, the player must first think about the answer and then reveal it by clicking on a button. If the player was correct, they can choose a "right" button, otherwise there are "wrong" and "no score" buttons. A right answer increases the player's score for the corresponding topic.
Quiz Challenge

Take part in this multi-choice freeware, quiz game created by Graham Benham in 1992. The program also gives you the option of adding your own questions to the quiz. The categories are music, sport, television, news, film, pot luck, history, geography and people.
Quiz Master: Genius Edition 1 And 2
A shareware quiz game possibly based on questions from the Trivial Pursuit games or at least named after them. The game was released by A. Chetham in 1989.
Quiz Wiz
A German language quiz program with over 700 questions from 12 different areas: general knowledge is required! Freeware game from Gerd Wagner from 1990.
Quizam!

Quizam! is a 1 - 8 player trivia game for multiple systems.

Eight mysterious dark satellites orbiting the Earth must be destroyed. Their onboard computers have malfunctioned, generating an enormous volume of questions that are strange, cryptic- even trivial! Knowledge must be combined with careful strategy if you are to gain access to the satellites and succeed in this mission!

Players move about the board, trying to gather the eight satellites present on the screen. At the beginning of each turn, the player tries to correctly answer a 4-question multiple-choice question. The player receives movement points based upon how quickly they answer questions. The player must have the correct number of movement points to end their turn directly on top of the satellite. There are 8 different board layouts, 8 different difficulty levels, and games can be short or long.
Quizmaster +
A German language quiz game released to public domain in 1988 by Critters.
Quizmaster 2.0

Quiz game for 1 - 4 people. Each player chooses a question from a field, after which four possible answers appear, which you can select with the joystick. With 300 questions/answers, HiScore list, score, time limit, risk, question editor to expand the question catalog and much more. Completely in German by author F. Zollner from 1989.
Qwak

Qwak is a 2D platform/puzzle game developed by Jamie Woodhouse. It was initially released for the BBC Micro and Acorn Electron in 1989 as part of Superior/Acornsoft's Play It Again Sam 10 compilation.
