An updated and enhanced Amiga version was given a budget release by Team 17 in 1993. This update added several new features, including a two player mode and additional levels. The game was re-released on the Amiga CD32 later that year in a double-pack with science fiction shooter Alien Breed.

The object of the game is to guide a green duck through eighty levels. Fruit and gems can be collected for points, and enemies are eliminated with projectile egg weapons. Progress through the game is earned by collecting gold and silver keys. There are a variety of power-ups also available, including 'chocolate egg' weapons and extra shots.

In addition to the normal-style levels, the challenge levels require the player to complete levels and collect all fruit within twenty seconds.

QX 2001 is a timed sci-fi arcade game. As a robot operator the player must find all parts of the indicated item (f.e. access card, transmitter) scattered around the base in order to get access to the next level. QX may shoot horizontally and vertically. The base is full of alien flying objects, turrets, laser barriers and robots. Contact with them means a loss of energy, which can't be supplemented.

The game features 3 levels.
R-SeaFox
A freeware AMOS game from Amiten (Johnny Acedvedo and Phornee de goblins doing music) for the Amiga 500. Fire torpedoes at underwater threats and missiles at surface threats and be king of the seas.
R-Squadron

Made available as a free download and developed by Kevin McGrory, R-Squadron was originally created way back in the 90's as a top scrolling shooter that put you control of a small spaceship that had to avoid being wiped out from just about everything that appears on screen. The game is not for those who prefer the simple life, as many of the enemies such as turrets and "Exterminate" voiced creatures are deadly and can be hard to avoid. “R-Squadron”, is created on the Amiga’s well known Shoot-Em-Up-Construction-Kit.
R-Type

R-Type is a side scrolling shoot 'em up best known for its extremely tough and strategic gameplay. You control the R-9 spaceship as it launches a last-ditch effort to repel the evil Bydo empire.
The player controls a spaceship equipped with a rifle and a powerful, rechargeable laser beam, and their task is to fight their way through 8 gruelling levels to defeat the alien invader. During the flight, it’s worth destroying the jumping droids, which leave behind upgrades for the ship and various weapons. The powerful laser beam can be fired by holding down the fire button for a longer period. Once you’ve acquired a support battle sphere, you’ll be able to use additional weapons. The sphere also provides protection against small projectiles and can be docked either in front of or behind your ship. When launched at vital targets, it wreaks havoc amongst enemy forces.
R-Type II

R-Type II is a horizontal scrolling shooter arcade game developed and published by Irem in 1989. It is the second game in the R-Type series.

The player controls a ship called the R-9C (or R-9 Custom), which is an improved version of its predecessor game's ship; the R-9. The ship's design was changed slightly, and the wave cannon was given homing capabilities. Two new types of weapons (the Search Laser and Shotgun Laser) were added, bringing the total number of weapon types up to five. A new anti-ground unit bomb was also added to the missile inventory.

Though the number of levels was decreased from the prequel, the number of enemies, their durability, and the number of bullets they shoot were greatly increased. Enemy movements and terrain were also made trickier, bringing the game's difficulty up considerably. The same revival system is used as in the prequel, where the player is brought back to a checkpoint whenever their ship is destroyed.
R.A.N.A.: Reckless Amphibian New Adventures

RANA - Reckless Amphibian New Adventures
A Frogger clone for Commodore Amiga OCS/ECS
R.A.Y. Pokeri
R.A.Y. Pokeri is a video poker card game based on common Finnish video poker machine. Keyboard is used to control game. No mouse or joystick needed.
R.B.I. Baseball Two

R.B.I. Baseball 2 features all 26 major league teams, each with a full roster of players. You can choose any National or American League team. You can even play one of the 1989 All-Star squads.

The game features One Player and Two Player options as well as a Password mode to enable you to play a full season (one game against every team in the division). In addition, a watch mode provides you with the best seat in the house for a computer-controlled match up.

This second version is similar to the original game in terms of gameplay. This time around the game uses the teams and statistics from the 1989 season. Just as in the original, you get to see what it's like to step up to the plate as Ricky Henderson, pitch the ball like Nolan Ryan, and catch a line drive like Ozzie Smith.
R.E.R.O.
Unreleased remake of the classic H.E.R.O., based on the c64 port.
R.O.M. Gold: Rings of Medusa

This is a remake of Rings of Medusa. Basically identical to the original in gameplay, the remake offers enhanced graphics, hardware supported sound and an improved interface. 
 
Rings of Medusa is a strategy game with light role-playing and business simulation elements. Located in a medieval kingdom, the game puts the player in control of the former king's son. Unfortunately, an evil sorceress called Medusa has taken control of the country and is now dominating the people.

The prince's task is to find five magical rings that will give him the power to overthrow the sorceress and claim back his heritage. In the beginning the hero will try to earn money by doing trade between different towns, or try his luck at bounty hunting or at treasure hunts. Once enough money has been earned to maintain a larger army, the prince will send forth his men to search for the rings which are in the possession of large soldier of fortune armies rallying the lands.
R3: The Art of Rocketry

A Thrust / Gravitar style 2D shooter, R3: The Art of Rocketry is a video game written by Bruce Webster for the Amiga released in 1995. It was a playable demo on the coverdisks of Amiga Power (issue 54) in October 1995 and on Amiga Format (issue 89) in September 1996.

The game was initially released as shareware, but the author later released the full game as freeware on Aminet in 2000. The registered version included Tritus from Davin Pearson, a three-player competitive Tetris-inspired game, much in the same manner of the game Super Foul Egg. 

R3 is a Thrust clone where the player navigates a flying craft by rotating applying power in that direction. Vertical movement is affected by gravity.

R3 adds the ability to purchase new and better craft, which are organized into five classes. Each craft in the same class has similar characteristics, such as class 3 being large on the cargo space and shields, but low on missiles and low on thrust power.
Race
A footrace game for up to 8 players, created by Ludde and Co and released in 1998. .
Race Drivin'

Race Drivin' is a sequel to the driving simulator Hard Drivin'. Game play is similar to the first game. The player must complete laps around the race track before a timer expires. There are several checkpoints around the track which increase player's time as he passes.

Race Drivin' has three courses, one of which is the track from Hard Drivin'. There is a new super-stunt track, and an autocross course. The player also may choose from three types of cars.
Racing Maniacs
A competitive racing game with 3D polygon graphics. Not the most finished graphics, but a good multiplayer competitive experience with excellent controls.
Rack Runner
Walk around, dig holes, climb ladders and edit your own levels. This game is written in AMOS by Andreas Paschke and released in 1993.
Rackney's Island
A scrolling screen platformer created by Roy Hanssen and published by Megatronix and in Amigo! Issue 06/93.
Racter

Racter strings together words according to "syntax directives", and the illusion of coherence is increased by repeated re-use of text variables. This gives the appearance that Racter can actually have a conversation with the user that makes some sense, unlike Eliza, which just spits back what you type at it. Of course, such a program has not been written to perfection yet, but Racter comes somewhat close. 

Since some of the syntactical mistakes that Racter tends to make cannot be avoided, the decision was made to market the game in a humorous vein, which the marketing department at Mindscape dubbed "tongue-in-chip software" and "artificial insanity".
Radar Rat Run

Radar Rat Run is an unofficial 16-bit clone of the Commodore VIC-20 and C64 game Radar Rat Race, which in turn were also clones, of Namco's Rally-X. This version was written in AMOS, was developed by Stephen Williams and released into the public domain in 1995. You control a ratty, who must grab all the pieces of cheese in a maze, and flee from all the other rats. Once you reach a barrier in the maze, you are automatically rotated, but you can always manually change direction. There are red ones who chase after you, and black ones who are activated when you get close to them - both types kill you on contact. When they are close, you can activate a Star Screen to block them off.

The Radar of the title is on the right of the screen, and shows you where each piece of cheese is, although the actual maze is not illuminated, so your next snack might be further away than you think.
Radical Moves
It's a fun cartoon-style game with Rob, being the radical dude at the centre of the action.
Radio Controlled Racer

Although purporting to feature radio controlled cars, this is essentially a standard Super Sprint style racing game, which one or two players can join in. It's viewed from above, with the races lasting for 4 laps of close-quarters racing between 4 cars, with the computer providing the extras.There are 8 basic circuit layouts, featuring bridges, tight short-cuts, chicanes and hairpins.There are also arrow-shaped patches of ice which can cause the car to get away from you.The race ends when the leader finishes, with the other cars frozen on the spot and given their final positions based on where they are in that millisecond
 After you have completed the 8 tracks, you start on track 1 again. But this time it's gets harder.
Raffles

An eccentric old millionaire stored all his gems and money in odd places around his mansion. When he dies, his widow is unable to find any of this, so she hires master thief Devon Aire to look in the places his criminal mindset suggests it will be stored.

Each room of the house is viewed isometrically, and contains all the features you would expect to find in a large house, from cookers and telephones to pool tables and paintings. Each one can be picked up, pushed, pulled and used, with the diamonds located in intricate and surprising places. 

Due to Mr. Croucher's keen interest in experimental science, there are also monsters moving through the rooms. Contact with these reduces some of the energy on one of your 3 lives.
Rage (Scorpius)

Rage is a shareware game for the Commodore Amiga. It can be best described as being similar to Universal Warrior, only without the shops. This is a top-down explorer and shooter, where you move around and shoot things to solve puzzles.
Rage (Unreleased)
A single-player horizontally scrolling shooter created by Gabriel Leroy and team at Computer Adventure Dream. It was to be published by Ubi Soft, but never was released.
Ragman
Ragman, the game from Bonzai is a maze game where you have to collect the dots and reach the exit before the time runs out.
Ragnov

Ragnov was the first game project of Softeyes in the late 1980s. A 2D sideways multi-directionally scrolling shooter. They did create a demo and sent that to several publishers, but the game never worked out and they started working on Hoi . Ragnov featured parallax scrolling and a split-screen mode for two players. The game's concept was processed into Hoi level 3 (where Hoi flies around with a jetpack on his back).
Rags

RAGS is intended to feel like a deluxe version of the last level of the C64 game Beach Head 2. The plot is simple: Two guys face each other in an arena trying to kill each other. This goal can be achieved by knifes, portable rocket launchers, mini-guns or by luring the opponent into a trap. The game can be played against a computer opponent, which was designed long before we had our first lecture in Artificial Intelligence, and is therefore not too smart, but the real fun starts when You play against a friend.
Rags to Riches
A public domain board game based on Monopoly for two to four players created by Jim Campey and Steve Howard in 1992.
Raid
A 2D vertically scrolling military shooter created by Fez Software using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit.
Raid III

The SEUCK based SWIV tribute game that is a sequel to Raid II: Mission X and the precursor to Raid IV: Super Raid. After your great victory in Mission X, you are again called upon to take out an EVD, a drug baron and his men, thus restoring peace to the people. Shoot anything that fires, collect civilians and peace through superior firepower!
Raid IV

The Sequel to Raid III: Total Fire and fourth and final game in the SEUCK based vertical shooter series. Raid 4 is perhaps the best the series had to offer. Another SWIV rip-off but very playable and deserving of attention. It suffers from hard difficulty level but is very worthy overall.
Raid Over Moscow

Raid Over Moscow is a Commodore 64 classic brought roaring back to life on the Commodore Amiga!

In this cold war thriller, a team of space-based commandos must save the U.S. from a Soviet nuclear strike! 

Requirements (for an actual Amiga): 

- 68000 and up
- OCS, ECS or AGA
- 1MB of Chipram OR 512KB Chipram, 512KB Slow Ram
- Floppy disk drive, OR
- 1MB of Hard Drive Space, OR
- CD-ROM - including CDTV and CD32

Full Game Description:

The USSR has launched a huge attack on the USA, and the only hope for the free world is for you (as leader of a US Squadron of fighters) to destroy their defense bases. This is done in a multi-stage action game with some similarities to the same developer's Beach Head. All the mini-games must be completed before the time limit on the bomb is expired.
Raiden

In the year 2090, Earth is invaded by extra-terrestrials. The World Alliance of Nations has developed a supersonic attack fighter, Raiden, to defend the Earth. A pilot must take control of the experimental fighter to destroy the alien warships that just happen to look like odd variations of typical military tanks and planes with gadgets attached to them.

Raiden is an over-head vertical-scrolling shooter, based on an arcade game of the same title. It features two forms of weapon upgrades and two types of missiles (normal or homing). You start the game with several bombs which you can use to destroy most enemies on the screen to get yourself out of a jam. Each level ends with a large boss or bosses.

Game finished and reviewed but not released by U.S. Gold as they went under before it could be distributed. Recovered from the original DAT tapes beginning in 2004 by one of the coders.
Raider

Raider is a Thrust variant. The player controls a space ship over planet surfaces with the goal to pick up a cog on each planet. After four planets are finished, the player needs to fly through a power plant to get rid of them.

However, there are gun turrets which try to shoot the ship. But the main problem is gravity which affects the ship and may cause it to bump in the ground or walls. This is of course unhealthy and needs to be avoided by using the rocket thruster to counter steer. Besides of this, the player can rotate the ship and fire shots to destroy the turrets. During the 40 levels, the game introduces additional obstacles like variable gravity levels or tractor beams.
Railblaze

Your ship has been captured by the evil Damidi empire, and imprisoned in the depths of their grid network. Collect blue orbs on each floor while dodging enemy fire and hazards to reveal the exit to the next floor.
Rainbow Islands

Sequel to Bubble Bobble, Rainbow Islands sees Bub and Bob (in 2 player mode), who are now curiously small boys rather than dinosaurs, attempting to rid the Rainbow Islands of bad guys.

Using the power to cast rainbows, trapping anything underneath, the boys must ascend vertically 4 levels each island, with a big, bad boss at the end of each.

By trapping beasts under your rainbows, then jumping on them to break them you can collect seven different colored gems, and there are also power-ups for extra speed and rainbows.
Rainbow Warrior
Rainbow Warrior is a video game for home computers produced by Greenpeace. The game is a collection of mini-games which relate to Greenpeace's environmental campaigns and actions during the 1980s.
Raise the Titanic!
A 3D adventure game by C. Millin, where you pilot a mini-sub to the wreck of the Titanic. Made in 3D Construction Kit, however this game is very responsive even on un-expanded A1200.
Rajd Przez Polske

Rajd przez Polske is an arcade racing game allowing to drive three old Polish cars: Polonez Caro, Fiat 126p and Fiat Cinquecento. The player drive through multiple roads between the larger cities of Poland. The goal requires reaching the destination point before the time runs out. Hitting the roadside or another car causing the loss of speed. All three cars differ in maximum speed. The game allows to choose one of six available sound tracks.
Rally Championships

A fine AGA racing game from the Flair UK. It features realistic car physics and driving, a car range: Porsche RS, Peugot 205 Rally, Opel Calibra, Lancia Delta, Ford Escort Turbo, and the Toyota Celica. Rally courses range from snowy Scandinavia to the dusty East African savanna, bustling city streets of France, lush tropical rainforests, and even very narrow passes on the Alps.
Rally Cross

Little top down car racing game for Classic Amiga computers inspired by Rally Cross DOS game. Source code can be downloaded free. 

Rally Coss is a collective effort from the following people:
Ozzyboshi: concept and code
Vectrex28: fonts Z3K / Tracks and background images
Lunix: Tracks and menu music
Oriens: Tracks Maze / mod.alfetta background music
O. Stokka (4pLaY): Coordination
Rally Cross Challenge

Rallycross racing was once popular on the BBC, featuring super-modified cars racing against each other on tracks combining tarmac and gravel sections. Rally Cross Challenge sees Anco bring it to life in top-view Super Sprint style.

There are six different circuits, and four cars in the game - 16-bit users with a Microdeal joystick adapter can have all four of these controlled by human players, other users are limited to 2-player. Computer cars have varying personalities and abilities. You must finish in the top 3 to move on to the next race.

The opportunity to upgrade your car comes after each race, with the points you earn from race results (4,2,1 for the top 3). There are six categories of upgrades - turbo, steering, traction, aerodynamics, repair time and brakes.
Ram Run

This single player demo puzzle game has 2 modes of difficulty, where you must avoid the Amiga ball and add your memory to the memory expansion board as in real life, the more RAM you have, the better! Game by CIS and released as freeware in 1989.
Rambo III

Rambo's mission is set deep in Afghanistan, in the days when the Soviets occupied it, and America was putting this right (we won't mention who they enlisted to do so). Colonel Trautman has been kidnapped by the Soviets, and you've gone in there to rescuing him. Doing so is a three-part operation approximately following the plot of the film.

In the first part, you explore the building Trautman could be in, through a top-down view of the building. It is heavily protected by infra-red security beams, which when activated unleadsh the enemies. The locations of the beams are only apparent if you collect the special goggles. Other hazards include mines, trapdoors and booby-trapped doors, but there are enhanced weapons to collect.
Ramify

A technological remake of a 3500 year old design. A remake and update of Mancala, the transfer game, perhaps the oldest game known to man. Mancala is so widespread it is considered to be the most played game in most of Africa. Thousands of years ago, n many ancient lands, royalty and common men alike played games consisting of pits and using pebbles or jewels as playing pieces. Sometimes the games were played for high stakes, including rubies, sapphires and slaves. Ramify is based on these Mancala games. We believe you will find it as addictive as the kings and maharajahs of old found it and we have modernized it for your computer. In this version you are playing for megabytes of RAM chips.
Rampage

George, Lizzy and Ralph were just ordinary Americans, until an experiment went wrong, turning them into a Gorilla, Lizard and Werewolf respectively. Following this, the three of them plan to go round destroying buildings, and up to 3 human players can join in.

Smashing at the edges of the buildings for long enough will make them collapse. The police and military are after you, and will shoot at you, so try to destroy them (failing that, you can avoid the bullets). You will need to eat regularly, with things like plants on offer, to avoid shrinking back to being human
Rampart

Rampart is a game combining strategy and artillery action. Build your castle from Tetris-style pieces, place your cannons, bombard the enemy, try to repair, do it all over again. The original arcade release has a single-player and a two-player mode; later revisions incorporate three-player gameplay.
Ramsbottom Smith and the Quest for the Yellow Spheroid

The key was inserted into the ornate lock and as it settled into place there was a gentle "click" ... Smith gripped the key and slowly turned it to the left but nothing happened. Taking a deep breath, he turned the key to the right and for a moment felt resistance to his pressure, then suddenly the lock clicked into place. Placing a hand on either end of the lid Smith carefully lifted it open.

Twenty seven years he had waited for this moment, twenty seven years of searching and wishing, twenty seven years of danger, hardship and deprivation. But now it could all be over ...

Leaning forward, Smith peered into the small casket and an immense wave of relief swept over him as he spied the small yellow spheroid nestling at the bottom of the casket.

SEVEN DAYS EARLIER ...
Ramses
A strategy game where the goal is to build a temple to the Pharaoh, it was developed by Christian Awizio of Cyberstyle and released on Amiga Fun 1992-03.
ranTrainer
Ran Trainer is a German language sports management game, developed and published by Greenwood, which was released in Europe in 1995.
Ranx: The Video Game

This action game is adapted from the Italian comic book Ranx à New-York by Stefano Tamburini and Tanino Liberatore. Here the player controls Ranx, a cyborg in a cyberpunk-style world. A lethal virus is spreading, and the President has caught it, so Ranx must go to New York with the antidote to save him. After this, he must rescue his girlfriend in Rome. 

Ranx will fight with ninjas, homosexuals, the Chinese, and others, using his kicks and punches. Items can be picked up including pieces for later repairs and items which can be sold when talking to other characters. Destroy street lamps to get money, but make sure the police don't see.
Rape Games
Someone spent a lot of time making homoerotic cartoony rape\sex scenes for you to play by yourself. Freeware in 1988 from the aptly named Smegma Soft.
Rape Games 2
Someone spent a even more timemaking homoerotic cartoony rape\sex scenes for you to play by yourself. Created in 1990 from the aptly named Smegma Soft.
Raphael's Revenge

A single player shooter created with SEUCK and published as freeware by Courbois Software in 1991. Finish off that pizza and take your sai weapons as we are going into the tunnels to take on ninjas, mole men and other baddies. Clear them out and make Master Splinter proud!
Raptor: Call of the Shadows

Raptor Call Of The Shadows Amiga Version

After completing each level you have the option of upgrading your ship with a powerful arsenal of weapons and goodies. Some weapons are effective on only ground or air targets, while some are on both. There are some really advanced weapons like the auto-track mini-gun which can effectively destroy almost any kind of targets without aiming the ship.

Dying in shoot'em ups can be annoying, especially if you have to start all over the beginning. However, in Raptor you can save your game between each level. If you have enough credit you can even buy multiple shields for further protection.
Rash Panic

8-bit style game where you need to trap monsters into holes. It's remake of much older game. Your only chance of survival is to kill the aliens that reside on the planet. To achieve this you must first dig holes for the aliens to fall info. Once an alien has fallen into a hole, you must then fill in the hole that you have dug so that the alien falls to the ground below. Some aliens though, may need to fall through more than one level to die. Powerups are there to help, some help you wrap around screen, extra life, takes aliens up a platform, oxygen booster, extra points and swap a life in team game play, slow down aliens, speed boosts and more.
Rastan

​Released in arcades in 1987, Taito’s Rastan was one of the best fantasy action-platformers of its time. Now, after eight months down in the basement, the Amiga version of Rastan emerges. This is a demo of the first level, featuring remastered sprites and brand new, reimagined backgrounds, all running on a stock Amiga 500 with 512kb extra ram!
RasterBike

"RasterBike" is a computer adaption of the motorbike race inspired by the movie "Tron". Two racers ride their futuristic motorbikes on the squared arena. The motorbikes leave the solid light trail which is fatal for any motorbike that will collide with it. The aim of the game is to conquer the opponent by making him to crash in the wall what makes him to lose one of nine lives. The game can be played with a computer or human opponent.
Rat Race

A German language joystick waggler with a track and field theme. Apparently, it was developed by a teacher at a centre for computer courses. Players select from a roster of three rats, then they are off to the stadium. The race lasts for a couple of seconds. Depending on the score, players may be able to enter their initials on the high score table. Afterwards, the game returns to the title screen.
Rat Trap

Your House has been overrun by rats. You must herd the rats into trap machines to clear them out. In order to do so, you must manipulate the environment to set up pathways so that the rats are headed in the right direction. Objects that you move around include blocks, fans, and pipe pieces.

Rat-Trap on the Commodore Amiga, it was developed by Fox Williams for the British software house Audiogenic, who licensed it to Acclaim Entertainment, the U.S.-based publishers of a range of games based on The Simpsons.
Ratco
A game very much like Scrabble for up to four players, created by WSOY Micro and released by WSOY Productions in 1988.
Rattle Snake
A freeware game from 1992 by Ben Ashley of Odyssey Software created in AMOS
Rattlesnake
A Renegade style beat'em up created by Park Productions in 2000.
Ravanelli Junior

A platform game by Gianluca Sclano. The aim of the game is to be able to save your father (Radanelli Senior) from the clutches of a mysterious kidnapper (Mr X).
In this adventure you will have to face an army of Mr. X's henchmen, who have undergone genetic mutations when subjected to dangerous radiation.
You will have to search far and wide in all the places where your father has enemies, and defeat the forces of evil present ...
Ravanelli’s Soccer
A promotional game sponsored by Play Video, the football\soccer game is based on the footballer Fabrizio Ravanelli and was released in 1994.
Raven's Curse
RAVEN'S CURSE – Graveyard Prelude is a free, fully playable Gothic tower-defense teaser for the Commodore Amiga 1200.
Razor

"Razor" is an horizontally scrolling shoot-em-up at the moment, but
I will include stages of vertically scrolling too. It's very classic stuff,
with power-ups, end-of-level guardians and interesting graphics. I'm trying
to put a nostalgic feeling to it, making a resemblance to good old Amiga
games of 1990-91, like R-Type, Z-Out, and the superb Project-X.The last is
hard to beat, but I wanna make my game the best as I can.
RCross

An open source conversion by BSzili and created by Franticware for the #hvdosdev2021 competition at https://www.high-voltage.cz where it won the first place, this is a 3D rally racing simulator. You control a small RC car on various terrains and race against time. Frca kindly agreed to share the source code, so it became a nice weekend project to get it running on the Amiga. The original game DOS needs an 486 DX with 8 MB RAM, and the Amiga version has similar requirements. To play it you'll need a 68040 or 68060 with an FPU, 8 MB Fast RAM, AGA chipset or RTG. When you pass between checkpoints marked with green blocks, the display shows if you are behind or ahead of the track record. I like how the car's suspension visibly reacts to bumps in the track. The game saves your lap times, and gives trophies for beating the top times Normal and Reverse; which is really addictive.
Reach for the Skies

Reach for the Skies is a combat flight sim focused on WWII's famous "Battle of Britain", splitting the battle into four stages and giving you the option to take part for either the Royal Air Force or the German Luftwaffe. As well as piloting a plane, you can also take on Controller duties, of planning which planes to deploy where on each day, trying to minimise losses. 

Eight planes are simulated, from Hurricanes and Spitfires to Ju88s and BF110s, each with their own cockpit displays and characteristics. When playing as the Germans, protecting the fragile and slow Ju88 bombers is crucial. There is a practice mode with indestructible planes, realism levels can be adjusted, and time can be accelerated while an enemy plane is not in sight.
Reach for the Stars: The Conquest of the Galaxy: Third Edition

Reach for the Stars is a "spaceploitation" game. The player has the opportunity to name his civilization and those of his (up to three) AI opponents before he begins his attempt at galactic domination. The 2D galaxy map is marked only by planets and their names in few different colors. Also, there is no diplomacy and no player control over tactical combat.

What remains is a hard-core game of grand strategic and economic production. The player must tweak his planets, build ships, research new tech levels, and deploy fleets. All of the underlying dynamics can be altered and customized by the player.
Read & Rhyme

Read & Rhyme is a 1 - 2 player educational reading game for multiple systems.

There are 2 levels of difficulty for each game.

 Alpha Blast: Alphabetize a list of 10 words to blast a rocket into space.
 Flying Saucer: Direct the flying saucer to the words in alphabetical order.
 Rhyming Challenge: Type as many rhyming words as possible in 10 tries.
 Rhyming Rockets: Select 1 of 3 rockets which have a non-rhyming word, and then send the rocket to the moon.
Real Genius
Computer game version of Rubik's Clock puzzle, created by Sphinx and published by CompuTec Verlag in 1989. The object of the game is to set all the clocks at 12:00 by pushing and turning the buttons.
Real Pacman
A Pac-Man clone collect'em up with a bunch of new mazes to navigate, it was created by Videobrakkers Peace and released in 1991.
Real Sports Boxing

Do you have what it takes to be a champ? Find out in this single person boxing game released as freeware in 1992. In the game you work your way to the championship by fighting lower ranked fighters in the style of Punch Out. Your first fight is against John Vein Sucker and make your way to the a title bout.
Reality

Sample game written with Backbone and AMOS released as part of the Backbone shareware package in 1999. Backbone is a powerful multitasking tool to create games without programming skills. Backbone allows you to design a variety of games; Scrolling or non-scrolling platform games, vertical and horizontal shooters and games viewed from above.Backbone allows you to design a variety of games; Scrolling or non-scrolling platform games, vertical and horizontal shooters and games viewed from above. Backbone includes 4 example games including Reality as one of them, sounds, graphics and documentation in AmigaGuide format.
Realm of Maiyessae
This Game is called Realm of Maiyessae from 1989, by Jennifer Diane Reitz in S.E.U.C.K.
Realm of Sendai
Realm of Sendai is an anime-influenced RPG for the Amiga computer. Adventure game a bit in style of Zelda (or Speris Legacy) with simple but working graphics. Contains Load / Save option.
Realm of the Trolls

The trolls are posing a threat to humanity, and it's your job to sort them out in this traditional-style platform game, which features over 200 screens. You have a gun and bolts of energy available to protect you. The graphics have detailed sprites but very plain backdrops, in an attempt to create a mood. Unusually a construction kit is included, allowing you to design your own levels down to the last detail. Another novelty is the option of mouse control on 16-bit systems, a seemingly impractical option for a platform game.
Realm of the Warlock

Realm of the Warlock is a text adventure with graphics for the Amiga.

Ashton is now a desolate place ruled by the strongest. Before the region was seized, several wise elders controlled the land. As Ashton matured, word of its prosperity spread throughout the world, and many came to ponder this glorious land. Then, as the elders gathered in the town of Fairshire, they were were abducted by a user of black arts. Without the wisdom of the Elders, Ashton quickly became troubled. You alone decided to search the hall in which the Elders were last seen, and came across the mysterious scroll responsible for the Elder's abduction. You have been brought into the Realm of the Warlock, and must save the kidnapped Elders.

Text adventure with graphics. All commands are via VERB NOUN entry. There is a save and restore option.
Realms

Realms is a medieval real-time strategy game located in a fictive kingdom where the player just has been named king. Your kingdom is threatened by the surrounding realms of different rulers and it is your task to defend yourself and expand your own kingdom in order to become ruler of all realms.

The game features 125,000 square miles of fractally-generated landscape, 128 armies with many thousand members each. You can order your armies into different battle formations and conquer countless towns with their inhabitants and its gold treasures
Realms of Arkania: Blade of Destiny

The first game in the Realms of Arkania trilogy was the Blade of Destiny. It combines all the best characteristics of that times RPG's, like an extensive story line, first person view mode, cave exploring, scenery and freedom over your own actions. This game was an immediate hit when it was first released, forcing the producers to make a new English version almost over night! This delayed the sequel to the game, Star Trail, for a whole year.

The game is incredibly huge for the time it was made. A lot of work was put into creating the world, including history, geography, folklore, races and NPC's. The story is epic, as all RPG's... You play the role of six different people; all looking for adventure and fame that arrives in the city of Thorwal. After a while, you are sent to the real quest of the game: hunt for the sword of legendary warlord Hetman Hyggelik. In order to find it, you will have to travel the world in search for pieces of a map, drawn by one of Hyggelik's warriors.
Reasoning with Trolls

A text adventure with still pictures with an educational theme. The game features a number of islands connected by bridges, and each bridge has a troll living on it that will only let you pass if you answer a logic problem correctly.
Reaxion

The computer system of a nuclear power plant has been damaged by a virus, and you have to debug it before the plant would explode!

This means in practice that there is a board consisting of tiles, on which you have to make every tile the same, as in turning either into a colored or uncolored state. You control a cursor, and if you click on a tile, that one and every other neighboring tile around it inverses its state. Each level starts with a different pattern, and there is a time limit too.
Reaxxion
A single player puzzle game from Mark Archer, created with AMOS and published in Amiga User International. Released as part of the Amiga Classix 5 compilation. This is a color matching puzzle game.
Rebel Boj o Moc
A war strategy game created by Zdenek Pletka and crew of the Cyber Alliance using AMOS and published in 1996.
Rebel Charge at Chickamauga

Rebel Charge at Chickamauga is a tactical simulation of the South's last major offensive thrust during the American Civil War.

The game uses a refined version of SSI's Gettysburg game system and is played in 13 turns each representing two hours of real time over a two day period. Players are awarded points based on casualties and territorial objectives. At the end of each turn and the end of the game points are calculated and compared to a chart which determines your level of victory. The game can be played under 3 different sets of rules (Basic, Intermediate, and Advanced) and can be played against another person or the computer can play either side.
Rebel: GW24 Solar System

Rebel: G24 Solar System is a science-fiction real time strategy inspired by Dune II. The action takes place in the G24 star system, where the rebels took over the planet. As a lead commander the player must restore the order by expansion of the base, scientific research, gathering and proper use of military power and harvesting raw materials. The game features only one linear campaign with classic genre goals, such as harvesting an appropriate number of raw materials, repulsing the attack of the enemy troops or destroying the enemy base. The game allows multiple control of the troops. Building the facilities and the troops requires two types of raw materials: Materian occurring on trees and Belon located in the sand - both require another type of harvesting unit. Military units are divided into ground and air troops. More advanced facilities and units require laboratory research.
Rebellion

Rebellion is a top down viewed shoot 'em up with multi-directional movement. In each of the game's single screen levels the player's task is to save a number of humans that have been captured by robots. The player enters each level from a drop ship and has to rescue the humans by simple moving up to them and touching them and then leading them back to the drop ship. At the same time numerous robots have to be destroyed but while doing so it's important to avoid killing the humans by mistake.

Each level has its own quota of humans that have to be saved and it has to be done within a time limit. There are numerous different robots with differences in pace, armour and weapons. Some power ups can be picked up such as shields, extra lives, invisibility and various new weaponry like rockets. At some locations there are fences that have to be destroyed and doors that have to be unlocked. There are also trap doors that have to be avoided.
Rebellion (Andreas Lunn)
A nice multi-direction scrolling shoot-em-up game similar to Asteroids or Photon Storm, created by Andreas Lunn and released in 1996.
Rebound
An update to the classic Pong game created as Shareware and released by Digital Design in 1993.
Rebound Arena

Version 1.0 released, according to game installer notes on 9/9/1996 by Aaron McDonald, Solaris Software. Bounce the red ball around the arena and hit the stars while avoiding the blocks. Difficulty can be set by adding blocks.
Recognize Me
Identify the picture that is different, find the odd man out. Number of sequences varies from 4 to 16 on two levels of difficulty. Supports 5 languages.
Recoil

Conversion from the original ST version:

The universe is under attack (again). On EMAR II, home of some rare energy crystals, an alien fleet stopped by. Defence is reduced to a single turret gun named "Kiss My Ass".

Recoil is a Defender clone. You control the ship and can scroll to both left and right by turning your ship into the desired direction. A huge radar map on the bottom of the screen show enemy activities. In the game, there is a twist on the original scheme: your ship is mounted on some building on the top of the screen and therefore constantly rising back to the top of the screen, which makes control a bit more challenging.

The goal is to destroy any moving enemy, while collecting energy and bringing those energy crystals to your base. You have three lives initially and can release a smart bomb as emergency exit.
Recovery
A horizontally scrolling shooter created by New Deal Productions, like a fast paced version of Microcosm. Converted from the Atari ST version by the original developers.
Rectangle

Rectangle is fundamentally a variation of Konami’s Quarth with some Arkanoid style elements.

The basic lay takes’ place on a single screen - the player controls a small character on the bottom of the display which can be moved to the extreme left and right of the play-field. Tetris-like block shapes descend from the top of the screen. The player can shoot projectiles which become square units upon contacting the blocks.

The aim of the play is to form rectangles or squares by way of filling in the remaining space on the vertical, or horizontal level of the blocks to score points, and when all are cleared, the next level is unlocked. Some blocks contain an ever-cycling power up - which if converted, will cause a bonus collectable to fall, e.g. giving the ability to eliminate blocks with one shot, faster player movement & shots, or even transform the players’ sprite into a bat & ball for Breakout inspired play.
Rectum

Dark hours approaches mankind. Half of the population have succumbed to an epidemic of something very unpleasant, which like an uncontrollable nuclear reaction has spread itself across the planet Earth. Anarchy and Beat Kaalsson reigns among the survivors. Chaos prevails everywhere. The only spoken language is the naked, brutal and unmerciful language of violence. War sweeps over countries like tornadoes on rape-fields and devastates everything in its way. Is this the end of mankind? Is there really no hope? And does this have anything to do with the game?? The questions are just as many as they are stupid, and the answers are just as uncertain as what the future holds in its bosom. 
 
Game supports tournament play.
Red Baron

Red Baron puts you in the pilot's seat of actual World War I fighter aircraft. This game features 28 different aircraft from both the Allied and the German sides presented in actual 3D graphics. Start a career as a pilot and rise through the ranks to become the most feared ace in the skies, or participate in a variety of single missions including simple fighter sweeps, balloon-busting, zeppelin hunting, or take on an actual WWI ace in one-on-one combat. If you're good enough, you may even be able to take on the infamous Manfred von Richthofen, the Red Baron himself.
Red Dwarf
Red Dwarf is a space shooter developed by Asa Margetts using the shoot 'em up construction kit. It was released into the public domain in 1994.
Red Dwarf Trivia Quiz

A trivia quiz game written in Blitz Basic by David Anderson and published by Astro Software in 1995. The quiz is centered on a UK sci-fi show and all the nuggets of information about it. Red Dwarf is a British science fiction comedy franchise created by Rob Grant and Doug Naylor, which primarily consists of a television sitcom that aired on BBC Two between 1988 and 1999. 
 
The main setting of the series is the eponymous mining spaceship Red Dwarf. In the first episode, set sometime in the late 21st century,[a] an on-board radiation leak kills everyone except lowest-ranking technician Dave Lister, who is in suspended animation at the time, as punishment for smuggling a cat aboard the ship. The cat, Frankenstein, who is revealed to be pregnant, is safe in the cargo hold. Following the accident, the ship's computer Holly keeps Lister in stasis until the radiation levels return to normal—a process that takes three million years.
Red Dwarf Trivia Quiz: Champion Edition

Even more difficult trivia question about the British science fiction comedy franchise created by Rob Grant and Doug Naylor, which primarily consists of a television sitcom that aired on BBC Two between 1988 and 1999. This championship version was released as freeware, in 1997. 

The main setting of the series is the eponymous mining spaceship Red Dwarf. In the first episode, set sometime in the late 21st century,[a] an on-board radiation leak kills everyone except lowest-ranking technician Dave Lister, who is in suspended animation at the time, as punishment for smuggling a cat aboard the ship. The cat, Frankenstein, who is revealed to be pregnant, is safe in the cargo hold. Following the accident, the ship's computer Holly keeps Lister in stasis until the radiation levels return to normal—a process that takes three million years. Lister therefore emerges as the last human being in the universe—but not alone on board the ship.
Red Heat

Red Heat is based on the Walter Hill film of the same name, starring Arnold Schwarzenegger and James Belushi. You take control of Soviet detective Ivan Danko (played by Schwarzenegger), who travels to Chicago in pursuit of the fearsome Georgian drug lord Victor Rosta. 

The game is essentially a side-scrolling beat'em up in the vein of Vigilante. As Danko, you proceed across four levels which follow the movie's original setting, where you are constantly attacked by members of the Cleanheads, a group of drug-dealers who are in business with Victor Rosta. To eliminate hostiles you can either punch them (slow but long-ranged) or head-butt them (close-ranged but faster). The only defensive move available is crouching, so as to avoid being hit - there is no jumping or any other evasive tactics. Occasionally, you can get hold of a handgun and fire six shots at the villains.
Red Lightning

Red Lightning is an operational level wargame of a potential conflict in central Europe between NATO and the Warsaw Pact. It's a game of a hypothetical World War III in the early 1990's. As the Soviet player, the mission is to sweep aside NATO forces and capture the Ruhr. As the NATO commander, the mission is to stop the Russion invasion.
Red Mars

Red Mars is a combination of real-time and turn-based strategy. Your main goal is to destroy the opposition (up to three players or CPU-controlled enemies can be played simultaneously) by achieving the highest level of technology possible. Gameplay is divided into two parts. In the RTS part you have to build new buildings, army, and prospect ground for minerals with a special unit called Pioneer. When you encounter enemy with your army, all combat becomes turn-based. The game has unique way of producing units. Each robot contains five parts: left hand, legs, torso, head and right hand. All can be combined to create almost an unlimited amount of different types of robots.

Multiplayer is available as play-by-email.
Red Storm Rising

The Soviet Union, under severe pressure after destruction of one of their biggest oil refineries, must secure a new source of oil, and to do that, they must disable the West... which means they must invade Europe and fight NATO to a standstill... And the only way NATO can prevent that from happening is to reinforce their forces with convoys from the US and other countries. 

You are in command of one of the US attack submarines. You must hold the ocean against the Soviet navy at all costs, or the land battle will go badly. Part submarine simulator, part dynamic campaign, and part WW3 simulation, Red Storm Rising is an amazing look at modern warfare.
Red Zone

Red Zone sees Psygnosis attempt to simulate motorcycle racing using 3D polygon graphics, in a similar way to Team Suzuki and No Second Prize. Ten different circuits are featured in the game's championship, although there are no bike setup options. The graphical detail level can be set, which affects the game's running speed and smoothness.

The mouse is used for control, with options to vary the sensitivity of the response as well as the skill of the opposition. The game keeps track of how many times you punted an opponent off, and how many times you endangered one with your riding.
Red41 The Silent Death

The game demo is called Red 41 The Silent Death and has the protagonist of a robot very reminiscent of Appleseed (you know the cop with the antennas?); this game remembers, at least in the graphic style of the backgrounds and choice of colors. Occasionally you will even fly with the your robot. Some say the game is closer to Genocide 2 from the X68000. The Demo was released in The Games Machine Settembre Numero 56 in 1993.
Redpill Puzzle

Simple and well made puzzle game. Shouldn’t take that long to finish. In Redpill Puzzle you move around a blue jewel and try to push the green and
purple jewels to the exit. However there is a red jewel that stands in the way so get rid of it however you can. This puzzle game is inspired by games like Sokoban and Atmomic.
Reederei

Reederei is a turn-based trading game where players can buy and sell goods to make profit. The game is totally menu driven and there are no action sequences. 

While playing, players try to run an Hamburg based maritime company. On each turn, each player has an option to send their ship to another seaport, buy goods from there and return to Hamburg where they can sell it for a good price. Players are also expected to buy ships to enhance their ship convoy thus increasing their buying quota from other seaports.

The goal of the game is to increase company value to a certain score. This score depends on the game difficulty. First player reaches this score (either human or computer) wins the game.
Reel Fish'n

Reel Fish'n is a fishing simulator. Starting small in a rented boat with a plastic worm, a spinner, or other tackle, you can work your way to tournament status, purchasing not only additional tackle, but also equipment such as depth finders and serious bass boats. The player takes over a character's life, balancing business and fishing. Game elements include examining the weather forecast and deciding where to fish. Regular work needs to be done to provide money for the fishing hobby, or tournaments can be entered for financial support when they are won. Once a fish has been caught, it needs to be managed carefully to reel it in.
Reel Skill

A 3+1 reel Fruit\Slot Machine game created by Stephen Eaborn with all the flashing lights goodness you would find on a real (or is that reel?) slot machine. With nudges and multiple betting lines and modes.
Reels
A homebrew slot\fruit machine game featuring 5 reel action, with 12 win lines from Tom & Kev.
Reflection
A pong game, written in AMOS and set against a brutal science fiction background.
Reflexity Pinball Challenge

Reflexity Pinball Challenge is a German pinball game. It has support to four players and features three tables with an Alien-inspired theme. There's a multiball feature: an U-shaped magnet on the tables holds up to three balls and releases them when a fourth touches the third. Each player starts with four balls. The player switches tables by hitting the teleporter with the ball. The teleporter area opens when a certain amount of points is reached (150,000 points for the second table, and 600,000 points for the third). A bonus table with a timer appears after teleporting.
Regent
Regent is a strategy game, developed by Martin Economic Simulations and published by Linel, which was released in Europe in 1992
Regnum

A top-down, turn based strategy game for 1 to 6 players, by Ralf Peters, published by Markt & Technik in 1989. Regnum means Kingdom. 
Regnum is your kingdom in an imaginary world consisting of countries, lakes, mountains and cities. The Amiga mouse serves as your scepter. Your task: Secure and expand your property with the help of political, economic and military actions. But reality quickly catches up with you: in this game, too, the economy and the military are depressingly closely interwoven with each other. Two to six monarchs can get into a fight, including the “claimant to the throne” (among computers) Amiga. There are several maps available to you as worlds, which differ in size and complexity. As a ruler chosen "by Computer's grace" your Serene Highness naturally has the power over you. Game contains a powerful world editor to create your own game situations.
Rejection

You are piloting a hovercraft equipped with a special magnetic generator, and your goal is to push a metal sphere—rolling across the playing field—into your opponent's goal by utilizing the magnetic force emitted by your craft. The craft is equipped with eight thrusters, each activated by moving the joystick in the desired direction. Thanks to the air cushion, friction is virtually non-existent; consequently, any thrust generated either increases or decreases the craft's speed, whereas the speed remains constant when no thrusters are engaged. To come to a stop, you must fire the thrusters opposite to your direction of movement. The craft changes direction upon contact with the field boundaries or the opponent's craft. The ball cannot be physically struck, as it rolls along the floor while the craft hovers on an air cushion just above the surface.
Relayer
Relayer is a two player competitive Qix clone for the Amiga. It was developed by Antonio Argentieri and released into the public domain in 1993.
Relics of Deldroneye 1.5
A point and click adventure that is a sequel to Relics Of Deldroneye: Book One - Falcon And The Medivians and Precursor to Relics of Deldroneye 2: Island of Debreen.
Relics of Deldroneye 2

Island of Debreen is a sci-fi/fantasy point & click adventure game, part of the Relics of Deldroneye saga. The main character Falcon, once-loyal to Deldronis royalty but now living alone in exile, has at least acquired his own full-size spacecraft to get around in. As the game begins, Falcon's ship is dangerously low on power and drifting through space, after barely escaping from an altercation with an unidentified hostile vessel. Falcon must carefully conserve remaining power between the ship's various sub-systems, and work out what to do next...

The interface splits the screen vertically: the current scene is shown in third-person perspective, above a panel which displays Falcon's current inventory items, and also a number of action buttons: "Move", "Look", "Take", "Use", "Talk", "Help", "Open", "Close", "Give" and "Show".
Relics of Deldroneye: Book One

Relics of Deldroneye is the first in a series of 3 point & click graphic adventure games. In this sci-fi/fantasy story, you play the role of Royal Venturex Falcon. As the game begins, Falcon is languishing in a filthy cell, imprisoned for theft. He must find a way to escape the prison, and get to the planet Zantis.

The interface splits the screen vertically: the top half of the screen shows the current scene, and underneath is a panel that shows the items that Falcon is carrying, as well as ten action buttons ("Move", "Look", "Take", "Use", "Talk", "Open", "Close", "Give", "Offer" and "Show"). The action panel also has secondary tabs that give contextual information about important characters, and displays the length of time that you have been playing.
Renaissance

Renaissance is a collection of four classic arcade machines. The games are reprogrammed and differently named, but they are closely modeled after the originals:
Rokstorm: Asteroids variant
Megapede: Centipede variant
Draxians: Galaxian variant
Invaders: Space Invaders variant
Besides the classic versions there are also contemporary versions of each game which offer updated graphics and sound. There are also slight gameplay additions, e.g. extra weapons, new enemies or shields.
Renegade

Renegade is a scrolling beat 'em up by Technos which started the Kunio / Nekketsu High series. The original takes takes place in a Japanese city, whereas its western version named Renegade is set on the mean streets of Brooklyn. This conversion later produced unofficial sequels Target: Renegade and Renegade III: The Final Chapter.

You must venture through to meet your girlfriend, and then rescue her from her kidnappers. This is split into five levels, taking you through the subway and the docks as well as some inhospitable streets. A wide range of aggressive moves are on offer, including headbutts, kicks, punches and flying kicks. Much of the game's violence is depicted in a fairly tongue-in-cheek style, with an element of attempted humour along the way.
Renegade AGA
My port of the Arcade game Renegade to AGA Amigas. Initial release is a single file so needs some fast RAM. I have tested it using 4mb fast on a standard
Renegade III: The Final Chapter

Renegade III was the third and last in the Imagine's series, based on the original coin-op by Taito. The hero's girlfriend has been beamed into the future, while the man himself has been sent back into prehistory. This sets the scene for a sideways scrolling arena combat game, where the player fights in various time periods. The settings varied from Egyptian and medieval, to a futuristic level. As such, gone are the attacks of street gangs from the first two iterations of the series, replaced by assailants such as knights in armor and robots. In each level you have six minutes to reach the finish, as this is all the time the time-travel portal is available for. There are many surface hazards to avoid, as well as multi-layered Green Beret-style areas. You can kick and punch at different heights, allowing you to deal with each of the diverse foes.
Renegade Legion: Interceptor

Adaptation of the board game from FASA, the game offers a space fighter phased combat, in both skirmish and a campaign mode. The player may play as either side, the Terran Overlord Government or the Commonwealth Rebels.
Renegades

Renegades is a two-player deatchmatch game seen from above. Two armed men must find and fight each other in a high-tech complex filled with bonuses, corridors and locked doors. Both graphically and layout-wise, it is very inspired by the Alien Breed series. On the technical side, it differs a lot from its graphical inspiration, with a horizontal split screen for each player.
Renegades (CompuTec Verlag)

Released 1992-04-03 on Amigo! issue 02/92. An editor is included on the disk. A single screen shooter, like Galaga with the added fun of dropped upgrades and items that alter gameplay and boss levels.
Renegades Deluxe

Alien Breed inspired 2-player split-screen deathmatch fun!

Choose from one of 6 battle-hardened mercenairies to do battle in one of 20 arenas in a fight to the death!

Old-school Amiga action in the Amiga .ADF file format for use with Emulators!

Featuring:
- Fake walls
- Jammed doors
- Power pickups
Repara Tronics
Repara Tronics is a clone of "Fix 'it Felix" developed by Amigatronics and released in 2019.
Rescue
A Chiplifter/Fort Apocalypse style 2D flying multi-directional shooter by Harald Müller and published in both Gamers' Delight and Gamers' Delight 2 compilations. Precursor to Rescue 2.
Rescue II

This Harald Müller shooter, which is similar to Gravitar is the sequel to Rescue, which was sort of a cross between Choplifter and Fort Apocalypse. Rescue II was published by both Intersoft and Schatztruhe in 1994.
Rescue on Fractalus
An Amiga port of Rescue on Fractalus!, the 1985 Lucasfilm Games classic for the Atari 8-bit.
Rescue!

Drive the Space Rover around the maps, find the reactors and destroy them 
to allow the captive to escape. The Captive must reach the teleport,
followed by you, before the timer expires to proceed to the next level.
Reshoot Proxima 3

RESHOOT PROXIMA III has been developed by Richard Löwenstein, Kevin Saunders, and Altraz Virgill with many features we expect from some of the team behind the excellent Reshoot R series. Features such as lots of blasting action, a cool soundtrack, deadly enemies, 5 uniquely themed stages, 24 bit color pixel art, a steady 50 fps frame rate, and much much more you'll just have to experience for yourselves if you have a Commodore Amiga A1200, A4000 and CD32.
Reshoot R

RESHOOT R is a super reactive game for classic Amiga hardware, a horizontal scrolling shoot-'em-up with lots of enemy objects and how to avoid them. The game features adrenaline gameplay, high-quality animation, a balanced difficulty curve, wicked graphics such as organic fog effects, jerk-free parallax scrolling, and finally the experience of many objects, some small, some big like you've never seen on the Amiga before.
Retaliator
Retaliator is a 1-2 player co-op shooter developed by Rob Massey and released into the public domain in 1989.
Retro
A multi-directional scrolling shooter in the vein of Thrust or Gravitar created by Stephen Strickland and published in Amiga Format Issue #129 on the Cover CD in 1991. A level editor was included.
Retro Wars: Episode IV 1/4

Amiga Game: RetroWars Episode IV 1/4 (2018): The release of multi-language versions:, French, German and English, along the Spanish version 1.4 the release of the boxed commercial version, leads us to bring here and now this great and fun AmigaWave game. A graphic adventure in a very distant galaxy but with funny dialogues, well done caricatures and very well finished. Turn yourself into Luk, followed by your droids and his master, in order to escape from the planet and the negative influence of retro-speculation, promoted by the dark side.
Retrouve L'Histoire

Finding the story offers the child several sequences of events. Each sequence involves three images, which he must manipulate in order to put them in the proper chronological order. Several levels and game play modes are offered in relation to the child's age and progress. This game was released in Europe, published by Carraz Editions in 1989.
Return of Valkyr

A Spanish language homebrew shooter created by Miguel Ángel aka Jiménez Santana. A remake of the classic MSX 'Valkyr', this game proposes that you must try to annihilate any alien that crosses your path, in the purest 'Phoenix' style. Programmed in AMOS it will give you a complex and addictive play. This game is based on a game called Valkyr that was released for MSX systems.
Return to Atlantis

Someone is trying to destroy the earth's oceans. As you are an expert on deep-sea diving and underwater combat, it's up to you to stop it. After planning your mission, choosing equipment and healing yourself from your Viceroy mobile base, you must dive into the oceans with your helpful robotic drone RUF and complete a series of 14 missions to save the world. 

There are around 100,000 unique locations to be explored in this 3-D side scrolling game, which is a cross between arcade style action and a role playing game. There are lots of things to explore and experiment with as you travel back to Atlantis. You will meet and question many NPCs throughout the game - talk to them carefully and wisely to gleam key information.
Return to Blacktooth
The last time we entered Castle Blacktooth we managed to find three crowns, but by that time I’d run out of donuts and Heels was lost somewhere in Safari World…
Return to Earth

Return to Earth is an Adventure\role playing game, developed by Fantastic Simulations and published by Wolf, which was released in Europe in 1988. Released both commercially and as shareware. The game allows you to build up a very complex network of intergalactic trading routes as you attempt to track down the lost world of Earth.
Return to Genesis

Return to Genesis takes place in the Zephyr system where twelve scientists work on secret projects. Of course every bit of help is appreciated and so every scientist is cloned 50 times for a better productivity. Unfortunately the evil Mechanauts have invaded and the player has the mission to save the scientists and drive the Mechanauts off.

This game is a side-scrolling shooter in which the player's main task is to shoot everything in sight - except the scientists of course, which should be picked up. They also can be shot to win the level, but then the player misses out on extra weapons: every scientist (along with his/her clones) has his own piece of equipment which can be activated at any time as long as the scientist is on board. In contrast to many other games of the genre, contact with the environment does no harm but causes the ship to reverse the flying direction at full speed. All in all there are 50 levels with twelve scientists each.
Return to Sinking Island

This program by Terry Fike is a colorful mix of adventure and role-playing games with a good dash of humor. It's about finding treasure on an island threatened by the flood. You are confronted with various problems that make life difficult (rising water levels, hunger, traps, etc.). It was released as freeware in 1989.
Reunion

Reunion is a strategy game where players must manage the resources and development of a colony. From a central command area, players select from among different menus to control different aspects of the colony. Many of these menus also need the appropriate personnel in charge (commanders), whose skills and price tag vary. Typical menus include: The research screen where specific areas are selected, the production/buy menu which turns resources into goods, the colony building menu where construction can be scheduled and the colony's facilities managed, the galactic map where new planets are chosen for a closer look, and eventually colonization. Players can also consult with their commanders or go to "space local", the nearby bar for all the gossip. In order to produce new material, the player has six different minerals to mine and discover on various planets in the solar system.
Revelation

Revelation is an abstract puzzle game based around cracking codes on safes. Each of the 80-plus levels is a top-down view of an arrangement of locks and dials, which must be aligned so as to unlock each section by having identical colors touching each other. Not all locks can be moved however, and all of this must be done within a time-limit. Your time to collect the gold (by opening each of the 9 doors in sequence in the hope of finding lots of bling) is limited by how long you took to crack the code. There is a bonus game to unlock, as well as extra lives and special power-ups. A password system ensures that a level need only be cleared once.
Revenge II

Sequel to Jeff Minter's REVENGE OF THE MUTANT CAMELS. 
REVENGE II was published 4 years before its predecessor on the Amiga, which finally saw a shareware release in 1992.
Revenge of Defender

A side scrolling shooter, the object is to defend your colonies from various waves of attacking aliens. Revenge of Defender features layered scrolling screens, and new background artwork and enemies for each of 7 levels.
Revenge of Renegade
A homebrew, unauthorized sequel to the Amstrad\C64 Beat-em-up classic, made by first time game maker Nor Dean aka Nour.
Revenge of the Mutant Camels

This typically zany Jeff Minter title sets you as a mutated camel, with an optional support one mimicking your moves elsewhere. The hordes of enemies to be taken on include falling umbrellas and drinks machines. Shot enemies release tokens ranging from points bonuses and energy recharges to control-reversers and poison.

Speaking of controls, the game uses the same system as Llamatron, which means that you fire automatically in the direction you're moving, but pressing the fire button allows you to rotate the direction of fire while immobile. This allows enemies in different parts of the screen to be attacked from less precarious positions.
Revenge: Armchair Assassin 2

The sequel to Armchair Assassin (The T.V. Chubbies in...). A highly entertaining murder simulator. Cute sprites burst from a wooden crate and run aimlessly in all directions. You move a crosshair and shoot at them with an arsenal of weapons and an endless amount of ammunition. Soon the screen is filled with blood, bones, and craters. You can change the music, the sounds, and even the sprites.
Reverse

Reverse is a board game, developed and published by Intersoft, which was released in Europe in 1993.

A Reversi or Othello variant played on a 16x16 grid. There is no music. You will play in contemplative silence against the computer, only interrupted by clicking sounds as more and more spaces on the board are claimed. Released via mail-order catalogue, on CD-ROM collections like Gamer's Delight 2.
Reversi (Avalon)
Reversi is an implementation of the famous board game by Robert Brandner of Avalon and was released as part of the Pixel 128 GREEK MAGAZINE compilation.
Reversi (Courbois Software)
A commercially released version of the popular board game Reversi\Othello that was released in 1991 and created in AMOS.
Revolution
A puzzle game featured on The One Amiga 50, disk B and the coverdisk of Amiga Computing 52, written by Colin Vella (Medina), Keith Bugeja (September).
Revolver (Aaron Fisher)

A puzzle game by Aaron Fisher released by The Assassins and options to start on level 1, 25 or 50 to begin. In it you revolve the centers of the squares in blocks of four and attempt to match the centers with the outside to move on.
Revolver (Chris Gregan)
A freeware Tron\Snake like game from Chris Gregan of Hung Like a Hamster in 1998.
Revs

An unofficial Amiga port of Geoff Crammond’s BBC Micro Formula 3 racing simulation, originally published by Acornsoft in 1985. Race against a full grid, practise laps and tune your car’s wings.
The port reconstructs the original engine in C and 68000 assembly, with native Amiga graphics, sound and input. It targets Revs Plus Revs 4 Tracks and includes Silverstone, Brands Hatch, Donington Park, Oulton Park and Snetterton, plus Nürburgring.
Rex and the Galactic Plague
This vertical shooter for the Commodore Amiga started off life as a SEUCK game back in 1993 but has been brought to life again thanks to the fantastic Scorpion Engine.
Rex: Into the Shadow Realm

Rex: Into the Shadow Realm is a new vertical shooter for Commodore Amiga. Featuring two distinct campaigns, players can choose to fight alongside Space Corps or join the Shadow Raiders, with each path offering unique stages, encounters, and perspectives on the conflict.
Riamel: Black Prophecy

A combination of isometric adventure game and a dungeon crawler, with tons of unusual possibilities, contains various cities, spells, ship cruising, battling 2D and 3D (vector) enemies and much more. Quite hard and a manual is a must. All that is available online as the original commercial creators worked with the Amiga scene to make sure it was available to TOSEC and Hall of Light. Every game can be different as a random shuffling of the puzzle parameters happens at the start of each new game.
Rick Dangerous

The game is largely based on the Indiana Jones movie Raiders of the Lost Ark. Set in 1945, British agent Rick Dangerous travels to the Amazon jungle to search for the lost Goolu tribe. His plane crashes in the jungle, and Rick must escape from the enraged Goolu. When the game starts Rick finds himself in a cave running from a rolling boulder, a famous scene from the Indiana Jones movie.

Armed with a pistol and dynamite, Rick must fight hostiles and evade countless traps in three more levels. The second level is set inside a pyramid in Egypt. In level three, Rick must venture to the Nazi stronghold of Schwarzendumpf castle to rescue captured Allied soldiers. The rescued soldiers tell him that the Nazis are planning a missile attack on London. Therefore, in the last level Rick must infiltrate their secret missile base.
Rick Dangerous 2

Our intrepid adventurer and all-round super-hero saved the world once from the wicked ways of the Fat Man, leaving the overweight ogre tied to a stake and held by the Goolus. But fortune has smiled on Rick's enemy, and a strange alien race has befriended him. Now the threat to the world is twice as great. Rick's called back to action - in a Flash !

Rick Dangerous II is the ultimate platform poser, packed with puzzles and teeming with traps. Pick up and play. And play. And play

Starting in the Flying Saucer which has landed in Hyde Park, shooting off to the planet Barf with its ice kingdoms and mud mines, before finally coming face to face with the Fat Man in his headquarters, Rick endures screen after screen of heart pumping action and death defying thrills.
Rick Dangerous 2.5
Rick Dangerous 2.5 is a one level demo of Rick Dangerous II not available in the full Rick Dangerous II game.
Rick Dangerous Enhanced

The game was originally developed by Core Design (Simon Phipps) and published by Firebird in 1989 and this version which is a backport of the Nintendo Wii edition (remake by Magic Team) with 32 color palette which is getting a graphical overhaul in development for the Amigamejam competition.
Rick Dangerous: The Other Levels

A little fanmade Rick Dangerous remake made in the gameeditor Backbone by the EAB member mjnurney. You play Rick Dangerous, an Indiana Jones type who's on a quest. Rick Dangerous is a platform game across many screens, in which Rick has his gun in one hand, and dynamite sticks in another. You must take a methodical approach to clearing each screen, as there are traps in place which will need memorizing and preempting where possible. Use the dynamite wisely, for enemies you can't get into the purely-horizontal range of your gun.
Rick Davis's World Trophy Soccer

This football simulation focuses on international football, allowing you to play a tournament or single friendly matches. Up to 8 human players can be involved in the tournament. Options include three skill levels, variable match lengths and a choice of sound or music (or both on some versions).

The match is viewed from the side, although it switches to a 3D view when the ball is close to the goal. The ball roughly sticks to the player's foot. Set pieces are controlled by moving an aiming cross-hair.
Ricochet

Ricochet v2.0 from Martin Longstaff on the Amiga was released in 1995.

The game is a table tennis/pong game with several difficulties and it's nicely presented.
Right Way

A 2D puzzler game by Michael Taupitz, reminiscent of Lemmings and released as Shareware. Two versions of Right Way exists. The original version and a Easter Edition. It can be really, really difficult as there are no continues, no passwords, no saves and we have to restart from the first level if you die.
Ring around the World

Ring around the World is a short, open world, bird's-eye view, point'n'click adventure where the protagonist wakes up on the shores of an unknown world with just two memories - one being of himself drowning in a stormy sea.
Ring War

Ring War is a pseudo vector based shooter similar to the arcade classic, Star Castle. It was developed by Eric Bazan and released as Charityware in 1991. Shoot the target in the middle by disabling its protective shield.
Ringling Brothers and Barnum & Bailey: Circus Games

Ladiiiieeeees and gentlemeeeeennnnn! Children of all ages! The Greatest Show on Earth proudly presents... Circus Games!

As a tiger trainer, you will have to put the tiger's through their various tracks. You have to do various stunts, like corkscrews and somersaults, on the trapeze.

As a tight rope walker, you need to go from one side to the other, doing handstands and somersaults along the way. There is also a lady daredevil that you do stunts with from the back of a horse.

If you do the international competition, you will have to do certain tricks for the trapeze, tight rope walker, horse trick-rider and make the tigers go through all the tricks in their routine.
Rings of Medusa

Rings of Medusa is a strategy game with light role-playing and business simulation elements. Located in a medieval kingdom, the game puts the player in control of the former king's son. Unfortunately, an evil sorceress called Medusa has taken control of the country and is now dominating the people.

The prince's task is to find five magical rings that will give him the power to overthrow the sorceress and claim back his heritage. In the beginning the hero will try to earn money by doing trade between different towns, or try his luck at bounty hunting or at treasure hunts. Once enough money has been earned to maintain a larger army, the prince will send forth his men to search for the rings which are in the possession of large soldier of fortune armies rallying the lands.

Sometimes the player takes part in small arcade sequences like sword fighting and sea fights, or controls an army on the battle field.
Rings of Zon

This action puzzle game from George Broussard was akin to a more intellectual Boulderdash where you must travel many trapped and tricky caverns to find the three ancient Rings of Zon to help defeat Korak, the Dark Lord and practitioner of the black arts. While you are just a sorcerer's apprentice, you are chosen by the Council of Magicians to take up this difficult task.
Rings of Zon Trilogy

A maze game with RPG elements from Micro Fix released in 1990. Important note for playing on emulators: Turn your joystick emulation off, in order not to block the Amiga numpad! Game can solely be controlled with numeric keypad, utilizing all keys from 1-9. To liberate Land Zon from the claws of the sinister Korak and his demon spawn, you fend off enemies charging from all sides while you find keys, refresh your life energy or collect symbols for sword strikes or teleporter jumps. Although these symbols increase your own combat power enormously, they can only be used to a limited extent. Despite everything, you will not reach the next level by killing enemies alone, a little strategic evasion and skillful handling of supplies is also essential.
Ringside

In Ringside you can chart your aspiring fighter's progress from untried stripling to awesome killing machine, well, almost, but you can rise up the world ratings by challenging and beating opponents.

There are a fair selection of punches and tactics. The punches themselves are hardly textbook affairs, nor are they aesthetically executed, but they do seem able to bruise your opponent.

Game has better than average graphics and well defined sprites, but a boxing simulation stands or falls on the flexibility of its play. Standing next to someone and thumping them can get very boring. Ringside is reduced to a fairly static and visually unexciting game. Not even the absurd sequence between rounds where you have to wave a towel over your boxer by fiercely woggling the joystick can alter this.

Ringside can be a good laugh either in the one player or in the two player mode. Then again, no-one gets their nose broken.
Ringworm

Released as part of APC&TCP Volume 3 CD, this Homebrew game by Herbert was released in 1996. A multi-play party game with simple rules and easy to distinguish sides. See who can stay going the longest in this worm like variant.
Rintivoorh
