It features Aerial combat in a late WW1 setting where you need to take out enemy planes, ground emplacements and tanks all of which are trying to blast you out of the skies.
Sky High Stuntman

Steven Squealburgh is directing his next big action blockbuster and needs a stuntman to help him film four big action scenes. You have been chosen and must fly a helicopter, balloon, jet fighter and a bi-plane. Remember you only have a limited number of takes to get it right or you are fired.

Sky High Stuntman is a top-down vertically scrolling shoot-em-up. The joystick or keyboard is used to steer while flying the helicopter, bi-plane and jet fighter. The fire button or space bar fire your weapon. Flying the balloon you use the joystick or keyboard to move a sight and shoot the enemy. Moving the sight so far will move the balloon in that direction. Fire button or space bar will fire your weapon.
Sky Shapers
Sky Shapers in an engaging and challenging 50 FPS vertical scrolling SHMUP from the new Norwegian developers Digilicious Nibbles, with lots of charm due to its distinctive hand crafted graphics
Sky Tower

Build to the skies!!! Drop your tower pieces to build up the size of the building. Time when to drop the next part to build as high as you can, try for perfect matches and strings of perfect matches. Don't be distracted as you pass balloons or the moon if you can last long enough. Keep calm as high winds whip the cable faster and faster and just keep building. Game created in AmiBlitz3 by Sami Vehmaa with the release to gold in 2022.
Skyblaster

Skyblaster is a shoot-em-up, in which the player flies a helicopter over a 3D landscape. The goal is to destroy enemy helicopter, tanks and planes. A strategic element applies, as the moving enemies not only approach the player's vessel, but also the player's home bases. The player must also defend the own bases while trying to destroy the enemy ones. The own bases can used to restore the own helicopter's health and the bases' health can be restored by destroying enemy bases.

Each of the three moving unit types exist in two different variations, which are different in their moving speed. Therefore the player always have to keep an close eye on the radar, on which the different types are displayed in different colors (light colors represent the faster types, dark colors the slower moving types). The player's helicopter has two different weapons to fight: missiles and machine guns. While the first is very good to destroy bases, enemy vessels can be easily hit with the machine gun.
SkyBlitz 2
SkyBlitz 2 is a Blitz/Bomber clone developed by Tom & Kev and released into the public domain in 1991.
SkyChase

Take to the skies and fight your opponent (computer or human) on a split screen or null-modem link. Takeoffs and landings are handled automatically, so players can focus on shooting each other down. Flyby replays are featured for crashes, so you can gloat over each victory. In one-player mode, the view from your opponent's plane is optional; either way you have a scanner to help locate them. Different levels of ammunition and missile stock can be set, to make for a variety of gameplay options. After the game has been ran for 3 hours, a hidden 'paper plane' mode is added, alongside a roster of topline machines such as the F-16 and MiG-29.
Skychase (Energy)
Made by Gore Design, Dark Energy and Sky of Energy , this Public domain, 4-player homebrew was released in 1993.
Skyfox

Aliens have invaded your beloved homeland, and you must help save it. You are flying the Skyfox, the most advanced attack fighter plane available to the Federation, from within the cockpit. Skyfox is complete with deflection shields, laser cannons, five guided and five heat-seeking missiles and a top speed of Mach IV. The 15 scenarios can be played at 5 skill levels. You will have to fight tanks, enemy planes and the mothership. Use the radar to locate enemy vehicles, and the long-range scanner to ensure that no wave reaches your base before you can take it out. Keep an eye on your shields, and on fuel levels - you can dock at the base to refuel.
Skyfox II: The Cygnus Conflict
Pilot a starfighter on a variety of missions, from locating lost artifacts to destroying the enemy, in this early 1st-person shooter in space.
Skærmtrolden Hugo

The first Hugo game based on the television show Eleva2ren was originally developed by Thomas Villadsen and Uffe Jakobsen for SilverRock Productions.

Skærmtrolden Hugo was released for the Commodore 64 in 1991, and for the Amiga shortly afterwards. The game took place in a gold mine, which Hugo had to navigate to collect treasure. The game mechanics were simple and a complete game could take less than ten minutes.
Slabs
Slabs is a Puzzle game, published by Magic Soft, which was released in Europe in 1991
Slackskin & Flint
Slackskin & Flint is an arcade, platformer game for the Atari ST developed by Synergy released in 1992 (by Fun Factory)
Slalom
Guide the skier through a series of flags and to the finish line, a game created by Jayenkai and released on December 25, 1997.
Slalom Speciale

A game of the Amiga Games Pack created by Luca Carminati of his Amiga games created from 1993 to 1998. This skiing game was originally created in 1993 with revisions in 1995 and 1997. In it you ski around the flags on the way to the finish line and try to get the best time possible, with penalties for missed flags, it supports up to 8 players.
Slam Tilt: The Pinball Game

Liquid Dezign featured many of the Digital Illusions team who developed 21st Century's hit pinball games, and after the generally-disliked Pinball Mania from another team, they produced one last Amiga pinball game.

The game features four different tables, each with different layouts and features. A large number of sub-games are included, as well as a variety of animations on the LCD panel at the top. Each table has multi-ball features, with the view automatically switching to full-screen when this is activated. in total there are six different viewpoints, and no less than 47 different game modes are promised.
Slamball

A shareware sports management game written by Michael Keith Lysons where version 1.3 was released in 1993. Develop your team and then pit them against other teams. The games are displayed with generated commentary on how the game progressed based on how well you developed your teams. Coach and transfer players between teams. Play matches and go for The Cup!
Slap 'N' Tickle

This SEUCK Game is called, Slap’N’Tickle by Sensible Software (This Game was given away with the special version of SEUCK distributed with CU Amiga Magazine)

In this vertically scrolling shoot ’em up, You are a Red Space Ship, flying throughout the worlds, You have plenty of fire power to take down everything what moves

As with all Shooters, Shoot anything what moves, from Pulsating Orbs, to Round Spinning Objects, avoid the Gun Fire and Bullets, and Have a Blast!
Slayer

As the ruthless Slayer you have hordes of enemies to wipe out in this horizontally-scrolling shooter. The paths are narrow and treacherous in a similar way to Scramble, so shooting out the wall-mounted installations is important. There are plenty of bonus weapons and shields available however, and 5 lives in total. Each of the 3 levels ends with a boss to defeat.
Slaygon

In Slaygon the player takes control of an advanced robot and has to infiltrate the facility of Cybordynamics, a corporation that is developing a toxic virus that potentially can kill all humans. The task ahead is to locate the main computer and disable it so that the cooling system of the facility's reactor will fail. To do so five override codes have to be found and entered into the computer. As the cooling system fails the facility will ultimately explode, but before that the player has to steal a top secret data disk and flee from the building.

The game is played from a first-person perspective similar to a dungeon crawler and is completely controlled though a mouse based interface. While exploring the facility, various objects have to be collected, such as key cards to get through locked doors. There are also traps such as force fields, ionizer beams and proton mines that require the right items to get past without harm.
Sleeping Gods Lie

Normally this type of deep and involved adventure game is just my cup of tea, especially if it is in a 3-D world vein. Sleeping Gods Lie though is an odd game. The puzzles are in there just waiting to be found and the game has considerable depth but to its detriment there is a heck of a lot of wandering around vast, barren terrain as well. The slow moving pace put me off initially but once I got down to some serious mapping it became quite a compelling adventure romp. The accompanying sound effects are surprisingly poor but the title screen music has a certain charm. Sprite expansion is well implemented but I found the character animation and movement occasionally a bit messy to look at. In short, a little long-winded but enjoyable all the same.
Sleepwalker

CTA's original IP stars a toon dog called Ralph who must stop his sleepwalking master Lee from waking up. Ralph must bridge gaps, beat up baddies, stop Lee falling into water, inflate his own body and float above obstacles, and generally be a selfless version of man's best friend.

Between each of the major levels, there is a dream sequence where Ralph can collect various tokens and trigger what he "really" thinks should happen to Lee.
Slez

An unreleased 2D multi-directional shooter in the style of Thrust or Gravitar created by coder : Johannes Lipp and musician : Holger Kral in 1991. It is a game in which you look to play as a strange looking sphere that has to traverse a pixelated maze while shooting at things and avoiding crashing into the sides. According to Amiga Games that Weren't ,Slez was one of three games developed by Johannes Lipp including Denjoy and Pot, and would most likely have been seen on German disk magazines (where a game is accompanied by a mini magazine) if released.
Slicks 'N' Slide

A native A1200 port of Timo Kauppinen's DOS shareware racing game Slicks 'N' Slide 1.51. The original 16-bit x86 game was recovered from its executable and rebuilt as native 68020 code: game and UI logic recovered into C and C++, with hot routines translated to hand-checked 68020 assembly, on a direct AGA/Paula platform layer. There is no x86 emulator and no generated-C CPU emulation; the original executable running under a PC reference emulator is the ground truth that every routine is tested against.
Slide It (Only Games)
A shareware slide and match game with increased difficulty caused by "magnets" that lock pieces in place, so careful where you slide! Created by Only Games and released in 1990.
Slide It AGA
A timed puzzle game by Tranquilizer of Secretly aka Mike Delling with a passcode feature to return quickly to levels. Slide the pieces around and match the colors to remove them from the field.
Slide It II
A sliding puzzle game from Only Games, this is the sequel to the original Slide It, Slide It II was released in 1992 with familiar gameplay but all new timed puzzles to stump your brain.
Slider (Cachet)

The classic 15 puzzle slider game created in teak and marble by W. Petermann with automatic shuffle, a configurable board size, demonstration solutions and a timer to show your best solution speed. Slider is a Puzzle game, published by Cachet, which was released in Europe in 1988 and in North America in 1991.
Slider (Joseph Carlson)

Slider is a picture puzzle game created by Joseph Carlson and released in 1996. A high res picture is shuffled and you must slide pieces in order to recreate the original picture in as little time as possible.
Slidercrash

A German language puzzle game for one player, Game idea by Christian Günther and Joachim Mertens. Coding in GfA Basic by Joachim Mertens. Graphics by Christian Günther and level design by Sascha Lehner and released in 1993.
Sliders

Sliders is a simple futuristic sports game that isn't a world away from Marble Madness. You control a ball over a futuristic landscape, the idea being to find the puck that's hidden somewhere in the level and "herd" it back to your starting point. Sounds simple enough, except for one thing; there's another player (either computer or human) trying to do the same thing.

This results in incredibly hectic gameplay. Add this to the fact that sometimes you're negatively charged to the puck (and thus kick it away) or positively charged (so the puck sticks to you) and you're in for a crazy time!
Sliding

A picture is broken down into 42 individual squares on the screen, which are then also scrambled. The player now has the honorable task of restoring the unadulterated original state of the little pictures with his mouse. Ahh, I know that, some people will now say to themselves, these sliding puzzles have always brought me to the brink of despair since my earliest childhood! Exactly right, as simple as the whole thing sounds, it is difficult in practice; In addition, you have to fight against a time limit when you're playing Sliding. The controls work perfectly, the sound is quite entertaining- and the pictures themselves? Well, one can say that the "United Graphic Artists" justifiably bear their proud name, because the graphics are really well done. Incidentally, the game is also excellently suited for several players who (one after the other) test their skills.
Sliding Skill

Sliding Skill is a Puzznic variant. In each of the hundred levels the goal is to destroy all movable blocks by sliding them into each other. As soon as a block is moved into a direction, it moves until it meets an obstacle. Blocks can only be pushed so it is important to plan ahead. Of course there are obstacles (e.g. moving walls, tiles which break away after being stepped on or the time limit) and power ups (e.g. a sucker to get a stone out of a bad position) which influence the gameplay.
Slightly Magic

Slightly Magic is a platform game not unlike Codemasters' own Dizzy and Seymour series, but is generally shorter and easier than most other games of that genre.

In Slightly Magic you are cast as Slightly - mischievous nephew of legendary wizard Bigwiz, who has suddenly taken off on some urgent business, leaving his castle in disarray with dragons and magical spells running amok. One of the dragons kidnaps the princess, and now Slightly has to save her.

In addition to standard inventory puzzles of Dizzy games, Slightly Magic introduces a magic system that requires multiple objects to be combined in order to achieve effects ranging from frightening the enemies to turning the player into a fish.
Slime

You have been sent to clean up. Hoover up the growing slime before it covers everything! When you fill your tank you must empty it, which takes some time, meanwhile the slime grows and multiplies and your time is running out! A homebrew game by Fay Latham, written in AMOS and released in 1993.
Slime Line

A game created by The Judge and Melf of the the Bastards in 1991. A one or two player Snake game where you eat the blue dots without touching the walls, lines yourself or your opponent. Eating the blue dots increases your score and also the length of your snake.
Slip Stream

Slip Stream is a shoot 'em up with a third person chase view similar to Space Harrier. The player controls an aircraft called the emerald fighter and has to fly through nine levels (here called streams) which have been overtaken by alien forces. In each stream there are various defence structures and crafts that are powered by a crystal located at the end of the stream. It is the player's task to destroy these crystals and thereby liberate the streams. 

Like in other chase view shooters the player's craft is automatically moving forward while the player can steer it left and right, climb, dive and shoot. Movement is restricted to stream though which is located in the centre of the screen. Various obstacles and enemies will come in the player's path and these have to be either avoided or shot down. Getting hit by a projectile or colliding with a structure will lead to a life lost and the level has to be replayed.
Slipstream (Niki Hemmings)

An unfinished attempt at a fully-fledged Wipeout clone for the Amiga using some new techniques to get some really fast texture mapping without cutting corners on visual effects. The game was created by Niki Hemmings in 1996.
Sly Spy: Secret Agent

With a clear James Bond influence, Sly Spy must stop terrorists destroying parts of the city in this collection of sub-games. Roughly half of these (starting with level 2, and alternating from there on) are side-scrolling Green Beret-influenced offerings, not entirely dissimilar to a great many Ocean movie licenses. There are bad guys to shoot and bullets to avoid, with boxes to climb up on and strategic positions to shoot from behind cover.

The first level involves skydiving down the screen and shooting at the agents as they themselves fall - complete this and you'll safely parachute to the ground. There's a motorbike chase, in which you must shoot out and dodge agents. Two underwater levels follow, in which more enemies and some sharks must be shot. Before reaching the final multiple-enemy showdown in a missile factory full of the baddies from the game.
Small Cars Drag Race

Got fourth place in the Retro Komp Gamedev Compo 2016. Simulates a drag racing, where two cars compete. The game was developed on an A500 with one Megabyte RAM. During the game, the player is tasked with accelerating as quickly as possible. A car with low coefficients will be more sensitive to steering slip, which will make trajectory correction necessary. The absence of trajectory correction causes the car to rub against the protective elements of the track. Collisions with track elements cause the car to slow down, and it's up to the player to avoid them. You will need to accelerate to avoid overheating the engine. The aim of the game is to eventually win more races and thus earn money to upgrade the current car or buy new vehicles.

The player will have the option to set a stake/bet to win or lose a race. The winnings will be added to the overall score and will constitute the game currency.
Smart

Another Sokoban style puzzler written in AMOS Professional. Coding by Luděk Roleček. Graphics by Tomáš Celizna. Music by Mário Závodník. Text in the title menu is in Czech, but the game is in Englsigh. Much later published in in Amiga Future no. 123, Nov/Dec 2016
Smart Cardz

A Non-AGA conversion of Klondike deluxe for all Amiga owners to use that retains the ability to load and use other card graphics sets. It uses all the standard rules of Klondike solitaire. There are many additional card sets that can be downloaded. Some currently out are based around Star Trek, Star Wars, reptiles, heroines, faces, famous art, anime, mammals, dragons, Achilleos and even adult themes of various kinds. While the card sets are required to be available to the public domain, not all card sets contain only public domain images.
Smarty and the Nasty Gluttons

Smarty is an 11-year old schoolboy whose grandfather is a wise and creative scientist. Smarty likes to spend his free time in Grandpa’s laboratory experimenting with all sorts of ideas and gadgets. Smarty has a dog called Slurpy who is his best buddy – besides Grandpa. Smarty also plays the saxophone but he often finds daily practice less interesting than something else.

One day Grandpa makes a huge breakthrough in his lab. The dream machine he’s been obsessed with for years finally works! With the machine, Grandpa has the ability to enter other people’s dreams. He’s planning to use this power for helping all those suffering from sleep disorders.

But then unexpected bad things start to happen. Dr. Nightmare – Grandpa’s archenemy and a less capable but highly vicious inventor – breaks into the lab and steals the dream machine while taking Grandpa into captivity.
Smash

Smash is a rather unusual tennis game, in that it is played from a 2D side view and therefore players cannot move sideways: in that respect it bears similarities with the Super Volleyball games. The player can move forwards or backwards as well as jump. When hitting the ball, the controller can be moved to influence the height and strength of the shot, obviously not the trajectory due to the limitations of the view. The camera always follows the ball, therefore the players are not always visible: a mini-map keeps track of the positions of each player and of the ball.

Four male and four female players are selectable, each with their own statistics and nationalities. The available game modes are single match and knockout tournament. The number of sets and games per set are customizable in single matches, however they progressively increase as the player advances through the tournament.
Smash Bang Wallop

A German language, 2 player Super Sprint clone released as shareware in 1993 by MS Software and published by Nordlicht Spiele. The game has 10 levels that you'll only see if you or your opponent don't destroy your vehicles. You can drop mines or leave oil slicks on the track too.
Smash T.V.

The year is 1999. The world's most popular television show is Smash T.V., an ultra-violent contest between two armed-to-the-teeth combatants, set loose in a series of deadly arenas that are filled to bursting with hordes of mindless beasts and killer robots. The aim of the game is to blast everything in sight and try to grab more cash and prizes than the other guy. Toaster ovens, VCRs, fancy cars and luxury holidays are there for the taking... for anyone who can survive long enough to enjoy them.

Smash T.V. is an insane shoot-em-up from the brain of Eugene Jarvis, creator of Robotron: 2084. It retains that game's frantic style of play and two-joystick control method, but adds plenty of gore, violence, a hint of satire and that all-important two player mode.
Smash Telly

Smash TV which used to be a popular arcade game has also been ported to the Amiga by the company Ocean. A fan of the game has also written this SEUCK based version which some believe is more playable than the Ocean Port. If you liked the arcade version then give this a go. For those of you who never played Smash TV it is basically a futuristic game show where the contestants have to fight to the death to win prizes.
Smash the Beast

Quite funny game with a decent graphics. The main task is to collect a letter and the given ammount of stamps and deliver it to the mailbox in time. Also avoid baddied and bad items that consume your energy.Only 6 levels so savor them!
Smash Thro
An AMOS mini-game created by Tony Kingsmill and released as freeware in February of 1991.
Smash TV: The Ripoff

A top down shooter, a second unofficial tribute to the grooviest of arcade genocidal blasters, Smash TV: the Rip-Off is the better of the tributes made, better than Smash Telly that is and in some ways an improvement on the original. It's faster, slicker, easier to control and much much closer to the spirit of the original game. Gloriously psychopathic action from start to finish. Unfortunately way too short.
Smile

A single player collect em up game where the goal is to pick up all the diamonds without retracing any of your steps and before time runs out. Created by Andre Voget and Johannes Selback for Peter Keim Software and released in 1991. The game was released with full source code.
Smokin' Colts

You ride into Dusty Creek with the sun at your back and a Colt on your hip. The town is scared stiff: Bart Hollis and his gang come and go as they please, the sheriff can't stop them alone, and the bank's safe is next on their list.
Smurf Rescue

You play as Smurfette (The female Smurf) and your mission is to save all Smurfs from the evil wizard Gargamel. He have placed all your friends in cages.

You must save them all to complete the levels. When you have saved them, the game will load next level. On the boss levels you also must kill them to complete the levels.

Some Smurfs may look impossible to reach. But they are not :)
All enemies can be killed by jumping on them. Fire is not used for anything in the game.
SmurfHunt

Game based on the Belgian comic franchise "The Smurfs" (aka "Les Schtroumpfs"), which was created in 1958 by cartoonist Peyo (Pierre Culliford). I consider Smurf Hunt to be a bit of a classic. Studio Peyo would not approve of a shooter in which you rampage through Smurf village, leaving bloody corpses and burning buildings behind. Pat Carson has blended Smurfs and S.E.U.C.K and come up with something fantastically memorable. Game was included in a SMC (software of the month club) package.
Smuś

Smuś is a platform game. The hero of the game was kidnapped by Ice Baron and player must help him escape from the old ruins. There are nearly 250 rooms to overcome. In each of them, the protagonist encounters baron knights, Indians and birds. The small dragon dies after contact with poisoned water and spikes. An additional complication are the moving platforms and the time limit - exactly 9999 seconds. Blue buttons allow to replenish the fire and open the bars blocking the way.
Snace

I made this in 95/96. so it doesn't represent my work today. It was my first "big" idea/project and later based on another game on aminet which involved controlling your "car" on a few coloured tracks.The game was playable, but it lacked versatility mainly because it was turned based. My "clone" is real time and uses 16 colors, but has just 2 players. the tracks you can select have different filename Prefixes(before filename) which means,

race:
E - an easy track
M - a mediocre track (average)
H - a hard track
misc:
F - a fun track
T - a test track , to test new combinations and drawings
B - a bad track. u cant reach finish,
 or my code doesn't handle the track the way its supposed to be
TUTORIAL - for beginners or when representing a new palette
I - a track with useful info or other miscellaneous things
Snacky Folies
An AMOS, freeware snake type game with a twist. Bombs appear and you have to avoid them!
Snail Race
A freeware AMOS racing game from Michele Berionne where you can wiggle that mouse/joystick to get your snail to the finish line!
Snail Racing

A shareware racing game for one to 4 competitive players created by Supurb Simulations. In the Feeding Game mode, you select which foods your snail gets to eat in the five days before a race: sugar, crisps, lettuce, cabbage, or apple. I did not understand how the different foods influence the performance of the snail. The manual says it is up to the players to figure that out.
Snake (Schatztruhe)
A Snake\Worm variant created by Harald Müller (Mueller) and released to the wild in 1994.
Snake AMIGA
This is a snake clone for AMIGA i have built from a demo in scorpion engine by Erik and compiled by Toolkitman.
Snake in the Grass

A snake\worm game that seems to be using two sounds from Anders Bjerin's freeware game SYS (1989): the smacking of lips whenever you eat a white mushroom and the "Yehaa!" when you pick up bonus mushrooms. While the smacking of lips is always sped-up, the "Yehaa!" is either sped-up or slowed-down, depending on what bonus you pick up. It was created by Peter Harris with these assets and released to public domain in 1993.
Snake Pit

Snake Pit is a Snake game in the style of Nibbler where the player has to guide his munching reptile through a maze full of food pellets. The aim is to eat all the pellets and then one or several exits will open up. The problem is that the snake body grows with every eaten pellet which makes it harder to find a path through the labyrinths without colliding with own body which leads to a lost life. A difference from other Snake games is that touching walls does not lead to death. Instead the player loses points and after a short while the snake will randomly choose a new direction to move in. In addition to normal pellets there are also those that shrink the snake when eaten. There are also special walls that can be pushed around by the snake as long as there is nothing on the opposite side of it.

The game has fifty levels and it's possible to start them in any order without completing the previous ones. Also included is a built in editor that allows the player to edit the levels.
Snake's Snack
Snake's Snack is a retro game developed in AMOS Professional by Alberto "BCO" Sgaggero for the legendary Commodore Amiga 500.
SnakeMan

Snakeman is a public domain Oil's Well style game. The idea is to extend a snake down into a maze to collect 'dots'. The body of the snake extends into the maze, and this can't be crossed over, however you may retract the snake in order to take a different route through the maze or to avoid enemies. Should an enemy make contact with your snake, you lose a life. A level is cleared by collecting all the dots in it. Bonus items are scattered around the levels, which reward the player with extra time, points or lives if collected.

Snakeman was programmed in the AMOS programming language.
Snakes (Excellent Design)
A shareware Snake\Worm game for one or two players.
Snakes (NC Gamez)

A freeware game from NC. Games for one or two players. This is a worm\snake game naturally, pick up the randomly placed numbers in order and avoid eating your own tail. The game has 20 levels to slither past.
Snaky
Eat all the dots but not your own tail! A snake\worm shareware game from Roger Schuttelaar and released in 1988.
Snapperazzi

If there was ever a game that could win an award for being the most sponsored in the software industry, this would have to be it. Not only is The Sun newspaper behind it, but so are Fizzy Chewits and Domino Pizzas. 

You play the Snapper, a small but willing photographer who wants to get into the world of the paparazzi. To prove his worth to The Sun editor, he has to race around some large, jerky levels, taking pictures of some of the most misshapen sprites ever seen, while collecting rolls of film and trying to avoid bills, shops and anything else that might try to takes his money. He also needs to collect enough delicious Domino pizzas, so he can then build a space ship to take him to the next level.
Snare

A game with at least a fellowship with Boulderdash, in that is takes plays in a multidirectional maze and is a collect-and avoid type game. This game by Enigma Software Developments was released in 1992 and is a precursor to Muzzy. This is the first release of this game, using the original title from the Spectrum version and featuring music by Andy Brown, who quit the team prior to the development of the enhanced follow-up, entitled MUZZY.
Sneech

Imagine Tron with up to 10 cycles on a screen which keeps filling up with walls and traps, and tons of powerups to collect. Vroom-vroom cycle noises and crazy spot sound effects taken from some weird Salvador Dali alternate universe. Plus a shop with a 3-page list of powerups, its not hard to imagine this game can be fun. Sneech is an excellent party game for up to 6 players. Another good game in the Amiga's strong library of shareware and freeware releases. Paul Burkey went on to work on the ambitious commercial release of Foundation, a clone of Blue Byte's The Settlers. Sneech was included as a bonus on the CD-ROM of Foundation Gold.
Sneer
Yet another game similar to snake. There are hundred levels, passwords, graphics change every fifth level, you can play with different music etc...
Snoball in Hell

Snoball in Hell is a Breakout variant mixed with a shoot 'em up. The player is in control of the Snoball battle tractor, a tank-like vehicle that can be moved up and down along the left edge of the screen. Like in any Breakout game, the objective of each of the game's 16 levels is to clear all bricks by hitting them with a bouncing ball but here there are also numerous enemies that fly from the right towards Snoball. These have to be shot down or dodged since any contact will lead to a life being lost. Missing the ball also leads to a life being lost, and the player has five lives in total.

In addition to the enemies, the player can shoot bonuses that aid the player and anti-bonuses that hinder the player. Bonuses include extra points, slower missile speed, auto rebound, shields, extra lives and level skip while anti-bonuses include minus points, slow fire rate, enemy attack wave, life lost and restart of level.
Snoisnemid

An AMOS freeware game created by Martijn Stam and Dennis van Koningsbruggen for Dimensions Software. The game title is the developers name backwards. It was released in 1995 and came with a built in level editor. Once upon a time in a country very, very near, there was a tragedy going on. The evil king Commodore had gone mad and wanted to destroy his only daughter, princess Amiga. Helped by his evil slaves, the liquidators, king Commodore is going to make a BIG MISTAKE. So it is time for you, prince Pleasance, to go to the castle in Maidenhead and defeat the evil ones. In the castle you will come across many dangers, as the king has turned his castle into a fortress. But with quick thinking, fast action, power ups and some bravery you will reach your beloved princess just in time! And if you need any help with the quest, prince Proudfoot is there to help you. Good luck, you will need it!
Snoopy: The Cool Computer Game

Sally's little brother, Linus, has had his precious security blanket stolen, and is likely to be break down unless he gets it back soon. There are several suspects as to who could have stolen the moth-eaten rag, but there isn't enough evidence to convict someone of the beastly crime. Controlling Snoopy, you must take up the case, and wander around the many flick-screen locations, gathering objects and solving puzzles, until you can eventually locate and return the blanket to Linus - however, time is of the essence, and unless Linus gets his blanket within forty-five minutes, he will surely collapse of a broken heart. Your adventures will see you pottering all over the small town where the gang live, and the game features all of the gang members - Lucy, Sally, Peppermint Patty, and Marcie - in cameo roles.
Snow Bros.

A conversion of the cult fave arcade rave. It's effectively Bubble Bobble in a snowy clime but with a few appropriate twists and some neat cartoon visuals. It looks and plays identically to its arcade parent - well, save for the absence of the simultaneous two player option (it wasn't implemented because the action would have slowed down from the ideal running speed). Although scheduled for release in mid-1991 and completed, the Amiga conversion was never published. Later, the game was rediscovered and released for free.
Snow Strike

You must fly an F14-LBC "Rapier" on a series of missions all along Colombia. You've land missions like free flight, destroy drug labs, bomb drug refineries, destroy drug stores and destroy drug convoy. You've aircraft carrier missions like free flight, destroy enemy aircraft carriers, destroy drug ships and destroy enemy oil supplies. In the air you can fight the MiG-27, Su-27, MiG-29 and MiG-31 armed with heat or radar guided missiles!

You can choose to be an existing pilot or to create a new one. You can choose between 2 levels of difficulty: beginner (less enemy attacks) or expert (the most dangerous). The weather will affect the mission. The good weather will be great for training, and the stormy will be dangerous but great for attacks, as you can hide into the clouds and approach the enemy unnoticed. You'll have a copilot that will help you telling what's going on every moment. You can avoid missiles using your skills, using chaff or... if you can't, you can use your parachute!
Snow Wars

The kids from a rival town are invading! You and your snowball skills are all that is standing in their way. Try to score the highest as wave after wave of enemies appear! There may be a polar bear or two as well...

Use joystick 2 to move left and right. Press and hold the fire button between the trees to build a snowball. You can build small, medium and large. Push up on the joystick when you are below a snowball to throw it. The larger the snowball, the more damage or does. You get more points for hitting further away enemies.

Good luck in the Snow Wars!
Snowfort

SNOWFORT lets you build snowforts and throw snowballs to your heart's content. You can be any of the characters in Snowfort: a Player, a snowman, or Death. Each has it's own special characteristics to master. Battle between 6 players to gain territory by rolling up large snowballs to either build impassible walls, or throw them at your friends. Players can
move and fire in all 8 joystick directions. Snowfort defines the highest levels of playability ever in any game.
Snowy

Snowy is a game for kids featuring 2 sub games, Pairs and Snakes and Ladders. Walk through Snowtown and pick the place for the fun you want. Or maybe you want to go to the party down the lane. A freeware game by John Knight in 1992.
Soccer Cards US 94
A game where you pick from random cards to determine the results of your league soccer games. Pull good cards and come out on top, believe in the heart of the cards!
Soccer Cards: FA Cup Championship

An AMOS based Soccer management game with cards for random events, like some strategy sports board games. 

The game was created by Frozen Ice Production in 1993 and centered around the teams and statistics for the 1992-1993 FA Cup.
Soccer Games 88
A single player German language soccer\football management game focused on the 1988 season and released that same year by Steffan Schwarz as freeware.
Soccer Kid

The game begins when Soccer Kid is waiting for the World Cup to start. However, the alien pirate Scab is scanning for trophies to add to his collection and starts beaming up the World Cup using his spaceship. While he beams the trophy into space, he collides with a satellite, blowing the Cup into five pieces that fall in random places around the world. It is up to Soccer Kid to recover the pieces.
Soccer King

Soccer King is an action oriented, side-scrolling soccer game. The player can either play a single match against the AI or a human opponent or create a league with up to six teams. Gameplay is action oriented and the controls offer only basic functions like shooting or passing. It is possible to set how many minutes a match plays out.
Soccer Manager Plus

Soccer Manager Plus is a managerial soccer simulation. The player takes control over a team from the second division and is responsible for its financial and athletic success. In the original German version the game used real athlete and club names, but the athletes are randomly divided between the clubs.

In various menus, the player can set ticket prices, visit a training camp or take action on the transfer market. Before the match, the athletes are divided into the team. Here the player should note each athlete's statistics (goal, defense, offense, mid field and energy) which determine his performance depending on where he is used. The last setting to take is toughness: the higher the setting, the higher the chances of success. The downside is a higher risk of injuries and cards.

The main part of the game is completely menu based, but the player may choose to watch match highlights, only the goals or directly the result. The match segments are shown in a side-scrolling perspective.
Soccer Pinball

Soccer Pinball is a pinball game with eight round split across three tables. On the soccer-themed levels, a 'goal' is guarded by 'defenders' who must be removed by hitting them. Score three goals to reach the next level - initially you will face another soccer-based table with more defenders. Other football-themed elements include 'throw-in' positions from the side and pop-up players to toggle for points. 

On the Amiga version, the later tables have a casino and gambling as a theme. Gameplay is fundamentally the same - hit the correct targets in sequence to advance, with other targets adding to your score.
Soccer Rivals

Soccer Rivals is a football management game in the style of a board game where you play against 2 other players (human or computer) and try to take your team from Division 4 to Division 1 and win the title. There are 32 teams to choose from and you have the choice of five skill levels. The actual game has the whole board going round the edge of the screen. The board is made up of various amounts of eight icons which when landed on allow you to buy and sell players, train players, adjust utilities like capacity, surveillance cameras and youth team. Other icons have random choices which have bad or good effects of your finances and team. The last icon is a small arcade sequence where you press S to kick a ball at a moving target, hit the target and you win money. In the middle of the board is your team and you can adjust the formation and select the players.
Soccer Superstars

Soccer Superstars is a 2D side-scrolling football game in which the player can chose from 32 international teams to take part in either friendly games or cup tournaments. These can be played against the computer or both computer and a friend, however there is also a demo mode in which you will be able to see an entire tournament -or a friendly match- as a mere spectator. You are also free to modify team line-ups (all composed of real national player names), select basic formation systems, and alter the game length. The game interface is multi-language.
Soccer Supremo
Soccer Supremo is a football management game, developed by Pirate and published by Crysys Software, which was released in Europe in 1987.
Soccer Team Manager

Your primary role is to manage a soccer team, and watch as they develop after each match, which earns or loses you money, without ever seeing or taking part in on field action.

Chose from British and Italian football leagues to custom your own team from selection of top players to hire, fire or exchange with another club. Decisions made will determine their success, chose poorly and it reflects in the overall results. To help in the process, you can review their salaries and receive weekly financial information after a game.

Pick avenue for your team to play, some are more expensive then others as are the top teams you play against. A good crowd turn out helps to boast profits as you gain a percentage of total ticket sales.
Software House

A shareware computer software house management game by Duncan Gunn from 1993. It was programmed in ASM 68k. Own your own Software company. Hire staff and design what type of game you want to put out into the market.
Software Manager

In 1994, Kaiko GmbH publishes Software Manager on Amiga, a strategy and simulation game. In this game, you run your own software company. Your responsibility is to hire and fire programmers and artists, buy decent concepts, then do your best to get the project done - and finally see if it is better than your competitors' products!
Soko

A cheap COMMERCIAL version of Sokoban. There are only 18 levels and game has no title or ending screen. At least this runs smooth with no slowdowns on A500 I recognize the music filched from Double Dragon 3 and the balls from Rock 'n
Soko Ban

Freeware game released on an Amiga Power Cover disk (Issue #37, May 1994). But better play the improved shareware version Push 'n' Shove.

The levels in both this and Push 'n' Shove, are very easy compared to the levels in the original version from 1981/1982. The levels in this one are easy compared to most Sokoban games. This game is not that bad, but it could be better with a relaxing tune. There are no ending screen and the high score table does not let you input your name.
Soko-Ban 84

Remake of the game Soko Ban released in 1982 and presented at AmiGameJam21 . Coded in AMOS, this is the first tukinem game.

The game has 53 levels. There are three display modes to choose from: CGA, Tandy, and Amiga. Soko-Ban is a classic puzzle game, the basis of many clones in recent years. It is installed in a warehouse. At each level, the player must push crates (from square to square) to bring them to the designated places; once each crate is in a marked location, the level is complete. Crates can only be pushed one at a time (so two side-by-side crates can't be pushed together) and can't be pulled - so it's possible to get a crate stuck in a corner, where it can't be recovered! At the later levels, you need to plan 40 stages in advance. 

Updates in 2022 added Dual Playfield and high scores.
Sokoban (Alderan)
A version of the Sokoban puzzle game by Alderan S.C. in 1994. You work as a warehouseman; great fun for days, an attractive puzzle game, dozens of boards.
Sokomond

A simple German language stone-PUSHing game in the style of Sokoban made by Silvio Lange of Diamondsoft. Push the stones to the X spots, using teleporters to avoid trouble spots and don't forget that there is a time limit.
Sol Negro

A millenarian spell, transmitted from parents to children, turned the muscular Bully into a fish and the indomitable Mónica into a hawk. Every full moon one of them suffers a transformation and the other recovers his normal form, which prevents them to be together. Only an extraordinary phenomenon can break the spell, something as extraordinary as a sun eclipse... the Black Sun. In order to break the spell, Bully must free Mónica (the hawk) of her cage for, turned he in fish, arrive on time together at the sacred submarine temple of the sun, a grotto located beyond the borders of the city submerged of Hidrionis, just at the moment in which the moon is embraced with the sun and a huge shade crosses the planet.
Solar Lords

Solar Lords by Alistair Duncan of Tiger Software, released as Shareware in 1993. You and up to 3 of your friends control warlords maneuvering to control six planets. Try to increase your per turn income to outpace your rivals, increase your military power keep up your science rating. Use spies, buy capitol ships, armor and outfit your fleet and rule the galaxy.
Solar Rescue

A simple space shooter with some great attention to detail created using the SEUCK game engine. It was created by Russell Smith and released as freeware in 1997. In general shoot everything, but pick up the heart cards\canisters when you see them. Two player coop is available, each of the ships is distinct in firing range and speed.
Solar System VoidBlast

A basic horizontal shooter written in AMOS by Alessandro Russo aka Axel. A simple but charmy space-game inspired by famous games like Nemesis, Gradius and ProjectX. Many sites have this game being initially released in 2014, but the first release appears to have been in 1992.
Solar System Wars

A glorious freeware shooter created by James Cleverdon in 1994. Your ships are orbiting a star (or two as you can control all options). Navigate the gravity and blast your opponent before they blast you! Use gravity to direct shots. Has support for two button joysticks. Use shields for protection and hyperspace is available.
Soldier 2000

Soldier 2000 is an Action game, developed and published by Artronic Productions, which was released in Europe in 1990. So it has come to this: the horror hostage scene of the future. Who exactly caused it is immaterial. Was it the Milton Keynes Liberation Army, was it the Free F. de Klerk movement? Who cares? Someone, somewhere, has captured a balding, fat, businessman, so the crack anti-terrorist team is going on.

You control a squad of fit, high-trained, ruthless brutal, cute girlies. I know they are cute because I saw one in her bikini at the arming stage, where everything starts. OK, so these girlies are pretty tough, but they are still human, so they cannot carry everything. Heavy items will slow them down until they are so overladen they cannot stand up. You will not be allowed to critically load your troops.

There are 14 items to choose from, ranging from small single-shot hand guns through machine guns to grenade launchers and experimental pulse lasers.
Soldier of Light

You play as Xain, the Soldier of Light, who must visit a number of invaded planets and wipe out the evil hordes that have attacked the human populations. The main bulk of the gameplay is a horizontally scrolling run and gun game, while some stages put you in an horizontal shoot 'em up scenario. You take control of Xain, who can jump or duck to avoid enemies and jump up to higher ledges. Lots of extra weaponry can be collected along the way, although this is lost when one of your five lives is lost. Each time you defeat a planet's boss, you control Xain's spaceship and have to go through a short horizontal shmup level, before selecting your next target planet.

The planets Cleemalt Soa, Lagto Soa, Cleedos Soa, Kworal Soa and Guwld Soa are all available for selection immediately.
Sole Defender
Created by Ken Vale of Antimax Software and released in 1992, this single player multi-directional shooter has you piloting a space fighter taking out baddies all over this space station complex.
Solid Gold

SOLID GOLD is a freeware (in electronic form) Jump'n Run with 8-way soft scrolling. It's written for the classic Amiga hardware and designed in the style of the early 90s.

You are John Kayle, an adventurer and archeologist, trying to recover important artefacts in four different places of the world, competing with a mysterious secret society.

The game features ten levels spanning four worlds, with different graphics and enemies. Each level's goal is to find an artefact which will lead the way to the next world. Most enemies can be killed by jumping onto them. It is important to hit them from above. Touching an enemy's side or contact from below are lethal for the hero. After collecting 50 gems of any kind you will be granted an extra life. Each level is concluded by a statistics screen. It will display the number of collected items and killed enemies, opposed to total numbers. Upon reaching the maximum possible numbers, an extra bonus is granted.
SolidQuad

A fast driving game where you blast through the countryside, splashing through rivers and puddles and jumping ditches and lava flows on 3 courses. Careen through puddles to extinguish any on board fires the lava may have caused. Press fire and pull back to get the most out of the jumps. Avoid pedestrians and hit the ramps when possible to jump ditches. Each course does seem to come with a mid-level boss where you can shoot the scarecrow heads you avoided in previous parts of the game at the boss. Some of what you need to do to be most successful is intended as a puzzle to be figured out according to the creator, J. Richard Evans who released this game to the public domain in 1992. The game and color palette heavily inspired by old Spectrum games.If you want more info just read the German or English versions of the readme.
Solitaire (Amiga Byte)

A strategy solitaire card game published by the Italian magazine, Amiga Byte as a cover disk in 1992. This is 'regular' solitaire. On the main part, you build down alternating colors, moving cards or piles of cards among the columns. If you develop an empty column, it can only be filled with a King. The Aces go into the upper left corner, and then you build up in the same suit. When you click on the deck, the next 3 cards are shown, or the deck is turned over.
Solitaire (Felix R. Jeske)

Solit aka Solitaire is a freely-distributable, shareware non-Klondike solitaire card game for the Amiga by Felix R. Jeske, it runs under Workbench 2.x. This is version 1.13 which contains some enhancements to version 1.06 found on FF882. There were two versions, the demo and a full version with extra features like undo and so forth.
Solitaire Royale

This was an early commercial instance of Card Solitaire. There are 8 different solitaire games, including Klondike, Calculation, and Three Shuffles and a Draw. You can also play "Aunt Anne's Tour" where you play all 8 in row, trying for the highest combined score, and 3 children's games. In addition, there are 10 different choices for deck art.
Solitaire Sampler
A collection of five solitaire games: Carlton; Martha; Pas Seul; Slider; and Poker Squares. Doubled as a demo for SERIOUS SOLITAIRE and published on Assassins Game disk #93.
Solitaire's Journey

One-hundred and five solitaire games rendered in beautiful graphics (for 1992). Games have full rules and will allow different users to "log into" the game and keep averages and high scores.

Players can also build their own "tournaments" by selecting a sub-set of the games and playing for the highest score.

"Quests" allow users to play solitaire games to navigate through a graphical house to find treasure.
Solius the Sorcerer
Solius the Sorcerer is a german Amiga multi screen platformer action game released in Europe in 1992 by CompuTec Verlag.
Solo Card Games
A collection of card games released in 1997 by Leon Pennington. It includes Klondike, Pyramid, Beleauered Castle, ST Helana, Calculation, Miss Milligan, Scorpion, Demon and Windmill variants.
Solo Flight

A cross between Scramble and R-Type games, lots of goodies and upgrades to grab, keep your fuel levels up by grabbing fuel cans avoid the cave walls as they mean instant death. Blast missiles and enemy ships. Game made by Sławomir Maguda and released as open source freeware in 2004.
Solomon's Key

Reverse engineered from the Atari ST version. 
 
Solomon's Key is a platform game with both action and strategy elements. On each level your goal is to retrieve a key which can then be used to unlock the exit. To help out, you have a magic wand which can be used to create and destroy blocks (though some blocks can't be destroyed). In order to reach the key you will need carefully to arrange the blocks on the screen so you can jump your way around safely. Wandering around each level are a variety of enemies which will cause you to lose a life if you're caught. Some creatures can be killed by destroying the block they are standing on, others must be dodged. Hidden bonuses and magic can be found on many of the levels, sometimes even hidden in blocks. Some treasures give you bonus points, others can form magic spells to help deal with the enemies. To make the game more difficult, each level has a time limit in which it must be completed.
Solomon's Key 2

The game's plot takes place before the original Solomon's Key, and is framed as a story being told by an elderly woman to her grandchildren. The story takes place on Coolmint Island, an island made of ice and home to the winter fairies. When the evil wizard Druidle begins sending flame monsters to attack and melt the island, the queen of the fairies summons the apprentice wizard Dana to defend them, granting him the use of ice magic to help extinguish the flame monsters.
Solos-7
An AMOS based freeware flight simulator created by Nicky Igoe in 1996.
SoloTrek II

A public domain Star Trek battle simulator. The intrepid search continues to boldly go where no Amigan has gone before. Or something like that anyway. In SoloTrek 2, your objective is to map out the entire galaxy, dealing accordingly with any Romulan, Klingon or Federation ships you 
encounter along the way. It’s an incredibly complex and involving game which is going to demand a good deal of time and effort from anyone seeking to really get to grips with it. If you persevere though, in the long run, it’s the sort of game which could prove infinitely more rewarding than a straightforward shoot-em-up. 

There are a whole host of gadgets to be clicked on as you navigate your way around the galaxy.
Something about the Bunny

This was an entry in the First Ever (And Maybe The Only) Interactive Fiction Mini-Competition. It was written by Graham Fyffe using the pseudonym of 'GLYPH'. A Happy Special Magic Production by Glyph (1998 Mini Competition) to you. Enjoy this game where you just might learn the meaning of life and help a few sorry sods in the process.
Somewhere in Time

Coverdisk available on Amiga Fun #35. Also released on issue 2 of Amigo!. This is not an ordinary racing game: it requires you to build immense skill to make your way through all the obstacles. Every time you crash against an obstacle, you will lose a life. You have to steer a car to the exit of the level within a limited amount of time. There are multiple pathways and quite a lot of dead ends. You need to memorize the most efficient route and carefully drive without bumping into obstacles.
Son of Zeus

“Son of Zeus” is an Amiga game whose development was unfortunately never completed.

 Displaying sometimes disproportionate graphics, it is in line with the Sword of Sodan type hack'n slash though the player is only fighting one enemy at a time. It should have found a publisher in Electronic Zoo in 1992, but history reserved a completely different fate for it.
Son Shu-Shi

Son Shu Shi is a game that nearly never was. Although released on the Atari ST, the Amiga version was previewed and reviewed in magazines but never appeared. The authors completed the Amiga version, but no longer have a copy of the source code or binary. However, a friend had still retained a working version.

The evil demon Taar-Ka has occupied the lovely kingdom of Tan Tao, which is why Son Shu-Shi is now allowed to act as a savior in the emergency. Technically very well balanced game, very colourful with beautiful background. The sound effects are clear and crisp and music is everywhere.

This is a brilliant platformer. Gameplay is no slouch and helps to make it thoroughly entertaining with fast and frantic playability. So beautiful and very addictive. Now I need “one more go”.
Sonic 060

Sonic 060 is an unofficial fan made port of Sonic The Hedgehog for high end accelerated AGA Amigas. It was 100% vibe coded by me with Claude, and it is based on architecture, research and design choices made by reassembler and RetroRic of the Aonic project. To see the full details of each developer's contributions to Sonic 060 as well as how the training information was obtained please read credits.htm in the zipfile.
Sonic Boom

Sonic Boom is an arcade game shoot 'em up with a vertically-scrolling perspective in which the player is a US pilot, armed with the super-powerful Sonic Boom aircraft. Players must face six levels of cannon-fodder enemies in order to prevent the world being destroyed, but has 5 continues with 3 lives each to make use of. There is a boss at the end of each level which must be beaten in a time limit in order to progress. Most enemies are aircraft, but there are also tanks, trains, and turret installations to wipe out. Defeated waves of enemies reveal improved weaponry and other bonuses.
Sonic the Hedgehog

Gotta. Go. Fast. While there was to be an Amiga port of the Sega Genesis platformer in 1992, that never materialized into a working game. This 2008 creation by Rebel is a fan-game project and includes the full Backbone package with all the necessary files to get you started making your own levels. If you want to help finish this project off, all the tools are available to you now! Like the original, The plot of the game is simple. The evil Dr. Robotnik has captured many of Sonic's animal friends and trapped them inside robots. Fortunately, Sonic can free his friends by destroying the robots with his spin attack. Grab coins and move fast, be a whole new speed of hero!
Sonic The Hedgehog (Reassembler)

This is a work-in-progress demo of my port of 'Sonic The Hedgehog' from the Sega Megadrive to the Commodore Amiga 1200. The port is entitled 'Aonic'.
It is directly based on the original code. Specifically, the disassembly published by the Sonic Retro team. As such, it plays identically, although the rendering has been heavily optimized and rewritten for the Amiga. Visually, there are necessary and obvious differences. This demo is the first Act of Green Hill Zone only. But architecturally I am scaling up to deliver the complete game. The major challenge isn't converting the code, but ensuring the engine is performant on a different architecture. Around 95% of the time spent on Aonic has been devising optimisations and rearchitecting the game to run at an acceptable frame-rate.
Sonic the Hedgehog Amiga Tech Demo

I had the idea of trying to bring Sonic to the Amiga earlier this year, but with the current projects I had in the pipeline, I decided to put it on the back burner and revisit it sometime in the future.
Sony Game

Sony Game is a German-language promotional platformer game controlled with the keyboard or joystick, starring a grinning Sony Walkman with arms and legs. There are various patrolling monsters that you need to avoid, while also keeping your energy levels boosted and completing the level before the time limit runs out. The camera moves around the level in a "flip-screen" way, instead of scrolling. There is an in-game shop system for buying power-ups, and a password-based continue system.
Sooty & Sweep

Sooty and Sweep are two famous characters from British children TV that have appeared in various shows for more than fifty years. This platformer is the first game featuring the characters and they have got themselves into some problems. Matthew has gone out and left Sooty in charge of the house. Problem is that Sweep has left all his old bones all over the house and left the door to the garden open so that all kinds of bugs have gotten in. The game simply involves collecting all of the bones while avoiding the creepy crawlies that are occupying the house. The player can choose to play as either Sooty or Sweep and they differ in the weapon they use. Sooty uses a magic wand while Sweep uses a water pistol. They both have the same effect on the enemies though, stunning them for a few seconds so that the player can move past. Different items can be picked up.
Sooty Paint
An educational painting and drawing game for kids.
Sooty's Fun With Numbers

Six short mathematical tests aimed at children up to 7 years of age come together in this package. Sooty the silent magical bear is one of the UK’s most enduring children’s characters, and his friends Sweep the squeaking dog and Soo the talking bear join him here. The games can be played with little or no computer knowledge, and feature full graphics.

In Magic Numbers the player must count how many wands Sooty has on the screen. Sweep’s Bones involves moving bones from a pile on the right (Sweep’s stash) to the left (the ones he will enjoy today). Soo’s Hats is an addition test. In Bigger/Smaller you are presented with 2 numbers, and asked to select the biggest or smallest, which Sooty will magic away with his wand. Order Order presents a line of numbers, some of which are filled in, and challenges the player to select the others (which are randomly arranged elsewhere on the screen) and place them in the correct positions.
Sophelie

Sophelie is a horizontally scrolling shooter where you control a bird. You travel through three parts of the game fighting various enemy types including spinning planets, killer trees and giant eyeballs. Additional lives can drop from dead enemies and the game can be continued if you die. The backgrounds feature colorful parallax scrolling effects that change with each part of the game.
Sopwith

Sopwith AGA brings the classic 1984 MS-DOS aerial combat game to the Commodore Amiga 1200, taking advantage of the machine's AGA chipset. Originally developed by David L. Clark for the Canadian company BMB Compuscience, Sopwith became one of the memorable early action games for IBM PC compatibles. Now, more than four decades after its original release, this little piece of gaming history has found a new home on the Amiga!
Sorcerer

Following the defeat of the evil krill in Enchanter, the intrepid apprentice have become a full member of the Circle, under the command of the famed Necromancer Belboz. Very soon, however, the hero notices that something strange has been happening to the master. He frequently talks to himself and seems to be under some sort of a malevolent influence - until one day, he is mysteriously kidnapped. Looks like the brave Enchanter must venture on a perilous journey once again, and bring back the leader of the Circle.

Sorcerer is a sequel to Enchanter, and is part of the Zork universe. Like its predecessors, it is a text adventure, in which the player interacts with the game world by typing combinations of verbs and objects. The spell system from the previous game is back; a new feature is the protagonist's ability to drink magical potions, which must be done sometimes in order to solve the game's puzzles.
Sorcerer Lord

Sorcerer Lord is a medieval fantasy game of tactical warfare.

The evil Shadowlord's army is threatening to overrun the peaceful country of Galanor. The alliance of races in Galanor isn't very fond of suppression, slavery or extinction, so they are preparing for war -- it's your job to coordinate the Galanorian defense.

Movement and combat are turn-based. You and the Shadowlord alternately recruit new troops, move armies on a 2D hex-map of the land and try to conquer the enemies garrisons. The outcome of fights is shown as plain text only. Although the gameplay is quite simple, there are a few tactical knacks like certain races fighting more fiercely in certain terrain types, fatigue levels and basic statistics for army leaders. Despite the game's title, magic is a rather unimportant element of chance in battles and not under your direct control.

The game contains a time limit; you've got 40 turns in easy level, less in advanced levels.
Sorcerors Apprentice

Sorcerors Apprentice is a platformer that places you in the part of wizened old man blessed with the King's magic powers. The reason for this gift is because the King wants you to free the land from the forces of darkness.
Sorcery Plus

Sorcery+ is an expanded re-release of Sorcery. Besides new graphics and sound, it features an additional scenario which is played after finishing the original content. Here the player visits 28 new locations in a quest to destroy the necromancer.
Sorefist

An attempt at creating a clone of the arcade and 8-bit home computer classic Renegade. The game, however, doesn't feel finished: There are only three levels and enemies hardly ever attack and the music has some corrupted samples.
Sorry!

A homebrew adaptation of the Parker Brothers, Sorry! board game released in 1990 for 4 players. This is the computer version of an old Parker board game from 1934. Also suitable for social gatherings.
Sort It
A slide puzzle game like a 15 puzzle but with an 8x8 board, luckily there is no time limit. The game was created by the prolific game creator, Harald Müller (Mueller) and published in 1995.
Soul Crystal

Your name is Dave, and these are your first holidays you're spending alone, without your parents. You're resting in a hotel near a mysterious Loch in Scotland. You go swimming in the lake and dive through a waterfall - on the other side of it, you're finding yourself in a strange fantasy-like world.

The game is a mixture of a graphical- and text adventure. All actions can be performed by typing or by clicking on the icons.
Soul Killa
Four knights, two cursed worlds and a demon who collects souls. Whoever finds the four Soul Stones first opens the portal to the Realm of Evil, and must face Soul Killa in the end.
Soumrak: Legenda Kouzelneho Medailonu
The game Soumrak or in English, Dusk is another of the series of Czech text adventures for the Amiga computer from MKCS. The environment of the game is a little different from the previous ones.
Sound the Space Cadet

SOUND THE SPACE CADET ** was included on the cover disk of Amiga Action Issue #65. A 2D platformer, collector game. A precursor to Ace The Space-Case. I started laughing the first time I saw the attack animation of the player sprite: It is literally impossible to shoot something that is right in front of you because shots fly out at an 45-degree angle. You have bounce shots off the ceiling, and even then, enemies are only affected by the explosion frame of the animation. Unexploded projectiles which you have just thrown do not hurt them. You will constantly spam the attack button, yet only a fraction of your shots will count. It is one of the most ineffective, frustrating-to-use weapons I have ever seen in a game, and I love it!
Space 1889

A role-playing adventure set in the "future" as seen by Victorian era science fiction writers. Players explore the far corners of the Earth (Atlantis, King Tut's tomb etc...) and travel between planets on ships made of martian "liftwood" (invented by none other than Thomas Edison). Based on GDW's pencil and paper roleplaying game. Similar in design to Paragon's MegaTraveller series.
Space Ace

Intergalactic hero Space Ace faces off against the evil Commander Borf, who hits him with an Infanto-Ray, turning Ace into an adolescent version of himself called Dexter. Now Ace/Dexter must not only rescue his girlfriend Kimberly but also prevent the destruction of the Earth at the hands of Borf.

Readysoft's version of the laserdisc arcade game Space Ace for 16-bit computers follows the mold of their earlier Dragon's Lair adaptation: only selected scenes from the original game are used, with all the graphics redrawn from the original cel animation to fit the capabilities of the target machines.

As in Dragon's Lair, the game consists of the cartoon movie running by itself, with the player being required to press the right button at the right time (either moving or firing Ace's gun) or see one of many death animations.
Space Ace (Stephen McLeod)

Not to be confused with the popular laserdisc based game related to Dragon's Lair. this harkens back to an even earlier shooting game with a first person cockpit perspective. The player can scroll his view in eight directions and lock his current vector to keep moving in that direction. Space ships will appear scrolling through the game world which have to be shot down. Some space ships also try to fire back at the player. The game is over when the shields of the player are depleted.
Space Ace II: Borf's Revenge

You might be surprised to note that despite coming on five disks, Space Ace II only really gives you about four sequences of action, which are then subdivided into the tiny little blow-by-blow segments or scenes which you actually play. This, coupled with the tendency of the animations and samples to be cut off abruptly, gives the game a very bitty feel. Secondly, it's lazy. The same death sequences are used repeatedly, even in very different scenarios.

Game looks pretty, and it's moderately entertaining for about the first 3 minutes but you will finish it inside three hours (absolute maximum) and you'll hate it so much by the end that you'll never want to see it again.
Space Assault

What happened so far... Strangers from the planet Dumcleps sent some ships to attack planet Enacirruh. They destroyed the cities and killed civilians without any reason. Their aim was to occupy the planet. The United Galaxy Forces charged you to rescue the planet and to defeat the evil. There is not much time until the whole planet is ruined. Try your best!
Space Attack
A 1-2 player cooperative space shooter developed by Michael Pratt and published by Berliner Spielekiste in 1990.
Space Attack 2
A cooperative space shooter for 1-2 players developed by Michael Pratt using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit, and published in 1990 by Berliner Spielekiste.
Space Ball

An action duel created as a playable demo by Amigos Development in 1993. Fly your ship around and smash the ball with it to move the ball towards and hopefully into your friend\foe's goal it before they do the same to you! Like Air Hockey except you fly the paddle!
Space Baller

Space Baller is an action game, developed and published by International Software Köln, which was released in Europe in 1987. And later released in both the International Arcade Action and the Amiga Stars Collection compilation packs. There were two versions, one with a blue ball and the other with a red and white Amiga ball. Humour, electric atmosphere and superb game play. Use the joystick to guide the bouncing ball through space, pick up different objects and bonuses but watch out for the aliens trying to shoot you down.
Space Battle

Space Battle is a one or two player version of the classic arcade game Asteroids where you have to survive being in a asteroid field where the rocks move about the screen. With a joystick you need to move about the screen or shoot them which makes them split into two. You keep splitting them till they are finally destroyed. If things get too hectic you can Hyperspace to another part of the screen but you can easily appear in the path of an asteroid. The game is viewed from above and the whole asteroid field is shown on the whole screen. There are three modes of the game, Solo (One player game), Team (One and Two players scores are combined) and Competition (One and Two players compete for the highest score).
Space Battle (Andrew Thomas)

A two player dog fighting game by Andrew Thomas. Created and released to PD in 1994. Two worlds are at war, the energy crisis has hit and all forms of energy are incredibly expensive. So save your cash if you want to survive!
Space Battleship

A shareware strategy game for up to four players that can be played in total versus mode or in cooperative teams by Raymond Saltel and released in 1995. Set up curved space, planets, nebula and asteroids, black holes, time limited turns, hit probability and if ships can exit the map. Define your ship, equip with weapons and propulsion.
Space Blob

Pick up all the glowing objects without getting hit by a moving object or by falling into a spike. There are 18 screens you have to complete before the game loops and restarts with the first one. Screen 6, 12 and 18 are bonus rounds with a time limit.
Space Bomber
A Defender style shooter complete with a scanner and humans to rescue. It was made by Harald Müller (Mueller) and published by Intersoft, which was released in Europe in 1993.
Space Bomber 2

The sequel to the original Defender style horizontally scrolling shooter created by Harald Müller (Mueller) and prequel to Space Bomber 3. Save the humans and destroy the aliens. It would be later re-released in the Gamers' Delight and Gamers' Delight 2 compilations.
Space Bomber 3

The final release in the set of Space Bomber games from coder : Harald Müller (Mueller), all published in 1993 and released in Germany. It is a 2D, horizontally scrolling Defender style game. Save the humans on the ground from the aliens in the air.
Space Cab

SPACE CAB was available via mail-order only from Tronic Verlag, the publisher of ASM Magazine (Aktueller Software Markt). The game was submitted to Tronic Verlag as part of their "Microwelle Competition", who sought to find a publisher for the game or, failing that, publish the game themselves.
Space Cavern Blaster

This platform shooter created by dotmos and submitted to the Retro Platform Jam#6 is available for a number of retro computers and consoles. Updates since the game jam on itch.io have fixed and improved the game as well as added a number of new levels.
Space Chase
An updated version of the seminal classic action collect'em up game by P. Hubert and released to public domain in 1988.
Space Chase (Michael Stickler)
Red Amiga Ball vs Blue Amiga Ball for two players in this game by Michael Stickler from 1988.
Space Cleaner Too

Was released as a Amiga Format cover disk, In this game by Kelvin Truswell you must avoid alien entanglements as you collect up all the cans in different sectors of space. You more you collect the higher your score, but each sector has a challenge all its own.
Space Combat

Space Combat is a project in REDPILL without much pretension. The only goal of the game is to get more points than your friends. Originally released for CAPACITOR PARTY 2017. A top down space shooter with the possibility of playing against each other in a two player mode.
Space Crusade

Space Crusade is a science fiction strategy game converted from the Games Workshop/Milton Bradley boardgame, in which you control a commander and four marines who are sent on different missions aboard hostile alien starships. Your commander starts off as a sergeant, but he can work his way through the ranks. The game allows three players, each commanding one marine chapter each. The alien team is `played` by the computer.

The game is a literal conversion of the board game in the same vein as Gremlin's earlier Hero Quest. It can be best described as a turn-based board game in which the player must fulfill the primary and secondary objectives to complete the mission, which usually involves elimination of entire alien force on board or destruction of mothership etc. This game features unique 3D close-ups during the battle scenes, a feature which was later adopted by games like the X-Com series.
Space Crusade: The Voyage Beyond

Space Crusade is a science fiction strategy game converted from the Games Workshop/Milton Bradley board game, in which you control a commander and four marines who are sent on different missions aboard hostile alien star ships. Your commander starts off as a sergeant, but he can work his way through the ranks. The game allows three players, each commanding one marine chapter each. The alien team is `played` by the computer. 

After the success of the original Space Crusade, Gremlin Graphics created 10 new levels. These had higher difficulty than the previous ones, and included new monsters and game features. This edition includes the original game and the new levels, making for 22 levels in total; a lower-priced pack with just the new levels was also released at the same time.
Space Day
A scrolling vertical Shoot 'Em Up created by Dimmen Gestel who did coding, graphics and music for this game, released to the public domain in 1989.
Space Dunk
An asteroids clone\update made by Harald Müller (Mueller) and released commercially in 1994.
Space Eclipse
Your spaceship has crashed on a planet and you must find yourself an escape plan. An AMOS game from the prolific Asa Margetts, released to PD in 1995.
Space Fight

A Space Invaders clone where the player controls a space craft that has to eliminate an incoming alien horde. The player's ship moves horizontally across the bottom and shoots at the advancing columns of aliens. The aliens move across the screen left to right, then one column down, then they start to go from right to left, repeating the process until either they are all eliminated or they get to the bottom in which case the player loses. The aliens can shoot back and there are three barriers between the player ship and the aliens that can be used as a short of shielding that erodes as they are shot. The aliens shoot back and a hit will eliminate one of the five starting lives. Once these are out, it's game over.
Space Gun

2039 A.D. Man begins deep space exploration in search of new life forms and usable fuel sources. What he discovers is trouble.

Until now, the success of past explorations was causing the space effort to grow by leaps and bounds. Until now, the explorers had found little more than fungus and small insects as alternative lifeforms. Until now, the chief dangers had been those posed by the hostile environment of space. Until now, the aliens had not known about THEM.

On the ragged edge of the galaxy, other creatures that roam the stars discover humans and spaceships to be excellent sources of food and other resources. Prepared at the worst for clashes with rival exploration teams, the human crews can do little to defend themselves as wave upon wave of nightmare creatures descend upon their ships and bases.
