The company has become extremely wealthy and powerful after inventing the CHIP, which is a cybernetic implant capable of altering the perceptions of human beings so that the reality of a dystopia is perceived as a utopia.

The citizens of North and South America, tired of high taxes and dangerous streets, are rebelling against Eurocorp control to regain their autonomy. Rival Syndicates are using the revolt as the ideal opportunity to gain the upper hand in the ongoing struggle for supremacy.
Sys

A game built on the addictive game PONGO but with several added features. You have been assigned the demanding task of cleaning viruses from your SYSOP's hard disk. To kill a virus, you simply kick a disk at it. There are fifty different levels, and on each level, the speed will increase and the viruses will be smarter and start to hunt you. Version 2.10, binary only.
SysBlaster
Control ship with joystick. Shoot with FIRE button. ESC quits game. You have limited fuel and ammunition. Your goal is to shoot enemy object (UFO). You'll get score for this.
System Defender

A side-scrolling shoot-em-up. Kill the aliens and rescue the little spacemen! Created by J. Kennedy and D. Irvine. Warning: this is not a drill! Alien fleet approaching Terran system. Central control predicts the alien fleet will attack the following locations: Terran Lunar System, Planet Earth, Mars. Mission objectives: Protect humanoids from abduction and mutation. 

Available weapons: Multiple fire laser, limited smart bombs and hyperspace entry shield.
System-4
Q*Bert clone with cute character designs and smooth gameplay. Similar to the original, if a bit more complex especially in later levels. It allows 2 simultaneous gamer play.
Syzyf

Syzyf is a timed puzzle-solving game, similar to Sokoban. The task requires making a passage to the evacuation point. There are two types of ground: standard and ice. Ice ground slides the vehicle to the first standard ground field. The cubes are divided into four types, two movable and two immobile. The first one moves just one field after pushing, the second one stops after contact with any obstacle, the third one may be only destroyed be using a bomb and the fourth one can't be removed at all. There are three types of vehicle visualization. The vehicle may carry an unlimited amount of bombs.

The game consists a total of 80 levels. After each completed level the player receives a password. The game features a level editor for up to 15 boards.
Szachista

Szachista is an adaptation of classic Chess game for up to two players (human or computer). The game allows to set a few additional visual options presented in adjustable windows, such as a list of defeated pawns, real-time movement analysis or turn clock. The player may use hints, undo last move, select of of three available difficulty levels. The database of the game includes most of the known Chess tactics showing the name of the recognized ones.
The game has a built-in tutorial explaining all Chess rules and allowing to practice prepared tasks.
Szalter

Szalter is a new puzzle game for the Amiga made by Benedykt Dziubałtowski and Czesław Mnich. In the game you must turn on all the light-bulbs. The light-bulbs switch on or off when you walk by them. The game can be played on a 68k Amiga (diskette or hard disk).
Szalter on Holiday
Amiga platform game made with Backbone by Czeslaw Mnich in 2013.
Söldner
A German language turn based, top-down, strategy war game created by Rainer Mosner that comes with a scenario editor and was released by Gamebench, a Markt & Technik company.
T Tec Maze

A licenseware maze game created by Trevor Taylor and released in 1991. The piece of software has been designed with a competition in mind. To reach the exit you must alter the maze by moving over switches which are circles of 1,2,4 or 6 colors. Each time you land on a switch, all the gates of the same color will move. In later levels some of the gates will take on false colors to make things more interesting.
T-Bird

Players control a Foourd T-Bird, a transportation system capable of great speeds up to 1346 mph. Their job is to destroy the swarms of aliens – including flying saucers, tie fighters, space jellyfish, unidentifiable blobs, and the like – and dodge their fire. This can be achieved by shooting them with the standard zapper or use a smart missile to destroy everything in sight. 

When an entire swarm is destroyed, getting the token that appears give the player a roving sight, sideways-firing missiles, extra lives, extra missiles, and so on. Between each swarm, a meteor shower appears, and players need to avoid being hit. At the end of each level, players have to destroy a guardian to proceed to the next, and the smart missiles cannot be used to destroy them.
T-Racer

T-Racer is a 2D side-scrolling shoot 'em up with a side view. Written for Amiga line of computers entirely in Assembly 68000.

Technically it offered the best that existed at the time: multi-layer parallax scrolling, hundreds of on-screen color, dozens of BOB (Blitter Objects, or sprite, for non-Amigans), scroll extremely fluid. Call me old-fashioned, but I'm in it for the effects--explosions are good, and the last blue 'rippley-looking level' really hit the eye-cones. Music's good. Overall: difficult, somewhat interesting.
T-Triz
An itty-bitty, tiny Tetris clone from Deadsoft published in 1991. This feels something like a joke game, but you decide if you have what it takes to go tiny.
T-Triz 2

Where the original tried to test the limits of the smallest playable Tetris game, this version flips that on it's head with an insanely large playscreen for very large tetrominos. Joke, or challenge...you be the judge.
T-ZerO

An old-fashioned horizontally scrolling shoot 'em up in the R-Type vein. Compared to the First-Person Shooters, it might seem quaint, but it's interesting to see this style done using later Amiga hardware capabilities and features.

There are 3 different ships on offer, as part of a high level of customisability, including an Arcade mode with bonus fruit, variable colour explosions, and variable background detail for those who find that the most colourful version obscures some of the enemies.

There are two different routes through each level, but either way results in hordes of enemies to take on - horizontally scrolling shooters tend to be tricky, due to the amount of things happening on screen at once. Like so many FPSs but so few scrolling shooters, you can design your own levels as well.
T.F.X.

T.F.X. (Tactical Fighter eXperiment) is a flight simulation where the player can fly with F-117A, Eurofighter 2000 or F-22 Superstar in various scenarios as a UN fighter pilot. Before the player begins his/her duty, there is a need to complete 10 training missions. Only then will the rest of the possible game modes be available. The game also contains a mission editor where the player can create his/her own missions in any of the chosen scenarios.

The Amiga version was never officially released by Ocean. It was later included as a give-away game on a CU Amiga cover disk.
T2: The Arcade Game

The story is that a terminator sent from the future to kill the leader of the resistance, Sarah Connor, failed miserably and now the enemy is targeting the future leader, Sarah's son John. But young John has a guardian angel (you) and your job is to protect him from the said evil.

Using a point-of-view perspective, you target a gunsight at a host of baddies and blow them to smithereens. These include Endoskeletons with rifles, machinegun-toting Cyborgs, acid-chucking laboratory technicians and various devilsome airborne craft. You start with a machine gun and 25 guided missiles, which are best used sparingly. Along the way, there are a whole host of pick-ups to gather including extra credits, protective shields, and a plethora of destructive firepower. They appear in kit cases and you must click to open them and click again to obtain them. It is seriously fast action. There are seven levels to tackle including a van chase where you battle against a T-1000 in a helicopter.
Table Tennis Simulation

"Realistic life on a table tennis table" is the poorly-translated promise for this recreation of a popular indoor game. You can play a full season of tournaments, with world rankings updated as you go. Singles and doubles matches are on offer, and their lengths are variable. A full ball-machine training mode is offered, which allows you to face a succession of shots, with a choice of shot styles and speeds to allow you to hone problem areas of your game. Two player matches can also be played, and mouse or joystick control are supported.
Tactical Manager

Following success with the mail-order Football Tactician series, Talking Birds entered the mainstream with this retitled version. It's a football management game, setting you in charge of one of the teams in the top 2 English divisions of the time and giving you control over transfers, tactics and training regimes as you aim to guide your team to success. Initially you can only manage the lower teams, but if you succeed over a few seasons you will become respected enough to have a chance to get the top roles.

The focus is on ultra-realism, which makes it very hard to quickly transform a club's fortunes, as there is a lack of money at many of the smaller teams and attracting players is harder than in the Premier Manager series and similar. Matches are viewed from top-down highlights, with 3 levels of detail (goals-only, highlights and kick-by-kick) offered.
Tactical Manager 2

The sequel to Tactical Manager goes much further than the predecessor, including a massive database with 30 championships with 60 leagues, with over 32000 players.

The game runs from a regular Windows interface, and all options can be selected with the mouse or the keyboard. Game options include the usual tactical selection, sending the player to train weaker parts of their game or send them to recovery.
TaeKwonDo Master

TaeKwonDo Master is a digitized fighting game. The game features three modes - single, duel (2 players) and tournament (3 to 6 players) and allows the player to choose one of six characters. Each character is described by height, weight and special blow and uses its own set of four unique moves. In contrast to the one year later released ECS side-scrolling version of the game, titled Super TaeKwonDo Master, TaeKwonDo Master uses enhanced AGA graphics and is played on a single screen board with 3rd-person perspective.
Tag

TAG is a 2-player shoot em up where you fly around a huge playing
field and blast your opponent! Simple, but very addictive!
Tag Team Wrestling

Now, Tag Team Wrestling makes its Amiga debut as a nearly arcade-accurate transcode for AGA Amigas. This conversion brings the original coin-op’s distinctive wrestling action and tag-team strategy giving Amiga players a chance to experience an early cornerstone of arcade wrestling.
Taito's Super Space Invaders

Remember that arcade classic Invaders? Well this game takes it to the next level with harder aliens, bosses, power ups, and a variety of scenery! Invaders come in several configurations for you to try to blast, and power-ups help you with more weapons to choose from.
Tajemnica Bursztynowej Komnaty

Tajemnica Bursztynowej Komnaty or The secret of the Amber Room is an adventure game with graphics presented in the form of photographs. The action takes place in the surrounding countryside of the old palace. The main goal of the player is finding the famous Amber Chamber. The character may carry up to eighteen items that can be used and combined. The game screen is divided into inventory/action panel, commentary field and photograph showing the current location.
Tajemnica Usticu

An unreleased Polish game from Logical in 1998. adventure and trading game with a pinch of RPG elements and tactical elements (fighting on a chessboard). The game takes place at an unspecified time on a planet inhabited by the Pel tribe. These are the indigenous people of this planet and the player takes on the role of one of the natives. Pelovians are not very technically advanced, the ambitions of most of them do not reach further than their own backyard, but there are exceptions who dare to dream of traveling to all parts of the planet. Such Pełs most often become traders or disappear without a trace. The character controlled by the player is the grandson of one of the traders, who leaves him an intriguing letter with some cash so that he can escape from his backwater.
Take 'Em Out

Take 'em Out is a typical Op Wolf clone, only more violent. Blood flows freely as you tear your way through wave after wave of terrorists and the odd civilian hostage. Before you are let out on your wave of carnage you have to qualify on the shooting range. The first of these has the standard targets flashing up to be greeted with a twelve gauge shot gun. Score the necessary amount and you are let loose in the armoury.

Take 'em Out is a respectable game, good fun to play with a laughably large amount of gore. Then you finish the third level, and you get the 'Congratulations you have completed your mission’ screen! If it was not for the lack of levels, Take 'em Out could be a substantially superior game to what it now is. As it stands though, it is a quick-finish gun 'em down and an expensive way to spend a commercial break.
Take the Money and Run
A timed freeware collect'em up game released in 1990. The game even came with a level editor to make and trade your own levels with friends.
Tale of Evil

Tale of Evil is an unofficial sequel of "Tower Of Evil" for the Commodore Amiga.

The Story:
Once upon a time there was a little girl, her name was Olivia. Like all strange children, Olivia loved to play in the nearby cemetery. It was here that she met the witch's cat Schrodinger, who went to the cemetery not to play, but to collect magic components as the witch's assistant. As days passed, the witch watched the forming friendship with more and more jealously. One day, she came to a terrible decision. She decided to put them both six feet, under the ground. Since the witch was not Schrodinger's first owner, he already had experience with mad scientists and poison capsules, so he managed to avoid his death, but sadly the little girl had no luck. Like all cats, Schrodinger moved easy between the world of the living and the dead.
Tales
A Polish educational game focused on math published by Techland Soft in 1994.
Tales from Heaven

Tales from Heaven is a 3D varied-viewpoint platformer resembling things like Mario 64 and Pandemonium, with over 2000 polygons on screen at a time, and morphing and transparency effects. In Tales From Heaven you play as Zak, who must chase after his beloved cat, not only for his own benefit but also to retrieve a sacred talisman required to save a land above the clouds.

Your main weapon to progress through the 12 levels are a supply of bombs, of which more can be collected as you play. These have a 3-second delay and can hurt you if you don't retreat. Many creatures can be killed by jumping on their heads. To help performance on slower systems, lo-res graphics are available and the background graphics are optional.
Tales from the Arabian Nights

A unique learning experience in reading comprehension.
Your child will be enchanted with the captivating stories of the Arabian Nights. The game includes three stories with stunning animated graphics:

Aladdin's Lamp
The Ebony Horse
Ali Baba

Each story has its own vocabulary building. The main learning objectives are to enhance your children's Reading Comprehension, Creative Writing and Language Arts Skills. The game contains over 600 multiple choice and fill-in reading and vocabulary questions.
Also included is a built-in word processor called TALE MAKER which enables your child to do creative writing, and a QUIZ MAKER authoring system to create their own questions and answers.
For extra value, there is a graphic ARABIAN MATCH GAME for developing memory and concentration skills.
Tales of Gorluth III
A Linear Action Adventure for the Commodore Amiga
Tales of Gorluth: The Tear Stone Saga

Tales of Gorluth: The Tear Stone Saga is an action adventure in old-school retro style. The game sets you in the role of Karn, a young warrior who is on a quest in the land of Gorluth. In the introduction, we see Karn as a child in a classroom, being tought the history of an old war with the Elves. As the game proper starts out, Karn is now a grown-up warrior, returning to his home village after a long time of training in the capital Aasan, finding it in disarray after someone had stolen a valued statue of the village founder, and made off with it - to a nearby crypt. Now the villagers are unhappy and some have left the village to look for a better place to live, since who could stand having a villainous thief so close by?

So what is Karn to do now, with the thief long gone? Go search the crypt to find the statue, of course.
Tales of the Unknown: Volume I: The Bard's Tale

The small country town Skara Brae was enjoying a peaceful life, until an evil wizard known as Mangar the Dark appeared. Monsters have invaded the town, terrorizing its inhabitants. Mangar cast the spell of Eternal Winter on the surroundings, isolating Skara Brae from any possible help. Guards that were entrusted with the task of protecting the town have disappeared within one night. Only a party of brave adventurers can save Skara Brae and defeat Mangar. 

The Bard's Tale is a fantasy role-playing game similar to Wizardry games, with first-person exploration of pseudo-3D maze-like environments, and turn-based combat against randomly appearing enemies. Unlike early Wizardry installments, the town can be explored physically, and parts of the overworld are accessible as well. Several dungeons must be explored before the player can tackle the final quest.
Talespin

Talespin is an adventure game creation system made by Mark Heaton and his family (wife and their five children), which allows you to create interactive graphic- and text-oriented adventure games, demos, books, tutorials, or whatever application you can think of. It offers graphics, 100 development commands, mouse control, no copy protection, hard drive support, and Telltale, a run-only module that allows users without Talespin to see your work.

Talespin also includes two sample adventure games: The Grail made by 19-year-old Rudyard Heaton and The Wolf made by another artist
Talmino

An oddly addicting puzzle game developed and published by Logistic Dreams and features single and head to head, split-screen play, which was released in Europe in 1998. It is a precursor to Talmino 2.
Talmino 2
Talmino 2 is a Puzzle game, developed and published by Logistic Dreams, which was released in Europe in 1998. While this is a sequel to the original, it only has a single player mode.
Tame Raider

This cool little 2D platform game is created with a game creator tool called Overbird. Which can be found on Aminet. The game is a pastiche of Tomb Raider, or at least presents itself as one. It features the busty heroine, Rhonda the Redhead as she progresses through levels beating up the aggressive men and other monsters she finds and kicking rocks out of her way, while squat thrusting to pick up treasures. The game has some simple puzzle and fighting elements.
Tanglewood

Ha! Here's something you didn't know: you've got an uncle called Arthur. He's not from East Enders and he doesn't have a mate called Terry but he does own the mining rights to T'ngl-y-wd. Spit in my eye, eh? Isn't the world a small place guv'nor? Well, yeah, it is a small place and that is why T'ngl-y-wd isn't on it – actually. It's a 'small undistinguished planet in a remote galaxy'. Arthur didn't worry about it much until he found out that it contained some pretty valuable stones, then he shot his mouth off over a couple of pints of beer and was elbowed out by the mining company. Yup, those nice men at the mining centre have hidden Arthur's documents and re-established the planet's operational base. There's a court case in ten days and Arthur (sounds a bit like my uncle, Ripperbile) needs to find those papers or he's out on his ear.

This is definitely an arcade-style adventure weighted towards the arcade.
Tangram

For around 4000 years the Chinese have been enthralled by this puzzle concept. It consists of a set of 7 shapes, representing squares, triangles and trapezoids, which must be arranged to form a pre-defined pattern. In this version there are 200, representing things such as animals and buildings.

The shapes are on the right of the screen, and you move the mouse cursor over one to select it, then place it onto the shape as required. They can be rotated using the right mouse button. 

All this is done against a time limit. As well as points for clearing a level, you get bonus time for completing them with time to spare. This bonus time can then be used on later levels if you run out of the allotted time. Once you have no bonus time, you can dig into your main score to provide more time.
Tank Attack

Tank Attack requires you to use a board game playing with the computer. It is a fold out map which features a hex map presented in war-gaming style. It is split into four countries with a variety of terrains.

There are four armoured divisions comprising of four armoured cars and eight tanks. Your aim is to destroy the bases of the other players countries by getting into range and blowing up the HQ.

The computer acts as a moderator deciding the outcomes of fire-fights and keeping track of the status of each force. At the start of a turn the computer rolls a dice to determine how many movement units a player can use. The player can decide where to attack and where to move.

The winner is the one with his bases still intact and the other players' destroyed.
Tank Attack (Camden Town Games)
A 2 Player death match Tank Game played on a single screen with bouncing bullets.
Tank Attack (Culture)

Tank Attack from Culture is a multiplayer tank battle game for up to 6 players released in 1995. You start on an overhead view of the small singe-screen battle field, all tanks randomly placed and you must destroy all the other players or computer controlled tanks. This only takes a hit or two, things go VERY quickly.
Tank Attack (Paul Kent)

Tank Attack is a public domain game for up to four players.

Each player controls a round tank which they manoeuvre around a play area which has scattered obstacles that provide cover. Naturally, for a game with the word 'Tank' in its title, the player's vehicle is equipped with a big gun. The good news is that shells from the gun can be made to bounce off the walls and obstacles. The bad news is that the gun can overheat at which point it stops working so the player must run, hide and dodge until it cools down enough to work again.
The objective is to destroy the other player's tanks before being destroyed themselves.

Power-ups appear randomly throughout the levels however they all look the same so no-one has any idea whether they will be beneficial or useful.

The game is joystick or keyboard controlled. There is no single player vs the computer option.
Tank Battle

Choose from several battlefields in this two player dueling tank game created by Robin Edwards and A. Murdoch and released as Licenseware in 1991. In this version the tank shots can bounce off walls for extra complexity and an element of surprise.
Tank Buster
1989 saw the release of Tank Buster on the Amiga systems, a scrolling, multi-directional shooter. Game is created by SoftTouch and published by Kingsoft.
Tank Combat
A two-player head-to-head dueling shooter by RGBSoft.
Tank Hunter

A two player public-domain tank duel shooter by Pink of Paradise Soft. Choose one or two players, choose level of difficulty and get to sniping! It will take several shots to fully disable your opponent.
Tank in a Dungeon

There was an earthquake in the Kilimanjaro Mountains in Africa. As a result, a huge cave was exposed. Researchers were sent there to check what was inside. Only one man returned, who told terrible things about huge dungeons full of dangerous robots. Some of the researchers could still be there. It was decided to send a tank there to explore the dungeons and destroy the aliens. You will command this tank - good luck!

Info:

There are 15 levels ahead of you. Every second one is randomly generated. Save your ammo. You can replenish it by collecting ammo in dungeons. You can also collect additional armor that will protect your tank from one hit. Watch out for the bombs lying around. You will get bonus points for collecting the missing researchers.
Tank Team

A tank shooter game created by Paul Ciulla, who has released both it and the source code in 1991. This isn't your average tank battle game, featuring original music, battlefields that make use of tanks, jets, rolling boulders, remote controlled gates and auxiliary canons and supplies. There are 13 different battlefields that are randomly selected. Setup screen for players to allow every game to be fully custom. Awards given for superior performance during the game.
Tank Wars

Inspired by the classic Tankz, this Blitz Basic game pits up to five human players in a battle tank-on-tank. The playfields are outfitted with some obstacles reminiscent to those used in a "snake" style game, offering protection from enemy fire. Bonuses pop up from time to time, though these bonuses may either increase or decrease your energy and firepower. As a result, apart from the usual "bomb your opponent to bits" method, one tactic in this game is to chase your opponent into harmful bonuses.

The game can be played in single matches or tournament style, where you may save your scores between rounds in order to resume later on.
Tank You

This is a Scorched Earth- And Artillery Duel-styled game for the Amiga. There are five weapons at the moment. The nice collapsing routine was done by Teijo Kinnunen, thanks! When you play this game, please remember that this isn't even close to finished version. Maybe I'll put this to shareware
some day...
Tanked Up

Tanked Up is a one player game of tank combat. You are driving a rocket firing tank around in a maze-like arena. The arena is populated with computer controlled tanks hell-bent on destroying you. Your mission is either to destroy all the enemy or escape from the level. Shortly after the game begins, enemy tanks are added to the arena by means of teleportation devices, they will soon start to hunt you down. Every level has a maximum simultaneous number of tanks in the game at one time (this is set by the skill level). There is a finite number of tanks for each level based on skill setting, once you kill past this point no more tanks will be spawned. Each rocket impact causes 1 point of armor damage. Enemy tanks take four hits to destroy. You can drive through automatic doors and pick up rocket packs and armor boost to refresh your depleted supplies.
Tankkk

A multi-player party tank game from the author of HippoPlayer for 2 to 4 players. The game can be downloaded from Aminet Created by Kari-Pekka Koljonen, T. Lindström, and J. Päijänen of Hippopotamus Design in 1996. Tankkk does nothing more than turn your (once) powerful Amiga into an Atari 2600. Moving tanks around a monochrome screen will be a familiar first gaming memory to many so perhaps Tankkk taps into a node of gaming nostalgia. Up to five players can enter the maze and shoot at each other, making the game a must for gatherings. Although not recommended as a Christmas Day family pursuit it's perfect for beer drinking sessions with friends. There are a couple of different mazes and a number of settings to tweak the game.

The main reason why Tankkk is so good is that bullets bounce off walls. This seemingly simple feature expands the game's potential greatly since bullets can affect parts of the area away from the tank's immediate vicinity.
Tanks Furry

Multiplayer action game inspired by Famicom game “Battle City”. Over 40 levels, single campaign, multiplayer modes for up to four people. The game awarded second place at Retrokomp 2015 Game Competition.
Tanks Massacre

This PD dueling tank shooter is a death-match without single player mode by Necropolis and released in early June 1994. Two or more tanks in a maze face off, you need at least one human opponent to play. Necropolis called this a game preview of a more fully featured game that was in the works, but perhaps never materialized.
TankX

A remake of the famous Tankkk, renamed to TankX and updated (after 27 years). This new version has been updated after a slight *cough* delay. It is now called TankX, and supports 7 simultaneous players (up from 4). Many other improvements have been made as well. This version was developed in co-operation with the https://www.amigalive.com discord-community, who provided improvements ideas, testing, new battlefields and in-game music. Cheers!

The original version was called Tankkk, where the number of k-letters denoted the amount of tanks in the game. This one should then be called Tankkkkkkk, but that would be silly. So up to 7 simultaneous players possible! - Tank #5 with a third set of keys which default to: U, T, 6, Y, F.
 - Tanks #6 and #7 with a parallel port joystick adapter.

Check out AmigaLive for some TankX online mayhem!
Tanx

Tanx expands the gameplay of the old arcade game Tanks. Two human players do battle over a randomly generated terrain, each of them in control of a tank. Taking it in turns, you must fire a shot of the correct weight and angle to hit your opponent's tank and destroy it.
Tanx (GN)
A four player, freeware tank shooter from Grid North in 1997.
Tanx Fetser
A clone of 'Artillery Duel' for up to eight players, including AI opponents.
Tanx n Stuff

A four-player tank game created by Paul Atkin, Grant Young, Ben Campbell, Daniel Oaks. The game can be played by up to four people at a time - computer players hill fill in for any hissing human's, the aim of the game is to collect more flags than anyone else before the time limit expires, your vehicle can only carry three flags at a time so you must drop then back at your base before you can pick up more, Other players can attack you at any time and take the flags you here carrying or go to your base and steal them. 
 
There was both a playable demo and a full version of the game available via
Tanx Squadron

Earth is under siege from an alien threat. Huge genetically enhanced insects rampage across the planet. Man tries to fight back but hopes of success all but fade when their crack team is captured by the alien hordes. Desperate and out of time, a group of 10 men and women break away from their unit and form their own. Using vehicle remains from previous battles the group construct their own vehicles and weapons to counter attack the alien invaders in an attempt to crush their forces and strike at the heart of their very own home world. The unit was code named TANX. 
 

 Turn Based Strategy System
 10 Different Vehicles each with unique strengths and weaknesses.
TapJewels

You need at least two identical jewels to remove them from the playfield. Find 3 or more identical jewels to fill the playfield with new items. The more you can remove at once, the more new you get. The game is over if there are no more matches.
Tapper

Tapper puts the player in the boots of a bartender who must serve eager, thirsty patrons (before their patience expires) while collecting empty mugs and tips! One game that many people remember so fondly that's all about serving patrons in a pub was that classic game 'Tapper.' A game by Marvin Glass and Associates released by Bally Midway, all those years ago in the Arcades in 1983. In fact, this game also appeared on the Atari 2600, Atari 8bit, Amstrad CPC, BBC MICRO, C64, MSX, and yes, even the ZX Spectrum. 
Old Bob has lovingly created a brand new version of "Tapper" for the Commodore Amiga,  requiring only an Amiga OCS with 1MB Chip Ram.
Taran im Abenteuerland

A German language fantasy, illustrated text adventure game made by Achim Kern and published by OASE in 1993. In the game you are Taran and you have to defeat the dark forces and help your king to regain his kingdom. More than 20 years later, developer did enhanced ports to AmigaOS 3, AmigaOS4 and other platforms. Taran is a knight in a fantasy kingdom who gets tasked by the king to find his lost insignia of power, his crown and sceptre. If Taran succeeds, he will get to marry the king's beautiful daughter and will have half of the kingdom for his rule.

The game plays like a classical text-adventure, but it has some graphical menus for convenience. Four standard commands and movements can be chosen from an interface. Choosing "examine" will give a list of all objects you can examine in the room. You can also use cursor keys for movements and the function keys for certain commands. The game has a hunger/thirst mechanic, so you need to eat and drink on a regular basis.
Target v2
Choose your weapon and shoot a variety of pop up targets in this shareware game by Ian Chisholm. released in 1996.
Targhan

The events of Targhan take place in medieval times; the game's setting and gameplay are similar to those of Golden Axe. The plot involves a lone warrior traveling the land far and wide, killing all manner of beasts, with the end goal in mind to kill an evil lord who has gotten too big for his britches.
Targis

Targis is an platform game with a look and feel reminiscent of Lode Runner, developed and published by Incognito, which was released in 1988. Brave the Proter's lair and retrieve all of the stolen rocket parts or have the terror of the Proters haunt the rest of the galaxy forever! 200 different levels of lair, full level editor create infinitely many levels. Player can modify all graphics, sound and animations to make Targis a totally difficult game every time. Incredibly addictive and endless hours of family enjoyment.
Task Force

A top down turn based Laser Squad style wargame created by Mark Sheeky of Scorpius and released in 1993. You have to control your team, equip them with various weapons, etc. Allied agents descend into enemy territory, ready for action. Agent ADAMS scans the area ahead with his cyborg eye. An armed figure is located by the entrance to the enemy complex, take him out before he has a chance to react. Your squad steps over the dead guard and the task force enters the enemy complex anticipating strong resistance to follow...
TaskForce

A tactical combat game for one or two players and editor in the tradition of Act of War. You take control of a group of heavily armed mercenaries and guide them through hell... A mission editor will allow you to design your own favorite arena. Created by Jens Granseuer. Pick one of the 8 built-in combat missions like BG1 Babysitter where you must stop the rebels from capturing or destroying the Beta Gleny Orgital Station.
Tass Times in Tonetown

Your grandfather has invented a device which makes real everything he can see in his dream. All the strange places and creatures he can dream about really exist in an alternate reality. One of those creatures, named Franklin Snarl, traveled through the device to our reality and kidnapped Gramps, teleporting him into the crazy world of Tonetown. He hopes that Gramps will always remain asleep, which assures Snarl's own existence!

Now it's up to you, the hero of the game to travel to the alternate dimension of Tonetown and to rescue your grandfather. You interact with the environment by either typing in commands, or choosing one of the action icons available as interface. The game, therefore, combines text-based interaction with the more modern "point and click" approach.
Tatort: Nachtexpress

Based on the board game of the same name, this shareware game by Markus Riehl and published by Lizard Soft in 1992. The game is based on the 1934 novel Murder on the Orient Express by Agatha Christie.
Tautrix

A single player shareware puzzler. What does a programmer do who can't think of anything right? Well, a pebble puzzle! And if he's really deep in the creative crisis, the 183rd "Tetris" variant will come out of it...
Ergo, we are again presented with the well-known blocks, but this time they appear in the middle of the screen and have to be puzzled together under time pressure to form single-color squares, which then disappear from the screen. The joystick or fire button is used to push and rotate, and the space bar is used to place them. If you get the right number of points, you get the password for the next level, where things get a bit more difficult due to the different shape and size of the "building site". The principle of the game means that more and more leftover bricks" reduce the area that can be built on, and of course blocks of the shape and color that you would need right now never appear, in short, the "Tetris". usual hustle and bustle breaks out.
Taxi
A Space-Taxi style, 2D Reaction & Navigation game by Harald Müller (Mueller), published in 1995.
Team 17 Tribute: Part 1

Created with AMOS Professional and intended as a loving memory of
Mr. Martyn Brown who sadly passed away recently... It is a very simple puzzle game.
Team 17 Tribute: Part 2

This is second part of my humble, yet sincere tribute to all Team17 Amiga games.
Created with AMOS Professional and intended as a loving memory of
Mr. Martyn Brown who sadly passed away in December 2024...
Team Gates

This is a remake of Ork Attack. In this version, you defend castle Commodore against an endless stream of attackers with the Microsoft Windows 95 branding. Can't quite put my finger on it, but the background music was taken from another game.
Team Suzuki

Team Suzuki uses official support to simulate motorcycle racing using polygon graphics. The action is viewed from the cockpit. Contact with other bikes or the scenery gradually increases the damage percentage, which will eliminate you at 100%. Crashing results in an external replay of your final moments.

Joystick and mouse control options exist, with the mouse being ultimately faster but harder to learn. 125, 250 and 500cc options exist, with the difficulty higher on the more powerful bikes. You can contest a full season, single race, or simply practice on a free track. 

16 circuits are featured, from Suzuka and Misano to Rijeka and Philip Island, with races over 5-50 laps. Your opponents are seven factory Suzuki riders from various classes at the time, including 1993 500cc World Champion Kevin Schwantz.
Team Tetris
A Tetris game for two players in cooperative mode from Jonathan Steven Horan of Trent Soft.
Team Yankee

Yankee can’t compare with M-1 for realism, but it’s an extremely playable and enjoyable sim. The essence of the game is a mix of tactics – critical in positioning your forces and timing artillery strikes – and arcade action. Swiveling the turret, finding the enemy, getting a laser lock-on, waiting for a round to be loaded then knocking a tank out all requires good reactions. Then as soon as the first shot hits, the rest of the platoon will know your position and return fire, so it’s critical to take them all out quickly. This is great fun, helped along by great graphics. Up close things are blocky, especially the UDG-style forests, but overall the effect is top-notch. The game’s only real drawback is the lack of scenarios. Enemy intelligence does increase dramatically as ranks improve, but new scenarios would’ve been best.
Tearaway Thomas

You control Thomas, a strange-looking but vaguely cutesy animal of some description in an ultra-fast platform game. There are 50 levels, split into 5 groups of 10.

Each one has a certain number of gems, and your task is to collect a certain number of them (for example, level 2 has 55 and you need at least 40) and then find the exit, all within the time limits. The yellow gems are worth 50 points and the purple ones 100, although the purple ones don’t appear to be more precariously-placed, and the total makes no distinction, so this is for colour as much as anything. Once you’ve got the required amount, the gems double in value, tempting you to continue to explore

The levels are infested with cutesy-looking baddies, such as birds and bears, which can’t be killed, and must be avoided, as contact with them costs you time as Thomas picks himself up. You can jump on the heads of some of them, which gives a small points bonuses.
Tech

Tech is a light cycle game in which the kingdom of TECHmania is being threatened by the evil lord Caraz. He sends his tech cycle drivers (the targanoids) to beat the king's elite squad which the player is the last surviving member of. To save the kingdom, the player has to win all battles against the enemy drivers. There are 25 levels in total and in each the player has to kill all of the opposition by trapping them so that they crash into a wall or into one of the cycles' trail. The player has three lives and when they are gone there is a continue option to keep trying at the level. The levels get progressively harder with more enemy drivers and obstacles such as turrets, walls and ditches. The game also has a two player mode.
Techno Ball
A two player, freeware pong style game by the Swedish, Division A, dropped in November 1992. Unsurprisingly the game is backed by techno music.
Techno Cop

Techno Cop is set in the near future. You are a cop who seeks to clear his town of all the criminal scum. The game consists of two parts; one driving-action and one sidescrolling-action. In the first part you drive around in your red Ferrari and destroy hostile cars; in the second part, you turn somersaults over gaps, use elevators and shoot lots of enemies until you reach the boss. After having killed / caught the villain, it's back to the road again for the next mission.
[
Techno Ninja
1993 saw the release of Techno Ninja on the Amiga systems, a platform game, created by Doublebyte Software and commercially in the DB Doublebyte compilation pack.
Techno Tron

You have laid your hands on a copy of the game TECHNO TRON, from the Swedish studios of Alive Software in 1991. The object of the game is to run the other players into the walls or the line that is drawn behind the vehicle. A two player only game. There are 25 levels of play.
Techno Venture

TechnoVenture is a fun and innovative platformer with strong puzzle elements, similar to classic Apogee games of yore. At first TechnoVenture might look like just another Sci-Fi themed platformer game, but closer inspection reveals it's actually much more.

The game begins with an advertisement for registration and the "Playfield" newsletter, which are quickly dismissed. You're not given any sort of introduction, but instead dumped right in the middle of the action. The "story", what little there is of it, tells you that you suddenly find yourself being a brand new XED-2000 robot, and your quest is to rid the land of the evil mutants. The story is told as you go along.

On the surface, TechnoVenture plays like a platform game. Your XED-2000 robot is subject to gravity, and can run on horizontal surfaces, or jump in the air. The physics model, while not entirely realistic, allows quite nice touches, such as being able to change your direction in mid-jump.
Techno War

A S.E.U.C.K shareware game by Loz in 1994. A sequel to this shooter called Tech War Mania Mode was released later the same year. You form part of a secret task force known as united freedom undercover operations in technology, code named Necoth, The latest project RAD is just under completion. The laser recharge isn't quite perfected yet but will charge on certain targets. INTRUDER ALERT! All defenses breached. All exits are blocked by the aliens the only way out is to fight your way through.
Technoban

A Sokoban type game written in assembler by Tim Schattkowsky and released in 1992. Features include 4 worlds with 10 levels each, new graphics and sounds in every world, 32 colors, 5 stereo sounds, smooth animation, an integrated editor, and a code for each level.
Technoban II
A Sokoban clone with good music. A puzzle game in which you must push the balls into the slots using a logical approach.
Technology 2

In the year 2105AD man, for so long held captive in our own solar system, is at long last free. Finally able to travel at speeds beyond warp, new frontiers have become available. You are one of the first to venture forth...
 
As you journey through space, you will visit many of the planets, stars and sights which you have seen in the night sky. you will be given help on your voyage and if you follow the right path, riches will surely come. You will have as an assistant a very powerful computer whose name is A.R.T.H.U.R.. It isn't good at navigation but is very good as a companion and teacher and really good in the leisure department. But it will not just be work, you have important tasks to perform. Arthur will help you solve the puzzles that lie in store for you. Only when you have completed your task can you hope to qualify as a pilot for the Federation Cartel. 

Game developed by Paul Robertshaw and music by John Biggin.
Tecnoball

It's another Breakout variant: with the help of a paddle at the lower edge of the screen, you have to play back a ball, and you have to remove the built-up stone formations. Besides the well-known clasps, bigger paddles and laser guns, there are also magnets, more effective balls and additional paddles. You can “pre-order” them in a shop for the next level after each game has been started. The game is well done: a lot of background, convincing animations and remarkable pieces of music.

Many, many years ago, Tecnoball would probably have become a hit, but today you get only the great yawning...
TecnoballZ

TecnoballZ is a “breaking blocks” game that was written for the Amiga platform. The aim is to break all the blocks in each level. The game is divided into Areas which are divided into Levels. Between some levels, you have to defeat a guardian to pass to the next level. When passing an Area, a new edge is open. You can buy weapons and bonuses between levels with the money earned during the game.

TecnoballZ AGA is an adaptation of TecnoballZ for the Amiga 1200. The game has been adapted to take advantage of the Motorola 68020 microprocessor and the new AGA graphics chips.
Teddy

A DynaBlaster/Bomberman clone without sound effects. In Teddy, you and all baddies can walk through bombs. This makes the game more difficult. On the other hand, since every level fits on a single screen, planning ahead is little easier.
Tee Off

Tee Off! is an overhead-view golf game using mouse control. There are four courses on offer: Sunnymede, Runcorn, Petersfield and Overbridge. Beginner, amateur and pro modes are offered, affecting the distances to the pin. Shot placement involves a 3-click routine to set pace and spin, with a full range of clubs (but no on-screen reminder of their maximum distance). Holes incorporate bunkers, trees and sand-traps, although trees are not considered to be Out of Bounds - on occasion you can end up having to play shots from atop a tree.
Teenage Mutant Hero Turtles [Mirrorsoft]

Teenage Mutant Hero Turtles, originally released as Fierce Turtle Ninja Legend in Japan and later as Teenage Mutant Hero Turtles in Europe, is a 1989 platform game for the Famicom/NES. The game was released in Japan through Konami themselves, then in North America through Konami's Ultra Games imprint, followed by a release through the European equivalent , Palcom Software, in PAL regions.

This was the first Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles video game, and is based on the 1987 TV series, which was in its third season at the time of the game's original release, although the art style more resembles the original TMNT comic series.

The game was ported to various home computer platforms in 1990, including the Amstrad CPC, Commodore 64, ZX Spectrum and Amiga. The DOS version is infamous, as it contains a gap that is impossible to cross without cheating.
Teenage Mutant Hero Turtles: The Coin-Op!

The Return of the Awesome Foursome!

Now two dudes or dudettes can join forces and double team Shredder and his turtle terminators in a bid to save April and Splinter. Choose which lean, green turtle you control and haul shell around this fully scrolling version of the coin-op game and save April from a burning building. Meanwhile Splinter gets kidnapped and you must trash dodgy dudes Bebop and Rocksteady to set him free.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles [Ultra Games]

With April O'Neil held hostage by The Shredder's thugs, Bebop and Rocksteady, once again, it's up to the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles to come to her rescue! Play as all four of the turtle heroes, rescue April, and then rescue your sensei Splinter from Mecha-Turtles clutches, and then go after The Shredder deep in the bowels of The Technodrome itself.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is an action game based on the late eighties/early nineties cartoon series of the same name. Play as Leonardo, Michaelangelo, Donatello and Raphael (one turtle only, but the ability to swap between turtles at any time) as you save your friends and battle The Shredder and his cronies. There are no 'lives', as such - when you lose a turtle, he becomes 'captured', and you cannot use him again until you rescue him from a place hidden in the overworld.

Gameplay takes place in two perspectives: a top-down view, which lets you run around and explore buildings, sewers and other places.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: World Tour

This computer coloring book is another part in the Electric Crayon series and it has 30 pictures of different world places, such as Kremlin, Redwood, Taj Mahal, Fuji, Alps, etc., with Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles to color.

Pictures could be colored from a palette of 16 colors. Choosing a color and clicking in the picture do a color fill in the area clicked. The finished, or in progress, coloring was automatically saved to disk. Player may also remove all colors applied previously to start coloring from the very beginning.

Each picture has an educative description and could be printed.
Teenage Queen

In this interactive poker game you meet in a park the beautiful female roller-skater, who is very interested in strip playing. During the game you come to night club, where the female shows her real body...
TeenAgent

Teen Agent is a huge adventure game in which a teenager is picked to solve the mystery of the disappearing gold. Captured by two men in dark glasses and long coats, you are sent to a training camp for secret agents. It's a fun point-and-click animated graphic adventure that is both humorous and exasperating, a worthy attempt to emulate LucasArts style and humor.
Teeny Weenys

A very good Lemmings-like puzzle game. For each level you get one of more of those little creatures, each sometimes carrying some item(s) like ladder or block (or can be picked up as well), and your job is to have the creatures, using the objects, make their way to the exit before the timer runs out.

As with Lemmings, it is controlled with the mouse. The game does have some frustrating elements though. For one, the creatures move quite slow, and worse still as you can only control one at a time, you can't order one to go some place and then switch to another while he gets there: instead you have to wait until he gets there before you can switch to another creature.

Also, the game seems to be one of those “get everything right the first time otherwise time will run out” type of games. Any slight miscalculation and it's over. The worse aspect of the game though is that you only get one life. Lose and you are back to the menu screen (though there are level codes).
TeleEpic

Based on the same engine as TeleWar, TeleEpic is a two-player medieval strategy game intended to be played via modem, alternatively via null-modem or taking turns at a single computer.

In a split screen fashion, the top half of the screen features scrolling low resolution graphics, while the lower half contains a high-resolution user interface and a chatlog. The game is entirely controlled using the mouse, cycling between your men and pointing them at their destination, choosing weapon and direction of attack using buttons at the bottom half of the screen.

Your army consists of a dozen men, all armed with throwing daggers, throwing axes, a bow and arrows and a sword for melée combat. Each man has a unique number of hit points and "stride" (movement points). In order to regenerate, he can be told to rest or heal for a turn. Battle may be done in eight directions, requiring careful placement of your units, and choosing a weapon with the correct range.
TeleEpic II
Part of the Telewar series (a.k.a TeleWar IV). Uses TeleWar engine. All known versions crash under emulation. This two-player only game is a strategy war game released in 1990.
TeleGames

TeleGames is a collection of three classic board games to be played against a remote opponent via modem or null-modem. It can also be played taking turns at the same computer.

The games in question are chess, checkers and backgammon. The graphics are colourful, and can be seen both in 3-d from several perspectives as well as in a flat view from straight above. The package contains a phone book to keep track of remote opponents.
Telemark Warrior

During the Second World War there was a scientific rivalry between the two sides, who wanted at all costs to produce what would later be called the atomic bomb. One of the most important elements for the development of this ultimate weapon was the heavy water and the Nazis had built a factory in Telemark, from which manufacture large quantities of this important component.

There were only two solutions to this: to make the atomic bomb before the Germans, which was quite unlikely, or to sabotage the heavy water plant in Telemark. The latter is the solution that has been taken. And you're going to have to help them.

The game is a typical side-scrolling arcade with a single man fighting against everything that crosses his way and its composed of four distinct phases: the surroundings of the factory, underground corridors leading into the interior, the interior itself, and finally, the office area.
TeleWar

TeleWar is a two-player strategy game intended to be played via modem, alternatively via null-modem or taking turns at a single computer.

In a split screen fashion, the top half of the screen features low resolution graphics, while the lower half contains a high-resolution user interface and a chatlog. The game is entirely controlled using the mouse, cycling between units of your army and pointing them at their destination, rotating turrets and firing using buttons at the bottom half of the screen.

The army consists of light and heavy artillery, light and heavy armour and supply trucks which can supply units with ammunition and fuel. Both supplies must be conserved, or your army will grind to a halt. Firing can be done in eight directions, requiring careful placement of your units. Each unit has different range, fire power and amount of fuel and ammunition. Since the screen is cramped, a single slow unit may block the advance of several others, necessitating careful movement.
TeleWar II

TeleWar II is the sequel to the original TeleWar, a two-player strategy game intended to be played via modem, alternatively taking turns at a single computer.

Two armies (the blue one and the red one) confront each other on a scrolling battle field, controlled entirely by mouse. The basic game is the same as the predecessor, but with new terrains and scenarios and updates to the engine.

The game is finished once the enemy army is destroyed, if a player cedes the game, or if the flag is captured.

A follow-up, TeleWar III was announced but never published, but the game was further refined into Operation Com•Bat, which for the first time added artificial intelligence, making one-player games possible as well.
Temperstorm

A game in the style of Tempest with simulated vector graphics. In the game you use your mouse to move your ship around the line structure, left mouse to fire. Right mouse will drop a "shadow". You advance in levels by killing the number of bad guys indicated by ships on the top of the display. If enemy sparks make it to the top you will die.

Published in the June 1992 Amiga Resource Disk accompanying the Amiga edition of Compute Magazine.
Tempest 1200

This is an early DEMO of Tempest2000 for the Amiga, written by Elton Bird of Mental Software.
Best played on a 28MHz or more A1200 with Fastmem. Lower spec. turn the fill OFF.
I'm kind of stuck with what to do with it! If you have any interest in perhaps buying a finished version for a coverdisk, I'd be happy to hear any offers. Obviously the fact that it's an Atari game that's now out on PC and imminent on PSX/Saturn
may be a problem for anything other than a PD release, but I think it's a little bit above being PD. Love to hear any feedback/suggestions. If you can, give me a ring and let me know what you think of it.
Temple of Apshai Trilogy

The Temple of Apshai followed the general idea of Dungeons and Dragons, with lots of monsters to meet in battle and treasure to be found.

You can start from scratch, with your character given a random 1 to 18 for six basic attributes: Intelligence, intuition, ego, strength, constitution and dexterity, together with a number of silver pieces. You can enter a previously saved character from disc. Thankfully this interpretation has superior graphics attributes of a character from an earlier game. You can restore a previous game saved at any point within Apshai.

Each realm has four levels. Dungeons and Dragons followers will find levels 1 to 2 are appropriate to third level, and the lower levels to fourth and sixth level characters.
Temple of Elemental Evil
Make your way carefully through the Temple of Elemental Evil in this text adventure homebrew version by Genasoft in 1989.
Temple of Enlightened Souls
Temple of Enlightened Souls is an Action game, developed by Dynamic and published by Softsell, which was released in Europe in 1989.
Temporal Misplacement

An AMOS based freeware text adventure written by Jason Strudwick in 1994. An accident in of the GSC Time-Laps where an uncontrolled distortion has caught up an energy crystal in a temporal rift. You will need to travel through the rift, repair the crystal to use to power a return trip and close the rift!
Temptations

A Redpill Amiga conversion of an MSX game released in the late 1980's, like in the original version, the Franciscan monk Noni wants to join the Vitigudina order. To judge his valor, the order asks for a test of virtue: the monk has to collect weapons and use them to exorcise all the demons of a village.

Temptations is a Spanish flick-screen platform game. The game is divided in a series of levels, each with a series of screens. The player controls the monk's movements with the ARROW KEYS or the JOYSTICK. Pressing the SPACE BAR or the FIRE BUTTON shoots the projectile weapon he is carrying. The friar is killed if he touches the demons or some of the screen objects. His movement has inertia: after landing on a platform he usually keeps sliding forward (that is something that must be taken on account when planning how to move from one screen to the other).
Temptris

A quick and dirty Tetris clone created by Jason Hildebrand In 12 August 1996. This version of Tetris has the following nifty features:

 - 5 two-player modes including collaborative, and competitive
 - configurable sound effects 
 - multitasks (OS-friendly)
TenaBlaster
Dynablaster\Bomberman clone made by Peter Bakota, Boris Ivic and Tibor Cxonkas of Tenax for up to four players. Tagged as being the ultimate multi player game.
Tenebra
Tenebra is an atmospheric puzzle game with rogue-like aesthetics. Guide the hapless protagonist to the exit. Poor guy is afraid of darkness and refuses to walk in the dark areas.
Tenebra 2

This is a direct sequel to my popular game Tenebra, with many exciting new game play elements, including a portal gun!
Similar to its prequel, Tenebra 2 is an atmospheric puzzle game with rogue-like aesthetics. . Guide the hapless protagonist to the exit. Poor guy is afraid of darkness and refuses to walk in the dark areas.
Tenebra 2 contains 35 levels and works on both PAL and NTSC machines.
Tennis Champs

Tennis Champs is a 1995 Tennis Game from Menta Image, followed the same year by the game Super Tennis Champs. It was pre-released under the name of Arcade Sports Tennis. Coded in AMOS by the excellently named Elton and Elliot Bird, manages to be better than all of them by taking its inspiration from the world of consoles and simply being a lot of fun. A clever and intuitive control system allows all manner of shots to be played with a one-button joystick. There are four different playing surfaces and a variety of players to choose from, and even a tournament mode.
Tennis Cup

Tennis Cup is a split-screen tennis game with the camera closely positioned at the athlete's back. The available playing modes are exhibition match (either single or double), training, the Davis Cup or the four Grand Slam tournaments. The player either controls one of the 32 available tennis athletes or creates a new one. Then there are 30 points to divide between abilities (e.g. forehand or volleys). This athlete can be saved to disk and further improved during the course of time. For exhibition matches, the opponent can be built the same way.

The game includes various hit types, depending on the player's position and timing. The direction of the ball can also be influenced when performing a shot. There are four different surfaces, influencing the gameplay, and three difficulty levels.
Tennis Cup 2

This tennis simulation recreates all the rules of the sport, from tie-breaks to break points. The action is viewed from behind one of the players, also featuring a split-screen option. You can play singles and doubles matches over 1,3 or 5 sets. There are 4 different types of court - grass, quick, hard and clay. You can play single matches, practice using a ball machine which fires a succession of shots at you, or play a season made up of major tournaments such as the Grand Slam events, the Masters and the ATP Cup. Player abilities can be adjusted to suit different styles of play.
Tensai
Demo (with a fully playable level 1!) appeared on Amiga Action issue 48 coverdisk in September 1993.
Teo

Teo is a side-scrolling platform game. The aim of the player is to reach the designated number of blue spheres. All the levels are full of hostile animals, poisonous plants and weeds, fire flames and other obstacles. Besides the blue spheres the player may collect numerous fruits (extra energy) scattered on the board, hearts (extra life), safety helmet (temporary invincibility) or use trampoline arrows for performing high jumps. The hostile creatures may be killed by a jump on their head. After each three levels the player receives a stage code.
Teratris

Released as version 3.0 of the beta, this Tetris inspired puzzle game by Studio V98 came out in 1994 and included the source code for the game. It included four modes of play: Enduro, Challenge, Vs Match and Theory.
Teresa

This game deserves at least 2 prices, one for the shortest adventure I have ever played, and one for the sleaziest game I've ever seen on Amiga. Oh, yes, then it uses a quite rare 1st person view, but for a game of this type it makes it more interesting (rare in adventures).

The entire plot of the game can be described as this: You've met a nice girl at a meeting, and she has accepted your offer to stay the night with you. The point is simply to... Well, you know what it is. It turns out a little more complicated, because she reveals that she has a birthday the following day, and due to the meeting she's so exhausted that there's no chance in the evening. So you have to get up before her, and find some interesting birthday-presents for her, if you find the right presents (and get up in time) it's a home-run.
Terminator 2: Judgment Day

Terminator 2: Judgment Day consists of several actions parts linked together. All parts are different, each resembling typical games of the genre (for example: 1st level is like a side-view beat 'em up). Between each level a small cutscene from the movie is shown.
Terrahawks

Terrahawks is an unofficial conversion of the Philips Videopac+ game of the same name (Called Attack of the Timelord on the Odyssey2 version). This was developed by Gary James and released into the public domain in 2017.

Game description:

The player has just attracted the attention of Spyrus the Deathless, the Timelord of Chaos, and his only defense is his Time Machine's laser cannon. The Timelord will now send his fleet of Time Ships to destroy the player.

In this space shooter the player controls the Time Machine horizontally with the directional stick and shoots its laser with the action button. The Timelord's Time Ships have four kinds of weapons to assault the player, and they will be introduced in the game's first four levels.

In the first level, the Time Ships will shoot missiles, which travel in straight lines toward the bottom of the screen. In the second level, the fleet will also use antimatter mines, which will follow the player's Time Machine movements.
Terran Envoy

Life as a detective is hard enough on one planet. After all, there's no accounting for the twists and turns of the criminal mind. With a whole solar system to hide in, what could a super criminal get up to? This particular one looks like overthrowing the galactic council and plunging the whole galaxy into chaos. It's your job to track him down and find out exactly who and what he is.

It's lucky that you've been kitted out with the latest in crime fighting technology - the ray of justice. This highly sensitive and powerful device needs to be used with caution and is powered with crystals. In fact the whole game revolves around the movement and manipulation of crystals. These can be mined from planets and their presence is located with the aid of the crystal detector. As you move around the solar system with your warp drives you will meet aliens. They can be communicated with and questioned in the hope of building up a picture of your prey.
Terror Liner

1989 saw the release of Terror Liner on the Amiga systems, a Qix variant, developed and released by Wolf in Europe.

Terror Liner is a Qix variant. The basic playing principle: the player controls a spider-like character which can draw lines on the screen and when a closed figure is drawn, the colour of the area changes. Additionally there are enemies, either confined to the uncoloured or coloured areas, which cause the player sprite to die if touched. The goal is to colour 75% of the screen.
Terror Liner II

TERROR LINER II is an adult "freeware" version of the game TERROR LINER puzzle game (hacked by Vision One for Alpha Flight), which was commercially released a year earlier in 1989 by Wolf Software. It is a Qix style game, wall off the sections of the picture and see the pixelated skin.
Terrorpods

Just because a region is bleak, desolate and inhospitable doesn't mean it lacks value. The planet Colian is a case in point; it has plentiful stocks of tough metal Aluma, the explosive Detonite, and the energy giving Quaza crystals. The units which are mining them are under the control of the Empire, and are forced to produce destructive Terrorpod units.

The rival Federation attempts to shut this operation down, and sends you to the surface in a Defence Strategy Vehicle. Your task is to find each of the six bases before the Empire can destroy evidence of them. Destroy all the Terrorpods in order to reach the bases.

The action is viewed from your DSV, as you move and shoot at any encroaching Terrorpods. Colian has a heavy inertia field, so you are always moving. You have guided missiles at your disposal, although these use up some of your limited Detonite stocks. Missiles will also be aimed at you; avoid these.
Terry's Big Adventure

Terry's Big Adventure looks and feels somewhat similar to Mario's, being a side-scrolling platform game using stylised block graphics and lots of ledges to climb up and around. Terry is armed with a yo-yo which can be directed as a weapon by pushing the joystick as you hold down fire - an idea later repeated by Trolls. On this occasion the use of the yo-yo causes Terry to recoil slightly, so be careful that this does not push him off a ledge or into the path of another enemy.

There are 12 levels in total, incorporating many rivers to cross as well as hordes of hedgehogs, snails and similar to kill. Hidden bonus objects and time extensions can be found. When you start a new game you start form the last level you reached, so you effectively have unlimited continues.
Teserae

Teserae was first created on the Atari ST by The Albanian Sausage Corporation - a sort of game and a demo with great music and whizzy scrolling backgrounds. I remade a version for the Amiga in the early 1990's to help learn some of the machines features.

Guide the Tetris shapes to form neat lines with no gaps. Each time a line is completed it is removed from the screen and everything moves down. Complete several lines to proceed to the next, faster level. But you know how Tetris works, right?
Test Drive

This mix of racing simulation and arcade game consists of driving a choice of 5 sports cars on a mountain strip at the fastest speed possible without getting caught by the cops. To avoid them, use your radar detector -- or just try to outrun them if they spot you. Manual stickshift only, so make sure you don't redline or you'll blow your engine.
Test Drive II Scenery Disk: California Challenge

This add on features a border to border race through the Golden State, divided into 7 stages, which are: The California/Oregon Border to the Trees of Mystery, Trees of Mystery to Eureka, Eureka to Rockport, Rockport to San Francisco, San Francisco to Carmel, Carmel to Santa Barbara and Santa Barbara to Mexico. This Add on requires a copy of Test Drive II.
Test Drive II Scenery Disk: European Challenge
This addon for Test Drive II features a race through Europe. Racing through the stages you cross following countries: The Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, France and Spain.
Test Drive II: The Collection
This compilation contains Test Drive II and all released add-ons, which are the 2 car disks: Musclecars and The Supercars and the 2 scenery disks: California Challenge and European Challenge.
Test Drive III

A port of the PC (MS-DOS, 256-colour VGA) version of Test Drive III to theAGA Amiga. The original 8086 game code was statically recompiled to native 68020+ code, so the polygon engine, physics and all game logic are the PC original. Graphics are the full 320x200 VGA picture in 256 colours on an AGA screen; music and sound effects come from the Tandy 3-voice sound driver, played through Paula.
Test Match Cricket

Superb cricket strategy game at a stadium near you, right at your computer. Test Match Cricket is a sports and management game, developed and published by Challenge Software, which was released in Europe in 1994.
Test Prawa Jazdy 1
A Polish language educational driving quiz\test developed and published by Atares in 1994. Version 2 of the quiz would be released at the end of the same year.
Test Prawa Jazdy cz. 2: Kat B
A Polish language educational driving quiz\test developed and published by Atares in 1994.
Testament

Testament is another Doom-clone for the Amiga. Compared to the other games released at about the same time, Testament looks a bit simple. It plays more like Wolfenstein 3D than Doom, with no staircases or elevations, and plenty of similar looking mazes.

The controls are quite simple, and you can't jump, crouch or anything like that. Each level consists of a maze laid out on one floor. The goal is to reach a scroll at the end of the level, and in addition to the enemies out to kill you, you'll have to find a set of four keys to unlock doors blocking your progress. What Testament scores high on is atmosphere and tension. It has bucketloads of both. The mazes are dark and scary, and the levels feel very claustrophobic.

The presentation is good. While the 3D engine is simple, it is also very fast. The sound effects do a good job of enforcing the dark, gloomy atmosphere of the game. There's also simple (but effective) background music playing on each level.
Testament II
Sequel to Testament, a horror-themed first person shooter with engine similar to Wolfenstein 3D. Game is basically the same as it's predecessor, but with new enemies, levels and few new textures.
Tetra Copy

The program's primary purpose was copying disks, however most people remember this program because of the worthy Tetris clone added to the program to give you something to do while the formatting and nibble level copies took place. The application was released as part of the Assassins Disk Copiers disk set.
Tetra Quest

In Tetra Quest the Galaxy is waiting in anticipation for the first Galactic Games, similar to the Olympic Games. But unfortunately an evil alien race stole the Phoenix Tablet and broke them into 64 pieces each. The player's goal is to recover all pieces and save the Games.

Each level (overall 384) consists of four screens which one coin each. The goal is to collect the coins in the correct order, but the player can only travel on interconnected lines - sometimes teleporter or switches have to be used to reach the goal. Also restricted to the lines are the aliens which try to harm the player, but they can be disposed of by shooting them. Some of them leave extras behind which help the player when picked up. If in a tight spot, the player can transform into a bird and fly over obstacles, but this costs an considerable amount of points.
Tetras
A Tetris written using Randyram Jam assembly course by Emiliano Esposito featuring up to 20 speed levels as on the Gameboy.
Tetren
Tetren is a public domain Tetris variant that can be played alone or with two people through split-screen. There is a password function, highscores and an option to toggle the music and effects.
Tetrid III

Game created by Shaun Watters of Zamara Productions and released in 1994. To complete the level you must cover 95% of the grid with Tetris shapes. You can reject current blocks but this reduces your time. Eventually this idea would be recycled in a 1-4 player game and called Blokus that would be made into a incredibly popular board game.
Tetris (Digital)
A well made side-by-side one or two player Tetris game, with statistics and multiple play modes from Digital, released in 1992.
Tetris (Gaz)
A Tetris clone created by Gaz released in 1994 and released in the Assassins Ultimate Games compilation.
Tetris (Hayrettin Yildiz)

A Tetris clone created by Hayrettin Yildiz and released in 1994. Configure the specific width and height of the planning field, drop mode and game modes, even set up the music to play during your game.
Tetris (Mirrorsoft)

The original commercially-licensed version of Alexey Pajitnov's classic Tetris puzzle game. Geometric shapes fall from the top of a playfield to rest on the bottom; fit the pieces together, and the line they form disappears. If the pieces don't form lines and eventually stack up to the top of the playfield, the game is over. Difficulty increases by dropping the pieces faster and faster over time.

Tetris is a verifiable classic game, translated to well over 200 electronic and computer platforms. It takes 2 minutes to learn, but a lifetime to master.
Tetris (Ross Fuller)

A single player Tetris clone, created by Ross Fuller in AMOS as shareware and released in 1992. It was written to be more faithful to the original. Blocks dropped from a greater height score higher as are removing multiple lines, uses mouse controls. The 1.0 version was released in April of 1992, with updates coming out until 1994.
Tetris (ShinobiZ)
Conversion of the original arcade ROM of Tetris, 1988, Atari Games arcade board
Tetris 1200
An unofficial port of the Tengen version of Tetris for the Amiga 1200.
Tetris 2
A two player, head to head version of Tetris created by Andromeda Software and released in 1988.
Tetris Duel

This Tetris clone is for those of you with AGA machines only. Created in Blitz BASIC 2 he graphics are very good and so is the gameplay. There are a few extra features such as 2 player support, bombs and other things that drop down instead of the normal blocks. Enjoy! Created by Nigel Hughes and Mike Richards of FUNdamental Software.
Tetris Pro

The basic Tetris gameplay, involving arranging each shape as you are given them to create complete lines, and then adjust to the remaining fragments falling down a line and perhaps blocking off lower lines, was reinvented in this title. The game is split into levels, and each one requires a set number of lines to be completed. As you do so, you gradually reveal a cartoony picture, varying from semi-naked girls to candles.

The levels usually have some amount of blocks already in place, which must be worked around, and often specify that picture lines are only awarded when you score 2 or more lines at a time. There are also power-ups, which come in some of the square blocks and are activated if you use them to complete a line. They include points bonuses, bombs to remove some of the existing tiles, and some ‘power-downs’, such as one which turns the screen upside down, and one that removes the preview of the piece.
Tetris Pro (Illusion Software)

This version of Tetris Pro for the Amiga was created by Robert Ciesnik of Illusion Soft. It has additional features and rules including bombs that will fill holes in an area, $ pieces that give additional points, D deletes a line, plus or minus to change speed of play and so forth. A picture of the author is displayed behind areas cleared out, there are multiple images in the game pack shown on other levels including some that are adult in nature.
Tetris Sex Special
A version of Tetris made by Sky Devils with mature images in it to draw interest. Unsurprisingly this is a single player version of Tetris.
Tetris: The Soviet Challenge

Hey! Tetris! One of the best games in the world - the only problem being that the original Mirrorsoft version was completely and utterly useless, saved only by the unspoilable basic Tetris gameplay. Now it’s been done again by Infogrames - a perfect chance to put al the wrongs right and use the power of the machine to produce what could be, quite literally, one of the best games there’s ever been. It’s one of the simplest games invented - surely just the laws of probability forbid it being buggered-up twice? Don’t they? You know what’s coming, don’t you? It defies belief, it really does, but this Tetris is another disaster. What is it about Tetris that turns Amiga programmers into inept halfwits?

Like I said, it’s hard to mess up the basic Tetris gameplay, but the ridiculous keyboard layout on this version comes very dose to it.
Tetrix

Tetrix is a clone of Tetris for the Amiga. It runs in a set of windows on an 8-colour OS screen or on the standard Workbench screen, and multitasks. The graphics are simple, but it has statistics over each type of block dropped and a preview of the next block. There are 15 difficulty levels — the higher the difficulty, the more of the screen is filled with blocks when the game starts. When a new game is started, you may choose to use the exact same sequence of blocks as in the previous game, a handy feature for setting up tournaments where every player is given the same chances.
