And sometimes he is even successful in his excavations - like with Tolteka, the underground city labyrinth that he wants to explore with remote-controlled robots. But our old professor is an excellent archaeologist, but he knows nothing about technology. Accompany Prof. Dr. Style to the remains of ancient civilization. Discover a new world of strategy gaming in the city labyrinths of Tolteka...
• 3fach splitter Screen
• 1 and 2 player option
• bidirektionales Scrolling
• lots of moving sprites
• 38 Level
• 60 different image elements
• Highscoreliste
• 10 different opponents
Tom & Jerry

There can be few people who have not heard of Tom and Jerry, the funniest double-act responsible for bringing more gratuitous violence to our screen then Rambo, The Professionals and Eastenders combined. With the exception of the later cartoons, which at generous assessment were rubbish, most of their adventures have stood the test of time and still manage to be funny at the fifteenth time of viewing. So if it works for a cartoon, the same zany formula should work for a computer game. Right? Well it is a good theory.

The game's opening credits are promising, with accurate renditions of both characters, and the Amiga's sound capabilities reproduce Tom's manic laughter perfectly. The action, such as it is, takes place in various places about the house that are linked by Jerry's mouseholes. The aim is to guide Jerry through rooms, over shelves and furniture, devouring as much cheese as possible within the time limit of 500 seconds.
Tom & Jerry 2

The game uses the exact same engine as 'Tom & Jerry: Hunting High and Low' (including the title screen). It is a level disk as a standalone game.

Two of the most popular cartoon creations of all time have now been brought to the computer screen. Everybody always refers to Jerry as the cutest little mouse you ever did see etc, etc, but I have a sneaking suspicion that true fans of the programs found him to be too good to be true and much preferred Tom, the anti-hero. Nevertheless, there is no option within the game; you must control Jerry. He is hungry and looking for a supply of his favourite cheese. There is plenty scattered around the house but Tom is out to do his best not to let him get any.

The action is that of a platform game as you leap round the furniture trying to reach the cheese before Tom grabs you. There are a number of devices that you can use to keep Tom at bay for a few vital seconds.
Tom and the Ghost

7-year-old Tom and his mother are visiting the old castle in Scotland, while evil sorcerer kidnapped the mother. Tom was very upset, but the brave ghost Sir Reginald Arrow appears to help Tom. Evil sorcerer kidnapped his beloved 500 years ago to sacrifice her for Lucifer. Tom's mother may become the last victim in the sequence of dark ritual, and Sir Arrow has only 24 hours to stop the ritual and free Tom's mother. 

In the game you are controlling Sir Arrow. He may walk; jump; duck; use weapon; collect, combine and use items. Tom is near, but he should be kept in good mood. He may help you to beat monsters, but his energy is exhausting and he should be fed with Hamburgers and Milkshakes. When he is upset, you should give him a Teddy Bear. All such items as well as many others required to progress in the game such as different weapons, magic harp, or lighter, etc. are scattered within the castle.
Tom Landry Strategy Football

Football simulation game featuring the likeness and strategic advice of legendary coach Tom Landry. You'll take the role of a new coach for the team of your picking who gets mentored by Mr. Landry himself along your career.

The game allows you to modify and customize your team to enhance its strengths, manage the acquisition of new players and perform general management tasks. Come game time the game takes away all the menus and windows and puts you in a side-scrolling view of the stadium from which you can watch the game take place. At any time you may issue offensive or defensive formations and make substitutions to try and indirectly affect the outcome of the game. 

Features VCR-style controls to speed up or pause the action and any time and an ubiquitous on-line hint and help system in the form of an "Ask Landry" window in which you can consult him on any aspect of American football coaching.
Tom Landry Strategy Football: Deluxe Edition

This Deluxe Edition of Tom Landry Strategy Football brings new features to the strategy football game. The new features include:

A league editor which allows the player to edit league and team attributes, offensive and defensive playcalling tendencies and individual players names and abilities.

Season play options which allows the player to create a pro football season, track games, track team standards, track season leaders' stats and play scheduled or exhibition games.

New offensive and defensive formations
The game also features the '92 Pro Season default team and players attributes
Tomb Lady

It's a Lady Tut inspired game for the Amiga 500, The game is completely free, I used AI, this is version 1.0, I could improve it furthermore in the future (for now after level 3 u got infinite ammo, but next version will be corrected).
Tomb Lady: Part II

Tomb Lady - Part II is a classic action-adventure maze game for the Amiga 500 (512kb) or Amiga 1000 (with the 256kb A1050 front panel expansion), loosely inspired by the 8-bit Commodore 64 classic Lady Tut. In this sequel, players guide fearless heroes through perilous, trap-filled ruins, ancient tombs, and mysterious underground caverns.
Tomb Raider IV

A single player, freeware puzzle game created by Marcin Oriowski and only related to the big game franchise as there was a puzzle in the Lara Croft game that served as an inspiration for this game's puzzle. Seen here from an overhead view instead of the first person view in that game.
Tombstones

Press space to start the game. Place your fingers on the keyboard while you GET READY. When a random character is displayed on the screen, you have to press the same character on the keyboard to draw and shoot your gun! If you are too slow, or you press the wrong character, you will get wasted.
Tomcat
Inspired by Tomcat Alley for the Sega/Mega CD, this game tries to offer full motion video sequences into this F14 Fighter game while you attack ground locations and have an occasional dogfight.
Tomcat (Gary Swann)
A single player, SEUCK based shooter released as Licenseware by Gary Swann in 1991. This shooter, inspired by the Top Gun movie has you blasting MIGs and dodging missiles, flying over the high seas.
Tommy Gun

Aliens have arrived and have taken control of the inhabitants of the five zones. Now you must take control of the killer tomato Tommy Gun and fight your way through the five levels, defeat the aliens and rescue your tomato friends that can be found imprisoned across the levels.

The gameplay of Tommy Gun is quite basic. It is a rail shooter with a third person perspective, where you take out your enemies one after the other scrolling from side to side. Each of the five levels have their unique setting and enemies. For example in the super market level you fight against vegetables and in the Paradise Island level you fight against crabs and pirate parrots, just to mention a few.

If you free the prisoners you'll get extra ammo, health packs, shields and other stuff that will help you stay alive a little longer. There is also a two player mode where the second player takes control of the sidekick Big Cheese.
Tomtespelet

Tomten are Swedish gnomes or elves and Tomtespelet translates as The Santa Game. It is a 2 player only, split-screen, game with similarities to Air/Table top hockey games. The upper gnome has a white ball and the lower one has a red ball and each try to score simultaneously.
Tonga

A platform game. Collect hearts and locate the hidden switch before finishing the level. A PD game from Gunter Meister in 1992. There once was the land of Tortiga, That's where the Nassars lived. Their chief was called Tonga. Now it happened that the sorcerer Orrara kidnapped Tonga's bride and held her prisoner in a secret dungeon. Tonga must try to find the dungeon. He has to face many dangers. He has to pick up objects that are hanging in the air on his way. There are secret switches that allow you to progress. Dangerous monsters cross his path that he has to avoid. Invisible traps complicate his journey.
Tony & Friends in Kellogg's Land

Tony and Friends in Kellogg's Land is a platform game that was developed by Factor 5 for Rauser Advertainment, and released on the Commodore Amiga and MS-DOS operating system in 1994 only in Germany; as the name suggests, it is a promotional game for Kellogg Company cereals, and stars Tony the Tiger, Dig 'Em Frog (but he's only referred to as "Smacks" throughout it), Coco the Monkey and Toucan Sam (Chocos the Bear will also appear to give them advice in German, when they jump up and hit their heads on the underside of the Super Mario Bros.-style question blocks which can be found throughout each level).
Tony's Glider Game

A simple game where you have to guide your glider down to earth avoiding all the planes etc. and do it as quickly as possible without crashing. Game was distributed to Public Domain with full source code.
Tony: Montezuma's Gold

A game featuring monochrome graphics (marmite for some!), but also deadly enemies such as bats and snakes, charming animations, nasty spike traps, and a nod to classic monochrome platformers games many of us still love to this day. The game is a tribute to Tony Halik.
Toobin'

Toobin' involves Biff and Jet racing their way down the rapids of a river, riding on tires. You rotate your tyre left or right, and drift as the current sends you, making sure to avoid the banks of the river, and the dividing lines in the middle. Hazards include crocodiles, stray logs and branches, and fishermen - you are armed with a limited supply of tin cans to take care of these. There are gates to slide through on the way down - these give you a points bonus. Each level has a strict time limit to adhere to, although there's a kickin' party at the end if you succeed.
Toobz

Toobz is a puzzle game involving coloured spheres, which are variously red, blue, green and yellow. They are fired into a level from various starting points, along a selection of tubes (or 'toobz'), and the aim is to guide them into finishing points of the correct colour. This is done using various rotation points, which can be turned so as to redirect each ball. If it hits the end of the point (with it not set to recieve a ball) it goes straight back where it came from.

The levels also include machines which recieve a ball and change its colour, in accordance with a pre-defined sequence.

After each finishing point recieves a ball, its target colour changes at random, so be careful of setting it up to recieve multiple balls in one go.

Points are awarded based on how much time you have left after getting the required number of balls across. Time is lost for each ball of the wrong colour that reaches the end - running out of time costs you one of your 3 lives
Took

A two player game based on a game by Magic Bytes called Blue Angel 69. The aim is to clean up a numbered field of stones. The level is that one player could only move and select stones horizontal, other vertical only. Very first one coded in Amos 1.3 and it seems to do nothing with the original one.
Top Banana

Top Banana is a game synthesised from everything that was hip, cool and "in" during the early nineties. With members from the experimental sampling music group Coldcut in the development team, it aimed to look no worse than a contemporary MTV video, with a cool rave intro, crazy "sampled" graphics composed of random imagery and lots of aaaciiiiiid.

What it all boils down to is a very simple platform game with very advanced graphics. You control a girl in a rave outfit who jumps through a series of platform worlds where you throw some love around in the form of hearts, which somehow ties into an environmentally conscious (the packaging was made out of recycled paper) theme where the enemies are representatives of big business. Also, similar to Rainbow Islands, a mass of water is slowly rising from below, so you must hurry upwards through the level.
Top Cat Starring in Beverly Hills Cats

Top Cat is in Beverly Hills to track down Benny the Ball, prevent him gaining the contents of a will that is not rightly his, and find the rightful heiress.

The game is a top-down puzzler of sorts. An object manipulation mode is used to pick up and use objects when necessary. Extra milk (for energy) and fruit (for points) can be collected. Skateboarders must be avoided as they can take objects and randomly move them.

The members of your gang must all be gathered up on the first level and must be kept on your side by ensuring that your energy doesn't drop too low.
Top Gear 2

This third-person racing game resembles Gremlin's earlier Lotus series, in terms of its general look and feel, right down to the text font used in the game. Your task is to race through 16 countries, each of which features four races, with many real-world circuits recreated in incongruous locations (such as the Monza layout in Ayers Rock, and the old Hockenheim in Vancouver). 

These four-race blocks each represent their own mini-championship, in which you race against 19 cars, needing to finish in the top 10 to continue, and with the top 6 scoring points 10-6-4-3-2-1, and the respective amount of money in thousands. This can be spent on various upgrades, ranging from engine to tires (wet and dry) and from shocks (front, side and rear) to gearboxes. The ideal approach is to buy the more expensive versions ASAP, as you get no saving when upgrading. If you win the four-race championship, you get the next password.
Top Hat Willy

A Jet Set Willy clone created by Tero Heikkinen and released in 1995. Top Hat Willy is an homage to the famous Jet Set Willy, a notoriously difficult flick-screen platform game with lots of screens. Guide Willy around his vast and very strange mansion, filled with death traps and dangerous creatures such as rolling razors, bunnyrabbits and flying TV sets, to collect his flashing items. A score panel on the bottom keeps track of how many of the many rooms Willy has explored and how many items have been picked up.

Even though THW makes some use of the Amiga's large colour palette, it remains true to its ZX Spectrum inspiration, so that each enemy is a single colour (or a single hue), dividing the screen in distinct 8x8 pixel blocks with separate colours for each block and having a black background.
Top of the League
Top Of The League a football\soccer management game and was ported by the original author from the Amstrad CPC title of the same name and published by Scogen in 1992.
Top Secret

Top Secret is a platform game played out on individual screens, each with a number of disks to collect. There are various enemies on the screen, which must be hit a number of times to be stopped. The ground-based creatures can then be walked over for points, while the birds simply stop for a few seconds. Your weapons have an arc similar to Kid Gloves, meaning that they hit the ground then rebound to a lower height, making precision aiming important. The level layouts are similar to Rodland, with gaps between platforms, and your character glides in a similar way - some of the disks are suspended in mid-air, and you must control the character's fall to pass over these - thankfully your character isn't harmed by falling. A number of bonus items are on offer, including extra points, extra lives and invincibility
Top Tilers

Top Tiler is an puzzle-arcade game with an idea in mind: to recreate the atmosphere of Japanese arcades we were used to see in the late '80s. The gameplay is very simple. To win, you have to move your character over the tiles in the background in order to reveal the image hidden behind them.
You have to avoid the roaming enemies too or you'll lose a precious life. Some tiles have special properties. The effect these tiles produce are described at the beginning of the game. The game has 6 levels, which are divided into 4 sublevels. It has a nice ending sequence with credits too.
Top Wrestling

Top Wrestling is a one-on-one wrestling game. The player controls one of 16 selectable wrestlers and must defeat all the others in a tournament, or selected individual opponents in a single match.

Selectable wrestlers include spoofs of actual then-WWF wrestlers (such as Hulk Hogan, Sergeant Slaughter, Brutus Beefcake or Shawn Michaels) and other celebrities, as well as original characters. The wrestlers have all the same set of moves: there are no signature moves or distinguishing techniques between them. The moves each wrestler can perform include a standard punch, knee strike, dropkick and throw. Diving drops can also be performed from a turnbuckle when the opponent is down.

Competitive multiplayer is available in single match mode. The game can be saved to disk during a tournament.
Topsy Turvy

A cute and fun Q-Bert clone game released in demo form in 1991 by Joerg Schmidt and Tarkus Team 91. The game has many features not featured in the original game, starting off much more difficult, in potentially requiring several color changes on all blocks, and having many baddies to avoid including springs, rubber balls, ghosts and other monsters as well as pickups that will help in game.
Torch 2081

Torch 2081 is essentially an improved version of Taito's arcade game Qix, where one fences off sections off the gameworld, trapping bonuses, enemies and whatever else inside. Once you have claimed enough territory, you proceed to the next level.
Tornado

A detailed flight sim of the Tornado strike fighter. Features high-speed, low-altitude precision bombing runs over a battlefield full of active friendly and enemy air and ground units. Allows you to utilize all the complex avionics in both positions of the two-man cockpit. Campaign mode contains a full-featured mission editor. The editor contains a dynamic battlefield map, which reflects the results of your latest missions. If you plan and execute a mission against a SAM site, it will be gone in the next planning session. The editor allows you to plot and synchronize attacks consisting of multiple flights of Tornados.
Tornado Ground Attack

Tornado Ground Attack is a horizontally scrolling shoot 'em up where the player flies a Tornado and has to take out a large amount of enemy planes. The main objective for each mission however is to destroy a target by dropping plenty of bombs on it. In addition to the fighter planes there are other enemies like helicopters and tanks and the player also has to avoid hitting objects like buildings and trees. Too many hits or collisions and the plane will explode and the player will lose a life. Parachutists will sometimes jump from shot down enemy planes and by collecting these the player gains ammunition and (occasionally) a bonus life or energy. To get additional and more powerful weapons the player can collect fuel pods that are dropped from some enemies when shot.
Torque

A fantastic horizontal shooter, obviously influenced by Uridium. Shoot up a section of a giant alien dreadnought ship, when you've destroyed enough of it and the fighters they send out to fight you and you can move on to the next section.
Torvak the Warrior

Torvak, a man with the typical barbarian looks, comes back to his homeland after an exile of five years. But instead of a warm greeting, he receives a telepathic message that an evil necromancer took over. So of course the next course of action is to travel through five levels while killing all of the necromancer's creatures on the way, including an especially nasty one at each level's end.

The levels are generally side-scrolling, but sometimes underground passages can be reached via holes. This has no significant effect, though. The gameplay consists of using the four melee weapons which three moves each to get rid of the enemies without dying from their hits. Helpful power ups can be found when destroying parts of the scenery. Besides health refreshments and invincibility, there are also permanent upgrades for Torvak available, e.g. an extended health bar, greater speed or magical enchantments for the weapons.
Total Carnage

The war of 1999 left the country of Kookistan in shambles. Naturally, a dictator named General Akhboob took control of the beleagured nation and began creating an army of radioactive mutants. With a virtually impenetrable stronghold, a bunch of hostages, and a legion of mutants under his command, the evil despot will stop at nothing but world domination. Only two men have the courage and idealistic naivete to take on Akhboob and his forces: Captain Carnage and Major Mayhem, also known as the Doomsday Squad.

As Captain Carnage or Major Mayhem, it is up to you or you and a friend (in simultaneous action) to rescue the hostages while shooting hundreds of mutants bent on your destruction. As you walk and run forward, backward, left, right, and diagonally through 20 battlezones of nonstop action, you'll always have your machine gun by your side.
Total Chaos 7

This is a turn-based strategy game board game card game, now with more monsters, more power-ups, more strategy. This is the 7th game in the Total Chaos series. This is the direct sequel to Total Chaos 6: The Newbie Edition.
Total Chaos City II

Two guys with guns try to kill each other. A top down dueling game. Pick up bigger weapons and upgrades to shoot each other with. Includes 6 different maps. A medical drop will take you back to full health, a magazine will take you up to full for your *current* weapon. A dozen different weapons with varied amounts of default ammo, damage, blast, range and rounds\minute.
Total Domination
A strategy game from Paul Huckstepp involving two colonies fighting over the same area of land. Released via Licenceware.
Total Domination 2

A vast strategy game involving colony creation and stabilization after the destruction of the Earth. Inspired by Utopia K240. Released via Licenceware by Paul Huckstepp as part of his Domination strategy series in 1996.
Total Eclipse

Uses 3D system called Freescape developed by Incentive Software Ltd.

A pyramid has been built to destroy anything that blocks the sun and now a total eclipse is about to occur. Collect ankhs to open doors, shoot mummies, drink water and maybe then you solve the puzzle of pyramid. Controlling yourself in 3D world, you may change angle of your rotation and width of your steps to avoid some obstacles. Also you can use your gun to shoot some doors or to eliminate some foes.
Total Excess
A horizontally scrolling wave shooter with absolutely fantastic music from Nick the Greek and released to the public domain in 1994.
Total Football

Named after the tactic invented by Rinus Michels and their "Clockwork Oranges" Dutch team of the 70's, Total Football is an International competition game including 52 teams (including an all-star team) and compete in a 16 team league, 32 team knockout and a 32 team tournament similar to the World Cup.

Featuring a low-angle isometric view (not compensated by the d-pad, meaning pressing right will move the player along the half-way line (his right), not in the direction of the right corner flag (the screens' right) like in most games featuring axonometric views, while buttons allow to pass the ball in different strengths or kick at goal. Managing is limited to the choice of eight different formations at the start of the game and half-time.
Total Pattern

Total Pattern is a new game by Digital Team with 20 puzzle levels. The game’s preview had it’s debut at Retrokomp/Loaderror 2015 party. After that djpiotrs was joined by Selur, who created new graphics and Andrzej Drozd, responsible for the soundtrack. 
The game is based on Sokoban, but with some tweaks and changes.
Total Recall

Doug Quaid is a mild-mannered construction worker with a gorgeous wife in an apartment on futuristic Earth. Plagued by restless feelings and dreams of Mars, he heads to Rekall, Inc. to purchase a commercial memory implant of a Martian vacation 'cheaper, better, and safer than the real thing'. However, the implant procedure uncovers latent memories of Quaid's real life as a secret agent for the Martian government. Pursued relentlessly by his former employers, Quaid must fight from Earth to Mars in a battle to reclaim his past and secure his future.

Total Recall for the Amiga and Atari ST has players controlling Quaid as he fights through seven levels on Earth and Mars. The game alternates between platforming levels and driving levels. Platforming levels require Quaid to fight guards and find the exit. The player may duck to avoid bullets and fight back with both captured weapons and meaty Schwarzenegger fists.
Total Species

This game is the sequel to Emotional Conflict. In that game you tried to hunt down Mutant Mickey, a head-case, but upon finding him, you let him slip through your slimy, greasy, oily fingers. Though you did manage to recover the rare, lost coin. And now we're back, back FOR REVENGE, I tell you. This time, MM has kidnapped your Mother and is holding her hostage in this maximum security hotel, where rich celebrities like Mikey stay. You begin in the lobby and begin your revenge from there! 
 
Game came packed with a sub game called Wormzies. Asa Margetts was the creator and developer of this overhead, point and click PD game.
Total War
A single screen board game in the style of RISK, released by Paulo Laureano and Francisco Cordeiro and released as shareware in 1991.
Totaltetris

A Czech game with many parts translated into English, this is a Tetris game with some bonuses and power ups. The game has 4 "game worlds" which correspond to 4 variants of tetris. Please note the menu has 20, but are not available in the basic version. There is no 2 player mode. A Czech editor is available by booting from floppy disk 4 to increase the number of worlds. Hard disk use is strongly recommended.
Touch 'n Go

Touch all colored tiles and go to exit. Fun little PD game. There's a witty double meaning in this title. You must guide a character from the start of a maze through to the end. The difficulty is that each square disappears after you step on it, meaning that you have to touch the square and go, without being able to return.

You're also up against a strict time limit, so it's all too easy to make a crucial mistake and be forced to step into oblivion. It's therefore definitely touch and go as to whether you can get through it.
Touchstones

A one or two player board game created by Spence Davies and released by Deja Vu Software in 1990. Touchstones is played on a 12 x 8 board using 72 'Stones'. Take turns to place Stones next to ones of same shape or color or both. (diagonally does not count). Stones placed around the edge of the board do not score and are of strategic importance only. The next stone to be placed is at the top of the stack on the right of the screen.
Scoring:
A 1 sided match A 2 sided match scores 1 pt scores 2 pts
A 3 sided match scores 4 pts
A 4 sided match scores 8 pts
Tough Nuts

Tough Nuts is a physics slingshot game for the Amiga 1200 (AGA) in the spirit of Angry Birds, with a world of its own: nuts knock bark beetles out of their forts. Nine worlds of ten levels, nine heroes with abilities of their own, bosses, cartoons and ten tunes — on two floppies or on a hard disk.
Touring Car Challenge

An addictive compelling Touring Car Management simulation. Touring Car Challenge gives you the opportunity to use your skill and judgement to manage a top Touring Car team, have your own on and off the circuit battles and perhaps influence the outcome of the championship, "if you're good enough." 
 
Select from any of the top teams, full drivers and manufacturers championship, 1-4 players, 4 difficulty levels, records and championship statistics. Setup your car, sign your driver and race!
Touring Car Racer

This game offers a simulation of the popular British Touring Car Championship of the early 90s. Four different cars are featured, from Toyota, BMW, Nissan and Vauxhall, which make up the 24-car grid. The game features accurate re-creations of Brands Hatch, Silverstone, Donington Park and Oulton Park. You can practice each track, or do single races or championships, over 3,5 or 7 laps, although you always start 10th on the grid with no qualifying. The race is viewed from above and behind your car, similarly to the Lotus Challenge series.
Tournament Golf

Select your level of play, and then head for the pro shop to choose between Black Carbon, Glass Fiber, and Ceramic Clubs.

Tee off by yourself or play 18 holes with a friend. Besides the One and Two Player modes there's also a practice mode, match play (head to head), and a full-blown international tournament, where you'll stroke it out against 15 competitors.

Tournament play lasts 12 rounds, 18 holes of golf each. Most rounds are standard "stroke" play but the seventh and eighth rounds are "match" games. Things really get serious when match game ends in a tie, and players move into a sudden death play-off.

During the tournament players earn higher skill levels, more knowledgeable caddies, and more power. You'll earn a password at the end of each round of the tournament.

The game let's you play on three different courses; Japan, the United States, and Great Britain.
Tower
A 3D Construction Set based adventure, created by Bruno Pommier and released as shareware in 1992.
Tower Block 2

The concept is simple: stack moving blocks on top of each other and build your tower as high as possible. Timing and precision are essential — misaligned blocks will make your tower narrower, making each subsequent move more challenging!
Tower FRA

Tower FRA is certainly different to the type of programs that Thalion are recognised for. Usually you can expect to see a below average arcade game, but Tower FRA is a totally different kettle of fish. Although the game doesn't look like too much has gone into it, it plays amazingly well. Although the graphics don't matter, they could still have been a lot better, and the supposedly sampled sound seems as if it's come straight off the Workbench voice utility. This game is not going to appeal to everyone, but for those of you who enjoy this type of thing Tower FRA is brilliant.
Tower of Babel

The Zapper, Pusher and Grabber robots were dropped onto the planet of the Shinerians, but are now desperate to return home. They have killed off the Shinerian race, but must climb a high tower, negotiating all the traps it holds, before they can contact their masters.

Each robot's name indicates what their main function and purpose is, and these skills must be combined for success. Each section has its own task - collecting energy pods and destroying mines and bombs for example. The creatures which fill the towers must be avoided, or used to your advantage.
Tower of Evil
An unofficial remake of the game TOWER OF EVIL from the C16, plus4, c64,Z80 to Amiga
Tower of Souls

Tower of Souls is set in the land of Chaybore in which seven crystals are responsible for the well being of its citizen. But the evil demon Baalhathrok has taken them and so the player controls Treeac to retrieve them.

In an isometric view, Treeac has to conquer the seven floors of Baalhathrok's tower. The player controls a ball with his mouse and clicks where Treeac should go. Fights are initiated with left clicking on the enemy, for other actions the right mouse button has to be hold while choosing a symbol on the bottom of the screen. Besides of fighting the enemies the player has to open several doors - either by finding the key, pressing the right buttons in the right order or using one of his four lockpicks. When using the lockpicks the player has to beat a mini game where he has to make the correct mouse movements. 

When searching the rooms of the dungeon there are various potions, herbs and magical pieces of equipment to be found.
Tower Toppler

You play a small green guy who needs to blow up eight towers, because their presence is somehow poisoning the water of planets which could potentially be ideal colonies. Unfortunately you need to get to the top of these towers to blow them up.

You make your way up to the top of the tower via walkways around the outside of the towers. You need to jump over, kick, and run from various enemies in your journey to the top. Most vertical movement is achieved by jumping onto moving ledges at the right moment.

The game was considered revolutionary in its time for its graphic technique. As the main character walked around the outside of the tower, the character was fixed in the middle of the screen while the tower itself rotated. This gave it a pseudo-3D effect.

Towers are linked together via a voyage through the sea in your trusty MK.7 submarine. This plays out as a side-scrolling collect-'em-up in which bonus points can be obtained.
Towers of Hanoi (Delboy)
Move all the counters from stack 1 to either stack 2 or stack 3. Only low numbers can be placed on high numbers.
Toy Box

Push the toy boxes and candies across the floor to squash the bugs and other threats before they get you. You can blast the boxes if you need to, but it won't help your score. Press Q if stuck. If you take too long more baddies will show up.
Toyota Celica GT Rally

On their way to becoming kings of the racing game, Gremlin produced this. It gives you a four-wheel drive rally car and a whole load of stages to race through.

You have a 3D behind-the-wheel view, including hands, gauges and everything! The simple idea is to stay on the track while going as quickly as possible.

You race the clock, not other drivers directly, and crashes earn you point penalties so care is needed. Nonetheless Celica is very exciting, and the implementation of a sliding, bucking rally car is very well done.

Churches, houses and other inconsequential objects rush by the windows, all done with smoothness and speed, and the sound is excellent. This is one computer game that actually sounds like a car.

The only problem is that you can’t race other cars directly, and that rallying is a difficult skill to master (seeing as you don’t have any feeling for which direction the car is actually traveling in.
Tracers

In the future all computers are connected to one central mainframe so a force called Tracers are created to stop hackers entering the computer by mind and stealing or corrupting vital data. You play a Tracer and you must enter the computer with your mind and play a battle of wits against a hacker who can be played by the computer or a friend.

Tracers is a Light-Cycle game where the game is viewed from above so your Tracer Module and your opponent are represented by squares. As each module moves it leaves behind a growing trail of data and if one of the modules touches a trail then they get their brain fried and after so many 'Burns' the person thrown out of the computer. Hackerdust can be found to raise your intolerance slightly to the burn. You can't control the speed of the module, just steer it but you can give yourself a limited short burst of speed. The whole arena is shown on the screen and a joystick used to control the modules.
Track Attack

A single player, freeware, graphical train track management game from Electrosoft in 1995. In this game, you have to direct colored trains into stations of the same color by switching points on the track. The trains are red, blue or yellow. To change a point, move the cross-hair over the point using the mouse and press the left mouse button (LMB). During the game, holding down the space bar will speed up the trains. pressing 'P' will pause/unpause the game and pressing, Escape (Esc) quits the current game. The Jolly Good sample can be toggled with the 'S' key if it gets on your nerves! The 'T' key can be used to force the release of another train from a station. 

Trains are released from stations randomly, with up to four running at any one time. When a train is released, a whistle sounds and the guard at the top of the screen holds up a flag whose color matches that of the station from which the train is leaving.
Track Suit Manager

In this simulation, you get to manage any one of the European national squads and take them through friendly matches and the various stages of the European Nations Cup and the World Cup. If you are feeling a bit masochistic, you can take on the managership of the England side with its built-in list of players. Or maybe you would fancy another country in which case you'll have to type in your own players a minimum of 30 and a maximum of 100 players in all. You specify their playing position - goalkeeper, defence, midfield or forward (and, optionally, their home club) and the program takes care of the rest.

TSM disappointingly makes no use at all of the Amiga's potential - it looks like a straight conversion job from 8 bit machines - it still manages to be an absorbing, addictive and stimulating game. If the above flaws could be attended to, it would be magnificent. As it is, Track Suit Manager is merely excellent. Go get it.
Track Suit Manager II

A football\soccer game, the sequel to the original Track Suit Manager by Goliath Games. The game uses a revamped version of the original TRACK SUIT MANAGER artificial intelligence system written by Goliath coder and then-director, Doug Mathews.
Tracker

Tracker is a mouse-controlled vector-graphics 3D strategy game depicting an ultra-violent TV show of the future. As a contestant, the player's mission is to be the first to ever complete it successfully. The task involves commanding a fleet of Skimmers charged with destroying various groups of combat vehicles, including Cycloids, Scouts and Defenders. Short and long-range scanners are available to aid in this.

The game takes place in a maze world containing a number of distinct sectors, each of which has its own type of enemy present. The Communication Centre powers the Cycloids, and are protected by the Defenders. Once these are taken out, the Centerpoint Sector must be destroyed to complete the level.
Tracker Hero

Tracker Hero is a musical game for the Amiga that uses MOD song files. It can be played with keyboard, Joystick, Guitar or Dance Mat (Using Paul

Willingham's or PSX64 PS2 to Amiga adapter). Other PSX to Amiga CD32 adapters may also work. It has been developed on an Amiga 1200 and WinUAE using Amiblitz2, Personal Paint, Protracker and some other tools. Additional songs can be downloaded from Aminet or from the game's page.
Tracker's Quest
A one or two player puzzle game created and published by Backwoods Software and Computational Software in 1989.
Tracksuit Manager 2
Tracksuit Manager 2 was another game inspired by classic Championship Manager. It's the sequel to one of the finest football management games of all time.
Tractor Beam

1992 saw the release of Tractor Beam on the Amiga systems, a Thrust variant, created by Plasma Software and released for free as a PD.

Tractor Beam is one of those games which can get really annoying quite quickly. The basic idea is to manoeuvre your droid ship from the left hand side of the screen to the right, pick up a box with your tractor beam and carry it back again. This sounds simple except for the fact that your tractor beam shows all the same properties as long strip of elastic, and so can rapidly become very difficult to control. Also, touching anything is fatal for you and the box.

You start each level floating in the left-hand pool of water, and the box starts in the right. Using the joystick you must move your droid so it is just above the box, and click fire to activate the beam. Then (very gently) drag the box back to your pool and gently set it down, clicking fire again to release the beam.
Trade Travel Fight
A German language strategy trading game.
Traders

Pit your business and marketing skills against as many as three other competitors while raising and lowering your buying and selling prices for a variety of goods on the interplanetary market. You can produce goods, such as perfume, by planting your fields with flowers. You'll have to purchase raw materials, such as water, which may raise the price of your finished products.
Trailblazer

An imaginative action game in which you must guide a ball-shaped craft through a succession of levels. These have a patchwork-quilt type display, with holes to avoid, and squares of various colors, which affect the craft's speed, both within its power potential and into warp, as well as a control-reverser and lots of holes. You can jump and thus avoid these holes, although you have a limited number of them for each level, and it's possible to adjust the speed through joystick or keyboard control. You also face a time limit on each of the levels, although your time is boosted every time you complete one.
Train Driver 3

The last in the Train Driver series, this one features dozens of routes across England and Scotland, with authentic sounding diesel and electric trains. Its tricky to start rolling, and difficult to know when to brake for stations, but it does give a warning if you missed one.
Trained Assassin
Trained Assassin is an Action game, developed and published by Digital Magic, which was released in Europe in 1989.
Trains
A clone of Locomotion coded by Barry "Dingo" Driver in Blitz Basic 2. Transport the passengers to their required destinations within the time limit using the Little trains.
Traitor

The third game in the series, following Kill Em All and Countdown to Extinction, it would be followed by Hangar 18. This adventure-shooter series is packed with 7 missions and tons of weapons. You are sick and are prepared for cryogenic sleep in 2025 as tensions between the superpowers is growing and Europe is uniting to throw the US off of European soil. You awake in Paris in the year 3655 in a time of heightened mental abilities but with the major cities in ruins from a great war between the superpowers and as resources became more limited. You are told the stories of the former wars and how your skills can help in their current battle, they need someone not sensitive to psychic attacks to fight for them and so you have been revived. Can you help them to finally achieve peace through superior use of firepower?
Transarctica

The Viking Union has a very dominant role in your society, as they control the vast railway networks. Could they be to blame for the disappearance of the sun and the resultant ice age? As a train captain, you must find out and overthrow them.

Transarctica is a strategic trading and combat game. You must keep your train running and make sure there is enough fuel. When you reach towns you can trade with local people, with each city having a primary function. These towns often contain useful information to put you on the right track in your mission. You are in possession of slaves, who are traded just like other commodities.

Contact with other trains results in combat. Buy upgrades to boost your performance in combat, to increase your chance of fending off the Viking Union.
Transplant

The basic Asteroids gameplay features of rocks which break into smaller rocks when shot, and the game’s playfield rotating around the player, are implemented in this shoot ‘em up. Besides the rocks, there are lots of spaceships, many of which shoot at the player, and some which are clearly ‘inspired’ by the designs in Star Wars. All of these must be cleared to complete the level.

The player starts the game with 3 very basic ships, having no firepower, flexibility or shield upgrades. On each level, money can be collected, which can be spent on these items. Every item can be upgraded through five levels, although these are increasingly expensive. There is no points system however.

Rather innovatively, the game hands out passwords after each game so the player can continue at the start of the level on which the last life was lost.
Transputor

Transputor is a Breakout-type game, which is played in an isometric perspective and therefore an additional dimension is added to them.

The game is inspired by CRL's own 8-bit game Ball Breaker, which used the idea with isometric perspective before. The ball physics are like in many other games of that type: hitting the ball with one side let the ball fly to this side, often with a speed change which is unpredictable.

The player's bat is sitting on the right side, moving up and down, blocks being hit are vanishing, and if there are blocks stapled above them, they drop to the ball level becoming destructible. There are many special stones, giving different amounts of points, adding lives, changing the size of the bat either to the good (bigger) or bad (smaller). The player have a certain amount of missiles, and some blocks can only be destroyed with missiles.

There are 32 levels to beat, with increasingly difficulty.
Transworld

Transworld is a business simulation where you play a young entrepreneur in the carrying business. You start off with a capital of 50.000 DM and a small firm in Frankfurt am Main with the goal of building a business empire.

Apart from managing the delivery of a variety of goods (ranging from oil to food and vehicles), you can also try to increase your wealth by operating at the stock exchange or evading taxes. There are also several other aspects to consider: Too much work will increase your stress level, and if you do not take enough vacations, you will fall ill with corresponding negative effects on your enterprise. Furthermore, the game evaluates your play in three categories (success in business, prestige and trade relations), and winning the game requires a certain number of points in each category.
Transylvania

Transylvania is an adventure with optional graphics, and a VERB NOUN interface. Two weeks ago, Princess Sabrina suddenly vanished and remained unseen since. King John the Good asks any travelers to help in locating her - you volunteer.

As you begin your quest in the dark forests of Transylvania, beware of the evil that lurks. You will encounter strange creatures like a vampire and a goblin, and experience strange things. Most importantly, a werewolf is constantly chasing you, until you find the pistol and bullets necessary to kill it. Remember fellow traveler, take care...
Trap 'Em

This AGA game is quite a find. It plays a lot like the arcade game Rodland. 

Coded by Paul Clarke and released by Lionheart in 1996.
Trap Runner

Trap Runner is a classic platform game with few twists. Mind traps, obstacles and monsters.

Beside the genre-typical jumping and running action you can cower yourself to avoid contact with low flying monsters. In later levels magic pills will help your task to save May. Collect potions to fill transparent ghost tiles with colour to make them solid. Other pills will change your own skin colour, allowing you to pass tiles with the exactly same colour.

Collect items to increase your score, gain extra lives or fulfil one of the special missions. Two of four levels a world have a mission to accomplish.
Trapped

Tarnak has finally been defeated and the curse of the demon has been lifted, saving the population of Kaldrion. Centuries have passed and the land of Kaldrion has become prosperous. But the ancient scrolls say that the evil one will rise again and the only way to stop him is to collect the twelve divine symbols that form Talmar's Wheel. This will ban Tarnak in his own world. It's now up to the player to go to the catacombs of the gods and find the symbols before Tarnak rises from his coffin.

Trapped is a first person role playing game similar to Ultima Underworld. There are four characters to choose from: Dwarf, Knight, Hunter and Fighter. Some characters are better with certain weapons than with others. Throughout the catacombs the player will pick up items that he comes across such as new weapons and potions that improves health, armour, strength and speed of movement.
Trapped II

The sequel to Trapped is, like its predecessor, a 3D first-person action role-playing game in the vein of Ultima Underworld. The player character has a sword to attack the hordes of spiders, insects and wasps with, as well as fireballs which require mana. Plenty of other weapons are on offer throughout the lair the protagonist is initially trapped in.

There's a full magic system to get to grips with, and plenty of spells to collect, use and unravel. There are also puzzles that must be solved to advance. The game allows the player to save progress in one slot.
Trapped in the Tomb

As you opened the ancient tomb's gates, you unknowingly triggered a mechanism that sealed you inside. Around you stretches a dark labyrinth filled with mysteries, traps, and riddles of the past. To escape to the surface, you must find crystal skulls that will unseal the closed passages. Every step is a race against time and your own fear, but somewhere in the darkness lies the path to freedom. Will you uncover the tomb's secrets and break free from its grasp?

The tomb is never the same twice—each time you enter, the artifacts are hidden in different locations, and your journey begins from a new starting point.
Traps 'n' Treasures

Captain Jeremy Flynn’s crew have been kidnapped in the Caribbean, and he must venture through 4 large baddy-infested levels to retrieve them. Along the way, you can collect money from handily-placed treasure chests, which can be spent in various shops to gain extra weaponry.
Travel Manager
German language travel broker management game made by Jo Seitz of Sayonara and released in 1998.
Trax (Hironymus Jumpshoe)
A puzzler by Hironymus Jumpshoe and DJ Braincrack. Released 1993-06-11 on Amigo! issue 03/93.
Trax (J. Lucas)

An arena, some cover and a trusty tank for each of us. What fun we'll have! Based on Combat for the Atari VCS. The object is simple, destroy your opponent as quickly as possible. Only one shot per tank can be on the screen at one time. This can be modified in the setup, if desired. Game created by J. Lucas, M. Taylor and D. Vernon.
Traylers

A one or two player Tron Lightcycles\Worm\Snake game with anime style graphics and voice samples from Sunteam and released as freeware in 1992. The bloody, explosions when you crash give the game a satisfying ending every time.
Treasure Island

A freeware text adventure game created by Tony Heap of Heyley Software in 1991 using the Hatrack II adventure game generator. The game was included on the Amiga Computing issue 37 (June 1991) coverdisk. Pit your wits against some cunning problems in this Treasure Island text adventure.
Treasure Island Dizzy

This is Dizzy's second adventure. Dizzy is a cute little egg character who must explore the strange magic kingdom that is Treasure Island, solving problems and puzzles in order to escape from there. Dizzy must journey through haunted mines, tree villages, and underwater caverns in order to find hidden treasures. They will be used as bargain items to buy parts for the boat. The secondary goal is to collect 30 coins so he can pay the bribe in order to safely get off the island.

Unlike the other installments in the series the player has only one life without any energy bars to complete the game and is unable to select any particular item from the inventory for use. Items are rolled up through the inventory so the top one is used or dropped.
Treasure of Usas
A lesser known classic from Konami's MSX library now ported to the Amiga
Treasure Search
Treasure Search is a public domain adventure game developed by Peter Hickman and released in 1990.
Treasure Trap

Treasure Trap is an isometric action game similar to Head Over Heels, but less abstract in its theme. The player guides the diver in a series of rooms (100 total) where the main goal is to collect gold. The main hazard encountered is the sea life that occupied the vacant ship. The character has no weapons, but carries a limited amount of "smart fishes", trained piranhas that attack and destroy all the enemies in the room.
Treasures of the Savage Frontier

The Heroes of Ascore have been magically summoned to help old dwarven allies retake the city of Llorkh from the foul Zhentarim legions. After that, there are more dangers that lurk in the wilds of the Savage Frontier...

The sequel to Gateway to the Savage Frontier is a role-playing game using SSI's standard Gold Box gameplay system. You can import existing characters from playing the first game. The game is viewed from above, as you move your party into mystery, buildings and combat. The game now includes weather changes that affect movement and NPC interaction
Treble Champions

Treble Champions is a football management game. The player can manage a squad, train players, and try to gain the way to the top of the leagues and cups. There are four divisions of 20 teams each and 1,500 (fictional) players with individual attributes are included in the game and purchasable for the manager. Beside the squad skills and injuries, the finances have to be managed for further progress in the game.

All menus and handling are presented in text based menus, mouse control is not supported. The matches are presented in text messages and an overview statistic about possession and shots. During the game, no interaction or intervention is possible. Loading and saving options are present. There are three difficulty levels and the player can chose in which league he wants to start (starting in the premier league is possible).
Treble Champions 2

Treble Champions 2 is a managerial simulation in which the player takes over a team in the fifth UK division. The goal is to become successful in the Premier League in the long run. In comparison to the Treble Champions the options, previously restricted to training, lineup and transfer market, were expanded: now the player also may change the ticket prices, expand the stadium, borrow money from the bank and set up friendly matches before the season, Every athlete has a number of stats. There is no match presentation except a statistics field which gets updated over time.
Trek Trivia: Volume 1

The first in the series of 10 Trek Trivia shareware games and question sets from Micro FX Software that all released in 1988. This game had a larger focus on the original series but embraced all things Trekkie.
Tressette a Perdere

A highly customizable Italian language Casino game for one player and up to 3 computer opponents created by Giovanni Iacobelli. Tressette a Perdere is a popular Italian card game. In this digital version the player will play against the PC's artificial intelligence that will split into three opponents. The game ends when one of the players reaches 51 points and 
it is won by the player who scores the fewest points.
Trex Warrior: 22nd Century Gladiator

In the 22nd Century, Gladiator battles are highly important. You are Trex Veteran Riano Bolor, and you must fight up to 5 Planets with 30 sundry enemies. You fight in your world and if you win you are the champion of your world and journeys to the next battle to fight and win for the champion.

If you win a battle you win credits to buy new equipment and weapons, which can also be sold on to pay towards improved kit. The degree of difficulty will higher and higher, as the enemies are increasingly skilled and well-equipped, and you must to plan your strategy to win the battle.
TrianGO

TrianGO is a variation of the board game Go that is played on a hexagon shaped board. The board is composed of 21 lines which cross to form triangles. The lines intersect to create 55 points where players can place their stones. The game is available for up to four players who take turns placing stones on the board. The aim is to capture the stones of the opponents by creating triangles. A triangle is created when three stones are positioned so that they can be connected with straight lines. All of the stones that are located within the triangle can then be captured if the player chooses to. When making a capture, both the player's own stones and those of the opponents are removed from the board. The player's own stones can be brought back into play while the opponents' are permanently out. To win the game the player has to become the last one still able to make a move (due to still having stones left).
Trick or Treat

So simple but fantastic fun. A shareware, 2-player split screen first-person shooter duel. You get some powerups like teleporters, invisibility, or fireballs by entering into the various doors in the arena. Hilarious death scene. Trick or Treat values gameplay over an advanced engine and is a fun texture mapped arena shooter for two players. Each player is allocated their own mini-view of the maze which allows simultaneous play.
Trick or Treat (RobSmithDev)

The aim of the game is to collect 20 pieces of candy (treats) before you collect 20 tricks (in this cane, spiders, ghosts, bats and skulls!). There is a strategy to winning this game, but I’m not going to share that with you. In this video tutorial I'll guide you through the entire process of creating this game, finishing with a great product. Full Source Code Included!
Tricky Quiky Games: Die Suche nach den verschollenen Seiten

Tricky Quiky Games: Die Suche nach den verschollenen Seiten is a promotional adventure action game by Nestlé, that was given free in Nesquik cereal packages.

The player must take control of Quicky the Nesquik bunny to recover pieces of the recipe to Nesquik cereal. The player must travel through a number of chocolate filled lands including forests, tropical jungles, underground, winterscapes, and the mountains. Armed with a small gun which shoots small red bullets, the player has a health bar represented by a bottle of chocolate milk, and takes damage when striking enemies.
Triclops Invasion

Triclops Invasion is an early 3D space combat game that was originally developed for the QNX operating system.

The solar system has bee invaded by the Triclops who parachute their giant walkers down to Earth. The only way to destroy a walker is to shoot off one of its three legs but as it has a cannon turret on its top the game's documentation suggests that destroying that first could be a good strategy. Once all five walkers and their satellite the game is won, if the Triclops destroy all three of the player's ships the Earth is lost.

The game also allows the player to record demo versions of the way they played the game and to turn off the enemy walkers so that they can just fly over the landscape.

The Amiga version was commercially released via mail order.
Tricycle Ball

An example game bundled with Easy AMOS, published by Europress Software in 1992. A top down, multi-directional sports game for one or two players. The single player game has two different AI levels so you can start off easily and get used to the game in progression before playing two player side by side competition mode. It appears to be modeled after Anco's Kick Off game.
Tricycle Race
An AMOS based, 2 player competitive racing game from François Lionet that was published by Europress Software in 1992 as an example game of the Easy AMOS system pack.
Trifle
A single screen shooter in the manner of Space Invaders, but with much better graphics. AGA Chipset required. Created by DJM and ToJa of DTA Software and released to shareware in February of 2000.
Trinity

Trinity is a text adventure game, its events beginning in the near future. The player character finds himself trapped in the London Kensington Gardens, as hordes of nannies mysteriously block the exit. To make matters worse, a Soviet nuclear missile is about to fall. The protagonist finds a strange door and steps through it. The bizarre location outside of space and time contains other doors, each leading to a site where a historical or a fictional nuclear explosion has taken place. The player has to interact with the environment and solve puzzles to change the course of history before traveling to the New Mexico desert on July 16, 1945, and affecting the events of the fateful Trinity Test.
Trio
A tabletop single-player card game from Markt & Technik in their Power-Disc magazine, specifically Power-Disc 6.
Trip 2: Trip War

Made in 1995, after releasing 'Keith's Quest' the same year on F1 Licenseware. Though complete, Trip 2: Trip War was never released until now. It is a two-player only strategy-dogfighting hybrid.

You are daring pilots of lightning-fast Trip Ships in the year 2060, embroiled in a bitter war. Who will be victorious?

The aim is to shoot down your opponent, while collecting powerups to increase your speed, shot power and shield.

In War Mode, the players must also play a turn-based strategy game to aquire territory on the map, building and upgrading while sending your Trip Ships into combat.
Trip-A-Tron

Another Jeff Minter psychedelic creation, a light synthesizer for your Amiga. Change the phase, the offset, colors and influence the lights with your Amiga mouse for a trip to the dark side of your monitor. Converted to the Amiga by Andy Fowler.
Triple X
Triple X is an Action game, developed and published by Axxiom, which was released in Europe in 1989. It was released in several classic compilations, including the Amiga Star Collection and Goldrush.
Tristam Island

After crashing your plane at sea, you end up drifting to a small island, with not much to survive. You explore, and find out the island was inhabited, years ago. But why did the people leave? And why is there a fence around the white house at the top of the hill?

TRISTAM ISLAND is a text adventure made from the mold of Infocom; expect a large geography to explore, lots of prose, a rich parser, diverse puzzles, some humor and some darkness. To use Infocom's classification, I'd rate the game's difficulty as "Standard"; however, the game's design is modern and eschews all the frustrations commonly associated with 1980s text adventures. No hunger timers, no frustrating mazes, no blocking situations that force you to restart!
Tritus

A three person Tetris game. Amiga User International said it was the best game of its genre. Each player has a well in which to drop various shapes. The aim is to completely fill a horizontal row of blocks, which will then disappear, leaving space in the well. Completed rows effect other players, with single rows pushing others up, doubles producing green slimers, triples will releases assorted tricks and quads are especially nasty. 

Tritus was first released a few years ago as shareware. Thank you to all who registered! Now we've decided that you can have this full version for free.

Play competitively against computers or humans in this game with super smooth control and animation. Your actions affect the other players. Amiga User International said it was the best game of its genre.
Trivia Game Show
Trivia Game Show is a Miscellaneous game, published by Impressions Games, which was released in Europe in 1991
Trivia Trove

Triva Trove is a quiz game that consists of four parts that has to be completed in order. The first level is a variant of Tic-Tac-Toe played on a 3x3 board where each square contains a category. Upon choosing a category a four alternative question is given and if the player picks the right answer he gets a cross on the board and gets to choose the next category. If he answers wrong the computer will instead put a nought in the square. The game is timed and the first two levels have to be completed in twenty seconds.

In the second level the board is made up of eight circles with four subjects flashing on and off in sequence. The player has to stop the flashing when the chosen subject is black and then answer a question. Each of the four subjects have to be selected in turn which gets increasingly more difficult.

The third level is completely different. Here the player has to click on one of several squares that constantly change colour.
Trivial Pursuit: A New Beginning

After recreating the original board game as closely as possible with the first licensed game, Oxford did something different with the sequel. Each player now controls a spaceship, and the overall aim is to convince the Elders of the planet Genus to accept your people's plan to colonize it.

The Elders are all located in different parts of the galaxy, and can only be reached by travelling through the galaxy answering questions correctly, and answering a specific question once you get there. As a result, the gameplay isn't vastly different from the original. 

The six question categories are the same as the original, and there are 50 levels of question to clear, but the big difference is that the question category is random, so players who are only knowledgeable in one or two areas are no longer at an advantage.
Trivial Pursuit: The Computer Game: Amiga-Genus Edition

This is the home computer incarnation of Horn Abbot International Ltd's classic board game, Trivial Pursuit. The game involves answering questions on one of six subject categories to gain moves, and answering questions on special squares to gain one of the six 'Wedges' you need to gain the right to take on the final winning question. Questions are aimed at British players - many entertainment questions are based on British TV, and sport questions relate to popular British sports.
Trivial Pursuit: The Language Laboratory Edition
Trivial Pursuit: The Language Laboratory Edition is a Miscellaneous game, developed by Oxford Digital Enterprises and published by Domark, which was released in Europe in 1992
Triz
A single player PD Tetris clone, referred to as a Sacred Geometry Puzzle, created n Blitz Basic by Tom Schoenlau in 1995 . This game contains a mode with extended shapes and also a level editor.
Troddlers

Troddlers is a puzzle game in the vein of Lemmings. The player takes control of an animal-like wizard who can create and remove blocks; these blocks are useful for both jumping onto and redirecting the path of the little Troddlers that you have to direct towards the exit. The tricky bit is that the Troddlers can climb walls and ceilings, following the edge of the world and the exit is often in the middle of the screen or with an obstacle in the way.
Trog

Trog! (Also known as 'Og') was the second game Dave Parsons of Confused Pelican wrote for the Amiga. It was a fairly short, sideways-scrolling game in the Wonderboy style. It used pixel-perfect collision detection routines and ran in 32-colour mode. He revisited it later and made a much more colourful AGA version which had 64 colours, much smoother sky colours and screen fades, and a 1-bit parallax background layer. Outside of the game itself, it's really not very polished, and has pretty awful music.
Trolls

This platform game features the small blue-haired cutesy creatures that were popular around the time (although surely not with most computer game buyers?). You play a Troll roaming the levels in the hope of rescuing as many baby trolls as possible - each level gives you a set minimum to retrieve before you can leave via the Pigstop.

Initially you have no weapons, and contact with the nasties costs you energy, but a Yo-Yo can be collected, which can be used not only to kill enemies, but also to smash blocks away and open up paths, and even (with practice) tied to a ledge to allow you to swing across a gap.
Tron (Darius Hardy)
Fire up your lightcycle and take out your opposition, wind and swerve and block them off when you can. A game based on the cycle competition from the Tron movie and made by Darius Hardy in 1995.
Tron 95
A two-player only 'Tron-Clone" that includes 4 different playing fields to choose from. The game was created by Manfred Linzner (Pink / Abyss) and released in 1995.
Tron'90
A two player Tron style Worm\Snake game created by Thomas Jansen and released as public domain in 1990. Based on the Tron Light-Cycle-Races from the immensely successful Film.
Tron: Light Cycles
A Tron style Worm\Snake game for one or two human players and up to 6 additional CPU based players created as PD freeware by Dynatron in 1992.
Tronic

Tronic is a little Breakout-clone with additional bells and whistles. Goal of the game is to use a racket, controlled by arrow keys or mouse, to hit balls that destroy bricks. When all the bricks for a level have been cleared, the player will advance to a next level.

The racket can fire rockets at any time by using a 'Gigablitz' weapon. To activate it, hold down the 'Alt'-key and wait for an indicator to reach the top. The trick is, in order to use Gigablitz, no balls must hit the racket, or the Gigablitz sequence will be aborted.

When some bricks are hit, they release gadgets that can be collected. Many of them enable more balls on screen, enlarge balls or let you advance to the next level. Beware though, do not collect red-coloured gadgets as they can shrink your racket, invert racket movement or substract points.

Finally Tronic also has a built-in level editor that lets you create, play and save your own Tronic levels.
Tronic Kids

A RedPill based game which is for all Amigas with at least 2MB memory as a minimum. As noted by the developer this game was through the culmination of 8 months of intense work and is inspired by the classic game of Booby Kids which appeared on the Acades and the NES. 
In this game you must traverse each of the many screens to collect all the treasures which are scattered about the level to open up the doors to allow you to progress. Once that is done you can progress onto the next level and experience all 6 levels in the game to complete the game for good. Just be aware there are enemies about, that although can be avoided, you can also dig holes for them to fall in and be hopeful they disappear for good.
Tronics
Tronic is a Tron Light Cycles variant for up to 4 players. It was developed by Unrelated Dimension and released into the public domain in 1995.
Tronn

This is a clone of a game known to all, it's Tron. This version was produced by a old hacker of the Amiga: Thierry Floquet. The game is simple: you're a pixel (if not a motorcycle) and you draw a line behind you in an arena. And It is thus necessary to "dual" longer than the opponent(s) in this arena to win. If you succeed, you pass at the next level. The difficulty is getting going on and we are rapidly in very arduous levels and with several enemies in the arena and full of obstacles.

Tronn remains very (perhaps too) classical, for example, music is missing during the game or multiplayer mode. But it can be a ton of fun to outsmart and outmaneuver the computer. Released as freeware by Thierry Floquet in 1998.
Troop Jugernort Chapter 1

A single player beat-em up game by developed and published by Sunteam, in 1992. There is a legend that states that during a time of great unrest, a child will be hatched from a great egg. This child will start his life free, with abilities beyond the understanding of men. The child shall be gifted with the power of goodness from the beginning, and will bring peace throughout the land. 
 
However, not all legends go according to plan... 
 
During the night the child was given to the world, a great battle between the dragon spirits of Good and Evil was taking place. Lightning lanced over the land and mountains crumbled to dust as the two ghostly figures fought for the possession of the baby. While the Good dragon spirit gave the enemy a fatal blow, the Evil dragon spirit swallowed up the egg and vanished. 
 
But a powerful monk found the tiny, bruised baby alive.
Trooper
A galactic cross hairs space shooter. The view is from the bridge of your ship as you control the weapons systems to take out the enemy ships as they are coming right for you!
Truckin On

Truckin On is a 2 player game with the object to make more money than your opponent
 over a given time period. Each player is allocated $10,000 to start a Truckin Company.

A knowledge of the trucks capacity and fuel consumption is required and this can be obtained at the relevant truckyard. Also an indication of the trucks mileage capacity is indicated at the Service Station. There are a number of pitfalls which may be encounted on the road but these are self explanatory and require little reference.

The record so far is to turn $10,000 into assets of $1,000,000 in less than 10 weeks, if anyone can improve on that they should be with Allen Bond.
Truckin On II

Truckin On II is a 2-4 player game with the object to make more money than your opponent over a given time period. Each player is allocated $10,000 to start a Truckin Company.

A knowledge of the trucks capacity and fuel consumption is required and this can be obtained at the relevant truckyard. Also an indication of the trucks mileage capacity is indicated at the Service Station. Their are a number of pitfalls which may be encounted on the road but these are self explanatory and require little reference.
Trucking

An AmigaBASIC game programmed by Ma We Crew and released as freeware in 1988. It is a German language trucking management company game. Trucking is a trading and business simulation for 1 - 5 players. The number of game participants is asked at the beginning, as well as their names and company names, since each player runs his own company as a freight forwarder. For each new game, the company was founded in January 1988. At the end of each year, the points achieved by the players are compared with the YUPPI list and an entry is made if necessary. Every player begins their entrepreneurial career with the same starting capital; only the available overdraft facility changes from player to player. A game for many exciting hours...
Trump Castle II

In the second installment of the series you are entering the creation of Mr. Donald Trump - not only to play the casino games, but also to explore this "casino-resort by the bay". While playing one of the six games - Roulette, Blackjack, Baccarat, Slots, Poker, and Craps - you also may explore the Trump Castle's apartments, converse with its inhabitants, and even read the "Castle Courier" newspaper.

The game allows up to four players and may be saved in progress. The gameplay is directed on winning as much money as you can making the bets based on the combination of your luck and the theory of probability. You may be a millionaire.
Trump Castle: The Ultimate Casino Gambling Simulation

In this game, become a gambler in Donald Trump's casino-hotel "Trump Castle". The six casino games are available: BlackJack, Craps, Keno, Poker, Roulette, and Slots.

The game bet limits are set at $10,000 by default, but this can be changed. Players can also increase or decrease bets at each table. Experienced gamblers may be enlisted in High Scores Table.
Truus
Dutch language draughts board game by Stef Keetman. The game is a draughts\checkers game played on a board with 10×10 squares, alternatively dark and light
Trzech Wesolych Pielegniarzy

Trzech wesołych pielęgniarzy! is a simple bloody action game. As an ambulance driver the player must deliver wounded patient breaking by crowds of city citizens before the time runs out. To achieve the objective, the driver can drive through pedestrians and throw grenades toward the inhabitants of the blocks. Suitable destruction provides a time bonus. Reaching the hospital area ends the game.
Tsch

A single player action/navigation game. Fly through the blocks in such a way that you can get the best speed and maneuverablity. Grab the jewels, avoid the reverse unless you really need to back for a goody or to reverse from a previous reverse or bouncy. Grab the extra lives, you'll need them. Watch the solid killer blocks and the gravity blocks will pull you down. Faster increases score, but is risky. 
 
Focus on the jewels, as getting them gets you to the next level.
Tube Madness
An updated, two player version of PipeMania for the Amiga, created by Elmar Bransch of Digital Express and released in 1991.
Tube Warriors

Tube Warriors is a versus fighting game exclusive to AGA-based Amigas. It is set in a Japanese undergound network, where each station and its surrounding area are controlled by a local street gang. The player must defeat the leaders of all the rival gangs and take over their territories, working their way up to Kyosci, the "King of the tubes". Gang leaders include: Kenju, a martial artist; Mitzuko, the only female gang leader; Mako, a baseball player; Ghork, a street punk; Satoru, a sumo fighter; Ranza, a restaurant chef; and Robby, a kid controlling a robot similarly to Baby Head from Captain Commando. Initially only Kenju is selectable in single player mode, however every street thug joins the player's gang once defeated and becomes selectable from that moment on.
Tubes
A shareware Pipeworks style AMOS game created and published by Chris Hodges in 1995.
Tubular Worlds

One of the most popular game genres in the late 80' and the early 90's so a bit unusual to see this kind of game made in 1994. Tubular Worlds doesn't offer anything new and in my opinion it looks like Dongleware was a bit too late with getting this game published since they missed the general game market with a few years.

Apart from that Tubular Worlds is a well developed game offering the usual side scroller interface where the entire goal in the game is to shoot up as many enemies as possible. The more you shoot the better your spaceship gets. You can get better weapons, faster movement and other great improvements. The game consists of many different enemies and also multiple levels so there are many hours of game play.

Overall a nice side scroller but both the graphics and sound could have been better considering the age of this game. Of course this is not the most important in a game and the developers have programmed with this on their mind.
Tudor Times

An educational licenseware game created by Harry Collier and published in 1997. True history begins with the reign of Henry VIII. the civil war swept from the land, the relics of the Feudal System, and a new and better order of things arose. During the Tudor Period was seen the dawn of commerce, literature and the breaking of the yoke of the Roman Catholic church. These were times when an Englishman was proud to be called so...
Tuesday

Tuesday is a game based on a series of non-existent graphic novels. In these novels, Gavin, the hero of the story, and his band of loser friends go on many adventures, which take them from comic shops to the mall, the sewers, a dinosaur park and beyond!
Tumbler Street

Tumbler Street is a miscellaneous gambling game, developed and published by Vidball, which was released in Europe in 1989. In it, the hoodlum hides the red ball under one of the 3 tumblers, and you have to guess where it is. If you guess correctly, you get some cash, incorrectly you lose. Randomly, the police will show up, and he will take off running...with your cash. The fact that this was sold commercially is a bit too on the nose.
Tumbling Tots

A two player action game, catch the tots tumbling out of the burning building, but beware as the tots will tumble out of the life net and you may have to bounce it twice into the ambulance. To make things more interesting once one baby bounces out of the inferno they all come tumbling down, you should be able to juggle them all in the air if you are fast and crafty. A freeware PD game from David Ashley in 1988.
Tunnel Run
A freeware racing, avoid-it game created by Matthew Goode and released in 1994. This game can't be completed. Just survive as long as possible to get a high score.
Tunnel Vision
