Other hazards include ice which prevents blocks from stopping until they go past it. Falling through holes loses you one of your 3 lives - you also have 5 attempts at each screen.
X-IT-50: The Quest for the Meaning of Life

Since man was first able to reason he has pondered the question of, "what is the meaning of life?... Until now the answer has always been elusive. Using your skill and dexterity, find your way through the 50 levels and exit and all will be revealed. The base launcher is controlled by the mouse. Ammo is fired by the base launcher. Atom is fatal if touched by base. Arrow disks can be used to move your pod in the indicated directions. Ammo disks will add 5 shells to your ammo until it reaches 39 max. Time disk adds 20 seconds to limit. Guide the pod around the levels and collect keys. Shoot to move tiles in that direction. When all the keys have been collected the exit will be revealed. 

Game comes with level editor... in case you would like to edit that last level and take a look.
X-Mas Disaster

Made for Christmas Tree Competition 2009, the game was put together in two weeks. Nice graphics and music. Santa's army has decided that this was the last Christmas the brats have their way and tries to take over the world by plunging it into deep winter and taking it over when everyone is huddled near the fireplace. Take down all the Christmas creatures and fight the boss, you must shoot each armor piece to remove it.
X-masTime: The Festive Season

It is a time of Chaos. It is a time of despair. It is X-MasTime!
 
Featuring: Santa Claus as himself
 
Game released at The Party 3 in Herning, 1993. 7 levels of Christmas platform fun. Then it repeats with more difficulty. Smash the bad toys with your bag and pick up the pressies. Grab clocks to get more time
X-Men: Mind Games

Mod for Gloom for both Amiga and AmigaCD32. Both 2 player co-op mode and 2 player combat mode are also available. In each level, your objective is to find an exit before your 3 lives run out. In specific levels, you must defeat (or escape) enemy bosses.
X-Out

It is 2019. Something unbelievable has happend, for which 12 billion people have waited for a long time. The first contat with extraterrestrial life! But the aliens were not friendly and conquered the earth bit by bit. The special thing was that they did not come from space, but from the seas. They are aliens, that live in the water and came here by an artifically created Einstein-Rosen Bridge. Through this wormhole came not only the aliens, but also strange alien sea animals and they now render the coasts uncertain. Unfortunately, the world government found no experienced submarine pilot, to pit himself against the water aliens. Only a retired submarine veteran with an alcohol problem could be persuaded for this mission...
X-Sector
The disk is damaged. Can you recover it? X-Sector is a new puzzle game for the Amiga.
X-Swap: Booming Edition

Unusual 'Jewel' type of game—drag two or three in a row to take them off the board. Problem is taking them off the board leaves a ‘hole’, putting you in a ‘corner’ so you can’t move other pieces. X-Swap Booming Edition is a Puzzle game, developed and published by Black Fantasy, which was released in Europe in 1997.
X-Vaders
It's a Space Invaders clone, The game is completely free, I used AI, this is version 1.0, I could improve it furthermore in the future.
Xap

Released as a game demo in 1993 on Amiga Format 54, this crosshairs shooter you guide the purple sphere-craft around the level, using the crosshairs to shoot multi-directionally. Avoid contact with the other creatures but rescue the fluffies and items and avoid mines. Alien Flux combines totally original gameplay, modern pseudo-3D graphics and unique sound effects to create a fast and furious shoot-em up style arcade game, the aim of which is to rescue Fluffies (the cutest creatures in the universe), from invading forces from the fifth dimension.
Xenex
Xenex is an action game, developed and published by Scorpius, which was released in Europe in 1994.
Xenomorph

You have landed your crippled ship at the Atargis mining station. The platform was deserted and no one answered your radio calls. Now you are forced to enter the station and find a way to get off the asteroid. Hopefully whatever happened to the 200 personnel in the labyrinth of mines under the station won't happen to you too.

Xenomorph is a first person RPG. Like in the Dungeon Master series, everything happens in real time. You move around in 10 footsteps and can turn 90 degrees. You have two hands to fight and use items with, a belt and holster for quick access to weapons, as well as an inventory for carrying things.

The objective of the game is to find parts to repair your ship. You must also find food and water for sustenance and guns, grenades and mines for self defense. Other items can help you during your mission such as environmental suits, security passes and a motion detector. Data disks found throughout the station will fill in the story.
Xenomorph (juande3050)

XENOMORPH is heavily inspired by ALIEN BREED, although a darker, more tense setting was sought.
The goal was to slow down the gameplay by being more careful when confronting the Aliens.
Xenomorphs 2

In this sequel to Xenomorph written by Aidan Boustred of Culture you must defeat the aliens. While the original was considered an RPG, this top down view game has a realtime wargame feel to it. It has 4 levels and supports one or two players and cooperative play. In this one you control the space marines who must secure the base from the alien threat.
Xenon

In this game the player assumes the role of a space pilot named Darrian. One day, he receives a report from a nebula space station, from which he learns that nearby human colonies have been attacked by mysterious aliens known as Xenites. Darrian wastes no time, and sets off to protect the humans and stop the aliens.

Xenon is an overhead shooter, in which the player controls a vehicle that is able to transform into a tank or a plane. The transformation can be usually performed by player at any time, to combat particular enemies; however, during some sequences the player is forced to use a specific type of vehicle. During the tank gameplay, the player controls the movement of the playfield (up or down) by simply moving the tank in the direction of choice.
Xenon 2: Megablast

No-one likes a bad loser. And no-one comes more universally despised than the Xenites. For a thousand years they have been plotting revenge for their humiliating defeat in the last Galactic Conflict. Now the very fabric of time is in danger... The Xenites have planted five Time Bombs through history. Only you can save the day - not to mention the Universe. The last time you met it was a playground scrap. This time it's war.
Xenon III
A virtually scrolling space shooter created with SEUCK, developed by Harry Hart, and is an UNOFFICIAL fan sequel to Xenon II.
Xenopew
A horizontal shoot-em-up made in Backbone by Lemming880 of the Netherlands in 2015. Shoot your way through a hazard filled maze and make it to the exit!
Xenophobe

Xenos. The very name strikes fear into every colonist's heart. A distress call is received from space stations orbiting your homeworld, then silence. A single ship escapes, piloted by a battered man who tells the tale of pods that hatch into acid-spitting Xenos. A small band of engineers has been dispatched to combat the Xeno threat before it takes over all the space stations and, eventually, your homeworld.

Xenophobe is a side-scrolling shooter with platform elements. Assemble your band of engineers and fight the Xenos on each station, striving to either clear it or abandon it. You start out with a standard issue laser, but can pick up additional weapons as you find them, including Phasers, Lightning Rifles, Poofer guns, and bombs.
Xenos Layer
A single player crosshairs shooter made by Furio Catalano and published as a Coverdisk in Amiga Live. In the twenty first century only a real man or woman can save the earth... YOU!
Xenostar

Xenostar is a multi-directional shoot 'em up modeled after the Sinistar (1982). While you guide your modest but frantic spacecraft around and try to mine minerals, red constructor ships are also busy mining them, protected by grey defense ships. With the minerals, they will try to construct Xenostar, an incredibly evil and hungry entity. Converting the minerals you collect into Xenobombs, you stand a chance of destroying this monster once he announces... "I live!''
Xevious1200

This is a transcode from the original arcade game (multiple Z80s) to 68K assembly.

FEATURES:

- game play is identical to the original arcade game, including the pseudo-random number generation

- original dipswitch options supported (except cocktail cabinet mode)

- all original graphics and colours reproduced perfectly on Neo Geo target

- 1 or 2 players supported

- high score load/save

CREDITS:

- Mark McDougall (aka tcdev): reverse-engineering, core and Neo Geo code and assets

- Jean-Francois Fabre (aka jotd): Amiga code and assets

- Andrzej Dobrowolski (aka no9): Amiga music

- Namco: original game :)
XFI

A freeware Worm\Snake game by Tony Cheetham, released in 1991. This action game featured 5 speeds of difficulty. To win you had to cause your enemy to crash or touch a warp gate (shown as a sphere on the playing field).
Xhyperoid

An AmigaOS4 port from the Windows 3.1 original game. Hyperoid was a really cool little game for Windows 3.x. It's essentially an Asteroids clone, but with a few extra features. There are three reasons I ported it as XHyperoid:

 - the decent game physics and enhancements over the original game
 make it probably my favorite Asteroids variant;

 - it's always sucked having to run it under Windows (admittedly, you
 can run the original under Wine, but it's less than ideal);

 - it's the first GPL'd program I ever saw, which gives it a certain
 special something for me. :-)

One of the first things I did on porting it was to add sound, so
that's another plus. :-)
Xiphos

As usual, a computer has been put in control of vast stretches of an intergalactic empire. As usual, it has failed and locked the entire area into limbo. As usual, you're the one who has to sort this mess out, by reaching the computer and destroying it.

Unfortunately, the area en route to it is vast and treacherous, with lots of obstacles to shoot out, and you will need to trade your items in order to get enough fuel to get there.

The gameplay resembles Elite, involving first-person space shooting and trading.
Xmas Lemmings (1991)

The first Christmas version of Lemmings for the Amiga. Contains two unique levels from "Oh no, More Lemmings" and two new Christmas levels. An Oh No! More Lemmings Christmas themed demo. Special Christmas music by Andy Whyte. Released as a cover disk.
Xmas Lemmings (1992)

The 1992 edition of Xmas Lemmings is another free demo intended to promote Lemmings and Oh No! More Lemmings. It includes four entirely new Christmas-themed levels, in the same style as the 1991 demo: Jingle Bells and other Christmas songs as background music and the Lemmings moving through snowscapes dressed in Santa outfits. The holiday levels from the earlier demo were comparatively easy, but this one also includes some brain teasers comparable to levels from the main games' higher difficulties. 
 
Lemmings and Oh No! More Lemmings Christmas themed demo. Contains four unique levels designed by Mark Tsai. Special Christmas music by Andy Whyte and Tobias (Toby) van de Peer.
Xmas Syman

Syman is a simple and fun memory game for all the family, playable by up to four people simultaneously. Syman is based on the original MB 'Simon' game, with inspiration drawn from the American Dad tv series, and is produced by a small team here at Ultimate Amiga. Simply watch the coloured tones played by Syman, and play them back.

The game was started from scratch on 12/12/09 with the goal of being finished in time for the Underground Arcade Christmas Competition which closed on Christmas Eve 2009.
Xmas World of Tetris

A one or two player, Christmas themed, Tetris clone by Jani Parviainen of Overdose, because when you think of Christmas you should think of Overdose. Clearing lines reveals a seasonal picture, but you will need to be good to see the whole thing.
Xorron 2001
Xorron 2001 is an 2D platform game, developed by Digital Dreams and published by Starbyte, which was released in 1989.
XP8

XP8 is a vertically scrolling shoot-'em-up featuring raytraced graphics with many reflections.

Eight different weapons are on offer, which can be powered up to several stages, and are collected from tokens, sometimes in hidden sections. A simultaneous two-player mode is offered, which makes getting through the five levels (with passwords for each one) a little easier. The introduction takes the form of a few static screens.
Xpedition

Xpedition is a side-scrolling science fiction action shooter. The game allows you to assemble a team of four members, including marines and mechs, assign equipment and select one of a few available extended missions. The player can control only one team member at a time. Aside of killing every hostile creature the game requires you to complete small side quests, such as repairing a broken mechanism or capture an alien.
Xploit

X-ploit is 2D side-scrolling action game with action set in future - mankind successfully defended against alien emperor, but people were turned into strange creatures. The player controls a green ball with feet, eyes and nose, named Spunky, who wants to destroy alien emperor. The game has simple rules - Spunky goes straightforward, jumps over holes and other obstacles, and collect various bonuses. He can shoot to destroy enemies and obstacles - but he has limited ammo. Spunky has small helicopter to fly, but fuel is also limited. Like in first Super Mario Bros. he can't go back (left).
XR35
XR-35 Fighter Mission is a horizontally scrolling shooter, developed and published by Anco Software, which was released in Europe in 1988.
XTreme Racing

XTreme Racing is a racing game that utilizes real 3D environments, as opposed to the sprite-based Lotus and the unshaded polygons of World Circuit. The game features a wide environment with full freedom of movement and some Mode 7-style effects. Various pre-made characters can be chosen to represent the player. A course designer and a sound editor are included as well. 

The difficulty level is customizable, and the cars don't "cheat" in terms of artificially keeping up with the player-controlled vehicle or pushing it out of the way and continuing at unabated speed. There many weapons on track to be picked up and fired at will, to deal with the opponents in a more unorthodox way.

Multiplayer options allow up to eight human players to compete, achieved linking two systems, similarly to Super Skidmarks.
Xybots

Xybots is a sci-fi shooter with pseudo-3D environments explored from a third-person perspective. The game can be played by one or two players; the two-player mode takes place on a split screen. The hero(es) must move through a series of Gauntlet-style underground mazes, killing the bad guys and collecting health and other bonuses from flying saucers. It's designed to be played co-operatively, although bullets from one player can harm the other.

The Xybots are out to stop the protagonists, and many have advanced attack patterns as well as bullets to fire at them. Being able to view round corners is useful, allowing the player to plan a strategy - often it's good to send one player forward and let the other play the waiting game, similarly to the tactics often employed in Gauntlet.
Xytronic

A game by Andreas Uhl under the name Silicon Generation and published initially in 1989 and then later in the Amiga Supergame issue #4, published by Logo Software in 1990 along with Colwyns Abenteuer, Raumstation, and Super Gridder.
Xzap
Original Game by Mark Wirt, released by Commodore Business Machines (UK) Ltd. in 1984 for Commodore 16 and Plus/4.
YachtC
YachtC is a public domain game based around the board game "Yahtzee". Better known as “Yahtzee” dice game for social hours created by Sheldon Leemon.
Yachtc Plus
A remake of the board game Yahtzee by DCAT and released in 1996. Also offers Craggy and Mogul games on the same disk.
Yachting

This is a game written in AMOS 3-D. It is the first game of its kind that I have seen anywhere. You are sailing a yacht in a race around a bay, navigating around marker buoys and trying to beat your opponents. This game has atmosphere! The display moves up and down just like the
real thing with all the appropriate creaks etc you'd expect to hear when sailing. Good fun.
Yactris
A basic freeware workbench Tetris homage from Jonathan Springer in 1993. It uses the number keypad and has no sound.
YAGG: Yet Another Gravity Game

YAGG is a shooter gravity game like Roketz and Bratwurst. 2, 3 or 4 player must destroy their opponents ASAP. Chose your ship and armaments and launch. Your ship and bullets will be impacted by the set gravity.
Yahzee!
A one to four player board game, this version created and released as Shareware by David Junod in 1988.
Yamina Perdue dans le Desert

YAMINA LOST IN THE DESERT. An idea from Christiane Walther, This software is SHAREWARE and If your children like it PLEASE send me 20 Frs
in the form that will be most convenient for you. This will help you prepare new programs. To avoid the Game Overview press CTRL and the D key and type: YAMINA. 

In this rare flying carpet vertically scrolling shooter you grab the fruits, flowers and water and blast the baddies across the desert. Grab coins and fruits in the entryway of the all seeing eye and blat the ghosts and ghoulies without touching the walls in the tombs. Avoid the night flyers in the court of the owls, blast the snakes, battle tortoises and other foes as you make your way across the land eventually making your way to the sultan's palace and sweet success.
Yars' Revenge Remaster

This is a remaster of the Atari 2600 classic for the Amiga. Yar, Qotile, the Swirl, the shield and the score digits all come straight from the original 2600 ROM, redrawn at double size with shading and a fuller colour palette. The Neutral Zone is built from the 2600 program’s own code bytes, the same way the original drew it. Copper rainbow effects run behind the playfield, and the sound uses the Amiga’s sound chip (Paula), including the flight hum that rises inside the Neutral Zone.
Yatcy
A freeware interpretation of the Yahtzee board game by Gary Henderson made in AMOS and released as freeware in 1994.
YAWoFFA

Name stands for "Yet Another Wheel of Fortune for Amiga". This version supports up to 4 players and was made by Zoopersoft Games and released in 2021 on AmigaLive. This is an Amigalive original and it's a fun one too for the whole family!

YAWoFFA is a small word puzzle for Commodore Amiga which is played much the same way as other Wheel of Fortune games. Spin wheel, choose letters and solve words/sentences.

You can also make your own puzzles. Just fill a textfile with questions and compress it with the pack program included on the disk. You can play your own puzzle by typing: yawoffa yourpuzzle.pak

Read the included readme text for more information.

Note: If you create a puzzle file you can send it to me and I can include it on the disk. Play as a single player or hot seat for up to 4 players. 8 puzzle categories. Easily make your own puzzles. Text-to-speech narration as well!
Yeet

In Nornheim, conflicts are not settled by sword or shield, but by the game of runes. Only a true Runemaster can guide and protect the people - and to earn that title, you must walk the path of the Rune Trial.
Yelp

A superb Amidar clone published in both ST Amiga Format #9 (superdisk 9), Mar 1989 and in Magazine The One #44 (coverdisk A), May 1992. Run over the borders of each shape to color them in in order to complete the level, while avoiding enemies.
Yerop
A platforming game written in Blitz BASIC by Kris Beaumont and published as an Amiga Format coverdisk.
Yeti

A Donkey Kong clone with a Christmas theme written by Marc Le Douarain and published in early January of 1993. Instead of barrels, the Yeti throws snowballs. Instead of fire, you get chased by mountain goats. Not so easy as it looks...
YF-22
A vertically scrolling shooter from Poland. It was developed and published via mail order only by Manhattan Soft in 1995.
Yo 2
A PD game created by Damien O'Donnell in Blitz BASIC 2 in 1997 where you guide the dot around the squares and home.
Yo! Joe! Beat the Ghosts

Yo! Joe! Beat the Ghosts is a platform game featuring two characters. The protagonists can jump, crawl, kick, beat, slide, and swim. They are even able to hold their breath when under water. If you are playing the game solely, "Joe" is your character of choice. A friend can take on Nat's part at the same PC.
Yoghurt Boy and Twit Man

An AMOS freeware text adventure game created by Jonjo Roberts and Peter Galey in 1991. It was part of the Yoghurt Boy & Defence two game pack in 1991. It all started at St Theresa’s primary school. For packed lunch I always used to bring a yoghurt and my friend Jonjo always brought a Twix. We
invented a game called Yoghurt Boy and Twit Man - two bungling heroes who would save the day, and then when the bell went change back into ordinary mild mannered school boys and go inside to do some French.

Now we're at high school together and have started acting more normal. But when danger strikes we are ready to become said heroes again...
Yogi Bear & Friends in the Greed Monster: A Treasure Hunt

All the toys in the World have been stolen by the Greed Monster, so Top Cat has sent Yogi's Treasure Hunters to find them all. Problem is, all the hunters have been captured by the monster except Yogi, so it's up to Yogi to find his friends and all the toys. The game is a flick-screen maze game viewed from a high elevated angle as you control Yogi. 

You have to search the surrounding areas looking for your friends and toys while avoiding or shooting various creatures. You are armed with sweets to shoot the creatures but these are limited. If you are touched by a creature or certain obstacles then you lose part of a food gauge and when this is empty then it is game over. As well as the toys and your friends, there are other items that can be collected and they are coloured keys to open the same coloured door, cans of pop to double your speed, extra sweets and jars of honey to make you invincible for a limited period.
Yogi's Big Clean Up

This licensed game sees Yogi Bear doing something constructive. Across five levels, he must locate or repair eight key items. After clearing Jellystone Park of litter, he must go underwater to fix its water supply. He must then explore a swamp to fix Ranger Smith's bike, find misplaced objects in a film studio, and finally reassemble the bed within his cave.

This takes place over platform-style levels, with lots of enemies to be avoided or shot, plus moving platforms and falls. He is armed with a bubble weapon, which is not required on the final level. Collecting pic-a-nic baskets will recharge Yogi's energy.
Yogi's Great Escape

Yogi Bear has woken from his hibernation and is now searching his home, Jellystone Park for Picnic Baskets brought by tourists. On one search, Yogi over hears an awful telephone conversation with Ranger Smith that the Park is closing and all animals must be caught and transferred to a zoo. Not wanting to live in a cage or enclosure, Yogi has decided to escape and thus the beginning of his adventure. You have to guide Yogi over six levels (ending in New York) keeping ahead of a tracker and his dog. You must complete each level in 2 minutes 40 seconds or it is game over. On the way there are obstacles like holes and water, as well as other characters to get in your way. Touching these loses one of three lives. Scattered over the levels are various food items which will give you 100 points as well as invisible ones giving 250 points. If you want a bigger score then on certain levels you can collect six items which reward you with 7500 points.
Yolanda: The Ultimate Challenge

The 16-bit box calls this ‘The Ultimate Challenge’ and they’re not kidding; this flick-screen platform game is one of the toughest you’ll come across. In the 8-bit versions Hercules has some titanic tasks to complete, whilst in the 16-bit versions his daughter Yolanda has been cursed and can only free herself by completing the same tasks.

Unusually, the game’s dozens of screens are given in a random order, with a different one after you lose each life. You have no weapon with which to harm the various creatures that lurk within. The pace of the enemies is quite hectic, but the real unique feature is that you must keep moving – each platform is set on fire a few seconds after you first touch it.
Yoomp!

Remake of the original Atari 8-bit version (The music is however a remix of the C64 version's music):. Like a combination of Trailblazer and an often-seen demoscene effect, you fall down a tube, landing on each square progressively in a rhythmic manner. Landing on certain tiles will have certain effects, such as making the screen quake, decreasing the brightness or forcing you to jump. Navigating the tube itself is a matter of planning ahead and compensating for your limited movement capabilities. 
 
the game would later be reworked and released under the name Jump.
York Powerbox

BE A POWERBOX SIGNALMAN!
Full Colour on Screen: Track Diagrams
Power Box simulations put you in the hot seat of a modern computerised signalling control centre. You set all of the routes for trains as they approach your area and are responsible for making sure that everything runs smoothly You have a colour on screen track diagram featuring coloured track circuits and moving train describers-just like in real life! All simulations contain an interesting variety of workings and traction All data is based on BR information to ensure realism and accuracy.
YORK POWER BOX
A very busy and challenging simulation. Featuring plenty of freight traffic on the avoiding lines as well as InterCity and Regional trains. A real bottleneck south of the station where trains have to be juggled between the fast and slow lines to keep everything running to time
You & Me: Lernen Deutsch

You & Me: Język niemiecki - Lekcja 1 (słówka) is a German language educational program, consisting simple six mini games. The first one requires saying the word in the picture. The second one includes matching the word to the image. The third one is all about proper signing the picture. The fourth one, it's a crossword puzzle. The fifth one requires you to guess the hidden picture. The last one - understanding of the spoken word.
Young Defender
Young Defender is a vertical shooting game developed by Eclipse Software and published by Eclipse Entertainment for the Amiga
YTZ: Professional
A Yahtzee style board game created by Jason Phelps and published as Shareware in 1997.
Yum Yum
A freeware Pac-Man clone created in AMOS BASIC created by M. Furnell in 1992. This is a playable game of Pac-Man for kids of all ages.
Yuppi's Revenge

In Yuppi's Revenge the player is assuming the position of a Harvard graduate, suddenly faced with typical managerial problems concerning the leadership of a multinational oil company. The goal is to earn as many monetary rewards and decorations as possible. Drilling for oil, dealing with oil tankers, or trading shares are just a few of the available chances. However, status in society also plays a significant role.

Up to four players can compete with each other. Even certain unfair practices can be conducted in order to prevail over the opponents.
Z-Out

Like its predecessor X-Out, Z-Out is a side-scrolling shoot 'em up. A horde of largely-organic enemies threaten the safety of your planet, and they must be destroyed over the course of six levels.There are power-ups available, but the game is less centered around these than some are. 

Whilst some shoot 'em ups are much easier with a second player, Z-Out takes design steps to legislate against this. In a 2-player game, most power-ups are unavailable, and even those which are only come into effect on level 3. Another variation is that the 1-player mode uses restart points, but the 2-player mode does not, so as to keep both players in the same place.
Zabawa: Grajek & Malarz

Zabawa: Grajek & Malarz is a commercial Polish title created by Jacek Korotkiewicz that allows children to develop painting and musical skills. There are two different modes available: painting and musical keyboard. The first one consists of simple painting features, the second one allows to play simple melodies.
Zack!
A type of Tetris inspired game where instead of different shapes you have to place sets of different hats and headware (kind of like Harris) two at a time.
Zak McKracken and the Alien Mindbenders

Zak McKracken is a tabloid reporter (and not a very good one at that). After having a psychedelic dream one day, Zak realizes that something is wrong -- space aliens are dumbifying the general public through the telephone system. Zak must stop this, but he can't do it alone. After finding a strange crystal, Zak manages to get the help of the anthropologist Annie and her friends, Melissa and Leslie. The four unlikely heroes must now figure out a way to destroy the dumbifying devices and save the Earth.

Zak McKracken and the Alien Mindbenders is a third-person puzzle-solving adventure similar in gameplay to Maniac Mansion. The player chooses verb commands (Open, Pick Up, Give, etc.; there are no Look or Talk commands) to interact with the game world. The game features up to four controllable protagonists; it is possible to switch between them at any time after they have been introduced, and also exchange inventory items if the characters are in the same location.
Zaklęta Wyspa

Zaklęta Wyspa is a puzzle-solving game with elements of adventure story. The game begins with the kidnapping of Princess Andora by the evil sorcerer. Mendor unleashed an army of demons to conquer villages in the kingdom of Aldeoria. Now, each of thirty villages, is possessed by a demon. The daemon can be defeated only by solving a logical mini task. The game allows to select training and adventure mode. Training mode features all the thirty tasks with unlimited access. The adventure mode is played on the kingdom map, where the player moves from one village to another using the roads. Accessing new villages requires passing the trial in current village. Succeeded trial unlocks the road and allows to choose one of available direction. The puzzles are based on logic, chess, mathematics rules or a well known board games, such as master mind, domino or ships.
Zalycon

This is a nice shoot 'em up which has been programmed by the scener group Fanatix in 1992. The composers have done very good work. The game is set in the year 2176 on a long range colony called Zalycon, with a moonbase on a nearby moon, which is shortly thereafter attacked by aliens. You are the closest ship with a hyperspace angine, no one else will get there in time. The fate of the colony is in your hands. 
 
The first stage of the game is an avoid it type game, where you avoid the meteor shower to get there in time. Level 2 is moon buggy style mayhem to get to the armory. There is a puzzle required for access. Then you have a maze of Wolfenstein-like corridors to go through, when you find the aliens in it, the game becomes a cross-hairs shooter. If you survive, you find your way to the lab. There you confront the alien boss.
ZapTris

ZapTris - Version 1.26 - Shareware (Amiga)
Exellent tetris-clone! - Much of special
things - Also normal Tetris-mode - Very
flexible (much of settings) - 80 levels -
Link- and demogames - You can play your own
background-musics - Three Top 10-lists &
much more
Zarathrusta

Zarathrusta is a cave-flying game influenced by Thrust. Apparently, the resistance forces have captured a number of space ships, which could aid in the struggle against the empire. However, these ships need fuel, and that fuel is find in the form of "klystron pods", which must be recovered from a range of hostile environments. 

Your task is to fly your small spaceship above and below ground, capturing the pods. Your spaceship can rotate in 360 degrees, allowing for easy movements through the cave systems, if it wasn't for gravity pulling you down, and inertia, which means you could crash into walls or other objects if you don't turn around and thrust in the other direction. 

Each level is cleared by recovering the klystron pods, which are the same thing as the ball you pick up in Thrust. Pick up the pod with your tractor beam, and a towing line will be attached.
Zarcan

A puzzler created in by Hungarian coders Laszlo Körber, gfx Edvard Juhász and music by Peter Tolnai in 1993 and released on several compilations including Hungary For Fun, Three for Hungary and as part of the Amiga Forever Game Pack I.
Zardoz

Great logical puzzler with awesome soundtrack (both in game and ending tune), created by Alive Designs and published in 1992. Recreate the picture in the top left corner in the game following the rules of piece movement on the level.
Zargon

A vertical shooting game for one or two players including cooperative play, created by Jürgen Malzacher\Juergen Malzacher and Stephan Brack and released in 1989, the game has no end. Game is included on Amiga Software Extra Issue 12, Disk 2.
Zaxxon

The Zaxxon defence system must be destroyed in this isometric-viewed shoot 'em up. The game has three stages, first taking you through Asteroid City, which is heavily protected by aircraft, guns and missiles. Many barriers are alarmed, leaving you with limited space to progress through, and fire must constantly be dodged.

Stage two is a space shoot out against hordes of enemy aircraft - those you failed to destroy in the first part of the task. Complete this and you reach the final battle with Zaxxon, the game looping with increased difficulty if you can survive the first time. There are three distinct skill levels, while controls involve using forward to dive and back to climb, in the manner
Zdrajca

Zdrajca is a black and white adventure game with digitized speech and video sequences. One day a holder of the Amiga learns about the new Playstation console. He decided to sell his computer to buy a dream gaming hardware. On the day of sale computer has been damaged and needs to be repaired within designated time.

The game screen is divided into action menu, inventory, destination places (with map as alternative travel possibility), conversation panel and picture/video box. Conversation allows to choose one of three available sentences, resulting in displaying the appropriate video sequences. The main task requires finding appropriate objects, performing mini-quest and connecting suitable objects.
Zdzislav Hero of the Galaxy 3D

A target with reticle, crosshairs 2D shooter using Amiga's enhanced HAM mode graphics. Gameplay is in the style of Operation Wolf with first person horizontally scrolling action created by Tomasz Rogacewicz (STO) and Rolpho (D6) of Deck Six and released as freeware in 1997.
Zdzisław

Zdzisław: Bohater Galaktyki is a sci-fi action adventure game with vector graphics. On the 4th of July an alien spacecraft stunned Zdzisław and kidnapped his girlfriend. In order to save her the player must fly through the galaxy, find and use useful items in proper places and sometimes prove his agility skills. The spacecraft has a limited number of fuel, replenished only on the Earth. Maneuvering off and landing requires great caution, too rapid flight may cause ship explosion - one of many ways of death. Death in the game means necessity to start all over again. Each planet is divided into a few single location with at least one occasion to die and one item to acquire.
Zebra 3

My entry for Blitzbasic Game Jam 2022.
A top down racer, with only 4 tracks.
Practice is advised before entering the race.
Avoid collision with the background and other cars
You can disable collisions with cpu cars, it will be easier.
Zeewolf

With a similar gameplay as the isometric Desert Strike, Zeewolf offers arcadesque helicopter combat in a 3D surrounding. Despite its mainly action-oriented gameplay, the 32 levels often involve support, transport and rescue missions - dropping or refueling friendly units in the combat zone, for example. In exchange, other units serve you as rearming points or help you fighting the enemy.
Zeewolf 2: Wild Justice

Binary Asylum's final release puts you in control of a helicopter and sets you 32 missions to complete. The level structures involve different military objectives of protecting or destroying a particular area. The surprise is in the graphics: patchwork-quilt style landscapes and a remote view reminiscent of Virus. The game offers joystick and mouse control options, as well as sections in which you must direct ships and planes. A range of weapons are offered with resupply ships on the water to dock with.
Zelda
A Zelda type RPG playable demo according to the author, Anthony Sherratt of ASP Software in 1996.
Zenek Saper

Zenek Saper is an adaptation of classic Minesweeper game for up to two players. The rules remain unchanged. The player needs to find all the mines as quickly as possible. Clicking on a field shows a number indicating how many mines are located in the fields nearest to it. One mistake results in a mine explosion and the end of the game. The game features three difficulty levels with 10, 15 and 20 mines on a 10x10 grid board. In two player mode each player makes a movement alternately. Winning is possible in two ways - through the discovery of the last mine or a deadly mistake made by the opponent.
Zeppelin: Giants of the Sky

Zeppelins were the sky's biggest aircrafts ever. So - have you ever thought about managing a fleet of them? In Zeppelin this is just your job. Invest in new technologies, build airships for several nations, find new flight routes and win the race with competing companies.

You can participate in flying competitions, take on special missions (such as time critical assignments), speculate at the stock-market, etc. The game also contains precise historical material; political and economical developments strongly influence the storyline.
Zerberk

Zerberk is a clone of the Stern arcade classic "Berzerk" for the Commodore Amiga. It was developed by Mathias Bock (aka Starfox) and released into the public domain in 1993. The game places you in a top-down maze environment, where your object is to kill all the robots on each level before you progress to the edge of the screen to begin the next level

The walls are electrified and will kill you on touch, Robots can also kill you if touched, or they shoot at you

There is a time limit on each level, when it is reached, Evil Otto appears, a smiley face character, who will follow you around the map, including through walls, until you either die, or get to the next level

You advance by clearing off all the Robots, and moving to one of the exits of the maze on screen, which will then increase the level number, and you then repeat, by clearing all the Robots and again advancing

There are Question Marks (?) which will randomly spawn, These can be fired at to give various special effects

Zerg

An early Amiga PD Role Playing Game, created by Mike Shapiro. It is a Sword and Sorcery, topdown, Ultima style RPG. Released in 1989 for Amiga on Fish Disk 252; new version released in 1990. The title is as bare-bones as you can get, with basic inventory and basic character development. Its primary virtue is brevity plus a certain wit. It is also a rare Ultima clone for the Amiga. (It displays a roughly-Ultima II technology level, minus the dungeons, with a quest system that goes back to Akalabeth.) 
 
The game takes place in the land of Zerg, which is having problems with monsters. Each player controls the same character, named "Wanderer," who starts out as a Level 1 fighter with 75 strength, 75 wisdom, 75 agility, and 50 hit points. The game begins next to a king's castle, where the king is looking for a hero to slay monsters and bring back their cadavers. The king will use these trophies "to help investors feel more secure."

Zero Gravity

At its most basic level, Zero Gravity can be thought of as a Pong game, as the player controls a bat which must be used to hit a ball as it comes towards you. The main twist is that the gameplay is completely 3-dimensional, with control over the horizontal and vertical positions of the bat. The game uses a split-screen view, with the top half viewed from the perspective of Player 1, and the bottom from that of Player 2, even when only one of them is human.

Each time you get the ball past your opponent's bat, a score is added to a tally, and a number of points are awarded. Along the side-wall of the playing arena there are 8 tokens to be hit, awarding extra points, speeding the game up, deducting points from your opponent, and so on.
Zero Gravity (PD)
A racing\reaction & navigation game where you fly your ship and avoid the blocking walls to get to the end of the track in the fastest possible time.
Zeron
A very well done defender clone, shoot the aliens, save the humans when things get crazy use the smart bombs.
Zerosphere

Our hero Squinty has been trapped by his arch ­nemesis Odak. On his way to freedom, Squinty will find himself in Odak’s laboratory complex, on the surface, and in clammy dungeons. He will not only have to collect all gems in every corner, but also avoid falling into the ocean, getting eaten by piranhas, disappearing into the void, getting stung by poisonous spiders, and burning himself with hot lava.

However, there is one special catch: Odak has used his latest invention, the »Dimensional Transformer« on Squinty—now, everything around him appears distorted and looks vertically stretched. Only if Squinty squints real hard, he can see the world around him normally for a short period of time.
Zeus: The Game

A single player puzzle\shape matching game in the style of Puzznic. Coding & graphics by Crazy/Zeus; levels by Sledge/Zeus. Music by Richard Holmes (Snake/Zeus). The original release of ZEUS: THE GAME contains a bug on level 32 involving a block that cannot be paired, which makes it impossible to proceed beyond this level to complete the game. Fortunately, a bugfixed version was released on EAB in 2017. Also released in the Spielekiste #617 PD compilation disk.
Zgadula

Zgadula is a Polish language game loosely based on the popular American TV game show, Wheel of Fortune for the Commodore Amiga. The players take turns guessing the consonants or buying the vowels to form a word or a saying. The game allows up to three human or computer players for on up to nine rounds. Each turn begins with the wheel spin, determining a win prize for the consonant or ending up with bankruptcy or loss of the turn. After the last round, a winner is the player with the largest amount of money.
ZGR3D

ZGR3D is an Amiga adaption of the DOS game Kret for the Amiga. The aim of the player is to destroy Tetris-like blocks that fall down from the top of the screen. With each move the whole line of blocks drops down one line unless it cannot go further because the composition of the game field does not allow it. The player needs to move carefully through the field destroying the blocks without being squashed.
Zillo

An action game where you can set the color of the ball by hitting the palette on the left, once the ball color is set you can remove blocks of the same color, unfortunately you will die if you hit a skull and crossbones of the same color. Avoid the same color crossbones and remove all the blocks to move to the next level. Just to make things more interesting, there's a time limit!
Zippy Race
This is a conversion of Zippy Race - an early 1983 arcade game by Irem to the OCS Amiga.
Ziriax

Ziriax is a side-scrolling futuristic "shoot-'em-up" set in a futuristic environment, similar to R-Type. The player controls a spaceship-like aircraft that is trying to survive amidst the fire of hostile ships and other enemies. There are five stages in the game altogether; each contains a fight against a boss enemy at the end. Small spheres are dropped by enemies; collecting these spheres bestows the player-controlled ship with various power-ups. These include two additional small ships above and below the main one, an ability to shoot backwards, and missiles that can be shot diagonally.
Zitrax

A freewae horizontally scrolling shooter created by Dimmen Produkties in 1988. This shooter is different because just like in reality, you only have one life so you had better guard it well. It was released in both International Arcade Action and the Amiga Stars Collection. 
 
Fast and furious arcade action. Dare you enter into space, if you do there are waves of aliens, doing everything in their power to stop you. For those with fast reaction and shoot-em up skills.... take the challenge.
Zmer Si Sve IQ
A Czech language AMOS based intelligence test created by Striped Dog and released as freeware in 1994.
ZNYK

ZNYK is, according to its documentation, yet another Tetris lookalike, but could just as well be based on Puyo Puyo, Pick 'n Pile or Columns.

From above, pairs of coloured balls come falling. The pairs can be swapped and rotated so as to match those balls already on the bottom of the screen. By making horizontal or vertical groups of four balls of the same colour, those groups are eliminated. The goal of each screen is to eliminate those balls present at the beginning of the stage, indicated by a white outline. The game then progresses to the next screen.

ZNYK is written in a mix of C and assembler, supports joystick or keyboard control and has a colourful, slick presentation with music, but is still multitasking-friendly. The source is (was) available for a small fee.
Zock Out
A gambling five-card poker style game gambling created by Digital Marketing and released in Amiga Fun in 1990.
Zodes

The game was originally available as a game demo on the file site Aminet and is classed as a 3D Voxel space shooter in a first person view point, now updated with more content from the original creator Ralf Schmidt.

The game only supports AGA based Amigas.
Zombi

In Zombi you control a team of four intrepid travelers, who have landed their helicopter on the roof of a shopping centre in the hope of finding fuel. The problem is that, with Hell full, Zombies are walking the earth, devouring humans as they please.

Zombi is a point and click adventure game in which you control the four characters (Alexandre, Sylvie, Yannick and Patrick) in turn, taking each of them individually through the abandoned complex. Lots of potentially-useful items have been left behind, some stored in cupboards - work out what they could be used for. 

Try to find a weapon with which to attack the zombies - bare-hands fighting only works for a few attempts before your character is worn out. Dead zombies should be placed in the freezer in the basement to stop them re-emerging. You have free rein over the shopping mall, and can use the bed shops to rest and the food shops for nourishment. Be wary of the dark and zombie-filled basement though.
Zombie

Zombie is a platform game. Trapped inside the pyramid, Czaka must find the way out. The task requires locating all the passes to the closed gates and a battery to activate the teleporter to the next level. The mission is complicated by the different mechanisms and creatures inhabiting pyramid. Contact with them means a loss of energy, which may be supplemented thanks to special flasks and life adding hearts.
Zombie Apocalypse

Zombie Apocalypse is a mouse controlled shoot-em-up where the goal is to kill as many zombies possible before you run out of energy. In every level you have to kill a certain number of zombies to be victorious. Some zombies that appears will throw hand grenades at you. Left mouse button is for normal fire and the right one is for throwing grenades. Ammo is limited but boxes with extra ammo will drop from the sky now and then (red boxes for bullets and green ones for grenades).
Zombie Apocalypse II

Zombie Apocalypse II is a mouse controlled shoot-em-up where the goal is to kill as many zombies possible before they reach the screen edge and zombie assistants before they perform the shot. At every level the player has to kill a certain number of zombies. The left mouse button is used for pistol fire and the right one for throwing the grenades. Ammo and grenades are limited, extra supplies are falling from the sky from time to time and are collected by shooting them down.
Zombie Mall

A strategy game that appears to be based on the movie, Dawn of Dead. It is a turn-based strategy game where you have to seal off the mall and kill off all of the zombies without losing any of your party members.
- Zombies in a mall
- Turn-based squad shooter
- laser squad style gameplay, more like Act of War (shareware)
- 2D top down view
- mouse controlled
- simplistic tile graphics
- can break into shops for supplies, i.e. ammo/guns
- can shoot out windows
- small footprint game, possibly only a single executable
Zombies

Alien Breed style game with a horror theme. You've been invited to a rave in an old mansion, but decide to join the fun. When you get there you find yourself trapped and the place is full of zombies, luckily you came prepared. The doors and windows are locked. You'll need to blast your way to the roof.
Zonal Division
An unfinished strategy wargame from Robin Siegemund from 1996.
Zonal War
A strategy war game by Dave King written in AMOS and released in 1997.
Zone 66

Rolling demo for a game where a pilot is warned by a mysterious stranger that something terrible is about to happen in his town. Rushing home, the pilot discovers that his wife and baby daughter were murdered. The stranger who tried to warn the pilot is gravely wounded; however, before dying, he passes some information to him. The hero is back on his plane, determined to avenge the deaths of his beloved ones, alone against terrorist forces whose true goals are yet unknown...

Zone 66 is a top-down shooter in which the player controls an aircraft, eliminating other planes as well as ground-based hostile units (tanks, etc.). The player-controlled aircraft is able to move in any direction, avoiding enemy fire or preparing a better angle for the next shot. There is a wide selection of aircraft to choose from and each of them, before the gameplay, can be individually equipped with different types of weapons like missiles and bombs.
Zone Warrior

In the distant future of the 30th century, the Earth is under attack by evil aliens, known as the Geeks. Their attempts at conquest have thus far proven unsuccessful due to humanity's advanced technology. But that might soon change: the Geeks have captured experimental time travel technology aboard an Earth defence satellite. Their plan is to travel into the past, disrupting the development of human technology, making conquest easy in the future. Our last hope is a lone soldier sent after the aliens. He must save Earth's scientists and destroy the Geeks in different time zones.

Zone Warrior is a side-scrolling platform game with exploration and shooting elements. It consists of five levels: Prehistoric, Egyptian, Medieval, Japanese and Future zones. Various enemies stand in the way, fitting the respective time period: dinosaurs and cavemen in prehistoric times, pharaohs in Egypt, robots in the future.
Zool 2

The intergalactic gremlin ninja Zool returns, and this time his enemies in the game were named Krool and his assistant Mental Block, whose goal is to stifle the world's imagination, causing rampant boredom. In his fight Zool is aided by his female companion, named Zooz (in a red costume), and his faithful dog Zoon. The ending contained a hint at a possible further sequel
Zool: Ninja of the 'Nth' Dimension

His name is Zool, and he is a gremlin-like creature from another dimension. He is forced to land on the Earth, but his sole goal is to attain the prestigious ranking of a Ninja. To do that, Zool will have to travel through six worlds, each divided into three stages, defeat his enemies, and prove himself worthy of that title.
Zoom!

Zoom! is an arcade style puzzle game. Your character Zoomer (a Pacman lookalike with arms & legs) must trace the outline of the squares on the game board to light them up. Points are awarded when full squares are formed, although the game also displays how many lines must still be completed. You proceed to the next level when all the squares have been lit up.
Zorb 2

A PD game by Kelvin Truswell, made in 1993. The goal for one player is to keep his marble on the board and for the other to use the many marbles to knock the other one off. There are stun, power punch and other items that give you more charge or punch when you collide.
Zorgons Revenge
Zorgons Revenge is an Amiga homebrew conversion of the 1983 Oric-1/Atomos game of the same name. The Amiga conversion was developed by Philippe Guichardon and released into the public domain in 2016.
Zork I

Zork: The Great Underground Empire is a classic text adventure game. The player begins as an "adventurer" standing near a white house in a nice forest, but soon descends into the Great Underground Empire, where most of the game takes place. The player's quest is to collect the Nineteen Treasures of Zork. 

As was typical for adventure games of its era, Zork does not use graphics. Instead, it communicates with the player via text, and the player interacts with the game by typing commands, such as "examine mailbox" or "take torch". For movement, the player types in geographical directions (such as "north" or "east" - or just "n" and "e"), and can check what items are being carried with the "inventory" command (or just "i"). 

The game was ported over from mainframes in the late 1970s, and is one of the first examples of its genre.
Zork II

Zork II: The Wizard of Frobozz is a text adventure, a sequel to the classic first Zork. Once again, the game is set in the Great Underground Empire, but this time the main goal is to face off against the titular Wizard. 

Like its predecessor, Zork II plays like any other text adventure: there are no graphics - only text - and the player types commands such as "lift cage" or "examine robot".
Zork III

In the third game of the adventure game series Zork, you are once again a nameless adventurer, only this time you won't travel through a beautiful magical land, but are immediately cast into a deep dungeon. Like in a dream, you hear a mysterious voice telling you that you have passed all the tests but one. When consciousness returns to you, you find yourself on the endless spiral of stairs, with only your trusty lantern near you... will you be able to survive the horrors of the Dungeon?

Like its predecessors, Zork III: The Dungeon Master is a text adventure game. You read descriptions of rooms and then interact with the game by typing commands. As all early Zork games, it is very easy to get stuck in the game, so you'll have to reload several times in order to find the correct way.
Zork Trilogy

Zork Trilogy is a compilation of all three of Infocom's original Zork games:

 Zork I: The Great Underground Empire
 Zork II: The Wizard of Frobozz
 Zork III: The Dungeon Master 

The package also includes an item that was featured as an in-game object in Zork games: the Zorkmid Coin.
Zork Zero

Lord Dimwit Flathead the Excessive was so much in love with himself that he ordered to erect a huge statue of himself in the Fublio Valley. This angered a local resident named Megaboz the Magnificent, who cast a curse over Dimwit and the entire Empire, and disappeared. Ninety-four years later, the curse is still in effect, and the king Wurb Flathead is looking for a brave adventurer who would find a way to remove it. This adventurer, naturally, is the game's protagonist, who possesses a piece of parchment given to him by his ancestors, which might be the key to the whole mystery...

Zork Zero: The Revenge of Megaboz is chronologically a prequel to the first three Zork games, and is a text adventure with a graphical interface and scene-based colors and borders. Like its predecessors, the game relies on puzzle-solving, including inventory item manipulation as well as logic-based puzzles.
Zork: The Undiscovered Underground

This was a free game released by Activision to celebrate and promote their newest game, at the time, Zork: Grand Inquisitor. It is a text only adventure done in the style on the original Zork games.

The year in 1066. You're a private, 7th class, in the Inquisition Guard. After getting relieved of your post at the Port Foozle Inquisition Gift Kiosk, you see the Pastor of Disaster, the Minister of Sinister, the Grand Inquisitor. It looks like he has a job for you. Yes, you. After asking about other, ANY other, guards to go instead, you have your orders. Sigh. Very well. Archaeologists have unearthed a tunnel that seems to lead to a new section of the Great Underground Empire or GUE. You are to enter this tunnel and explore the Great Underground Empire. You'll be back in no time. You hope. 
 
This Amiga version was made using the Amiga Frotz interpreter.
ZorkLand
ZorkLand is a classic-style arcade shooter developed for the Commodore Amiga.
Zorro C64
A static-recompilation port of the Commodore 64 game Zorro to the Amiga 1200, built with the same approach as the Buggy Boy C64-on-A1200 port.
Zorton Brothers
Zorton Brothers (Los Justicieros) was produced by Spanish company Picmatic in 1993.
Zut Alors!

A shareware adventure game from Brian Asbury, originally a Quilled adventure for ZX Spectrum, inspired by Games Workshop's En Guarde. The later Amiga version was written using Hatrack II and dates from 1991. The Amiga version was included on the Amiga Computing issue 43 (December 1991) coverdisk. Version 2.3 (from August 1994) fixes several serious bugs, such as issues with the drop/remove and save/load routines, as well as adds extra features. 
 
Zut Alors! is a text-only adventure in which you play the part of Cyrano de Bergerbar, a young blade recently arrived in Paris to seek his fortune. Cyrano has a burning ambition to join the King's Musketeers like his idols Athos, Porthos, Aramis and D'Artagnan, and, indeed, this is the object of the game. To win, you have to become a Musketeer. This is not as easy as it sounds, as you must firstly prove yourself in the ranks of lesser regiments.
Zut Alors! 2

Zut Alors II is the second shareware, text-only adventure in which you play the part of Cyrano de Bergerbar, a young blade who has recently arrived in Paris with a burning ambition to join the King's Musketeers like his idols Athos, Porthos, Aramis and D'Artagnan. This he has now achieved, and the second adventure takes up a few months after the first ended. Cyrano has now found better lodgings near the Musketeers' HQ and has acquired a dim but loyal servant named LePlank. The only black cloud on his otherwise bright horizon is the fact that his girlfriend Constance has left him.

Beyond that, the actual plot of the game will become clear as you play it...
Zuvicky Bukvicky
The first level of a rather unconventional text adventure from the near future, where it is not acceptable to be heterosexual. Created by Crudesys and released as freeware in 2008.
Zyconix

Colored blocks raining down on a playfield, we’ve seen that before. Zyconix takes the Columns principle (align three or more bricks of the same color to make them disappear) and adds a few twists of its own:

First, there are no groups or columns of stones, only single blocks.
Second, several of them slide down at once, and you select and move them with a cursor.
Third, only horizontal and diagonal lines disappear, but not stacks of the same color.
Add a few special objects from bombs to drills to a breakout ball that you can actually deflect grabbing a brick as a paddle, mix with four play modes (normal, pre-filled playfield and two time trial variants), and the result is a fast-pasted, tricky test of agility. 
Two players can compete in split-screen mode, where each removed line turns the corresponding number of bricks on the opponent’s field into indestructible obstacle blocks.
Zynaps

This horizontally-scrolling shoot 'em up features 16 levels and 450 screens of Nemesis-inspired action. You pilot a spacecraft through the levels, shooting as many of the encroaching meanies and mounted turrets as possible. Power-up tokens are offered for shooting some, which can be used to obtain better weapons including ground-attack lasers, speed ups and multiple bullets. Extra lives are on offer as well, which you'll certainly need, especially as you have to go back a long way when losing a life.
Zyrad

Zyrad is a shareware game by Steven Scougal that is similar to that of the Worms/Snake type game. Basically you have to collect objects whilst avoiding your ever growing tail. This game has a sequel, Zyrad 2.
Zyrad II

It's been a year since you got all the power crystals from the doomed star station Zyrad. All seemed quiet, but now, the Ena are back. This time they have attacked the Z2 superstation. It is all up to you again. A snake game, gather up the power crystals.
Zzzep

Released with issue 3 of the German magazine Amiga Fun, this flyabout multi-directional shooter lets you take your airship\zeppelin through the enemy controlled cave system. Bombing will help you get in, but only your wits can keep you alive! Gravity is constantly pulling you down, so get to the next refueling station if you want to keep this baby in the air.
Züri
A single player German language point and click adventure game created by Andreas Suter and Phillipp and Claude Gressly and released as freeware in 1994.
Świdroń

Świdroń is a Boulder Dash variant. As a miner the player must collect the designated number of diamonds in an abandoned mine and reach the exit doors before the time runs out. The task is made difficult by falling rocks and growing magma. The equipment includes cement bags and explosives. Cement surrounds the place where the miner stood, and the bomb will blow up the nearest surrounding fields, therefore you should leave the place very quickly. Rocks may be pushed on the drilled field and will fall on such field if it rise underneath. Walking through already drilled tunnels is much faster. To change magma into diamonds Świrdoń need to block it from each side.
Świąteczna Awaria

Świąteczna awaria is an arcade platform game for up to three players. Mischievous penguin has stolen Santa's sleigh with gifts moments before Christmas. To save Christmas the player must collect the designated number of yellow packages, avoiding penguins, birds, wastebaskets, computers and other hostile creatures. In addition to jumping ability each of the three main characters (Santa, snowman, bear) has a unique temporarily stunning weapon (star, snow ball, colorful ball) and may use numerous power ups (long jumping, extra weapon, shield, fast running, temporary paralysis of all opponents). Occasionally defeated enemy pops up a green package. Gathering it moves to one of two timed mini-games: find two same pictures and find one designated picture. Passing a mini-game is rewarded with an extra life. Originally released as a coverdisk\covermount for Amiga Computer Studio 2/98 in Poland. It was eventually released worldwide in 2008.
